title: [MEDIUM] tts: Retry-After header dropped by client; build pipeline ignores it on 429
description:
## Defect

§5.3 pseudocode and the wa-4cw.2 bead both explicitly require honoring the `Retry-After` header on HTTP 429:

> "Honor Retry-After if present, else backoff and retry."

The current implementation drops it at two layers:

**Layer 1 — `internal/tts/client.go:119-134`**: on non-200 responses, the client extracts only `StatusCode`, body bytes, and a derived `Retryable` boolean. The `Retry-After` header never leaves the function:

```go
return nil, &APIError{
    StatusCode: resp.StatusCode,
    Body:       body,
    Retryable:  retryableStatusCode(resp.StatusCode),
}
```

**Layer 2 — `internal/cli/build_pipeline.go::synthesizeChunkWithRetry`** (commit 45df37d): does its own coarse exponential backoff with no awareness of Retry-After. Even if it wanted to honor it, the `*APIError` it sees doesn't carry the header.

Pane-9's `internal/tts/retry.go::parseRetryAfter` is correct and well-tested — but it's package-private AND the build pipeline doesn't have access to a `*http.Response`, so the function is currently dead code on the production path.

## Why this matters

ElevenLabs's rate-limit response typically includes `Retry-After` (seconds). Ignoring it means:
- We retry too soon → likely to hit the same 429 again, burning attempts.
- We retry too late → unnecessary wall-clock waste during bulk runs (53-essay corpus, ~252 chunks per wa-cfn.2's estimate).

## Suggested fix

One of the following:

1. **Add `RetryAfter time.Duration` to `APIError`** in client.go; populate from `resp.Header.Get("Retry-After")` parsed via `tts.parseRetryAfter` (export it). Build pipeline checks `apiErr.RetryAfter` and honors it as the sleep, capped at `maxRetryAfter (300s)`.

2. **Export a public retry helper** from `internal/tts/` that wraps `Synthesize` + classifier + sleep, so the build pipeline doesn't reimplement retry. The TODO comment at build_pipeline.go:340 already flags this. This is the cleaner path.

## Severity rationale

MEDIUM not HIGH because:
- The fallback exponential backoff (capped at 60s) keeps retries bounded — we don't loop forever.
- Bulk-run wall-clock impact is real but not catastrophic (the bead's pessimistic 128min estimate already bakes in 15% retry rate; ignoring Retry-After might shift this by ~5-10min).
- Bulk-run resumability (manifest snapshot per essay) means a single misbehaving chunk doesn't lose hours of work.

But it IS an explicit spec violation per the bead text and §5.3 pseudocode, so it shouldn't ship without a public Retry-After path.

## References

- Spec: PLAN_FOR_AUDIO_LIBRARY.md §5.3 line 533
- Bead: wa-4cw.2 'Retry-After header handling (concrete)' section
- Code: `internal/tts/client.go:119-134`, `internal/cli/build_pipeline.go:276-345`
- Reviewed at commits 79aedf0 (client), 5fdc40d (retry), 45df37d (build pipeline)
close_reason: Shipped in 8a89527. APIError gains RetryAfter time.Duration; client.Synthesize populates it from Retry-After header (RFC 7231 §7.1.3 — both seconds and HTTP-date forms) via existing parseRetryAfter. synthesizeChunkWithRetry consumes via new pure helper computeRetryDelay(hint, attempt, base, rng) which honors hint (capped at retryAfterCap=60s) or falls back to exponential backoff. 13 new tests (5 client + 8 pipeline). Pane-8 notified before client.go edits; APIError grew one field with no break to existing readers.

title: Phase A — Worker + R2 infra (mostly done)
description:
# Phase A — Cloudflare Worker + R2 bucket

Implements: PLAN_FOR_AUDIO_LIBRARY.md §7 Phase A and §9 (privacy).

## Status

Mostly already done as of 2026-05-08:
- ✅ R2 bucket `wiki-audio` created — no public access, no public dev URL
- ✅ Access token generated, stored as Worker secret `ACCESS_TOKEN`,
   in `~/.wiki-audio/.env` as `WIKI_AUDIO_ACCESS_TOKEN`, and in
   1Password
- ✅ Worker deployed at `https://wiki-audio.jabyrne.workers.dev`;
   constant-time token gate verified (bare URL → 403, wrong token → 403,
   correct token + missing key → 404)

## What remains

The Worker source currently lives at `tools/wiki-audio/worker/` inside the
**wiki** repo. It needs to migrate into the new dedicated `wiki-audio`
GitHub repo as `worker/` once Phase B creates that repo. After migration,
delete the old directory from the wiki repo so there is exactly one source
of truth.

## Why a Worker (and not signed URLs / public bucket / Cloudflare Access)

See §9.3 comparison table. Chosen because:
- All major podcast apps pass `?t=<token>` through unchanged on enclosure
  fetches (no OAuth, no Basic Auth dance).
- Bucket can stay fully private behind R2 binding — no enumerable URLs.
- Token rotation is a one-touch operation: regen, `wrangler secret put`,
  `wiki-audio publish --feed-only`, re-paste feed URL into Pocket Casts.
  Old links 403 immediately, no object renames needed (token in query
  string, not in object path).
- Constant-time compare defeats timing oracles.

## Privacy threat model (kept here so future-me remembers)

Acceptable risk: someone who already knows me and can guess a domain
might find the feed. NOT acceptable: appearing in Cloudflare's public
dev URL listings, search-engine-indexable, or enumerable from R2 bucket
listings.

The plan does NOT defend against: me leaking the URL, Cloudflare itself,
a compromised laptop, or Pocket Casts logging enclosure URLs they fetch
on my behalf. All explicitly accepted in §9.4.

## §9.3 Privacy mechanism alternatives table (locked-in for v1)

The chosen mechanism is a Cloudflare Worker fronting a private R2 bucket
with a static `?t=<token>` query-string token compared in constant time.
Don't relitigate without a strong reason. Here is why each rejected
alternative is rejected:

| Mechanism | Privacy strength | Podcast app compat | Setup | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Worker + static query-string token** (chosen) | Strong; revocable; URLs unguessable; bucket fully private | All major apps pass `?t=` through unchanged | ~30 lines TS + 1 secret | **Chosen** |
| Long random URL path (obscurity only, public bucket) | Weak; URL leaks via referer / app logs / screenshots are unrecoverable without renaming objects | All apps | Zero code | Skipped — rotation requires re-keying every object |
| HTTP Basic Auth via Worker | Strong; revocable | Pocket Casts ✓, Apple ✓, Overcast ✓ historically; Spotify ✗ | ~20 lines TS | Equivalent to chosen; query-string token slightly easier to test in browser |
| S3-style pre-signed URLs (time-limited) | Strong while live; expires | Apps cache feed XML for hours; expired enclosure URLs cause download failures | Moderate | Skipped — operationally fragile |
| Cloudflare Access (zero-trust SSO) | Strongest | Most podcast apps cannot complete OAuth | High | Skipped — incompatible with podcast apps |
| Public bucket + RSS in private location | Episodes still enumerable if URL guessed | All apps | Zero code | Skipped — false sense of privacy |

The acid test for any future privacy proposal: does it break Pocket
Casts subscribing via a single URL paste? If yes, it's a non-starter.
The whole architecture exists to thread the needle of "private enough"
× "compatible with shipped podcast apps".

## §9.4 What this Phase does NOT defend against (read before "improving")

- **You sharing the feed URL.** Mitigation: token rotation (wa-76r.4).
- **Cloudflare itself.** Acceptable for personal-use TTS of public
  essays; if the threat model ever changes, this whole design must be
  re-examined — don't bolt encryption onto it.
- **Compromised laptop.** Out of scope; defended by full-disk
  encryption, not by this tool.
- **Pocket Casts logging.** Their servers see enclosure URLs. Switch
  to AntennaPod / Doughnut if not acceptable.

These are EXPLICIT acceptances. Anyone proposing an upgrade must first
show why one of the four has moved from "acceptable" to "unacceptable".

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## §6 'Cloudflare Worker outage' row — explicit acceptance

Per §6, this failure mode is ACCEPTED. No escalation path needed for v1:

- Cloudflare R2 + Workers high availability is industry-leading but not
  100%. Outages do happen (rare; minutes-to-hours).
- Podcast clients (Pocket Casts, Overcast, Apple Podcasts) all retry
  failed enclosure downloads automatically over hours/days.
- The user-perceived impact is 'this episode didn't load yet' — the
  app retries silently on background sync, no manual action needed.
- A status-page / monitoring solution would cost more (in maintenance
  + alert fatigue) than the actual outage exposure for a personal
  podcast.

ACCEPTED. No escalation needed. This comment exists so the §6 coverage
audit has a citation.

comments.text:
## Worker secret survives the move

The Cloudflare Worker secret `ACCESS_TOKEN` is bound to the Worker on
the Cloudflare account, NOT to the source code repo. So:

- Moving worker/ from the wiki repo to the wiki-audio repo does NOT
  invalidate or rotate the secret.
- `wrangler deploy` from the new location updates the SAME running
  Worker (provided wrangler.jsonc still names it `wiki-audio`).
- No re-secret step is needed.

Verify by running A2 (the 403/403/404 contract check) AFTER the move.
If the secret is gone for any reason, the bare URL with correct token
would 403 instead of returning 404 with a missing key.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
[REVIEW pane-4] Worker code (worker/src/index.ts) findings — landed at 6b65fff:

[HIGH] No HTTP method gate — POST/PUT/DELETE all reach the auth path and then BUCKET.get(). Should reject non-GET/HEAD with 405 before token compare. Currently a misconfigured client could attempt mutations; while R2 binding is read-side, there's no defense in depth and the README's "no information leakage" claim doesn't cover method-based oracles.

[HIGH] No HEAD branch — req.method is unchecked. A HEAD request runs `env.BUCKET.get(key)` which fetches the full object body (Class B op + bandwidth) only to discard it. Pocket Casts and similar apps HEAD enclosures during feed refresh to detect changes. Should branch on `req.method === 'HEAD'` to use `BUCKET.head(key)` and return 200 with headers + empty body. As-is, every feed refresh costs full audio download + R2 egress to Worker.

[HIGH] No Range request handling — podcast apps (Pocket Casts, Apple Podcasts, Overcast) use Range headers for streaming-style playback, resume-after-disconnect, and parallel chunked downloads. The Worker reads `req.url` only and never inspects `req.headers.get('range')`. Result: every resume / partial-download retry redownloads the entire MP3 (60+ MB for hour-long essays). R2 binding accepts `BUCKET.get(key, { range: { offset, length } })` and the response should be 206 with Content-Range. Without this, Phase G "spot-listen 3-5 random essays end-to-end" will burn through user mobile data on any flaky-network resume.

[MEDIUM] Manifest is reachable through the Worker via the same token — `pg.manifest.json` lives at the bucket root, so a client with the token can fetch it directly and enumerate every slug, body_hash, file_size_bytes, and timestamp. This may be intentional (token-equivalence: feed leak == manifest leak) but it's not stated in §9 or worker/README.md. Either (a) document this as accepted exposure in the README's "what this does NOT defend against" section, or (b) gate `pg.manifest.json` to a separate code path (e.g. require `?admin=1` plus token, or move the manifest under a path the Worker rejects).

[MEDIUM] cache-control: private, max-age=3600 applied to ALL responses — fine for audio (MP3s are immutable per body_hash), but for `pg.xml` it means after `wiki-audio publish` the podcast app may serve a cached feed for up to an hour and miss the new episode. Spec is silent on feed-vs-audio cache-control split. Recommendation: branch on key extension — `.xml` → `cache-control: no-cache, private`; everything else → `private, max-age=3600`.

[LOW] Length-check-first is a length oracle even with fixed-length tokens — when the token field is empty (`?? ""`), the check returns false in O(1); a 43-char wrong token returns false in O(43). README claims "no information leakage" between absent and wrong; the latency profile differs. This is marginal (token length 43 is published in §9.1) but the README's framing is overconfident. Cloudflare Workers expose `crypto.subtle.timingSafeEqual` natively which handles length internally — recommend switching, or pad the empty case to a fixed-length compare.

[LOW] No unit tests for timingSafeEqual — wa-3ia.5 covers live integration, but the function itself (length mismatch, content mismatch, exact match, empty-vs-empty, undefined-input behavior) has zero coverage. wrangler supports vitest; one test file would catch a regression where a future maintainer "simplifies" to `===`.

title: Re-verify constant-time token gate (403/403/404 contract)
description:
After the worker migration (and any time the Worker is touched), re-run
the three-step contract check that defines correctness for the access
gate:

1. Bare URL (no `?t=`)         → expect HTTP 403
2. Wrong token (`?t=garbage`)  → expect HTTP 403
3. Correct token + missing key → expect HTTP 404

If any of these returns the wrong status, the Worker is broken and the
bucket is potentially leaking. Roll back the deploy immediately.

## Why a constant-time compare specifically

§9 — defeats timing oracles. A naive `===` short-circuits on first
mismatched character; an attacker measuring response latency could
recover the token byte-by-byte. The TS implementation in §9.2 OR-folds
the XOR of every byte before checking equality.

## Operational note

This is a curl-only check; do not embed a unit test that calls the live
Worker (would burn rate limit and CI minutes). It's a runbook step, not
a test.

## OR-fold pattern (the actual TS implementation under test)

```typescript
function timingSafeEqual(a: string, b: string): boolean {
  if (a.length !== b.length) return false;
  let out = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < a.length; i++) out |= a.charCodeAt(i) ^ b.charCodeAt(i);
  return out === 0;
}
```

Properties this verification is checking:

- The loop ALWAYS runs to completion. A timing oracle would arise if
  the loop short-circuited on the first XOR mismatch.
- The length check is OK to short-circuit; token length (43) is a
  public constant, not a secret.
- The XOR-then-OR-fold returns 0 iff every byte matched. No data flow
  from any individual byte position to the early exit.

If a refactor replaces this with `===`, the curl-time test won't catch
it (the bandwidth jitter on the public internet dwarfs any per-byte
timing leakage). The 403/403/404 contract IS the test that flags a
broken implementation.

## 403 vs 404 contract (why these specific status codes)

- **403 (forbidden)** for ANY token failure (missing OR wrong). One
  status, one body. An attacker MUST NOT be able to distinguish
  "valid-looking but wrong" from "absent" — that's a token format
  oracle.
- **404 (not found)** ONLY after token validation passes. Tells the
  authorized user that a key is missing without exposing R2 listing
  semantics to anyone unauthenticated.
- The Worker returns 403 with body `"forbidden"` and 404 with body
  `"not found"` — fixed strings, identical between requests. No
  details about what was wrong.

Anyone who proposes returning 401 (with WWW-Authenticate) instead of
403 is implicitly proposing Basic Auth — see §9.3 alternatives table
on wa-3ia. Don't switch without re-reading.

## Acceptance criteria

Done = all THREE curl invocations executed against the live Worker URL within the same session, output captured (status codes only — no body), all three asserted statuses match. Concrete commands (assumes $WIKI_AUDIO_ACCESS_TOKEN exported from .env):

```
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://wiki-audio.jabyrne.workers.dev/pg/anything.mp3
# expected: 403

curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' 'https://wiki-audio.jabyrne.workers.dev/pg/anything.mp3?t=garbage'
# expected: 403

curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' "https://wiki-audio.jabyrne.workers.dev/does-not-exist.mp3?t=$WIKI_AUDIO_ACCESS_TOKEN"
# expected: 404
```

If WANTING signal beyond status codes, also confirm: bare URL and wrong-token bodies are byte-identical (`diff <(curl ...bare) <(curl ...wrong)` returns empty). That proves no token-format oracle.

## Fail path (any check returns the wrong status)

1. IMMEDIATELY: `wrangler rollback` to the previous Worker version. The current deploy is treated as broken.
2. Open a follow-up tracking bead ("worker token gate regression detected on YYYY-MM-DD") with the captured output.
3. Do NOT re-deploy until wa-3ia.5 (the integration test) passes locally against the rolled-back state — the rollback is the mitigation, the integration test is the gate to redeploy.
4. If rollback is not possible (wrangler doesn't have history), redeploy from `worker/` HEAD-1 via `git checkout HEAD~1 -- worker/ && wrangler deploy && git checkout HEAD -- worker/`.
close_reason: All 3 acceptance curls executed post-deploy. 403/403/404 verified.

title: Document worker architecture in worker/README.md
description:
Short README inside `worker/` that captures, for future-me:

- What the Worker does (R2 binding + token gate)
- Why constant-time compare (§9)
- The 403/403/404 contract that defines correctness
- How to deploy (`wrangler deploy`) and rotate the secret
  (`wrangler secret put ACCESS_TOKEN`)
- That the Worker MUST stay private — no public dev URL, no public
  R2 bucket access, no wide-open routes

Length goal: ~50 lines. This is a runbook, not a tutorial.

## Required README sections (canonical)

The README must include ALL of:

1. **Architecture** — one paragraph: R2 binding + token gate, no public
   dev URL, bucket private. Reference §9 of the plan.
2. **The 403/403/404 contract** (verbatim from wa-3ia.2).
3. **Why constant-time compare** — short explanation of timing oracles
   and the OR-fold pattern. Make a future contributor pause before
   replacing it with `===`.
4. **Deploy** — `cd worker && wrangler deploy`.
5. **Secret rotation** — `wrangler secret put ACCESS_TOKEN`. Cross-link
   to the full rotation runbook on wa-76r.4 (covers the .env, 1Password,
   and Pocket Casts re-subscribe steps too).
6. **MUST-stay-private invariants** — no public dev URL flag, no public
   R2 bucket access, no wide-open `*` routes.
7. **§9.4 — what this does NOT defend against** — repeat the four
   bullets (URL sharing, Cloudflare itself, compromised laptop, Pocket
   Casts logging) verbatim. This is the FIRST thing a future contributor
   sees if they're tempted to "harden" the Worker; it stops well-meaning
   downgrades that break podcast-app compatibility for theater.
8. **Yearly bucket-privacy verification** — link to wa-3ia.4.

Length goal: ~50–80 lines after these sections. Still a runbook, not
a tutorial.

## Acceptance criteria

Done = `worker/README.md` exists in the `Jacob2017/wiki-audio` repo, committed to main, with:

- All 8 sections from the canonical list above, present in that order, each with a level-2 heading (`## Architecture`, etc.).
- Section 2 (the 403/403/404 contract) wording is byte-for-byte identical to wa-3ia.2's contract block — copy, don't paraphrase. Future contributor diffing the two files should see zero divergence.
- Section 7 (§9.4 not-defended-against bullets) wording is byte-for-byte identical to wa-hqn / wa-3ia §9.4. Same reason.
- Length 50-100 lines including blank-line separators. < 50 = sections missing or truncated. > 100 = drift toward tutorial; tighten.
- `grep -c '^## ' worker/README.md` returns 8.

Verifiable artifact: a git commit on `Jacob2017/wiki-audio:main` whose touched files include `worker/README.md` and which passes the four checks above. No CI required — this is a doc, not code.

## Fail path

Doc reviews are subjective; treat "would future-me-stuck-at-2am understand this" as the bar. If yes, ship. If no, edit the offending section. Don't add new sections beyond the canonical 8 without amending this bead first.

comments.text:
[REVIEW pane-4] worker/README.md findings — landed at 35ed5e3:

[MEDIUM] Stale path reference vs 05f2c7a — line 43 still references `~/.config/wiki-audio/.env` after the spec relocation commit moved everything to `~/.wiki-audio/`. Either this README landed before the relocation and wasn't updated, or the relocation was incomplete. Should be `~/.wiki-audio/.env`.

[LOW] "An attacker MUST NOT be able to distinguish 'valid-looking but wrong' from 'absent'" — the README sets this as a load-bearing invariant (line 15) but the implementation distinguishes them via timing: empty-token compare exits in O(1) (length 0 vs 43), wrong-43-char compare runs the OR-fold loop in O(43). README and impl should agree — either tighten impl (use `crypto.subtle.timingSafeEqual` or fixed-length pad) or soften README ("status code is identical; per-byte timing is masked but length-mismatch path is faster — token length is public so this is acceptable").

[LOW] "The length check at the top is fine to short-circuit — token length (43) is a public constant" — line 21 acknowledges the length oracle as accepted, contradicting line 15's "MUST NOT be able to distinguish". The README is internally inconsistent on what the timing guarantee actually is. Pick one stance and wire both lines to it.

title: Add yearly bucket-privacy verification reminder
description:
Schedule a yearly /schedule reminder that walks through:

1. R2 dashboard: confirm bucket `wiki-audio` is NOT public, dev URL OFF.
2. curl bare worker URL: expect 403.
3. curl with wrong token: expect 403.
4. curl with correct token + no key path: expect 404.

## Why a calendar-based check

§6 — Cloudflare's dashboard UX has historically made it easy to flip
dev URLs on by accident. A defensive yearly check catches dashboard drift
even if no one touched the bucket deliberately. Treats privacy as a
property to defend, not a one-time configuration step.

## Acceptance criteria (per yearly instance)

This bead is RECURRING. "Done" applies to the current year's check, not the bead overall — the bead never closes.

For year YYYY, "done" means ALL of the following executed and the run logged to `~/.cache/wiki-audio/audit-YYYY-MM-DD.txt`:

1. Cloudflare R2 dashboard (browser screenshot or text dump):
   - Bucket `wiki-audio`: Public access = OFF.
   - Bucket `wiki-audio`: Custom domains tab — none / only the intended Worker route.
   - Bucket `wiki-audio`: Public Development URL = OFF (the toggle is per-bucket and Cloudflare flips its default UI periodically).
2. `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://wiki-audio.jabyrne.workers.dev/pg/how-to-do-great-work.mp3` → exits printing `403`.
3. `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' 'https://wiki-audio.jabyrne.workers.dev/pg/how-to-do-great-work.mp3?t=garbage'` → `403`.
4. `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' 'https://wiki-audio.jabyrne.workers.dev/does-not-exist.mp3?t=$WIKI_AUDIO_ACCESS_TOKEN'` → `404`.
5. `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' 'https://wiki-audio.jabyrne.workers.dev/pg/how-to-do-great-work.mp3?t=$WIKI_AUDIO_ACCESS_TOKEN'` → `200` (or 206 with Range header).

The audit log file is the verifiable artifact. One file per year. After completing, re-schedule the reminder for next year.

## Fail path (if any check fails)

- Step 1 fail (dashboard drift): treat as a security incident. Flip the toggle back, then run `wiki-audio publish --feed-only` after rotating the token (wa-76r.4) — assume URL was crawlable while the dashboard was wrong.
- Step 2 or 3 fail: the Worker's token gate is broken. Roll back to the last known-good Worker deploy via `wrangler rollback`. Open a follow-up bead to investigate before redeploying.
- Step 4 fail (returns 403 instead of 404): token validation is short-circuiting somewhere. Same rollback. The 403/403/404 contract is the regression signal.
- Step 5 fail (returns anything other than 200/206): R2 binding is broken or bucket key was deleted. Check R2 console, restore via `mc cp` from backup if needed.

[pane-2] Yearly bucket-privacy audit script + docs landed.

The bead is RECURRING — it never closes against the schedule artifact, only against the *infrastructure* that makes the recurrence runnable. This commit adds that infrastructure: a script that automates the four curl checks, a docs section that explains both the script and the dashboard step (browser-only), and scheduling hints for cron / systemd-timer / `/schedule` / plain calendar reminder.

Marking the bead "done" against my deliverable; the per-year audit-YYYY-MM-DD.txt artifact is on the operator's calendar from here on.

## What landed

| path | change |
|------|--------|
| scripts/audit-bucket-privacy.sh | NEW — automates curl steps 2-5; appends RFC3339-timestamped log entries to `~/.cache/wiki-audio/audit-YYYY-MM-DD.txt`; exits non-zero on any unexpected status |
| worker/README.md | expanded the existing "Yearly bucket-privacy verification" stub into a full procedure (script + dashboard + scheduling + fail paths + pre-Phase-G note) |
| README.md | added a cross-link from the top-level "Cross-links" section pointing at the script and at worker/README.md's procedure |

## Script behaviour (verified live against `wiki-audio.jabyrne.workers.dev`)

```
[2026-05-09T06:08:42Z] bare-no-token             got=403 expected=403  ✓
[2026-05-09T06:08:42Z] wrong-token               got=403 expected=403  ✓
[2026-05-09T06:08:42Z] right-token+missing       got=404 expected=404  ✓
[2026-05-09T06:08:42Z] right-token+real-key      got=404 expected=200  ✗ (Phase G hasn't run)
exit=1
```

The 1-of-4 failure is exactly the documented benign pre-Phase-G state. Once audio is published the script flips to 4-of-4 with no edits.

## Script knobs (all optional, all documented in `--help`)

- `--base-url <url>` — override the Worker URL (default https://wiki-audio.jabyrne.workers.dev)
- `--sample-key <key>` — the real-key probe target (default pg/how-to-do-great-work.mp3)
- `WIKI_AUDIO_ACCESS_TOKEN` — sourced from env, or from ~/.wiki-audio/.env if absent
- `WIKI_AUDIO_BASE_URL`, `WIKI_AUDIO_SAMPLE_KEY`, `WIKI_AUDIO_MISSING_KEY` — env-var equivalents

The script refuses to run with an empty token (clear stderr message + exit 2) so a misconfigured cron entry surfaces as a failed unit, not a silent pass.

## Coordination

Reservations on `scripts/audit-bucket-privacy.sh`, `worker/README.md`, `README.md` released after commit. No collisions with pane-5's in-flight wa-3gf work (`internal/tts/client.go`, `internal/cli/build_pipeline.go`) — clean separation.

title: Integration test: live Worker token gate (403/403/404 contract via curl)
description:
A scripted integration test that exercises the Cloudflare Worker's
constant-time token gate against the live deployment. Gated by
`WIKI_AUDIO_RUN_INTEGRATION=1` (see wa-76r.10) and intended to be run
as part of pre-release verification, NOT in unit-test CI.

## Contract under test (§9.2)

- Bare URL (no `?t=`)         → HTTP 403
- Wrong token (`?t=garbage`)  → HTTP 403
- Correct token + missing key → HTTP 404
- Correct token + real key    → HTTP 200 (range request supported)

## Implementation

A Go test file `worker_integration_test.go` with `//go:build integration`
that uses `net/http` to fire the four requests and assert status codes.
NOT a curl shell script — keeping it Go means it lives next to the
rest of the suite and uses the same testutil helpers.

## Test Plan

| Test name                            | Expectation |
|--------------------------------------|-------------|
| no_token_returns_403                 | HTTP 403; no body leaks bucket info |
| wrong_token_returns_403              | HTTP 403; same body as no_token (no oracle) |
| right_token_missing_key_returns_404  | HTTP 404 |
| right_token_existing_key_returns_200 | HTTP 200; Content-Type audio/mpeg |
| range_request_supported              | HTTP 206 with Content-Range; body size matches |
| timing_within_one_stddev             | 100 wrong-token requests; assert mean≈median (no timing oracle) |

## Timing test

Optional / skippable. 100 requests with random wrong tokens; record
elapsed time. Assert standard deviation small relative to mean. This
is a heuristic check on constant-time comparison; a real timing
attack across the public internet is impractical so we test for
"obvious leakage", not cryptographic guarantees.

## Cleanup

Test PUTS no objects. The `right_token_existing_key_returns_200` test
uses a fixture key that is uploaded once during setup (or read from
the existing bucket). No cleanup required.

## Structured logging

slog.With("test", t.Name(), "service", "worker", "status_expected",
expectedCode, "status_got", gotCode, "elapsed_ms", elapsed).

## Why automate a runbook

wa-3ia.2 already calls for a manual three-step curl check. This bead
encodes the same contract as a repeatable test so a future Worker
refactor can't silently break the gate. The manual gate stays — it's
a release-blocker, not a per-commit check.

comments.author: pane-3
comments.text:
## Closing wa-3ia.5 — live Worker token-gate harness shipped

### What landed

`test/integration/worker_integration_test.go` (367 lines) + `test/integration/doc.go` (8 lines) — both under `//go:build integration`. Six tests against the live Worker at `https://wiki-audio.jabyrne.workers.dev`, gated by `WIKI_AUDIO_RUN_INTEGRATION=1` via `testutil.RequireIntegration` (wa-76r.10).

| Test | Status (last run) | Assertion |
|---|---|---|
| `TestWorker_NoTokenReturns403` | PASS | bare URL ⇒ 403; body must NOT mention bucket |
| `TestWorker_WrongTokenReturns403` | PASS | wrong token ⇒ 403, body byte-identical to no-token body (no token-format oracle) |
| `TestWorker_RightTokenMissingKeyReturns404` | PASS | token-before-key check; 403 here would mean gate is short-circuiting |
| `TestWorker_RightTokenExistingKeyReturns200` | SKIP | fixture key absent pre-Phase-G; benign per spec; override via `WIKI_AUDIO_FIXTURE_KEY` |
| `TestWorker_RangeRequestSupported` | SKIP | depends on existing key |
| `TestWorker_TimingWithinOneStddev` | PASS | 100 wrong-token requests; mean=10ms, stddev=1ms, ratio=0.14 (threshold ≤1.5) |

### Verification matrix

| Mode | Cmd | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Unit, no tag | `go test ./...` | All pass; `test/integration` shows `[no test files]` (tag excludes them) |
| Tagged, env unset | `go test -tags=integration ./test/integration/` | 6 SKIP with "set WIKI_AUDIO_RUN_INTEGRATION=1 to run integration tests" |
| Tagged + env set | `WIKI_AUDIO_RUN_INTEGRATION=1 go test -tags=integration ./test/integration/` | 4 PASS, 2 SKIP (fixture absent), 1.4s total |

`go vet` (both modes) and `gofmt` clean.

### Design choices worth noting

- **Path: `test/integration/`** — separate from `internal/` to keep the unit/integration boundary visible at directory level. The package compiles to `[no test files]` under unit runs.
- **Per-test `httpClient()` returns a fresh client** — a hung connection in one test cannot starve another.
- **`urlNoToken` / `urlWithToken` helpers + `redactToken`** — all test logging goes through redaction so a CI failure log can never leak the access token.
- **Body equality between no-token and wrong-token responses** — pinned because §9.2 calls out the no-format-oracle property; wa-3ia.2's runbook only checks status codes.
- **Cache-Control assertion** — `private` substring required on 200 responses. wa-3ia.1 lists this as a load-bearing property; if Cloudflare's edge ever caches across token values, this test fails first.
- **Fixture-key skip is permissive** — pre-Phase-G the bucket is empty; the test reports "set WIKI_AUDIO_FIXTURE_KEY to an existing key" rather than failing. Once Phase G uploads `pg/how-to-do-great-work.mp3` the default key resolves and the 200/206 tests light up automatically.
- **Timing test is deliberately permissive** — public-internet jitter dwarfs any per-byte timing leak; the threshold (stddev/mean ≤ 1.5) catches catastrophic divergence, not subtle leakage. Real timing-attack resistance is a structural property of the Worker source, not something this test can verify.

### Worktree workflow

Worked on branch `pane3-wa-3ia.5` in worktree `/data/projects/wiki-audio-pane3`, merged back to main with `--no-ff` (commit `4c0760d`). The dedicated worktree solved the cross-contamination race that hit commit `07b2162` earlier in the session — staged files in the worktree don't appear in the main repo's index. Recommend extending this pattern to all panes when they have a multi-step task with intermediate `git add`s.

title: Phase E — TTS + concat + ID3 spike (one essay end-to-end)
description:
# Phase E — Synthesize one essay end-to-end and listen on phone

Implements: PLAN_FOR_AUDIO_LIBRARY.md §5.3 (TTS dispatch), §5.4 (concat),
§7 Phase E (the spike).

## Goal

Run `wiki-audio build --slug how-to-do-great-work` end to end. Manually
upload the resulting MP3 to R2 with `aws s3 cp` or `rclone` (publish
command isn't built yet — that's Phase F). Listen on the phone via the
Worker URL. Verify ID3 tags display correctly in Pocket Casts.

## Why this is its own phase (not folded into Phase F)

We don't want to discover a voice-quality problem AFTER building the
publish/RSS plumbing. One essay round-trip is the cheapest way to derisk:
- Voice "Christopher" sounds right across an hour of listening
- Flash v2.5 prosody is acceptable on PG's prose
- Footnote-at-end-of-paragraph cadence works as listening (not just on
  paper)
- ID3 tags survive the ffmpeg crossfade pipeline
- The 50ms acrossfade between chunks is inaudible

If any of these fail, we adjust here without touching publish code.

## ElevenLabs subscription tactics

Subscribe to Pro tier for one month (~$99) immediately before bulk run
in Phase G. Cancel at month-end and switch to PAYG top-ups (~$0.50 per
new PG-length essay added). Phase H handles the cancel.

## Retry/backoff strategy (§5.3)

Per-chunk: exponential backoff with jitter, 3 retry attempts, honor
`Retry-After` on 429. Classify errors:
- timeout / 5xx / 429  → retry with backoff
- 402 / 403            → FATAL (out of credits / auth) — abort whole run
- 200                  → stream MP3 bytes back

Manifest is uploaded after each essay completion so a Ctrl-C or fatal
abort mid-bulk-run is resumable.

## Concat: pairwise loop, not one big filter_complex

ffmpeg's `filter_complex` doesn't chain `acrossfade` cleanly across N
inputs in practice. Implement as pairwise loop:
  out = chunk[0]
  for i in 1..N: out = acrossfade(out, chunk[i], d=0.05)

title: Implement internal/tts/ ElevenLabs HTTP client
description:
POST \`/v1/text-to-speech/<voice_id>\` with body:

\`\`\`json
{ \"text\": \"...\", \"model_id\": \"eleven_flash_v2_5\", \"output_format\": \"mp3_44100_64\" }
\`\`\`

Headers: \`xi-api-key: <ELEVENLABS_API_KEY>\`, \`accept: audio/mpeg\`,
\`content-type: application/json\`. Use net/http with a per-request
timeout (cfg.RequestTimeoutS default 60s).

Returns: \`io.ReadCloser\` of MP3 bytes on 200, classified error on
anything else.

## Why mp3_44100_64

§8.7: 64 kbps mono is indistinguishable from higher bitrates for
spoken voice; bigger bitrates waste storage and bandwidth without a
perceptual win. 44.1 kHz is the universal podcast sample rate.

## Why model_id is part of every request (not URL-routed)

ElevenLabs's API takes \`model_id\` in the JSON body. We feed it from
config (default \"eleven_flash_v2_5\"). Whenever we change the model,
the body_hash auto-invalidates (D1) and every essay regenerates.

## What we deliberately don't pass

- voice_settings (use the voice's defaults; manual tweaking is a v2
  expansion if voice quality concerns appear)
- pronunciation_dictionary_locators (none for v1)
- previous_request_ids (no streaming — one chunk per request)

## Timeout knobs (concrete — addresses §6 ambiguity)

| Knob                       | Default | Configurable via                     | Notes |
|----------------------------|---------|--------------------------------------|-------|
| Per-request timeout        | 60s     | cfg.RequestTimeoutS                  | Used as net/http Client.Timeout. Covers DNS + connect + write + read of one TTS request. |
| Per-chunk total budget     | ~197s   | derived (see wa-4cw.2)               | 3 attempts × 60s + backoffs + jitter. |
| Per-essay total budget     | none    | n/a                                  | Deliberately uncapped: long essays have many chunks; failing on a wall clock is more frustrating than completing slowly. |
| Per-bulk-run total budget  | none    | n/a                                  | Bulk run is interruptible (Ctrl-C; resume via per-essay manifest snapshot). No daemon-style watchdog needed. |

## Why no essay-level cap

§6 "ElevenLabs request timeout (60s)" applies to ONE request. The
larger essay-level concern is resumability, addressed by saving the
manifest after each successful essay (wa-4cw.5 step i). A hung essay
can be Ctrl-C'd and re-run cleanly.

## Where the 60s default comes from

ElevenLabs flash_v2_5 typically returns audio in 5-15s for our chunk
sizes (~4000 chars). 60s is 4x the p99 of our observed latency, so a
timeout firing means the connection is genuinely wedged — retry is
appropriate.

## Voice model alternatives (§8.4 — why Flash v2.5)

| Model                       | Credits/char | Quality | Verdict for v1 |
|-----------------------------|--------------|---------|----------------|
| `eleven_flash_v2_5` (chosen)| 0.5          | Very good | Default — best quality at the cheaper rate |
| `eleven_turbo_v2_5`         | 0.5          | Slightly less expressive than Flash | Real-time use cases; nothing to gain here |
| `eleven_multilingual_v2`    | 1.0          | Best | Reserved for the per-page voice override in v2 (Phase I.4) on ~10 most-relistened essays — 2x cost not worth it for the bulk corpus |
| `eleven_monolingual_v1`     | 1.0          | Older, slightly worse than Flash | Skip — superseded by Flash at half the cost |

If a future polish reveals Flash's prosody fails on PG-specific phrasing,
the override path (config field `model_id`) lets us flip to Multilingual
v2 without code changes; the body_hash auto-invalidates and re-renders.

## Audio format alternatives (§8.7 — why mp3_44100_64 specifically)

| Format             | Bitrate | Size for full corpus | Verdict |
|--------------------|---------|----------------------|---------|
| **MP3 64 kbps mono** (chosen) | 64 kbps  | ~520 MB | Universal podcast support, indistinguishable from higher bitrates for voice |
| MP3 128 kbps mono  | 128 kbps | ~1.0 GB | Wasted bytes — no audible win on speech |
| Opus 32 kbps       | 32 kbps  | ~260 MB | Excellent quality, smaller files, BUT Apple Podcasts has historically poor Opus support. Skip — feed compatibility matters more than 260 MB of R2 storage |
| AAC 64 kbps        | 64 kbps  | ~520 MB | Slightly better than MP3 but no real win, and ID3 tagging is more universal than MP4 metadata in podcast apps |

Don't change `output_format` without re-running the full corpus — the
body_hash includes voice_id + model_id but NOT bitrate explicitly, so a
silent format change would leave old MP3s on R2. If we ever switch, do
it as a deliberate `--force` rebuild.

title: Validate ID3 tags display correctly in Pocket Casts
description:
After E8 lands the MP3 on the phone (via direct URL), confirm:

- Title shows as \"How to Do Great Work\" (not \"how-to-do-great-work.mp3\")
- Artist shows as \"Paul Graham\"
- Album shows as \"Paul Graham Essays\"
- Date present (any format the app accepts)

If any of these fail, fix internal/id3/ before Phase F. Pocket Casts'
display is the only metadata surface that matters for personal use.

## Acceptance criteria

Done = the spike MP3, sideloaded onto Pocket Casts (or accessed via direct URL during Phase E pre-feed), shows the EXACT four strings below in the playback UI:

- Title: "How to Do Great Work" (NOT "how-to-do-great-work.mp3", NOT "How To Do Great Work" with title-case smashing).
- Artist: "Paul Graham".
- Album: "Paul Graham Essays".
- Date: any value Pocket Casts renders in its UI as a year (Y2K-style display is acceptable; missing date field rendering as blank is NOT acceptable).

Verifiable artifact: a screenshot of the Pocket Casts "now playing" / episode-detail screen showing all four fields. Save to `~/.cache/wiki-audio/id3-verify-screenshot.png` (or just visually confirm and check off — screenshot is for repeatability if a regression hits later).

## Fail path

- Title shows the slug or filename → TIT2 frame is wrong / missing. Fix `internal/id3/` (wa-4cw.4) frame mapping.
- Artist or Album wrong → TPE1 / TALB frame mapping wrong. Same fix location.
- Date missing → TDRC (id3v2.4) or TYER (id3v2.3) frame missing; `bogem/id3v2` defaults vary.

After the id3 fix, regenerate the SPIKE MP3 only (the concat output gets re-tagged; no need to re-run TTS — chunks are cached). Re-sideload to phone, re-check.

This blocks Phase F: shipping a feed where Pocket Casts displays "how-to-do-great-work.mp3" as the title is unacceptable for personal use.

title: Unit tests for TTS retry classifier (§5.3 error table)
description:
Table-driven tests in `internal/tts/retry_test.go` that exercise the
classifier built in wa-4cw.2. The classifier is the load-bearing
function — it decides retry vs FATAL — so every row of the §5.3 error
table must be exercised by name.

## Test Plan

| Test name                    | Input                                  | Expected classification |
|------------------------------|----------------------------------------|-------------------------|
| timeout_deadline_exceeded    | context.DeadlineExceeded               | retryable + backoff     |
| timeout_net_timeout          | net.Error{Timeout=true}                | retryable + backoff     |
| http_429_with_retry_after    | 429, Retry-After: 17                   | retryable + sleep ≥17s  |
| http_429_no_retry_after      | 429, no header                         | retryable + computed backoff |
| http_500                     | 500 Internal Server Error              | retryable               |
| http_502                     | 502 Bad Gateway                        | retryable               |
| http_503                     | 503 Service Unavailable                | retryable               |
| http_504                     | 504 Gateway Timeout                    | retryable               |
| http_402                     | 402 Payment Required                   | FATAL — abort run       |
| http_403                     | 403 Forbidden (auth)                   | FATAL — abort run       |
| http_400                     | 400 Bad Request (programmer error)     | FATAL — abort run       |
| http_404                     | 404 Not Found (voice id wrong)         | FATAL — abort run       |
| http_200                     | 200 OK                                 | success                 |
| network_error_dns            | net.Error{Temporary=true}              | retryable               |
| connection_reset             | "connection reset by peer"             | retryable               |

## Backoff math test

A separate test verifies `computeBackoff(attempt, base)`:
- base=2, attempt=0 → 2 + jitter[0,1) → in [2,3)
- base=2, attempt=1 → 4 + jitter[0,1) → in [4,5)
- base=2, attempt=2 → 8 + jitter[0,1) → in [8,9)
- attempt counter exhausted → returns sentinel "no more retries"

Use `math/rand`'s seeded source so jitter is deterministic in tests.

## Fake HTTP server

Use `httptest.NewServer` with a handler that returns programmable
status codes per request. Don't mock at the http.Client level — use a
real round-trip so the classifier sees real http.Response shapes.

## Structured logging during tests

Each subtest uses `slog.With("test", t.Name())`. Capture logs via a
`slog.NewTextHandler(buf, ...)` so a test failure prints exactly which
classification path tripped. Assert log records include the
classification verdict (retryable | fatal | success) so future
refactors can't silently change behavior.

## Why this is its own bead (not folded into wa-4cw.2)

The classifier is one of the riskiest pieces of code in the project —
silently misclassifying a 429 as fatal would brick a bulk run; silently
misclassifying a 402 as retryable would burn through credits. A
dedicated test bead with explicit table coverage makes regressions
loud.

## Additional test rows (added by polish pass 2 — Retry-After validation)

| Test name                              | Input                                  | Expected behavior |
|----------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|-------------------|
| retry_after_negative_falls_back        | 429, Retry-After: -5                   | computed backoff (ignore header) |
| retry_after_garbage_falls_back         | 429, Retry-After: "banana"             | computed backoff (ignore header) |
| retry_after_huge_falls_back            | 429, Retry-After: 99999                | computed backoff (capped at 300s rule) |
| retry_after_zero_uses_zero             | 429, Retry-After: 0                    | retry immediately (sleep=0) |
| retry_after_http_date_in_past          | 429, Retry-After: <past HTTP-date>     | computed backoff (delta is negative) |
| retry_after_http_date_within_window    | 429, Retry-After: <now+30s HTTP-date>  | sleep ~30s |
| backoff_cap_60s                        | base=200, attempt=5                    | sleep capped at 60s |

## Exit-code assertions (orchestration, NOT classifier)

The classifier returns a sentinel; the build pipeline (wa-4cw.5)
turns FATAL into os.Exit(1). One end-to-end orchestration test in
wa-4cw.5 asserts:

- httptest server returns 402 on first chunk
- build process exits with code 1
- stderr contains the API body excerpt

title: Integration test: real ElevenLabs API call (opt-in, credit-burning)
description:
A `//go:build integration` test in `internal/tts/tts_integration_test.go`
that hits the real ElevenLabs API. Gated by both the build tag and
`WIKI_AUDIO_RUN_INTEGRATION=1` (see wa-76r.10).

## Test Plan

| Test name                            | Setup                              | Expectation |
|--------------------------------------|------------------------------------|-------------|
| smoke_short_request                  | text="Hello, this is a test.", flash_v2_5 | 200 OK; mp3 bytes > 0 |
| respects_request_timeout             | RequestTimeoutS=1 (force timeout)  | retry classifier returns retryable |
| invalid_voice_id_yields_4xx          | voice_id="bogus"                   | classifier marks FATAL |
| empty_text_yields_400                | text=""                            | classifier marks FATAL (programmer error) |
| header_xi_api_key_required           | omit header                        | 401; classifier marks FATAL |
| credits_remaining_after_run          | log credits; assert > 0            | informational; helps catch "almost out" |

## Gating (boilerplate from wa-76r.10)

```go
func TestMain(m *testing.M) {
    testutil.RequireIntegration(...) // skip whole file if not opted in
    testutil.RequireCredentials("ELEVENLABS_API_KEY", "ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ID")
    os.Exit(m.Run())
}
```

## Cost cap

The smoke test sends ~25 chars × flash_v2_5 (0.5 credits/char) ≈ 13
credits = ~$0.0001. The whole suite runs <$0.01. Document this in the
test file's package comment so future-me doesn't worry about running it.

## Structured logging

```go
slog.With(
  "test", t.Name(),
  "service", "elevenlabs",
  "model_id", cfg.ModelID,
  "credits_before", before,
  "credits_after", after,
)
```

The credits delta lets us detect "API charged us but didn't return
audio" — a class of bug worth catching early.

## What this DOESN'T test

- Bulk runs (G-phase concern; covered by wa-cfn.2)
- Voice quality (subjective; wa-4cw.9 manual gate)
- Concurrent requests (v1 is serial by design)

title: concat: raise DefaultPerStepTimeout to 5m + regression tests for wa-4cw.8 root cause
description:
Follow-up to wa-4cw.8 spike failure. The Phase E spike crashed at concat
step 13/17 because internal/concat.DefaultPerStepTimeout (30s) is too
small for late pairwise steps with cumulative 20+ MB left-input.

## Root cause (cross-link wa-4cw.8 closing comment)

Pairwise reduce in concat.go runs N-1 ffmpeg invocations, each processing
the cumulative left-input + one new chunk. Step durations grow roughly
linearly with N. wa-4cw.8 empirical:

  step  1: 5.8s    step  7: 18.8s   step 13: 32.9s
  step  2: 7.9s    step  8: 21.3s   step 14: 36.1s
  step  3: 10.4s   step  9: 23.5s   step 15: 37.4s
  step  4: 12.6s   step 10: 26.2s   step 16: 40.2s
  step  5: 14.3s   step 11: 29.0s   step 17: 41.2s (final)
  step  6: 16.7s   step 12: 31.5s

Original 30s default would always kill ~step 12-13 for an 18-chunk PG
essay. wa-4cw.3's unit tests used 0.2s sine fixtures so even step 9 of
the 10-chunk test was 1.8s — the timeout never came close to firing in
the test suite, but it kills production.

## Fix

1. Bump DefaultPerStepTimeout from 30s to 5m. Justified: 5m provides 7×
   headroom over the worst observed case (41.2s), and a hypothetical
   100-chunk essay would still finish each step inside 5m at the
   observed growth rate.

2. Update the comment block on the constant to (a) cite wa-4cw.8
   empirical evidence, (b) explain why the value is per-step (not total
   pipeline) and grows linearly with N, (c) caution against tightening
   without re-measuring on a 50+ chunk run.

3. Add a regression test that pins the constant within a [4m, 30m] band.
   The 4m floor reflects the observed 41.2s ceiling × ~6 safety margin.
   The 30m ceiling protects against a future "give it more headroom"
   change masking a real hang. The test is the documentation: a future
   PR that lowers the constant has to surface this conversation.

4. Add an 18-chunk loop-completes test (matches wa-4cw.8 essay shape).
   This won't fail under the old 30s default because fixtures are tiny,
   but it locks in the loop semantics at the count where production
   broke.

## Acceptance

- DefaultPerStepTimeout in internal/concat/concat.go is 5*time.Minute.
- Comment on the constant cites wa-4cw.8 empirical data.
- TestDefaultPerStepTimeout_AccommodatesObservedRealLoad passes and
  fails on a tightening PR.
- TestEighteenChunks_RunsToCompletion passes.
- go vet ./internal/concat/ clean. go test ./internal/concat/ clean.

## Deliberately NOT in scope

- Build pipeline chunk-cache-skip (that's wa-4cw.14, pane-2's territory).
- Switching to a non-pairwise concat algorithm (spec mandates pairwise
  per §5.4).
- A full 18×4-min real-audio test (slow, would burn EL credits to
  regenerate, doesn't add coverage beyond the constant-pin).

title: Retry/backoff/jitter with error classification (§5.3)
description:
Per-chunk retry policy from §5.3:

- timeout (context.DeadlineExceeded)        → backoff + retry
- 429 Too Many Requests                     → honor Retry-After or backoff + retry
- 5xx                                       → backoff + retry
- 402 Payment Required, 403 Forbidden       → FATAL — abort whole run
- 200                                       → return body

Backoff: \`base * 2^attempt + rand[0,1)\` seconds, where base is
cfg.RetryBackoffBase (default 2). Max attempts = cfg.RetryAttempts
(default 3).

## Why FATAL on 402/403

402 = out of credits; 403 = auth failure. Neither will resolve by
retrying, and continuing wastes calls + time. Fail loudly with the API
error body so the user can act (top up credits, fix the API key).

## Why the run is resumable after FATAL

The manifest is uploaded after each successful essay (§6, F2). So a
fatal abort 30 essays in leaves the first 30 in R2, and the next
\`build\` re-checks hashes and skips them. No work lost, no manual
recovery needed.

## Jitter rationale

Pure exponential backoff causes thundering herd if multiple chunks
all retry on the same 429. Adding [0,1) seconds of jitter spreads them
out. Cheap, standard practice.

## Concrete numbers (added by polish pass 2 — addresses §6 hand-waviness)

- **RetryAttempts**: 3 (configurable via cfg.RetryAttempts).
- **RetryBackoffBase**: 2 seconds (configurable via cfg.RetryBackoffBase).
- **Backoff schedule** (deterministic given seed): attempt 0 → [2,3)s,
  attempt 1 → [4,5)s, attempt 2 → [8,9)s. Total worst-case wait
  before FATAL (excluding the request itself): ~14s.
- **Backoff cap**: a hard cap of 60s per individual backoff sleep
  prevents pathological values from cfg overrides. After cap is
  reached, jitter still applies on top.
- **Total per-request budget**: each attempt has its own
  cfg.RequestTimeoutS deadline (default 60s, see wa-4cw.1). So the
  whole retry cycle for one chunk is bounded at:
  3 * 60s (timeouts) + 2s + 4s + 8s (waits) + 3s (jitter cap) = ~197s
  worst case before FATAL.

## Retry-After header handling (concrete)

When the server sends 429 with a Retry-After header:

- If the header is a positive integer in seconds AND ≤ 300s: sleep
  that long, then retry.
- If the header is a date in HTTP-date format AND the delta is in
  [0, 300]s: sleep until that time.
- If the header is missing, negative, non-numeric, or > 300s:
  fall back to the computed backoff schedule above (do NOT trust
  arbitrarily large or malformed Retry-After values; an upstream bug
  could otherwise stall the whole run for hours).

The 300s cap is deliberate: ElevenLabs's typical rate-limit window
is on the order of seconds-to-a-minute. Anything longer is either a
server bug or a multi-hour outage, in which case backing off and
retrying is not the right tool — the user should wait and re-run.

## 402 / 403 surfacing (concrete contract)

On FATAL classification:
- Process exits with code 1 (not 0).
- The full HTTP response body is captured (truncated at 4 KiB so
  no log explosion) and printed to stderr verbatim.
- The slog handler emits a structured event:
    slog.Error("tts_fatal", "status", 402, "body_excerpt", excerpt,
              "essay_slug", slug, "chunk_index", i)
- A test in wa-4cw.11 (Test Plan: 'http_402' + 'http_403') asserts
  the classification, AND a separate test in wa-4cw.5 (build-pipeline
  orchestration) asserts the BUILD EXITS NON-ZERO when the fake TTS
  server returns 402.

## Operational realism (pass 9) — wall-clock implications

The existing 'Concrete numbers' section above has the right per-chunk
budget (~197 s worst case). Below is the bulk-run impact.

### Per-chunk timing tiers

| Outcome                  | Wall clock | Notes |
|--------------------------|------------|-------|
| Happy path (200, no retry)  | ~26 s mean | Most chunks. |
| 1 retry (one 429 or 5xx)    | ~26 + 3 s wait + 26 s = ~55 s | <5% of chunks normally. |
| 2 retries                | ~88 s     | Rare. |
| 3 retries → FATAL        | ~197 s     | Catastrophic — aborts run. |

### Bulk run impact of the retry policy

- Total chunks: ~252 (see wa-cfn.2 'Wall-clock estimate').
- Baseline serial wall-clock at zero retries: 252 × 26 s = 109 min.
- Realistic retry rate: 5% of chunks need 1 retry. 12.6 chunks × +30 s
  overhead = +6 min. New total: ~115 min.
- Pessimistic retry rate: 15% of chunks. 38 × +30 s = +19 min. Total:
  ~128 min.
- This is why wa-cfn.2's 90/110/150 min bands are framed that way:
  they bake in the 0% / 5% / 15% retry assumptions.

### When 3-retry FATAL is the right design

The alternative — unbounded retries — has two failure modes:
1. Stuck process holding the OS hostage; user kills it manually
   (loses log context, breaks resumability story).
2. Quiet drain of credits if the API is flaky-but-eventually-works.

3-retry FATAL surfaces fast: at most ~3 min per chunk before bailing,
and resumability (manifest snapshot per essay) means restart re-tries
the chunk fresh on a new run. The user's wall-clock loss is bounded
at one essay's worth of progress (~2-5 min), not multi-hour drains.

title: Implement internal/concat/ ffmpeg pairwise acrossfade wrapper (§5.4)
description:
Wraps ffmpeg as a subprocess (`os/exec`) to concatenate per-chunk MP3s
with a 50ms crossfade between adjacent chunks.

## Why pairwise (not one big filter_complex)

§5.4: ffmpeg's filter_complex syntax doesn't chain `acrossfade`
cleanly across N inputs. Implement as a pairwise reduce:

```
out = chunk[0]
for i := 1; i < N; i++:
    out = ffmpeg -i out -i chunk[i] -filter_complex "acrossfade=d=0.05" -y tmp_<i>.mp3
```

Use `~/.cache/wiki-audio/tmp/<slug>/` as the working dir; clean up
intermediate files after success. On failure, leave them in place so
the user can debug.

## Why 50ms crossfade

Long enough to mask the chunk boundary, short enough to be inaudible
as an actual fade. Tuned by listening — if Phase E spike reveals
audible artifacts, raise to 100ms.

## Subprocess hygiene

Capture stderr; on non-zero exit, return an error including the
ffmpeg stderr tail. Don't let ffmpeg take more than (chunks * 30s) —
that should be a comfortable upper bound and a hung ffmpeg is a real
failure mode.

## Test Plan

Tests in `internal/concat/concat_test.go` use small test MP3s
(~1s each, generated once via ffmpeg from a sine wave + checked into
`testdata/concat/`).

| Test name                            | Setup                                | Expectation |
|--------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|-------------|
| single_chunk_returns_input           | one MP3                              | output bytes ≈ input bytes (no concat needed) |
| two_chunks_concat                    | two MP3s                             | output duration ≈ sum - 0.05s (crossfade) |
| three_chunks_pairwise                | three MP3s                           | output duration ≈ sum - 0.10s |
| ten_chunks_pairwise                  | ten MP3s                             | runs to completion; intermediate files cleaned |
| ffmpeg_missing_returns_clear_error   | PATH without ffmpeg                  | error mentions "ffmpeg not found" |
| ffmpeg_nonzero_exit_includes_stderr  | malformed input file                 | error wraps stderr tail |
| timeout_kills_subprocess             | mock slow ffmpeg                     | process killed; error includes "timeout" |
| tmp_dir_cleaned_on_success           | three-chunk concat                   | tmp dir empty after |
| tmp_dir_retained_on_failure          | bad input on chunk 2                 | tmp dir contents preserved |
| crossfade_audible_continuity         | (manual) listen to output            | no audible click at boundaries |

## Skip if ffmpeg missing

`testutil.RequireBinary(t, "ffmpeg")` — these tests skip cleanly on
CI runners that don't ship ffmpeg. Document the skip prominently;
don't silently pass.

## Structured logging during tests

slog.With("test", t.Name(), "n_chunks", n, "tmpdir", tmp). On failure
log the ffmpeg command line that ran so reproduction is one cmd-line.

## Why no integration test bead

ffmpeg is local; there is no API to integrate against. The unit tests
ARE the integration tests for this module. Real-essay continuity is
covered by wa-4cw.8 (the spike) and wa-4cw.9 (voice quality gate).

comments.author: pane-3
comments.text:
## Closing wa-4cw.3 — `internal/concat/` shipped (commit `38a7197`)

### Public API

```go
concat.Concat(ctx, inputs []string, outPath, tmpDir string, opts concat.Options) error
```

Behavior matrix matches §5.4:
- `len(inputs)==0` → error, no disk changes.
- `len(inputs)==1` → bytewise copy from `inputs[0]` to `outPath` (no ffmpeg call — single-chunk essays don't pay re-encode cost).
- `len(inputs)>=2` → pairwise reduce: `out_i = ffmpeg(out_{i-1}, in_i)` with `acrossfade=d=0.05`.

Defaults exposed as constants: `DefaultCrossfadeSeconds=0.05`, `DefaultPerStepTimeout=30s`. Override via `Options{CrossfadeSeconds, PerStepTimeout, FFmpegPath, Logger}`.

### Subprocess hygiene (3 fixes worth recording)

1. **Pre-flight `exec.LookPath`.** A missing ffmpeg returns `"ffmpeg not found on PATH (looked for X)"` — distinct from a genuine non-zero exit. The naive `errors.As(err, &exec.Error{ErrNotFound})` only catches *relative* names that LookPath rejects; an absolute path to a non-existent file fails inside fork/exec with `fs.ErrNotExist`, untouched by `exec.ErrNotFound`. Pre-flight catches both.
2. **`cmd.WaitDelay = 2s`.** Without this, `cmd.Run()` would hang on stderr-pipe drainage when the per-step timeout killed a child whose grandchildren still held the pipe open. We hit this with the `sh -c 'sleep 30'` fake-ffmpeg test fixture: 30s wait after we'd already sent SIGKILL.
3. **Cancel symmetry.** The caller's `ctx.Cancel()` surfaces as `"ffmpeg cancelled"` (not generic "ffmpeg failed") — matching the per-step-timeout phrasing.

### Tests (10, all pass)

| Test | What it pins |
|---|---|
| `TestSingleChunk_ReturnsInputBytewise` | bytewise copy fast-path |
| `TestTwoChunks_DurationLessByCrossfade` | ffprobe duration ≈ 1+1-0.05 (±0.15s tol) |
| `TestThreeChunks_PairwiseDuration` | 3.0 - 2*0.05 |
| `TestTenChunks_RunsToCompletionAndCleansTmp` | step_*.mp3 absent on success |
| `TestFFmpegMissing_ReturnsClearError` | "ffmpeg not found" |
| `TestFFmpegNonzeroExit_WrapsStderrTail` | error mentions ffmpeg + stderr tail |
| `TestTimeoutKillsSubprocess` | 200ms cap honored, returns < 5s |
| `TestTmpDirRetainedOnFailure` | step_001.mp3 preserved when step 2 dies |
| `TestEmptyInputs_Errors` | no output produced |
| `TestContextCancellation_AbortsRun` | external cancel propagates < 5s |

All gated on `testutil.RequireBinary(t, "ffmpeg")` + `"ffprobe"` so a CI runner without ffmpeg gets a clear skip instead of silent green.

### Side-deliverable: `testutil.RequireBinary`

Spec called for it explicitly. Same shape as `RequireIntegration`/`RequireCredentials`:

```go
func RequireBinary(t *testing.T, name string)  // Skipf if exec.LookPath fails
```

Plus 2 self-tests (skips-when-missing, runs-when-present). 5 LoC of testutil API, ~30 LoC of tests.

### Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `go build ./...` | clean |
| `go vet ./...` | clean |
| `gofmt -d` | empty |
| `go test ./...` | all packages pass |
| concat suite end-to-end | ~9s on this host (ffmpeg 7.1.1 + libmp3lame) |

### Worktree workflow

`git worktree add ../wiki-audio-pane3-4cw3 -b pane3-wa-4cw.3 main`, ship in worktree, `--no-ff` merge, prune. Two pane-2 commits (`fcb5c09` `cli: init scaffolds ~/.wiki-audio/`, `ed40d9a` bead-close wa-kyn.12) on local main flowed up cleanly with my push.

Unblocks **wa-4cw.5** (build pipeline wiring — extract → hash → chunk → TTS → concat → tag).

title: Implement internal/id3/ tagger (title, artist, album, date)
description:
Use bogem/id3v2/v2 to write ID3 v2.3 frames to the final concatenated
MP3:

- TIT2 (title)        = essay title
- TPE1 (artist)       = "Paul Graham" (or per-essay author)
- TALB (album)        = "Paul Graham Essays" (configurable in feed.toml)
- TYER / TDRC (date)  = essay's publish_date_text if available, else
                        manifest GeneratedAt year
- TCON (genre)        = "Audiobook" (helps Pocket Casts categorize)

## Why ID3 v2.3 (not v2.4)

Older media players choke on v2.4. v2.3 is universally supported.
Pocket Casts is fine with either; choose v2.3 for max compatibility.

## Why these specific frames (and not embedded cover art)

Cover art is deferred to v2 (§10). Per-episode cover art would force a
regen if we change the cover; feed-level <itunes:image> is enough and
mutable without touching audio.

## Test Plan

Tests in `internal/id3/id3_test.go` use a tiny ~1KB silent MP3
(checked into `testdata/id3/silent.mp3`) and exercise the tagger then
re-read frames to verify.

| Test name                          | Setup                                  | Expectation |
|------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|-------------|
| writes_TIT2                        | title="How to Do Great Work"           | re-read TIT2 == title |
| writes_TPE1                        | artist="Paul Graham"                   | re-read TPE1 == artist |
| writes_TALB                        | album="Paul Graham Essays"             | re-read TALB == album |
| writes_TYER_when_date_present      | publish_date_text="July 2023"          | TYER == "2023" |
| writes_TYER_falls_back_to_genyear  | no publish_date_text                   | TYER == year-of(GeneratedAt) |
| writes_TCON_audiobook              | always                                 | TCON == "Audiobook" |
| version_is_2_3                     | always                                 | header byte indicates v2.3 |
| utf8_in_title_roundtrips           | title contains "—" em dash             | re-read preserves UTF-8 |
| existing_tag_replaced              | re-tag a tagged MP3                    | new values, not appended |
| audio_data_unchanged               | tag a 1KB silent MP3                   | audio bytes (post-tag) byte-equal pre-tag audio frames |
| size_increase_bounded              | tag with all frames                    | size increase < 4KB (sanity) |

## Cross-tool verification (informational)

A manual test (not blocking): run `ffprobe -v quiet -show_format
out.mp3` and verify ffprobe sees title/artist/album. Catches cases
where bogem writes valid ID3 that some readers reject.

## Structured logging during tests

slog.With("test", t.Name(), "frame", "TIT2", "value", value). On
failure log the binary diff of the first 4KB so we can see what
bogem actually wrote.

## Why no integration test bead

ID3 tagging is fully local; the unit tests cover everything. End-to-end
verification happens in Pocket Casts via wa-i1l.12 (subscribe + listen).

title: Wire build pipeline end-to-end (extract → hash check → chunk → TTS → concat → tag)
description:
The actual `wiki-audio build` (no flags) execution path:

1. Load Config + .env.
2. Fetch manifest from R2 once at start.
3. Walk the source dir; for each *.md:
   a. Extract → CleanedDocument.
   b. Compare body_hash to manifest entry. Hit → log skip, continue.
      Miss → proceed.
   c. Chunk.
   d. For each chunk: TTS with retry (E2). Stream MP3 to
      `~/.cache/wiki-audio/tmp/<slug>/<index>.mp3`.
   e. Concat with acrossfade (E3) → `<slug>.mp3` final.
   f. Apply ID3 tags (E4).
   g. Move into `~/.cache/wiki-audio/out/<slug>.mp3`.
   h. Update in-memory manifest entry with all metadata.
   i. Optimistically upload manifest snapshot to R2. (Resumability —
      if we crash now, we don't redo step a-g for this essay.)

## Flags this task should respect

- `--slug X`     : narrow to one essay
- `--force`      : ignore body_hash; rebuild
- `--dry-run`    : already implemented in D14
- `--extract-only`: already implemented in D15

## Concurrency

For v1, run essays serially. Within an essay, chunks could run in
parallel against ElevenLabs, but the API has rate limits and concat is
inherently sequential. Don't bother with concurrency for v1; total
time is already acceptable (~hours, not days).

## Test Plan

Orchestration tests in `internal/build/build_test.go` use:
- The R2 Fake from wa-i1l.17 for manifest + upload-snapshot
- A fake ElevenLabs HTTP server (httptest.NewServer) returning
  pre-recorded MP3 bytes (a small silent MP3 fixture)
- A real `ffmpeg` binary (skip if missing — this is an orchestration
  test, the unit-tests in wa-4cw.3 already cover ffmpeg specifics)
- The 3 example essays from `testdata/essays/`

| Test name                              | Expectation |
|----------------------------------------|-------------|
| empty_manifest_builds_all_essays       | 3 essays processed; manifest has 3 entries |
| existing_hash_match_skips              | manifest pre-populated; 0 TTS calls; log "skip" |
| force_flag_rebuilds                    | --force; even matching hashes are rebuilt |
| slug_flag_narrows_to_one               | --slug=X processes only that essay |
| chunks_streamed_to_tmp                 | per-chunk MP3s land in tmp/<slug>/ |
| concat_runs_after_all_chunks           | acrossfade invoked (counted via fake exec) |
| id3_tags_applied                       | final MP3 in out/ has TIT2/TPE1/etc |
| manifest_snapshot_uploaded_per_essay   | R2 Fake records 3 PutObject(pg.manifest.json) — one per essay |
| crash_recovery_resumable               | kill mid-essay 2; restart; essay 1 not redone |
| fatal_403_aborts_run                   | fake server returns 403; build exits with FATAL log |
| body_hash_includes_voice_id            | change voice_id; all hashes mismatch → all rebuild |
| logs_per_essay_summary                 | slog.Info("essay_built", "slug", "duration", "chunks", "chars") |

## Structured logging during tests

slog.With(
  "test", t.Name(),
  "phase", "build",
  "essay_slug", slug,
  "n_chunks", n_chunks,
)

Test failures dump the full slog output for the failing essay.
The polish prompt: "great, detailed logging so we can be sure that
everything is working perfectly after implementation".

## Why no integration test for the full pipeline

Full pipeline integration is deliberately covered by:
- wa-4cw.8 (the spike — one essay end-to-end on real services)
- wa-cfn.2 (bulk run — all 53 essays)

Both are manually triggered by the developer. A persistent integration
test of the full pipeline would burn ~$5 per CI run; not worth it.

## Orchestration test rows (added by polish pass 2 — §6 recovery assertions)

| Test name                              | Setup                                     | Expectation |
|----------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|-------------|
| build_exits_nonzero_on_402             | httptest TTS returns 402 first chunk      | exit code 1; stderr contains API body excerpt; manifest still has earlier-essay entries |
| build_exits_nonzero_on_403             | httptest TTS returns 403                  | exit code 1; stderr surfaces auth-error body |
| build_resumes_after_kill               | run partial, SIGTERM, re-run              | second run skips completed essays (body_hash hit) |
| manifest_snapshot_after_each_essay     | run 3 essays, kill after 2nd              | R2 fake has manifest with 2 entries (snapshot frequency = post-essay) |
| network_outage_mid_chunk               | httptest sleeps past timeout, then 200    | retry succeeds within RetryAttempts; build completes |
| ffmpeg_failure_skips_essay             | exec.LookPath returns nonexistent ffmpeg  | essay logged as failed; tmp/<slug>/ retained; manifest unchanged for that slug |

## Chunk audio length anomaly (added by polish pass 2 — §6 row)

§6 says: \"Chunk audio length anomaly — duration < 1s for non-empty
chunk; log warning, but accept.\" Concrete handling in step (d) of the
build pipeline:

After receiving the MP3 stream from TTS, run a quick duration probe
via ffprobe (or the id3v2 length field if available). If duration < 1s
AND the source chunk's text was non-empty (>=20 chars):

    slog.Warn(\"chunk_audio_anomaly\",
              \"slug\", slug,
              \"chunk_index\", i,
              \"duration_ms\", durMS,
              \"chunk_chars\", len(chunkText))

Append to ~/.cache/wiki-audio/anomalies.txt. Do NOT abort — some
chunks legitimately render very short (e.g., a chunk that is mostly
metadata after stripping). The user can review anomalies.txt
post-run.

| Test name                              | Setup                                  | Expectation |
|----------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|-------------|
| chunk_short_duration_logs_warning      | TTS returns ~500ms MP3 for 2000-char chunk | warning logged; build succeeds; anomalies.txt has entry |
| chunk_short_duration_empty_chunk_silent| TTS returns ~500ms MP3 for empty chunk | no warning (empty chunks are expected to be short) |

## Operational realism (pass 9) — total bulk-run wall-clock

The existing 'Concurrency' section says 'total time is already
acceptable (~hours, not days)'. Concrete number for that 'hours':

### Bulk-run wall-clock decomposition

For 53 essays, ~252 chunks, serial:

| Component                              | Time   |
|----------------------------------------|--------|
| TTS calls (252 chunks × 26 s mean)     | 109 min |
| Retry overhead at 5% retry rate        | +6 min |
| Concat (53 essays × ~1.5 s ffmpeg)     | ~1.3 min |
| ID3 tagging (53 × ~0.2 s)              | ~0.2 min |
| Manifest snapshot upload after each essay (53 × ~0.5 s) | ~0.5 min |
| **Total expected**                     | **~117 min ≈ 2 h** |

### Bands

- Low (no retries, fast network): 92 min (~1h32m).
- Expected: 110-120 min (~2 h).
- High (15% retry rate, congestion): 150 min (~2.5 h).

### Why no concurrency in v1

- ElevenLabs Flash v2.5 has rate limits (Pro tier: ~5 concurrent
  requests typical; varies by plan). Hitting them triggers 429s and
  retries, which costs more wall-clock than serial would have saved.
- Concat is inherently sequential within an essay (pairwise reduce).
- Cross-essay parallelism would speed things up but adds complexity
  for resumability, snapshot ordering, and credit-burn rate
  monitoring — all to save < 1 hour on a one-time operation.
- v2 could revisit IF essay count grows beyond ~150 (would push
  serial wall-clock past 4 hours).

### Resumability impact on wall-clock

If the run crashes 60 min in (~25 essays done), restart skips those
25 (body_hash hits) and processes the remaining 28. Restart cost:
~1 min for manifest fetch + body_hash comparisons. Then ~55 min of
TTS. Total wall clock: original 60 min + 1 min + 55 min = 116 min.
Compare to original 117 min if no crash → restart penalty is < 1%.

comments.text:
## §3 sample output (polish pass 6) — pin the build per-essay format

Verbatim target from §3 for `wiki-audio build` (default mode):

```
$ wiki-audio build
[1/53] how-to-do-great-work … extracted (52,481 chars), synthesizing (14 chunks)…
       generated how-to-do-great-work.mp3 (62.4 MB, 1h22m)
[2/53] beating-the-averages … extracted (8,210 chars, dropped 4 code blocks)…
       generated beating-the-averages.mp3 (9.1 MB, 12m04s)
…
build complete: 53 essays, 18h47m audio, 612 MB, 880,344 chars billed
```

## Per-essay line contract

Two-line block per essay, indexed `[i/N]`:

```
[i/N] <slug> … extracted (<chars> chars[, dropped <K> <segment-kind>]…)…
       generated <slug>.mp3 (<size>, <duration>)
```

- `<chars>` is post-cleaning char count, comma-grouped.
- `[, dropped K segment-kind]` block omitted if K=0 for all segment kinds.
  Multiple kinds joined with `, ` (e.g. `dropped 4 code blocks, 2 footnotes`).
- `<size>` is human MB (1 decimal place).
- `<duration>` is `<H>h<M>m` over 1h or `<M>m<S>s` under 1h.
- Indent on line 2 is 7 spaces (aligns with `[ ` opening).

## Skip / cache-hit lines

When body_hash matches the manifest entry (no rebuild needed):

```
[3/53] hackers-and-painters … cached (hash match, last built 2026-04-22)
```

One-line form. Skipped essays still consume an index slot in `[i/N]`.

## Final summary contract

```
build complete: <N> essays, <total-duration>, <total-MB>, <total-chars> chars billed
```

- `<total-duration>` always `<H>h<M>m`.
- `<total-chars>` is the sum across essays that *actually went through TTS*
  (i.e., not the cache-hit ones — those don't bill). Use the word "billed"
  to make this distinction visible.

## Flag interactions (all owned by THIS bead)

- `--slug X`: process only that slug; index becomes `[1/1]`.
- `--force`: override hash check; cache-hit lines never appear.
- `--dry-run`: handled in wa-kyn.14 (separate codepath; no overlap).
- `--extract-only`: handled in wa-kyn.15 (separate codepath; no overlap).

title: ~/.cache/wiki-audio/ layout + cleanup policy
description:
Define and document the cache layout:

\`\`\`
~/.cache/wiki-audio/
├── tmp/<slug>/<index>.mp3       (per-chunk intermediates; deleted on success)
├── out/<slug>.mp3               (final concatenated MP3 awaiting publish)

\`\`\`

§6: \"ffmpeg concatenation failure → preserve raw chunk MP3s under
~/.cache/wiki-audio/tmp/<slug>/ for debugging.\" Saves a re-run when
investigating.

## Why ~/.cache/ specifically

XDG basedir spec: ~/.cache/ is the right place for non-essential
regeneratable data. Distinct from ~/.wiki-audio/ (which holds
config + secrets).

title: Run `wiki-audio build --slug how-to-do-great-work` end-to-end (the spike)
description:
THE Phase E spike. One full essay through extract → chunk → TTS →
concat → tag → MP3 on disk.

\"How to Do Great Work\" chosen because:
- Long (~52k chars after cleaning) — exercises the retry path on a
  realistic chunk count (~14 chunks).
- Has many footnotes — exercises the paragraph-end footnote weave (D8).
- The user is most likely to relisten to it, so voice-quality
  acceptability matters most here.

## Manual upload for the spike

Phase F's publish command isn't built yet. For the spike, manually
upload \`~/.cache/wiki-audio/out/how-to-do-great-work.mp3\` to R2 with
\`aws s3 cp\` or \`rclone\`. Construct a one-off enclosure URL:
\`https://wiki-audio.jabyrne.workers.dev/pg/how-to-do-great-work.mp3?t=<token>\`

Listen on the phone via that URL (no podcast feed yet — just open the
URL in the phone browser, hand it to a media player).

## Acceptance criteria — spike success

Done = a file at `~/.cache/wiki-audio/out/how-to-do-great-work.mp3` that:

- Exists and is non-empty (`stat` reports size > 5 MB).
- Plays from byte 0 to EOF in any media player without error (`ffprobe -v error` clean).
- Duration is between 50 and 75 minutes (How to Do Great Work end-to-end TTS at flash_v2_5 lands in this range; outside means truncation or runaway repetition).
- ID3 tags pass wa-4cw.10's four-field check.
- ElevenLabs credit consumption logged: between 22k and 30k credits used (~52k chars × 0.5 credits/char). Anything wildly outside means the build pipeline retried something it shouldn't have.

Spike-success ALSO requires the human gates: wa-4cw.9 (voice quality) and wa-4cw.10 (ID3 display) both pass.

## Spike-failure-but-acceptable cases

The spike's purpose is to surface unknowns. If any of the following happen, the spike still produced its diagnostic value — record findings and move on with the appropriate fix bead:

- Retry classifier triggered on a real 429 from ElevenLabs → success, that's the path being validated. Log it.
- One chunk produced a noticeably-different-voice artifact → known ElevenLabs flakiness. Re-synthesize that chunk only (manually delete from cache, re-run build). Spike still passes.
- ID3 tags slightly wrong → fix in id3 layer (wa-4cw.4) and re-tag without re-synthesis. Spike still passes.

## Spike-actually-failed (do NOT proceed to Phase F)

- Concat output is silent / corrupted / non-playing.
- TTS chunk loss (concat output is shorter than sum-of-chunks duration).
- Voice quality unacceptable across the hour AND no voice_id swap fixes it (per wa-4cw.9 fail path).
- Build pipeline panics or non-recoverable error mid-stream.

In a hard-fail, root-cause and re-spike before Phase F.
