comments.text:
## Spike failed at concat step 13/17 — concat per-step timeout (30s) too small for late pairwise steps

**Per the runbook: "DO NOT retry blindly. Each retry burns credits." Surfacing diagnosis only; not retrying.**

### What happened

Wall: 5m45.94s total (`time` output). Synth phase completed cleanly in ~98s; concat phase ran for ~4m7s before failing on step 13.

```
06:15:59  starting full build
06:15:59  chunked  n_chunks=18 chunk_max_chars=4000
06:17:37  concat step 1/17  (5.5s)   left=000.mp3   right=001.mp3
06:17:42  concat step 2/17  (8.0s)
06:17:50  concat step 3/17  (10.0s)
…
06:20:16  concat step 11/17 (29.0s)  left=step_010.mp3 right=011.mp3
06:20:45  concat step 12/17 (29.0s)  left=step_011.mp3 right=012.mp3   ← step_012.mp3 = 21 MB
06:21:15  concat step 13/17 (30.0s)  ← KILLED at PerStepTimeout
06:21:45  build essay failed: ffmpeg timeout after 30s … signal: killed
06:21:45  build complete   manifest_entries=0
```

ffmpeg's own progress log at the moment of the kill: `time=00:42:56 size=19968KiB speed=87.3x` — it was 87× realtime through a 42-minute output. The job was making real progress; it just didn't finish in 30s.

### Root cause

**My bug in wa-4cw.3** (`internal/concat/concat.go`):

```go
const DefaultPerStepTimeout = 30 * time.Second  // line 29
```

The comment I shipped said "even a slow Pi-class host concatenates two ~3MB MP3s well inside 30s; if any step actually takes longer, ffmpeg is hung." That sizing was for the FIRST pairwise step — left + right both ~3MB. Pairwise reduce makes step N process the cumulative left-side, which grows linearly. By step 12, left was 21 MB; by step 17 it would have been ~50 MB. ffmpeg processes them at ~87× realtime → step 13 needed ~33s, step 17 would have needed ~50s.

The bug is in my own concat.go. wa-4cw.3 acceptance was 10 chunks; this spike is 18. The defect didn't surface in my unit tests because I sized fixtures at 0.2s each, so even step 9 of the 10-chunk test was 1.8s of audio — the timeout never came close to firing.

### What's preserved on disk

- **18/18 synth chunks** at `~/.cache/wiki-audio/tmp/how-to-do-great-work/{000-017}.mp3` (~58 MB total)
- **13/17 concat intermediates** at `~/.cache/wiki-audio/tmp/how-to-do-great-work/concat/step_{001-013}.mp3` per concat.go's retain-on-failure contract
- **manifest unchanged** — `manifest.json` reports 0 entries; no accidental publish state

The 33.5k credits (~$5-7) of TTS spend is **NOT lost** — chunks 0-17 are on disk and byte-stable. A retry strategy that reuses them costs zero credits. A naive `wiki-audio build --slug …` retry would re-synth all 18 because `internal/cli/build_pipeline.go:211` (`synthesizeChunkWithRetry`) does not check for an existing `<NNN>.mp3` before calling the API. That's worth a separate bead.

### Three recovery paths — operator pick

**A. One-shot recovery (cheapest; ~5 min wall, $0 credits)**
Write a small standalone Go program that calls `internal/concat.Concat` with `PerStepTimeout: 5 * time.Minute` against the existing 18 chunks, then ID3-tags the output, then drops it at `~/.cache/wiki-audio/out/how-to-do-great-work.mp3`. Operator listens for wa-4cw.9. Concat.go gets fixed separately.

**B. Fix concat then resume (medium; ~5-10 min wall, $0 credits IF a chunk-cache-skip is added)**
Patch `internal/concat/concat.go`:
- Raise `DefaultPerStepTimeout` from 30s → 5m (safe upper bound for any plausible pairwise step on 50+ MB cumulative)
- Add a unit test that synthesizes 18× 0.2s sine fixtures and concats — pins the regression at the 18-chunk mark.

Then patch `internal/cli/build_pipeline.go` to skip TTS if `<NNN>.mp3` already exists and is non-zero size. This is a small change but it's pane-2's file (their wa-4cw.5 build pipeline). I'd need to coordinate.

Then re-run `wiki-audio build --slug how-to-do-great-work` — synth no-ops because chunks exist; concat retries with the new timeout.

**C. Fix concat, accept the re-synth cost (medium; ~10 min wall, ~$5-7 credits)**
Skip the chunk-cache patch. Just fix the concat timeout, re-run the full build. Wastes credits but doesn't touch pane-2's file. **Not recommended** when (A) and (B) avoid the spend.

### Recommendation: A then B as a follow-up bead

(A) is the fastest path to a listenable MP3 for wa-4cw.9, and the diagnostic deliverable for wa-4cw.8 is already captured (the failure mode is now well-understood; a future bead can land the spec change).

The structural fix (B's concat-timeout raise + chunk-cache-skip) belongs in dedicated beads. I propose:

- New bead **wa-4cw.13** (P1): "concat: raise DefaultPerStepTimeout to 5m + 18-chunk regression test" — this is mine to fix; ~10 LoC + 1 test.
- New bead **wa-4cw.14** (P1): "build_pipeline: skip TTS for chunks that already exist on disk" — pane-2's territory; ~10 LoC + a unit test that asserts no client.Synth calls when all chunk files exist.

Both close fast and de-risk the entire Phase E re-spike + Phase G bulk run.

### Status

- wa-4cw.8: still in_progress. NOT closing — the bead's success contract is "MP3 on disk + duration in band + ID3 tags", none of which are met yet.
- Monitor and until-loop both stopped (process exited cleanly).
- No further commands run. Holding for operator decision on (A) vs (B).

## wa-4cw.8 closed via Path A — MP3 produced from preserved chunks; $0 additional credits

The operator-authorized Path A recovery worked end-to-end:

```
$ /tmp/wa-recover-concat \
    --chunks ~/.cache/wiki-audio/tmp/how-to-do-great-work \
    --out    ~/.cache/wiki-audio/out/how-to-do-great-work.mp3 \
    --title  "How to Do Great Work" \
    --artist "Paul Graham" \
    --album  "PG Essays" \
    --year   "2023" \
    --genre  "Audiobook" \
    --step-timeout 5m

… 17 concat steps completed in 6m45.79s …
recover: id3 tagged title="How to Do Great Work" artist="Paul Graham" album="PG Essays" year=2023 genre=Audiobook
OK /home/ubuntu/.cache/wiki-audio/out/how-to-do-great-work.mp3 (29302684 bytes, 27.9 MB)
```

### Acceptance criteria — all green

| Criterion | Required | Got |
|---|---|---|
| Exists, non-empty, > 5 MB | yes | ✅ 27.9 MB (29,302,684 B) |
| `ffprobe -v error` clean | yes | ✅ stream parses, mp3 codec, 44.1 kHz mono, 64 kbit/s |
| Duration in 50-75 min | yes | ✅ **61.05 min** (3,662.785 s) |
| ID3 frames TIT2 / TPE1 / TALB / TYER / TCON | all 5 | ✅ all 5 present (title=How to Do Great Work, artist=Paul Graham, album=PG Essays, year=2023, genre=Audiobook) |
| First-second + last-second decode | both clean | ✅ both `ffmpeg … -f null` exit 0 (no truncation, no header damage) |
| Credit consumption | 22-30k / 33,558 estimated | ✅ **0 additional credits** — preserved chunks reused |

### What enabled Path A

1. **Synth phase had completed before failure** — all 18 chunks at `~/.cache/wiki-audio/tmp/how-to-do-great-work/{000-017}.mp3` survived the spike crash and were byte-stable.
2. **concat.go's retain-on-failure contract** kept the 13 partially-completed concat intermediates on disk. The recovery tool reuses neither — it concats from the original chunks fresh — but the intermediates were available as evidence for the diagnosis.
3. **`internal/concat.Options.PerStepTimeout` is exported.** I bypassed the broken 30s default and passed 5 minutes. Production fix lands as wa-4cw.13.

### Empirical step-duration evidence (for wa-4cw.13 timeout sizing)

```
step  1: 5.8s    step  7: 18.8s   step 13: 32.9s
step  2: 7.9s    step  8: 21.3s   step 14: 36.1s
step  3: 10.4s   step  9: 23.5s   step 15: 37.4s
step  4: 12.6s   step 10: 26.2s   step 16: 40.2s
step  5: 14.3s   step 11: 29.0s   step 17: 41.2s (final)
step  6: 16.7s   step 12: 31.5s
```

Linear growth ~2.4s per step. Original 30s default would have killed at step 12 (31.5s). 5m default (300s) provides 7× headroom for the worst observed case (41.2s). Even a 100-chunk essay (hypothetical) would project ~240s for the final step — still inside 300s. Recommended pin for wa-4cw.13: **5m**, with a comment about why pairwise late-step duration scales linearly with N.

### Spec-fidelity note

Path A was implemented via a Go wrapper (`cmd/wa-recover-concat/main.go`) that calls the same `internal/concat.Concat` production code with only the timeout overridden — NOT via ffmpeg's `concat` demuxer (which would have been ~5s wall but would have skipped the spec-required 50ms acrossfade between chunks). The output is therefore byte-comparable to what production will produce once wa-4cw.13 lands.

### Followup beads

- **wa-4cw.13** (P1, mine): raise `DefaultPerStepTimeout` to 5m + add an 18-chunk regression test that would have caught this. Claiming next.
- **wa-4cw.14** (P1, pane-2's territory): chunk-cache-skip in `internal/cli/build_pipeline.go` so a future spike retry is also $0 credits.

### Operator-side action remaining

**wa-4cw.9** — listen to `~/.cache/wiki-audio/out/how-to-do-great-work.mp3` for an hour. Voice-quality acceptance is not a swarm-side check.

### Cleanup intent

`cmd/wa-recover-concat/` is a one-shot recovery tool, untracked in git. Leaving it in place for the moment in case wa-4cw.14 / wa-4cw.13 land bugs that need a second recovery — will unlink after both follow-ups close, or commit it as a permanent recovery binary if the operator prefers (operator decision).

title: Voice quality acceptance gate (across an hour of listening)
description:
Listen to the entire \"How to Do Great Work\" MP3 from E8. Acceptance
criteria:

- Voice (\"Christopher\") sounds right — not jarring across an hour
- No audible chunk boundaries (acrossfade working)
- Footnote-at-end-of-paragraph cadence works as listening, not just on
  paper
- Prosody on technical prose is acceptable (PG isn't reading code, but
  he uses jargon liberally)

If any of these fail, decide before Phase F:
- Voice issue → swap voice_id, regen all chunks (body_hash invalidates)
- Acrossfade too short → bump to 100ms in concat (E3)
- Footnotes feel intrusive → revisit policy (rare; would invalidate
  every essay via footnote_policy_version bump)

## Why this is its own bead (not just a paragraph in E8)

It's a HUMAN gate. The build can succeed and produce a valid MP3 that
nonetheless sounds wrong. We need a discrete moment to decide \"ship\"
vs. \"adjust\" before sinking more work into Phase F.

## Acceptance criteria

Listen end-to-end (no skipping > 30s blocks) to the spike MP3 (`how-to-do-great-work.mp3`, ~1 hour) on the actual phone hardware that will be used in production (Pocket Casts on phone, NOT desktop or Web Player — the phone speaker / earbud output is the real signal).

Pass means a YES to ALL of:

- [ ] Voice consistent across the hour (no mid-essay timbre shift suggesting voice_id collision).
- [ ] Zero audible chunk seams (a seam is a perceptible pause / volume change / breath cut at chunk boundaries; acrossfade smoothing should hide them).
- [ ] Footnote-at-end-of-paragraph cadence is parseable as a listener — "Footnote N: ..." sounds like an aside, not a glitch.
- [ ] Technical jargon (PG-isms: "Lisp", "Bayesian", proper nouns) pronounced acceptably. Mispronunciations of common-English words = blocker; mispronunciations of obscure proper nouns = note-and-accept.
- [ ] No truncation at start or end of the file (first sentence audible; last sentence ends cleanly).

Done = all five boxes ticked AND no follow-up bead opened from listening notes.

## Fail path (any box unticked)

- **Voice issue (timbre / wrong character)** → swap `voice_id` in `config.toml`. The body_hash includes voice_id (per wa-kyn.1 invariant), so changing it auto-invalidates every chunk on next `build` — re-run will regenerate everything. Cost: ~440k credits if Phase G already ran. PRE-Phase-G: ~14 credits for one essay re-run, cheap.
- **Audible chunk seams** → bump acrossfade duration in concat from 50ms to 100ms (E3, internal/concat). Re-run `build` (cached chunks reuse, only concat re-runs — cheap).
- **Footnote cadence intrusive** → revisit footnote_policy_version (E5/D8). This is the heaviest fix because changing the policy invalidates every essay's body_hash. Worth it if the listening experience is actually broken; not worth it for minor preference.
- **Truncation** → bug in concat or TTS chunk reconstruction. Open a P0 bead, do not proceed to Phase F.

After any fix, re-listen to a representative ~10-min sample (not full hour) before re-checking the boxes.
close_reason: Operator approved 192 kbps full-essay listening test (61 min, 84 MB, lossless concat). Sibilant clarity acceptable after wa-aoa wire fix + wa-7t6 default bump.

title: concat: raise DefaultPerStepTimeout to 5m + 18-chunk regression test
description:
Surfaced by wa-4cw.8 spike failure. Root cause: `internal/concat/concat.go::DefaultPerStepTimeout = 30 * time.Second` sized for first pairwise step (~3MB + ~3MB) but pairwise-reduce step N processes cumulative left-side which grows linearly. By step 12 of an 18-chunk essay, left=21MB; by step 17, ~50MB. ffmpeg at ~87× realtime needs ~33s for step 13, ~50s for step 17.

## Fix

Patch `internal/concat/concat.go`:

```go
const DefaultPerStepTimeout = 5 * time.Minute  // was 30s; sized for cumulative pairwise reduce on 50+ MB
```

5 min is a safe upper bound for any plausible pairwise step on the largest essay (~70k chars / ~30 chunks worst-case).

## Regression test

Add `internal/concat/concat_18chunk_test.go`:

- Generate 18× 0.2s sine-wave MP3 fixtures.
- Run Concat() with default timeout.
- Assert: completes successfully, output length ~3.6s.

This pins the bug — wa-4cw.3 acceptance was 10 chunks (1.8s of total audio at the failing step), so the timeout never fired in unit tests.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `internal/concat/concat.go::DefaultPerStepTimeout` is 5 * time.Minute.
2. New test `Test18ChunkConcatNoTimeout` lives in concat_18chunk_test.go and passes.
3. `go test -count=20 ./internal/concat/...` is 20/20 green (no flake).

After this lands, wa-4cw.8 spike can re-run. The 18 chunks already on disk at `~/.cache/wiki-audio/tmp/how-to-do-great-work/{000-017}.mp3` are byte-stable and reusable IF wa-4cw.14 (chunk-cache-skip in build_pipeline) lands first; otherwise the build re-synthesizes (re-burning ~33.5k credits / ~$5-7).

## wa-50g closed — concat timeout fix shipped (commit `1aec1d0`)

### Patch

`internal/concat/concat.go`:

```diff
-	DefaultPerStepTimeout = 30 * time.Second
+	DefaultPerStepTimeout = 5 * time.Minute
```

Plus a 14-line comment block on the constant carrying the wa-4cw.8 empirical data and the sizing rationale (linear growth with N, 6× headroom over the worst observed step, 100-chunk projection still inside 5m).

### Two regression tests landed

`internal/concat/concat_18chunk_test.go` (92 lines, 2 tests):

1. **`TestDefaultPerStepTimeout_AccommodatesObservedRealLoad`** — constant-bound check. Floor 4m (reflects worst observed load × ~6 safety margin); ceiling 30m (protects against a future "more headroom" change masking a genuine ffmpeg hang, which is the symptom the original 30s value was trying to catch). The test is documentation: a future PR that lowers the constant has to surface this conversation.

2. **`TestEighteenChunks_RunsToCompletion`** — loop count where production broke. Fixtures are 0.5s sine each (NOT 0.2s — late concat steps at 0.2s occasionally produce MP3 frames that ffmpeg's own demuxer rejects with `Failed to find two consecutive MPEG audio frames`, which is a separate bug worth tracking but orthogonal to wa-50g's timeout fix). Pins the loop semantics + `step_NNN.mp3` naming + cleanup-on-success at the count where the spike died.

### Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `go test ./internal/concat/` | 12/12 pass in ~14s |
| `go test -count=20 ./internal/concat/` | **20/20 green** in 291s |
| `go vet ./internal/concat/` | clean |
| `gofmt -d` | empty |

### Pairs with

- **wa-cfx** (pane-2, commit `8cafec1`): build_pipeline cache-skip — `internal/cli/build_pipeline.go:211` now no-ops the synth call when `<NNN>.mp3` already exists. Together: a future wa-4cw.8-style spike retry costs **0 credits** AND survives the late-step concat duration.
- **wa-4cw.8 closing comment** (commit `fd66fa6`): per-step duration table that justified the 5m sizing.
- **`cmd/wa-recover-concat/main.go`** (untracked): one-shot recovery tool that produced the v0.1.0 spike artifact via `internal/concat.Concat` with a 5m override BEFORE this commit. Operator-decision pending (delete vs commit-as-permanent-utility) now that wa-50g + wa-cfx have landed; my recommendation is delete since both layers are now structurally fixed.

### Out-of-scope (deliberately not addressed in this bead)

- Late-step MP3 malformedness at 0.2s fixtures (separate failure mode, found while writing tests, deserves its own bead if anyone hits it on small-fixture tests).
- Switching to a non-pairwise concat algorithm (PLAN §5.4 mandates pairwise).
- A real-audio 18×4-min regression test (slow, would burn ElevenLabs credits to regenerate fixtures, doesn't add coverage beyond the constant-pin + loop-count tests we shipped).

title: [REVIEW] Phase D model+extractor spec analysis
description:
# Phase D model+extractor spec analysis

Cross-read of PLAN_FOR_AUDIO_LIBRARY.md §2 (data model) + §5 (extractor)
against the 19 wa-kyn.* beads. Findings below are gaps/contradictions/
ambiguities that will surface as bugs or test churn during Phase D
implementation if not resolved BEFORE wa-kyn.6 closes and code starts
landing on main.

Severity: [HIGH] = blocks a wa-kyn bead from passing as-written.
[MEDIUM] = will cause rework or silent miscompilation. [LOW] = minor
ambiguity, would be caught in review.

---

## [HIGH] F1: `CleanedDocument` is missing a `Malformed` field

- §2 defines `CleanedDocument{Meta, Body, BodyHash, CharCount, WordCount, SkippedSegments}`. No `Malformed bool`.
- wa-kyn.9 acceptance: "If `len(body) < 200` … mark the document as malformed and skip during build" plus test row `body_under_200_marks_malformed → document marked Malformed=true`.
- wa-kyn.1 will compile a struct that has no field for the bit wa-kyn.9 wants to set.
- **Fix:** add `Malformed bool` (and probably `MalformedReason string`) to §2 + wa-kyn.1, OR rewrite wa-kyn.9 to return `(CleanedDocument, error)` with a sentinel `ErrMalformed` and have build-loop catch it.

## [HIGH] F2: CharCount semantics — runes vs bytes — silently inconsistent

- wa-kyn.9 pins `CharCount = utf8.RuneCount` for `CleanedDocument` (matches ElevenLabs billing).
- wa-kyn.10 chunker uses byte length (`cur.Len()`, `len(p)`) and the example sets `AudioChunk.CharCount: len(c)` (bytes).
- wa-kyn.22 asserts `total_chunk_chars_match_body` — sum(chunks) == CharCount. This will FAIL on any essay containing em-dashes, smart quotes, or any non-ASCII (every PG essay has em-dashes).
- §2 says only `CharCount int` for both types — no spec.
- **Fix:** either (a) AudioChunk.CharCount is also runes and chunker computes both, or (b) drop the wa-kyn.22 equality assertion and rename `CharCount` on AudioChunk to `ByteLen`. Decide before wa-kyn.10 lands.

## [HIGH] F3: `footnote_policy_version` constant has no home

- §2's hash formula references it. wa-kyn.1 calls it "v1". wa-kyn.8 calls it the cache-bust knob.
- No bead specifies WHERE the constant lives (`internal/model`? `internal/extract`?), what its initial value is (`"v1"` vs `1` vs `"2026-05-08"`), or how downstream tests pin it.
- If two PRs disagree on the value (or one PR exports it as a hashable int and another as a string), every cached MP3 silently invalidates on merge.
- **Fix:** declare in wa-kyn.1 — `package model: const FootnotePolicyVersion = "v1"`. Hash unit tests in wa-kyn.9 reference `model.FootnotePolicyVersion`.

## [HIGH] F4: Slug derivation algorithm is undefined

- §2: `Slug string // filename stem, kebab-cased`.
- Real fixtures: `How to Do Great Work.md` → `how-to-do-great-work`; `High Agency — In 30 Minutes.md` → ??? `high-agency-in-30-minutes` or `high-agency-—-in-30-minutes`?
- No bead implements slug derivation. wa-kyn.4 reads the file but doesn't compute slug.
- The em-dash, ampersands, and apostrophes (e.g. `Don't Worry About X.md`) all need explicit rules.
- The slug is the R2 key, the manifest map key, AND the RSS guid suffix (`pg-<slug>`) — getting it wrong invalidates the entire manifest on rename.
- **Fix:** add a wa-kyn sub-bead specifying: lowercase, strip diacritics, replace any run of non-`[a-z0-9]` with single `-`, trim leading/trailing `-`. Pin with golden fixtures.

## [HIGH] F5: `EssayMeta.SourceURL` and `PublishDateText` have no extractor

- §2 declares both fields. Beads never populate them.
- Their natural source is the Readwise `## Metadata` block — but wa-kyn.4 step 3 says "Drop everything from `## Metadata` to the line before `## Full Document`."
- Step ordering is wrong: must PARSE Metadata to populate EssayMeta, THEN drop. No bead does this.
- §5.1 step 3 also says drop, never parse. PLAN itself is the source of the gap.
- **Fix:** insert a step 2.5 in §5.1 "parse Metadata key/value pairs into EssayMeta.SourceURL/PublishDateText" and a wa-kyn bead to implement it. Otherwise rip those fields out of EssayMeta (they're consumed by §5.5 RSS `<description>` — `Originally published July 2023.` requires PublishDateText).

## [HIGH] F6: wa-kyn.11 is missing — chunker fallback has no implementing bead

- PLAN §5.2 step 5 specifies a sentence-style fallback for paragraphs > maxChars.
- wa-kyn.10 explicitly defers: "D11 implements the sentence-style fallback. For now, this task can ignore — D11 is its own bead."
- The `br list` returns wa-kyn.10 then wa-kyn.12 — there is NO wa-kyn.11.
- An overlong paragraph in any essay will currently emit a chunk that exceeds ElevenLabs' 5000-char limit and 400 the request.
- **Fix:** create the missing bead (chunker overlong-paragraph fallback per §5.2 step 5) before wa-kyn.20 (v0.1.0 cut). Until it exists, wa-kyn.22's `chunks_each_under_max_chars` assertion is unsafe on real PG corpus.

## [HIGH] F7: `SkippedSegments` element type is undefined

- §2: `SkippedSegments []string` — what string?
- wa-kyn.7: "Strip fenced code blocks. Record count in skipped_segments." Implies count, not strings.
- wa-kyn.9 test: `code block + image → SkippedSegments == 2`. Implies length-of-slice == count.
- wa-kyn.7 step a (image refs) says "Remove ![alt](url) image refs entirely" — but doesn't say to record them. wa-kyn.9 test row asserts both are recorded.
- Three valid interpretations: (a) reasons (`["code:lisp","image:foo.png"]`), (b) raw snippets (the dropped text), (c) human-readable labels (`"code block","image ref"`). Tests will pass on (c) only.
- **Fix:** pin the format. wa-kyn.7 currently records only code blocks; bead text must also record images (or wa-kyn.9 test will fail). Choose (c) for diff-friendly goldens in wa-kyn.22.

## [MEDIUM] F8: wa-kyn.4 introduces a title fallback not in PLAN

- PLAN §5.1 step 2: `title = first line matching ^# (.+)$`. No fallback specified.
- wa-kyn.4 adds: "If absent, fall back to the filename's title-cased stem."
- Behavior divergence: a malformed essay (no `# Title`) would produce empty Title per PLAN, but a synthesized title per bead. The synthesized title goes into RSS `<title>` and ID3 tags — i.e. into the user's podcast app forever.
- **Fix:** add the fallback to PLAN §5.1 step 2 (preferred — bead is right that empty title is worse), OR drop it from wa-kyn.4.

## [MEDIUM] F9: `EssayMeta.Author` parsing contradicts the dropped Metadata block

- §2: `Author string // default "Paul Graham"`.
- wa-kyn.22 fixtures include "High Agency — In 30 Minutes.md" (non-PG); wa-kyn.19 says "tests author-agnostic logic".
- But Author can ONLY come from the Readwise `## Metadata` block, which wa-kyn.4 drops without parsing (see F5).
- Either the default "Paul Graham" is hardcoded for every essay (incorrect for High Agency), or the Metadata block must be parsed first (see F5).
- **Fix:** couples to F5. Otherwise wa-kyn.19's spot-check on the High Agency essay will record Author="Paul Graham" incorrectly into the (eventual) ID3 artist tag.

## [MEDIUM] F10: Notes-section split has no positional safety check

- PLAN §5.1 step 5: "split at the **Notes** or ## Notes heading (case-insensitive; whichever appears first, **near end of essay**)".
- wa-kyn.5: "Split raw_body at the FIRST occurrence". No "near end" enforcement.
- A non-PG essay with a `## Notes` mid-essay subsection (e.g., a study-notes essay) would have the entire latter half mis-classified as footnotes.
- "near end" is an informal ⅔-of-document rule. Not implementable as written.
- **Fix:** either drop "near end" from PLAN (matches wa-kyn.5), OR pin a heuristic ("only match in last 30% of file") and add a unit test.

## [MEDIUM] F11: `OutputFormat` is excluded from body_hash, silently

- §2 hash = `sha256(body + voice_id + model_id + footnote_policy_version)`.
- §5.3 sends `cfg.OutputFormat = "mp3_44100_64"` to ElevenLabs. Switching to e.g. `mp3_44100_128` (higher bitrate) wouldn't change the hash and existing MP3s would never regenerate.
- The PLAN justifies the hash composition as "if voice or footnote behaviour changes, every essay must regenerate" — same logic applies to bitrate.
- **Fix:** either include OutputFormat in the hash (and update wa-kyn.1, wa-kyn.9), OR document explicitly in §2 that bitrate changes require manual `--force` rebuild.

## [MEDIUM] F12: Init writes token to .env vs prints it — contradiction

- wa-kyn.12: "create `.env` with `chmod 600` and **empty values**" AND "If `WIKI_AUDIO_ACCESS_TOKEN` is empty, generate a token … Print it once".
- §9.1: token is "stored … in `~/.wiki-audio/.env` as `WIKI_AUDIO_ACCESS_TOKEN`".
- If init only PRINTS the token, the user must manually paste it into .env before doctor passes — but doctor (wa-kyn.13) requires the var populated. Friction.
- If init WRITES the token, .env is no longer "empty values".
- **Fix:** clarify wa-kyn.12 — generate, write to .env, AND echo to stdout with instructions to mirror in 1Password + Worker secret.

## [MEDIUM] F13: Test fixtures drift between live disk and `testdata/essays/`

- wa-kyn.19 reads from `/data/projects/wiki-audio/*.md` (user's working copies).
- wa-kyn.22 says "Step 1: copy them into `testdata/essays/` and git-add them".
- These two locations have no sync mechanism. If user edits the live copy (typo fix, new note), tests pass against stale fixtures while wa-kyn.19 spot-check sees the new content.
- **Fix:** wa-kyn.22 should run wa-kyn.19's spot-check off the same `testdata/essays/` files. The user's working copies are out-of-band.

## [MEDIUM] F14: Manifest doesn't track skipped/malformed essays

- §6: malformed body < 200 chars → "append slug to local `~/.cache/wiki-audio/skipped.txt`. Don't fail the run."
- Manifest schema has no `Skipped []string` or `LastSkipReason`.
- Next run has no way to surface "you've been skipping this essay for 3 builds — investigate". Local `.txt` is on the wiki box; if the box is reinstalled (the whole point of stateless wiki box per §1), skip history is lost.
- **Fix:** add `Manifest.Skipped map[string]SkipRecord{Reason, FirstSkipAt, LastSkipAt}` or accept the loss explicitly in PLAN §6.

## [LOW] F15: `AudioChunk.Index` 0-based or 1-based — undeclared

- wa-kyn.10 example: `for i, c` (Go convention, 0-based).
- §3 build output: `[1/53] how-to-do-great-work` (1-based progress).
- ID3 frames historically use 1-based track numbers. wa-id3 (Phase E) will need to know.
- **Fix:** state in wa-kyn.1 — `Index int // 0-based; UI may display Index+1`.

## [LOW] F16: `defaults_applied` test in wa-kyn.21 — mechanism unspecified in wa-kyn.2

- wa-kyn.2 lists 8 defaults to apply but doesn't specify the application mechanism.
- BurntSushi/toml leaves omitted fields at zero values. Loader must inject defaults post-Unmarshal — the bead should call this out so the implementer doesn't try to use struct-tag defaults (Go has none).
- **Fix:** add to wa-kyn.2: "after `toml.Decode`, call `applyDefaults(&cfg)` which sets each field listed above iff currently the zero value".

---

## Recommended action

Resolve F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7 (HIGH) before wa-kyn.1 lands —
they all touch struct definitions or constants that other beads
depend on. F8–F14 (MEDIUM) can be triaged into PLAN.md edits +
bead-text edits in parallel with implementation.

Filed by pane-5 during wait-state for wa-jlb.6 (Phase B scaffold).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
[pane-2] Phase D retrospective review against shipped impl. Phase D code itself is in good shape — the wa-k8a F1/F2/F3 audit caught the impl bugs, and v0.1.0 ships clean. Where I now find drift is in **PLAN_FOR_AUDIO_LIBRARY.md §2 / §4 / §5.1 / §5.2**: the spec was written before the impl shook out, and the corrections have not been backported. Future-me reading the spec without the wa-k8a context would re-introduce some of the bugs we just fixed.

Filing 10 findings, prefixed `R#` so they don't collide with pane-5's F1-F7 series (which my wa-k8a closed). Severities: 1 HIGH, 6 MEDIUM, 3 LOW.

---

## [HIGH] R1: Slug derivation algorithm is undefined; multiple ad-hoc copies in the tree

**Drift.** §2 declares `EssayMeta.Slug` as "filename stem, kebab-cased" (line 65) but does not pin the algorithm. Three call sites today derive a slug independently:

- `internal/cli/build.go::slugFromPath` — lower + replace " " and "—" with "-", collapse "--", trim "-".
- `internal/cli/extract_only.go` — uses `slugFromPath` (same as build).
- `internal/e2e/extract_chunk_e2e_test.go::slugify` — lower + replace " " and "—" with "-", collapse "--", trim "-". Same algorithm but a separate copy.

For v0.1.0 this is invisible because all three converge on the same output for the corpus. The risk is **Phase F**: the publish path needs to diff `pg/<slug>.mp3` against the manifest's stored slug. If publish lands a 4th copy of slug derivation (or composes `model.EssayMeta.Slug` directly without re-deriving), and that copy disagrees on a corner case (e.g. an em-dash run, a parenthesized title, a non-ASCII letter), unchanged essays will look stale and re-upload.

**Fix.** Add a canonical `model.SlugFromTitle(title string) string` (or `SlugFromPath(path string)`). Pin its rules in §2. Have build, extract-only, e2e, and Phase F's publish all call it. Test row: any input → idempotent (`Slugify(Slugify(x)) == Slugify(x)`).

This carries forward pane-5's earlier F4. wa-i1l.16 (manifest read/write) will need this fixed before publish ships.

---

## [MEDIUM] R2: §2 struct definition omits `Malformed` / `MalformedReason`

`internal/model/types.go::CleanedDocument` has both fields (added in wa-kyn.1 per pane-5's pre-fix F1). PLAN §2 still shows the pre-F1 struct without them (line 74-81). A new contributor reading §2 and re-writing the struct from scratch would lose the §6 sanity-check signal.

**Fix.** Patch §2's `CleanedDocument` snippet to include both fields with comments referencing §6 (`MinBodyChars` threshold).

---

## [MEDIUM] R3: §2 doesn't surface the constants exported in the model package

The impl exports a useful set of named constants at the bottom of `internal/model/types.go`:

```
DefaultAuthor           = "Paul Graham"
DefaultModelID          = "eleven_flash_v2_5"
DefaultChunkMaxChars    = 4000
DefaultRequestTimeoutS  = 60.0
DefaultRetryAttempts    = 3
DefaultRetryBackoffBase = 2.0
DefaultOutputFormat     = "mp3_44100_64"
DefaultFeedPath         = "pg.xml"
DefaultLanguage         = "en-us"
MinBodyChars            = 200
FootnotePolicyVersion   = "v1"
ManifestSchemaVersion   = 1
```

§2 inlines these as TOML comments (`// default 4000`) but never names them. Three downstream behaviors depend on them:

1. `MinBodyChars` is the §6 sanity gate — explicit constant, easy to grep, not in spec.
2. `FootnotePolicyVersion` is the cache-bust knob for §5.1 step 11. The spec says "bundle into hash" but never names the constant or documents the bumping policy ("any change to hash inputs must bump").
3. `ManifestSchemaVersion` mirrors `manifest.KnownManifestVersion` for the wa-76r.1 forward-compat guard.

**Fix.** §2 grows a "Named constants" subsection enumerating these. Bumping policy for FootnotePolicyVersion called out in §5.1 step 11. ManifestSchemaVersion cross-references wa-76r.1.

---

## [MEDIUM] R4: §5.1 step 2 doesn't say to drop the title line

Spec line: `2. title = first line matching ^# (.+)$.` That is a capture instruction; nothing instructs the implementer to remove the line from `raw_body`. The original impl chose conservative-keep, which produced the audibly-bad title-double-read regression that wa-k8a F2 fixed.

**Fix.** Spec step 2 should read `2. title = first line matching ^# (.+)$. Drop that line from raw_body.` Saves the next contributor from re-discovering F2 the hard way.

---

## [MEDIUM] R5: §5.1 hard-codes Readwise headers as the only header shape

Steps 3-4 assume the input has `## Metadata` and `## Full Document` headers. wa-k8a F1 added a YAML-frontmatter alternative (`---\n…\n---\n` at the top), and an essay in the test corpus (`How to Get Startup Ideas.md`) actually uses it. The spec does not mention this branch.

**Fix.** Spec grows a "step 0" or amends step 3-4 to dispatch between two header shapes:

- Readwise canonical (`## Metadata` / `## Full Document`) — current behavior.
- YAML frontmatter (`---` fence at top); title from `title:` key.

Files matching neither are rejected with a clear error. Mirrors `extract.stripHeaders`.

---

## [MEDIUM] R6: §5.1 step 8 phrasing contradicts the edge-case table

Step 8.b.i says "Find all `[N]` markers (where N matches a key in footnote_map)." Read literally, that means non-matching `[N]` markers are NOT found — and therefore not stripped. But the edge-case table immediately below says: "Marker `[N]` in prose with no matching note in `footnote_map` → Strip marker silently".

The impl follows the edge-case table (find `[N]` regardless, strip all, emit footnote line only if in map). Anyone reading step 8.b.i in isolation would write the bug.

**Fix.** §5.1 step 8.b.i should say "Find all `[N]` markers (digits in brackets, with link-debris guard). For each marker, look up N in footnote_map; emit a Footnote line only when found. Strip the marker either way."

---

## [MEDIUM] R7: §5.1 step 7d "skipped_segments" element format is undocumented

Step 7d says "Strip fenced code blocks ```...```; record count in skipped_segments." The impl records *strings*, not a count: `code_block` or `code_block:python`. wa-kyn.7 pinned this; pane-5's earlier F7 flagged the gap. wa-kyn.9 happily passes them through to `CleanedDocument.SkippedSegments`.

If a future bead adds image entries (e.g. `image:<alt>`), the format becomes heterogeneous and JSON consumers can't distinguish "what category is this entry?".

**Fix.** §2 grows a `SkippedSegments` element format pin: `category[:detail]`, where `category ∈ {code_block, image, ...}`. Or, more structured: change the type to `[]SkippedSegment{Kind, Detail}` and document each kind. Trade-off: heterogeneous strings are simpler today; structured is forward-compat. Spec should pick one explicitly.

---

## [LOW] R8: §5.2 step 5 cites a regex with lookahead that Go's RE2 cannot express

Spec regex: `[.!?]\s+(?=[A-Z])`. Go's RE2 engine has no lookahead. The impl works around it by matching `[.!?]\s+` and post-filtering for `next-char ∈ [A-Z]`. The behavior is equivalent, but the spec's regex would not compile in Go.

**Fix.** §5.2 step 5 should note that RE2 implementations split on `[.!?]\s+` and filter for an ASCII-uppercase next character separately. One-line clarification prevents a future port to a regex-engine-aware refactor that "fixes" the spec.

---

## [LOW] R9: `EssayMeta.SourceURL` and `PublishDateText` are declared but never populated

§2 declares both fields. The Readwise metadata block has `URL:` and the body sometimes has `July 2023`-style date prefixes — both could populate these, but stripHeaders drops the metadata block before parsing, and no one parses the body's date prefix. The fields ship as empty strings.

For v1 this is harmless (RSS doesn't use either). For v2 the user might want podcast `<pubDate>` to reflect the original publish date rather than `generated_at`.

Carries forward pane-5's earlier F5.

**Fix.** Either (a) parse the metadata bullets BEFORE dropping the block (extractor change in a future bead) and populate both fields, or (b) drop the fields from the struct and document the v1 scope decision in §2. Currently they are aspirational dead weight.

---

## [LOW] R10: HTML inline tags, blockquote `>` prefixes, and list markers pass through to TTS

The High Agency fixture has all three: `**bold**`, `*italic*`, `> quoted line`, `1. numbered list`, `- bullet list`. The extractor strips no markdown tokens beyond images/links/wikilinks/code fences (§5.1 step 7), so `**bold**` is read literally as "asterisk asterisk bold asterisk asterisk", `> ` as nothing-or-"greater than" depending on TTS engine, and list markers as their literal characters.

PG essays don't use most of these constructs (`*italic*` is occasional). High Agency uses them heavily. The TTS output for High Agency is therefore audibly worse than for canonical PG essays — not a v0.1.0 blocker (only PG essays ship), but worth recording so a future "any-author corpus" bead doesn't ship with this surprise.

**Fix.** Document under §5.1 "Edge cases the extractor handles" that markdown emphasis (`*foo*`, `**foo**`), blockquote prefixes (`> `), and list markers (`1.`, `- `) survive into the body. Future bead can decide whether to strip emphasis tokens (cheap), skip blockquotes (semantic question), or normalize list markers.

---

## Summary

- 1 HIGH: slug derivation algorithm undefined (`R1`) — wa-i1l.16 (Phase F manifest read/write) will need this fixed before publish ships.
- 6 MEDIUM: §2/§5.1 spec patches to backport F1/F2/F3 lessons + format the constants/SkippedSegments contract.
- 3 LOW: spec wording, dead fields, markdown-emphasis passthrough.

**Phase D code itself is sound** — the `internal/extract/`, `internal/chunk/`, `internal/model/` packages are tested end-to-end (e2e harness + 3 real-essay goldens) and the wa-k8a fixes are in production. title: Cross-cutting concerns (error handling, security, docs)

Implements: PLAN_FOR_AUDIO_LIBRARY.md §6 (error handling), §9 (privacy),

Several behaviors thread through every phase and don't sit cleanly under

Tracking these here keeps phase epics clean and gives us a place to
record runbooks without burying them in implementation tasks.

title: Manifest schema versioning + forward-compat guard
description:
Implementation policy:

- Manifest.Version is an integer, starts at 1.
- Each binary embeds a constant \`KnownManifestVersion = 1\`.
- On load: if Manifest.Version > KnownManifestVersion, REFUSE to write
  back. Print: \"manifest schema is newer than this binary; run
  \`wiki-audio upgrade\` and try again.\"
- On schema change: bump KnownManifestVersion by 1 in the same PR
  that introduces the new field. Old binaries fail closed.

## Why a write-time guard (not just read-time)

Reading is forgiving (json.Unmarshal happily ignores unknown fields),
but a write-back from an old binary would silently DROP fields the
new schema added. That corrupts state for newer binaries running on
other machines (or future-me on a forgotten upgrade).

## Why we don't do migrations

§6: simpler to refuse-and-upgrade than to write migration code. The
manifest is small; the user runs ONE binary; cross-version coexistence
is not a real scenario. Refuse-and-upgrade is correct for this scale.

## Test Plan (added by polish pass 2 — §6 \"Tool version mismatch\")

The actual test rows live in wa-i1l.16's manifest test plan (see
`version_guard_refuses_overwrite` and `version_guard_allows_older_read`).
Cited here so the §6 coverage matrix is unambiguous about which suite
covers this row.

Behavior pinned by those tests:
- Version > known → Save returns error; bytes NOT written.
- Version < known → Load succeeds; Save bumps Version to current.
- Version == known → both Load and Save succeed.

A separate sentinel test that may live in `internal/manifest/` (see
wa-i1l.16) covers the user-facing message:

| Test name                              | Setup                                  | Expectation |
|----------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|-------------|
| version_guard_message_is_actionable    | Manifest.Version = current+1           | error contains \"manifest schema is newer than this binary; run wiki-audio upgrade and try again\" |

The literal message is part of §6's recovery story.

| internal/manifest/version_test.go | 13 hermetic tests |

## API

```go

var ErrSchemaTooNew = errors.New(
    "manifest schema is newer than this binary; run `wiki-audio upgrade` and try again")

func CheckCompatible(loaded *model.Manifest) error
func Load(r io.Reader) (*model.Manifest, error)
func Save(m *model.Manifest, w io.Writer) error
```

- m.Version greater than KnownManifestVersion → ErrSchemaTooNew, NOTHING WRITTEN (verified by TestSave_NewerVersionRefusedNothingWritten).

title: Integration test gating mechanism (WIKI_AUDIO_RUN_INTEGRATION env var + build tags)
description:
Establish the project-wide pattern that distinguishes free, hermetic
unit tests (always run) from credit-burning integration tests (opt-in).

## Convention

All tests that hit a real external service (ElevenLabs API, R2 bucket,
the Worker URL) live in files with the build tag:

```go
//go:build integration
// +build integration

package <pkg>
```

AND check `os.Getenv("WIKI_AUDIO_RUN_INTEGRATION") == "1"` at the top
of TestMain (or the first integration test in the file). Both gates
must pass for the test to run:

- The build tag means `go test ./...` skips the file entirely.
- The env var means `go test -tags=integration ./...` ALSO skips
  unless explicitly opted in. Defense-in-depth.

## Run modes

```
go test ./...                                            # unit only
go test -tags=integration ./...                          # compile but skip (env-gated)
WIKI_AUDIO_RUN_INTEGRATION=1 go test -tags=integration ./...  # actually run
```

## Test Plan — verify the gating itself

Add a test `internal/testutil/gating_test.go`:

| Test name                          | Expectation |
|------------------------------------|-------------|
| unit_run_no_integration_files      | go test (no tag) doesn't see integration files |
| tagged_run_skips_without_env       | go test -tags=integration skips when env unset |
| tagged_run_with_env_runs           | both conditions → test runs |
| skip_message_clear                 | t.Skip message names the env var to set |

## Helper: `testutil.RequireIntegration(t)`

```go
func RequireIntegration(t *testing.T) {
    t.Helper()
    if os.Getenv("WIKI_AUDIO_RUN_INTEGRATION") != "1" {
        t.Skip("set WIKI_AUDIO_RUN_INTEGRATION=1 to run integration tests")
    }
}
```

Every integration test file's TestMain (or first test) calls this.
One-line consistent gate.

## Helper: `testutil.RequireCredentials(t, vars ...string)`

Skips if any required env var is empty. Lets the gate be specific —
"ELEVENLABS_API_KEY required" is more useful than "missing creds".

## Structured logging during integration tests

slog.With("test", t.Name(), "service", svc, "integration", true).
Plus a startup log at TestMain that prints the run mode (which gates
were passed) so future humans know they actually hit the real service.

## CI policy

CI runs `go test ./...` only — never `-tags=integration`. Integration
tests are run manually by the developer when wiring up a new service
or before a release. They burn ~$0.01-0.50 per run depending on
which service.

## What goes in integration tests

- ElevenLabs: small request returns audio bytes, retry classifier
  handles real 429s if the test account is mid-rate-limit (wa-4cw.12).
- R2: real PutObject + GetObject roundtrip, multipart for >5MB
  (wa-i1l.18).
- Worker: token validation, 401 on bad token, MP3 streaming
  (wa-jlb.7 region — separate bead).

Each of those areas gets its own integration-test bead that depends on
this gating mechanism being in place.

title: Atomic local writes (os.CreateTemp + os.Rename)
description:
Every disk write that matters (final MP3, manifest snapshots in
~/.cache/, skipped.txt) MUST use the atomic write idiom:

\`\`\`go
tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(filepath.Dir(target), \".tmp-*\")
// ... write to tmp ...
tmp.Close()
os.Rename(tmp.Name(), target)
\`\`\`

## Why

§6: \"Disk full during write — atomic local writes via os.CreateTemp +
os.Rename ensure partial files don't replace good ones.\"

Same defense applies to every \"replace this file\" operation. A power
failure mid-write that leaves a half-written MP3 in place would cause
publish to upload the half-MP3 to R2; the atomic rename means the old
file stays in place until the new one is fully written.

## Where to enforce

Add a small \`atomicwrite.WriteFile(path, data)\` helper in internal/
and use it everywhere we touch disk for outputs.

## Test Plan (added by polish pass 2 — covers §6 "Disk full" row)

Tests in :

| Test name                              | Setup                                  | Expectation |
|----------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|-------------|
| writes_creates_target                  | empty dir                              | target exists with bytes |
| overwrites_existing_target             | target pre-exists with old bytes       | target == new bytes |
| crash_before_rename_leaves_old         | call WriteFile but kill before Rename  | target unchanged (still old bytes) |
| enospc_does_not_replace_target         | tmpdir on a tmpfs sized to N; write N+1 bytes | target unchanged; tmp file removed; clear ENOSPC error |
| enospc_cleanup_removes_tmp_file        | (same as above)                        | filepath.Glob ".tmp-*" returns empty |
| concurrent_writes_one_wins              | two goroutines WriteFile same path     | target has bytes from exactly one (not interleaved) |
| readonly_filesystem_returns_error      | target dir read-only                   | clear error; no panic |
| permission_preserved                   | pre-existing target with mode 0644     | new target has mode 0644 (not 0600 from CreateTemp) |

## Simulating ENOSPC

Use a tmpfs mount sized to a known small value, OR use a custom
filesystem-error-injecting wrapper. For Linux CI we can mount a 4MiB
tmpfs at /tmp/wa-test-enospc; macOS CI skips this test (build tag).

The point is to assert the safety property: ENOSPC mid-write does
NOT clobber a previously-good target file. The atomic-rename idiom
guarantees this; the test pins it.

## Permission-preservation rationale

If we're overwriting a file that previously had mode 0644, the
atomically-written replacement should have the same mode. Otherwise
secrets-adjacent files like manifest.json could end up world-readable
through this code path. Use os.Chmod after Rename or fchmod on the
tempfile before close.

comments.text:
[pane-2] Atomic write helpers shipped in `internal/atomic/`; existing call sites converted.

## What landed

| path | purpose |
|------|---------|
| internal/atomic/doc.go | package overview |
| internal/atomic/atomic.go | `WriteFile`, `WriteAtomic`, `IsSpaceError` |
| internal/atomic/enospc_unix.go / enospc_other.go | platform-specific ENOSPC sentinel |
| internal/atomic/atomic_test.go | 11 hermetic tests |

## API

```go
func WriteFile(path string, data []byte, perm fs.FileMode) error
func WriteAtomic(path string, write func(io.Writer) error, perm fs.FileMode) error
func IsSpaceError(err error) bool
```

`WriteFile` mirrors `os.WriteFile` so call sites swap one-for-one without rewriting their argument list. `WriteAtomic` is the streamed variant for io.Copy-style writes (final MP3 in concat, future R2 download paths). Both:

1. Create temp via `os.CreateTemp(filepath.Dir(target), ".tmp-<base>-*")` — same dir as target so the rename stays within one filesystem (Rename atomicity caveat documented in godoc).
2. Invoke caller's writer.
3. fsync + Close.
4. `os.Chmod(tmpName, perm)` BEFORE Rename — closes the publish-window race where target temporarily carries CreateTemp's restrictive 0o600 mode.
5. `os.Rename`.
6. Defer-based cleanup removes the temp on any error path.

## Call sites converted

| call site | what changed |
|-----------|--------------|
| internal/cli/init.go writeConfigFile | `os.WriteFile` → `atomic.WriteFile` for ~/.wiki-audio/config.toml |
| internal/cli/init.go writeEnvWithMode | `os.WriteFile` + `os.Chmod` → `atomic.WriteFile` (chmod no longer needed; helper does it before Rename) |
| internal/concat/concat.go copyFile | `os.Create` + `io.Copy` → `atomic.WriteAtomic` for the single-chunk-essay final MP3 path |

## Tests (11, all passing in 0.014s)

| name | covers (bead test plan) |
|------|-------------------------|
| TestWriteFile_CreatesTarget | writes_creates_target |
| TestWriteFile_OverwritesExisting | overwrites_existing_target |
| TestWriteAtomic_WriteCallbackErrorLeavesTargetUnchanged | crash_before_rename_leaves_old |
| TestWriteFile_ReadOnlyDirReturnsError | readonly_filesystem_returns_error |
| TestWriteFile_PermAppliedOnOverwrite | permission_preserved (the 'not 0o600 from CreateTemp' check) |
| TestWriteFile_PermRespectedForRestrictiveMode | sister case for 0o600 secrets |
| TestWriteAtomic_StreamedWriteFromReader | streamed io.Copy variant works (1 MB) |
| TestWriteFile_TmpCleanedOnSuccess | filepath.Glob('.tmp-*') empty after success |
| TestWriteFile_TmpCleanedOnError | filepath.Glob('.tmp-*') empty after error |
| TestWriteFile_ConcurrentWritesNeverInterleave | 16 goroutines → final == one payload, no interleave |
| TestIsSpaceError_RecognizesENOSPC | ENOSPC mapping |

`enospc_does_not_replace_target` (full ENOSPC simulation) deliberately deferred — requires a sized tmpfs which is platform-specific. The crash-mid-write test exercises the same defended invariant (write callback errors → target unchanged + temp cleaned), so the safety property is pinned without the platform-specific setup.

`go test ./...` clean (atomic + concat + cli all pass post-conversion). `go vet ./...` clean. `go build ./...` clean.

## Future call sites flagged for the bead's stated targets

The bead lists "final MP3, manifest snapshots, skipped.txt" — these write paths don't exist in production code yet:

- **Manifest snapshots** — `internal/manifest/` is a stub (only doc.go). When wa-cfn.* / wa-76r.1 wires the real Save/Load pair, it should call `atomic.WriteFile` for the JSON write.
- **skipped.txt** — `internal/cache/SkippedPath()` is a path getter only; no production writer yet. The bulk-build malformed handler that lands the append-write should use `atomic.WriteFile` (or a small `AppendFile` companion if append is the right shape — happy to follow up).
- **ffmpeg final-output** — concat's intermediate `step_NNN.mp3` files are written by ffmpeg directly; converting THOSE to atomic would mean ffmpeg writing to a .tmp and Go renaming. Larger refactor; not in scope here. The `copyFile` single-chunk fast path IS now atomic (most direct route from chunk to outPath).

The pattern — and the helpers — are now in place for whichever bead lands those write paths next.

title: Logging: log/slog with structured handlers, no secret leaks
description:
Use stdlib \`log/slog\` with the text handler at INFO level by default.
Flags:
- \`--verbose\` (-v): switch to DEBUG.
- \`--quiet\`   (-q): switch to WARN.
- \`--json\`         : switch to JSON handler (structured-log-friendly).

## What to log

INFO: per-essay progress (\`extracted X chars\`, \`uploaded Y bytes\`).
DEBUG: per-chunk progress, retry attempts, hash check decisions.
WARN: skip events (malformed essay, footnote orphan), retry failures.
ERROR: terminal failures.

## What to NEVER log

- ELEVENLABS_API_KEY (or any secret from .env)
- WIKI_AUDIO_ACCESS_TOKEN
- Full request URLs (they include the token in query)

## Implementation hint

Add a small redaction wrapper or just discipline. The log lines that
print URLs should always strip the query string before logging.

comments.text:
[REVIEW pane-4] internal/cli/redact.go + root_test.go findings — landed at 6941d63:

[HIGH] RedactURL allowlist contradicts the spec quote in its own doc comment — the comment says: 'log lines that print URLs should always strip the query string before logging' (citing wa-76r.3). The implementation only strips three known parameter names: `t`, `token`, `access_token`. A URL with the same secret material under any other name (e.g. `auth=...`, `key=...`, `access=...`) — or new params added later — will leak. Test case `?other=keep` actively codifies this allowlist behavior. Two paths to resolve:
  (a) Match the spec literally — strip the entire query string. Update tests so `?other=keep` becomes `?` (or drop the query entirely).
  (b) Update the doc comment to reflect that this is allowlist-based, not a full-strip — and document the maintenance burden ("any new query param carrying user secrets MUST be added to the allowlist in redact.go").
The current state — code says one thing, comment says another — is the worst option because future readers will trust the comment.

[MEDIUM] RedactURL silently returns input on parse error — `url.Parse` is permissive and rarely fails, but if it does, a malformed URL containing a literal token leaks unredacted. Defense in depth: even on the err-return path, run a regex fallback (`(?i)([?&](t|token|access_token)=)[^&\s]+` → `$1<redacted>`) before returning. Cheap; matches the function's stated intent.

[LOW] No userinfo handling — a URL of the form `https://user:secret@host/` has no `t` param and so is returned unchanged. `u.User` exposes the password. Edge case; this codebase doesn't construct such URLs, but if it ever did (e.g. some R2 endpoint with embedded creds for testing) the password would leak. Worth one-liner: `u.User = nil` before `u.String()`.

[LOW] Tests don't cover the `url.Parse` error path — no test pins the behavior on a malformed URL. If the parse-error branch silently returns input (as today) vs runs a regex fallback (as recommended above), the tests should pin which.

title: Token rotation runbook
description:
Documented procedure. Save in worker/README.md and link from main
README.md. Steps:

1. Generate new token: \`openssl rand -base64 32 | tr '+/' '-_' | tr -d '='\`.
2. Update Cloudflare Worker secret:
     \`cd worker && wrangler secret put ACCESS_TOKEN\`
   (paste the new value at the prompt).
3. Update local env: edit \`~/.wiki-audio/.env\` to replace
   WIKI_AUDIO_ACCESS_TOKEN.
4. Update 1Password.
5. \`wiki-audio publish --feed-only\` — regenerates pg.xml with new
   token in every enclosure URL.
6. On phone in Pocket Casts: unsubscribe from old feed URL,
   re-subscribe to new feed URL (the URL itself contains the token
   now).
7. Verify old URL 403s: \`curl <old-feed-url>\` should return 403.

Old token is invalidated immediately at step 2. No object renames
needed because tokens live in query string, not path (§9.3).

## When to rotate

- Any time the token leaks (screenshot, accidental commit, suspicion).
- Yearly as hygiene (no need; query-string tokens have no expiry
  baked in).
- After any laptop loss or compromise.

## Canonical rotation procedure (every storage location)

The token lives in EXACTLY 3 places (per §9.1) and must be replaced in
all of them in this order; deviation breaks the "old token immediately
invalidated" property.

| # | Location | How | Effect |
|---|----------|-----|--------|
| 1 | Cloudflare Worker secret `ACCESS_TOKEN` | `cd worker && wrangler secret put ACCESS_TOKEN` (paste new value) | Old token starts 403'ing within seconds (Worker propagation) |
| 2 | `~/.wiki-audio/.env` line `WIKI_AUDIO_ACCESS_TOKEN=...` | edit file; verify `chmod 600` still set | Local builds will stamp the new token into the next published feed |
| 3 | 1Password entry "wiki-audio access token" | replace value; keep prior version in 1P history for ~30 days | Restorability if a botched rotation leaves nothing working |
| 4 | (derived) `pg.xml` enclosure URLs in R2 | run `wiki-audio publish --feed-only` | Republishes feed XML with new token in every `?t=` |
| 5 | (derived) Pocket Casts subscription on phone | unsubscribe from old feed URL; re-subscribe to new feed URL | App now fetches with new token; old cached enclosure URLs stop working |

## Verification AFTER rotation (all four MUST pass)

1. `curl -I "https://wiki-audio.jabyrne.workers.dev/pg.xml?t=<OLD_TOKEN>"`
   → expect HTTP 403. (Old token must be dead.)
2. `curl -I "https://wiki-audio.jabyrne.workers.dev/pg.xml?t=<NEW_TOKEN>"`
   → expect HTTP 200 + `content-type: application/rss+xml`.
3. `curl -s "https://wiki-audio.jabyrne.workers.dev/pg.xml?t=<NEW_TOKEN>" | grep -c "?t=<NEW_TOKEN>"`
   → count must equal `1 + (# of episodes)` (self-link + each enclosure).
4. In Pocket Casts: pull-to-refresh; latest episode plays.

If verification step 1 fails (old token still works), Worker secret
update did not propagate — re-run step 1 of the rotation procedure.
If step 3 returns < expected count, the feed re-publish at step 4
of rotation didn't run — re-run `wiki-audio publish --feed-only`.

## Threat-model context (§9 — keep in mind during rotation)

Rotation is the ONLY mitigation against §9.4 leak vectors (you shared
the URL, Pocket Casts logged it, etc.). Don't skip rotation when in
doubt about a leak — the cost is ~5 minutes; the cost of not rotating
is "stranger has indefinite access to your audio library".

There is no per-episode token. One token = one rotation. Per-episode
tokens would multiply rotation work without strengthening the threat
model — see wa-i1l.6.

## Token format (must match §9.1)

- 32 random bytes from `crypto/rand`, base64-url-encoded with NO
  padding → exactly 43 chars of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`.
- Generated either by `wiki-audio init` (Go binary; see wa-kyn.12) OR
  out-of-band: `openssl rand -base64 32 | tr '+/' '-_' | tr -d '='`.
- Both methods produce the same format. Don't paste a token in any
  other format — the Worker compares as exact-length string.

## Never log the token

- During rotation, redact the value from any shell history if
  pasted on the command line (`history -d <N>` after the session).
- `wrangler secret put` reads from stdin and never echoes; prefer it
  over `--secret <value>` flags.
- The Go binary never logs WIKI_AUDIO_ACCESS_TOKEN (slog redaction;
  see wa-kyn.3 — secrets live only in os.Getenv, never in Config
  struct fields).

title: Pre-commit hook / gitleaks config (defends .env from accidental commit)
description:
Two layers (already mentioned in C9, this bead extends to local hooks):

1. Server side: gitleaks in CI on every push (C9).
2. Client side: pre-commit hook that runs gitleaks on staged content
   before letting the commit through.

The .gitignore in the wiki-audio repo excludes .env, so this is a
defense-in-depth — catches a secret accidentally inlined into source
or a test fixture.

## Pre-commit framework choice

Just a plain \`.git/hooks/pre-commit\` shell script that calls gitleaks.
No pre-commit framework needed — keeps the dev environment minimal.

comments.author: pane-3
comments.text:
## wa-76r.5 closed — `.githooks/pre-commit` shipped (commit `e7abb31`)

Defense-in-depth alongside wa-8gt.9's CI gate. Three-layer prevention chain:

```
  1. .gitignore excludes .env / .env.* / *.mp3           (file-level)
  2. .githooks/pre-commit runs gitleaks on staged diff   (commit-level — this bead)
  3. .github/workflows/gitleaks.yml on push + PR         (remote-level — wa-8gt.9)
```

### Hook design

- `gitleaks protect --staged --redact -v --config=.gitleaks.toml`
  - `--staged`: only the diff about to commit, not full history (that's CI's job)
  - `--redact`: keeps any leaked secret out of the hook's own output (no scrollback re-leak)
  - `--config=…/.gitleaks.toml`: pins local scan to the repo's shared config from wa-8gt.9 (placeholder hostnames + test-fixture allowlist), so local and CI agree on what counts as a leak.
- Missing gitleaks → prints an install hint (`brew/apt/go install`) and **exits 0**. Hard-failing on a missing tool punishes contributors who haven't read the README; CI catches anything the local hook misses. Friendly pass-through is the right-direction incentive.

### Per-clone opt-in

```
git config core.hooksPath .githooks
```

Documented in AGENTS.md §5 ("Security posture", "Pre-commit guard" bullet). The prior bullet mentioned "the agent-mail pre-commit hook" — that was a stale reference to a planned-but-not-shipped MCP-tool path; updated in this commit to point at the actual `.githooks/pre-commit` mechanism.

Bypass for emergency commits: `git commit --no-verify` (CI will still flag).

### Behavior matrix (all paths verified locally with gitleaks v8.30.1)

| Scenario | Expected | Got |
|---|---|---|
| Empty staged diff (gitleaks present) | exit 0, no leaks | ✅ |
| Clean staged diff (gitleaks present) | exit 0, no leaks | ✅ |
| Stripe + Slack + 64-hex `api_key` staged | exit 1; commit blocked | ✅ — 3 findings flagged; `git log -1` unchanged after attempted commit |
| gitleaks not on PATH | exit 0 + install hint | ✅ |

Direct test of (3): created a temp file with a `sk_live_…` Stripe key, an `xoxb-…` Slack bot token, and a 64-char hex `api_key`, staged it, ran `git -c core.hooksPath=.githooks commit -m "intentional leak test"`. gitleaks emitted three `RuleID` findings (`stripe-access-token`, `slack-bot-token`, `generic-api-key`); the commit DID NOT land (verified via `git log -1` showing the prior commit unchanged); fixture unstaged + unlinked.

(An earlier test attempted `AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE` — that's the AWS canonical docs example, deliberately allowlisted by gitleaks' default ruleset. The commit briefly landed locally before I noticed the false-negative; reverted via mixed `git reset HEAD~1` + `unlink`. Never pushed. Lesson recorded in this comment for whoever revisits the .gitleaks.toml allowlist.)

### Shellcheck + syntax

`bash -n` clean; `shellcheck v0.10.0` clean.

### Notes for the future

- The `gitleaks` Go module declared path is `github.com/zricethezav/gitleaks/v8` — the `gitleaks/gitleaks/v8` redirect on the upstream URL doesn't propagate through go.mod's path-declared check. Install via the legacy module path: `go install github.com/zricethezav/gitleaks/v8@latest`.
- `.gitleaks.toml` is shared between this hook and the CI workflow. If a contributor adds a legitimate placeholder hostname or test-fixture token shape, edit there once and both layers update.
- The opt-in pattern (vs. mandatory) means a fresh clone has no hook active until the developer reads AGENTS.md and runs the one-liner. That's deliberate per the runbook — avoid surprising contributors on first clone.

title: ToS / copyright periodic review (annual) (deferred)
description:
DEFERRED. Once a year: re-read ElevenLabs ToS for changes that affect
personal-use TTS of third-party essays.

§10: \"ElevenLabs ToS / PG copyright — Risk accepted by user;
personal-use, no redistribution. Not revisited.\"

We accepted the risk for v1. This bead is the calendar-based
re-validation. If ElevenLabs changes ToS to forbid personal-use TTS of
copyrighted works, we'd need to reconsider — though personal use without
redistribution is generally a strong fair-use posture.

## Acceptance criteria (per yearly instance)

RECURRING bead. "Done" applies to the current year's review.

For year YYYY:

1. Open https://elevenlabs.io/terms (and https://elevenlabs.io/privacy) and skim diff vs previous year. Look for changes affecting:
   - Personal-use TTS of third-party copyrighted text.
   - Restrictions on synthesizing celebrity / real-author voices (we use a stock voice — flagged for awareness only).
   - Output ownership / redistribution clauses (we don't redistribute, but a clause requiring credit / attribution would change README guidance).
2. Open the current PG essay corpus license page (https://paulgraham.com — there is no formal license; the position is implicit personal-use fair-use). Note any explicit terms-of-use surface added since last year.
3. Append a one-paragraph note to `~/.cache/wiki-audio/tos-review-YYYY.txt` with: review date, sources checked, verdict (continue / re-evaluate / stop), and one-line reasoning.

Verifiable artifact: the dated `tos-review-YYYY.txt` file exists. The bead never closes; re-runs annually.

## Fail path (verdict = re-evaluate or stop)

- If ElevenLabs ToS now forbids personal-use TTS of copyrighted works without license: stop running new builds; existing R2 episodes may still play (consumer cache), but DO NOT regenerate. Open a tracking bead for the next steps (switch engine, reach out for license, sunset).
- If PG adds an explicit no-derivative-works clause: same posture. Episodes already on phone are personal use; new synthesis pauses pending decision.
- If a verdict of "continue" is reached: the artifact file says so. No further action.

title: Centralize `feed.toml` example with comments
description:
Ship an annotated config.example.toml in the repo root. \`wiki-audio init\`
copies this to \`~/.wiki-audio/config.toml\` on first run.

Every key has a one-line comment explaining what it does. Default
values match D2's loader defaults so the example file is functional
out of the box (modulo placeholders the user must fill in).

## Why a separate example file

config.toml on disk is the user's mutable state. config.example.toml
in the repo is the reference. Editing the live config doesn't
desynchronize the docs.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
[pane-2] Annotated config example landed at repo root.

## What landed

| path | change |
|------|--------|
| config.example.toml | NEW — annotated TOML at repo root, byte-for-byte mirror of `init.go`'s `configTemplate` const |
| internal/cli/init_test.go | NEW test `TestConfigTemplateMatchesRepoExample` — drift guard pinning the two copies in lock-step |

## Why this shape (not go:embed)

`go:embed` cannot reach files outside the package tree (`../../config.example.toml` is rejected by the compiler), so a strict "single source of truth" via embed would force the example file to live under `internal/cli/` — defeating the bead's stated reason for shipping it ("config.example.toml in the repo is the reference"). Operators browsing the repo on github.com expect to find it at the root, not buried four levels deep.

The two-files-with-a-drift-test pattern is the next-cleanest option:

- `init.go`'s `configTemplate` const seeds new installs at compile time. `wiki-audio init` keeps using it as before — no behavior change, no runtime file dependency.
- `config.example.toml` at the repo root is the human-readable reference. Future-me skimming the repo finds it without unpacking the binary.
- `TestConfigTemplateMatchesRepoExample` reads `../../config.example.toml` from the package working dir and asserts `string(bytes) == configTemplate`. Edit one without the other and CI fails with a clear message naming both files and citing wa-76r.9.

The test gracefully `t.Skip`s when the example file is unreachable (e.g. running tests against an installed Go module rather than a checkout), so it never spuriously fails.

## Content (mirrors init.go's existing comment annotations)

Every key has a one-line comment. Defaults from §2 / `model.Default*` are noted in comments rather than written out, so editing the loader's defaults doesn't desynchronize this file. Required-fields are flagged ("Required."). Placeholder values match what `wiki-audio init` writes to disk today.

## Tests / verification

- `go test ./internal/cli/...` → ok 0.250s
- `go test -run TestConfigTemplateMatchesRepoExample` → PASS
- `go test ./...` clean across all 14 packages
- `go vet ./...` clean

## Coordination

`README.md` already cross-references `config.toml` from the "Where things live" section (wa-76r.8). I'm leaving `wiki-audio init` to load the embedded const at runtime — switching to a runtime file-read would (a) require shipping the example file with the binary or fetching it during install, (b) break a fresh install if the example file is missing or path-rewritten. The drift test catches the only realistic regression mode.

Reservations on `config.example.toml`, `internal/cli/init.go`, `internal/cli/init_test.go` released after commit.

title: Bump default output_format to mp3_44100_192 + re-spike validation
description:
## Decision (operator-validated)

User compared flash @ 64-kbps-requested-128-served vs flash @ 192 kbps on the same opening text + same Christopher voice. Verdict: 192 is "much better" — sibilants (s, t) noticeably less squeaky/sharp at 192 vs 128. PLAN §8.7's rationale ("64 kbps mono is indistinguishable from higher bitrates") was empirically wrong for our voice + corpus.

## Implementation — three coordinated changes

### 1. Code defaults

`internal/model/types.go` (or wherever model.TTSConfig defaults live):

```go
// was: OutputFormat = "mp3_44100_64"
DefaultOutputFormat = "mp3_44100_192"
```

Audit grep: `rg "mp3_44100_(32|64|128)" internal/ cmd/` — convert any other places that hardcode the 64 kbps default.

### 2. Configuration template

`internal/cli/init.go` (or wherever the configTemplate string lives):

The TTS section should mention `mp3_44100_192` as the default. Brief explanation: "192 kbps mono — sibilants are noticeably cleaner than 64/128. Storage cost is rounding error (~3.6 GB for 53 essays vs ~1.2 GB)."

### 3. PLAN §8.7 spec update

Rewrite the "Why mp3_44100_64" rationale block. New rationale:

> ## Why mp3_44100_192
>
> 44.1 kHz is the universal podcast sample rate. 192 kbps preserves
> sibilant clarity (s, t, sh) — A/B testing on Christopher voice + flash_v2_5
> showed audible degradation at 64 kbps (effective 128 kbps from EL flash) vs 192 kbps.
> Sibilants live at 4-8 kHz where MP3 compression bites hardest at low bitrates.
>
> Cost is ~3× storage and bandwidth vs 64 kbps. For 53 essays at ~1 hour each:
> 192 kbps = ~3.6 GB total = ~$0.054/month R2 storage. Rounding error.
> ElevenLabs bills on input characters, not output bitrate, so synth cost
> is unchanged.
>
> Originally specced 64 kbps based on assumption of imperceptibility for
> spoken voice. Empirical testing (Phase E spike, 2026-05-09) disproved.

## Re-spike validation

After the code change lands:

1. Delete existing chunks (they're at 128 kbps — wrong bitrate for the new default):
   ```
   rm -rf ~/.cache/wiki-audio/tmp/how-to-do-great-work/
   ```

2. Re-run the build (chunks will re-synth at 192 kbps, then concat losslessly):
   ```
   set -a; . /data/projects/wiki-audio/.env; set +a
   go build -o /tmp/wa-bin ./cmd/wiki-audio
   /tmp/wa-bin build --slug how-to-do-great-work
   ```
   Expected: ~2 min wall (synth) + <30s wall (concat).

3. Upload to R2 (overwriting the 128 kbps version):
   ```
   cd /data/projects/wiki-audio/worker
   wrangler r2 object put wiki-audio/pg/how-to-do-great-work.mp3 \
     --file=/home/ubuntu/.cache/wiki-audio/out/how-to-do-great-work.mp3 \
     --content-type=audio/mpeg --remote
   ```

4. Surface to orchestrator:
   ```
   "wa-* SHIPPED + RE-SPIKE COMPLETE. Default mp3_44100_192. New full-essay
   MP3 at ~/.cache/wiki-audio/out/how-to-do-great-work.mp3 (~85 MB) and at R2
   pg/how-to-do-great-work.mp3. Operator: re-listen + close wa-4cw.9."
   ```

## Acceptance criteria

1. `internal/model/types.go` default is `mp3_44100_192`.
2. configTemplate references `mp3_44100_192`.
3. PLAN_FOR_AUDIO_LIBRARY.md §8.7 has the updated rationale.
4. `go test ./...` clean.
5. Re-spike runs cleanly: 18 chunks re-synth (~$5-7 in credits), concat in <30s, MP3 at ~85 MB and ~61 min duration.
6. R2 object is the 192 kbps version (verify via `ffprobe https://wiki-audio.jabyrne.workers.dev/pg/how-to-do-great-work.mp3?t=...`).

## Coordination

- Pane-5 owns CLI/config domain — natural fit.
- Reserve `internal/model/types.go`, `internal/cli/init.go`, `PLAN_FOR_AUDIO_LIBRARY.md`.
- Pane-3 (concat owner, idle) and pane-2 (extract/build_pipeline owner, idle) clean separation.

## Why P1

- Phase F implementation (wa-i1l.1+) cascade unblocks once wa-4cw.9 closes.
- wa-4cw.9 closure is gated on operator full-essay listen at the new defaults.
- This bead is the last code change before Phase F starts.

comments.text:
# wa-7t6 spike report — partial

## Status: code/spec shipped (acceptance #1, #2); spike BLOCKED (acceptance #3, #4) on wire-level bug

### Acceptance criteria progress

| # | Criterion | Status |
|---|-----------|--------|
| 1 | Code default = mp3_44100_192; template + PLAN updated | ✅ shipped in commit `3314013` |
| 2 | `go test ./...` clean | ✅ all green |
| 3 | Re-spike produces ~85 MB MP3 | ❌ produced 56.0 MiB (correct for 128 kbps × 61min) |
| 4 | ffprobe bit_rate=192000 | ❌ ffprobe shows bit_rate=128000 |
| 5 | R2 upload of the 192 kbps version | ⏸ NOT performed — would have uploaded a 128 kbps file labeled "192" |

### What I committed (good — keep)

`3314013 config: bump DefaultOutputFormat to mp3_44100_192 (wa-7t6)`

- `internal/model/types.go` — `DefaultOutputFormat = "mp3_44100_192"`
- `internal/model/types_test.go` — updated assertion
- `internal/cli/init.go` — configTemplate comment + 5-line rationale crumb
- `config.example.toml` — mirrored per wa-76r.9 byte-for-byte invariant
- `PLAN_FOR_AUDIO_LIBRARY.md` §2 + §8.7 — full Audio Format rationale rewrite, old 64 kbps row preserved with "rejected post-spike" verdict
- `README.md` — config reference + cache-footprint estimate (3.6 GB) + headroom note

### What the spike surfaced (BAD — wa-aoa filed)

ElevenLabs API expects `output_format` as a **query string parameter**:
```
POST /v1/text-to-speech/{voice_id}?output_format=mp3_44100_192
```

`internal/tts/client.go::Synthesize` marshals it into the JSON **body** instead. ElevenLabs silently drops the body field and serves the **default (128 kbps for flash_v2_5)** regardless of the configured value.

ffprobe on the spike output:
```
codec_name=mp3
sample_rate=44100
channels=1
bit_rate=128000        <-- expected 192000
duration=3672.502857   <-- 61 min, correct
size=58760676          <-- 56 MiB, correct for 128 kbps × 61min
```

The 128 kbps result is consistent with the user's pre-wa-7t6 observation that "64-kbps-requested served 128" — that's exactly what happens when `output_format` is dropped: the API uses the flash_v2_5 default.

### Filed as: wa-aoa [HIGH]

`wa-aoa: tts: output_format goes in query string, not JSON body — wire-level bug`

Fix is small (~5 lines in client.go: move `output_format` from JSON body to URL query). Belongs to pane-8's reservation on `internal/tts/`. Test addition in `client_test.go` to pin the query-vs-body location for future maintainers.

### Cost spent on this spike

- Synthesis: 18 chunks × ~3700 chars/chunk avg = ~67k input chars × 0.5 cred/char = **~33,500 EL credits** (~$5-7 on Pro tier)
- Output: 56 MiB at 128 kbps (we can't use this for the 192 quality A/B since it isn't 192)

The credits are sunk. A second spike post-wa-aoa-fix is necessary for legitimate 192 kbps output. Not retrying autonomously per orchestrator's "don't burn credits blindly" guidance.

### What I did NOT do (and why)

- ❌ Did NOT upload the 128 kbps MP3 to R2 — defeats the purpose of the spike. If operator wants the 128 kbps file as a control sample, easy to upload separately; flagging here so it's not silently shipped as "the new default."
- ❌ Did NOT close wa-7t6 — acceptance criteria #3 and #4 fail. wa-7t6 is now logically blocked-by wa-aoa; will close after the wire-bug fix lands and a re-re-spike confirms 192 kbps.
- ❌ Did NOT retry — second attempt would also produce 128 kbps (same bug). Net: another $5-7 wasted.

### Recommended sequence

1. Pane-8 (or whoever picks up `internal/tts/client.go` reservation) ships **wa-aoa**: move `output_format` to query parameter, add test pinning the location.
2. Once wa-aoa lands, anyone (likely me again, since the muscle memory is fresh): re-re-spike → ffprobe check → R2 upload → close wa-7t6.
3. If the wire bug had a longer history: pane-6 may want to re-evaluate whether the original wa-4cw.8 spike had any 64-vs-128 signal (probably not — the API was always serving 128).

— pane-5

title: Phase C — Release plumbing (goreleaser + install.sh)
description:
# Phase C — Cross-compile, release, install

Implements: PLAN_FOR_AUDIO_LIBRARY.md §3 (Install), §7 Phase C.

## Goal

A `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jacob2017/wiki-audio/main/install.sh | bash`
one-liner that:
1. Detects platform via `uname -s`/`-m` (linux/amd64, linux/arm64,
   darwin/amd64, darwin/arm64).
2. Fetches the latest (or `bash -s -- v0.3.0` pinned) tarball from GitHub
   Releases.
3. Verifies SHA-256 against the published checksum.
4. Drops the binary at `/usr/local/bin/wiki-audio` (or `~/.local/bin`
   when non-root).

Built by:
- `.goreleaser.yaml` — cross-compile matrix, tarballs + sha256sums.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` — runs goreleaser on `v*` tag push.

## Why these mechanics specifically

beads_rust set the bar. The user wants the same install ergonomics:
one shell command, no Python/Node bootstrap, idempotent re-runs.
SHA-256 verification is non-negotiable — without it the install line
is a supply-chain vulnerability.

## What \"done\" looks like for v0.0.1

A stub binary (literally `cobra.NewCommand(... Run: return nil)`) tagged
`v0.0.1` and pushed. `curl ... | bash` on the wiki box puts the binary in
PATH; `wiki-audio --version` prints `v0.0.1`. No real functionality yet —
the point is to derisk the distribution path before writing any logic.

## Dependent: `wiki-audio upgrade`

A subcommand that just re-runs install.sh. Idempotent. Lives here because
its existence is part of the distribution story, not a separate feature.

title: Write .goreleaser.yaml (matrix: linux/amd64+arm64, darwin/amd64+arm64)
description:
.goreleaser.yaml configured to:

- Cross-compile for: linux/amd64, linux/arm64, darwin/amd64, darwin/arm64.
- Output one .tar.gz per target containing just the binary.
- Generate a checksums.txt with sha256 lines for every tarball.
- Inject version info via -ldflags="-X main.Version={{.Version}}".

## Why these four targets (not windows, not 386, not freebsd)

The wiki box is Linux. The user's primary laptop is macOS arm64. A second
machine might be macOS amd64 or Linux amd64. Other targets are added
weight in the release pipeline with no real consumer.

## Why tarball + sha256 (not just raw binary)

§3 install: install.sh verifies SHA-256 against the published checksum
before moving the binary to PATH. Tarball is just the carrier — the
sha256 is what makes the install line not a supply-chain vulnerability.

## Reference

beads_rust uses the same pattern. Look at its .goreleaser.yaml for a
proven config to copy from.
