title: Write .github/workflows/release.yml (goreleaser on tag push)
description:
.github/workflows/release.yml triggered by \`v*\` tag pushes:

- Checkout, set up Go 1.22.
- Run \`goreleaser release --clean\`.
- Permissions: contents: write (for creating the GitHub Release).

No release-please, no semantic-release, no auto-version-bumping. The
human pushes a tag; CI mirrors it as a Release. Simpler is better here.

## Why no Docker / multi-arch buildx

We're shipping a tiny static binary, not a container. goreleaser's
native cross-compile is enough.

comments.author: pane-3
comments.text:
## Closing wa-8gt.2 — `.github/workflows/release.yml` shipped (commit `930cb4a`)

### Workflow summary

Tag push (`v*`) → GitHub Release. Single Ubuntu job, three steps:

1. `actions/checkout@v4` with `fetch-depth: 0` — full git history so goreleaser can build its changelog block.
2. `actions/setup-go@v5` with `go-version-file: go.mod` — pin from the source of truth (currently 1.25; spec text says 1.22 but go.mod is what compiles).
3. `goreleaser/goreleaser-action@v6` with `args: release --clean`, version constraint `~> v2`. Reuses the `.goreleaser.yaml` from `8f7cc30` (wa-8gt.1).

### Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| YAML parse | ✅ `python3 -c "yaml.safe_load(...)"` clean |
| GitHub Actions schema lint | ✅ `actionlint .github/workflows/release.yml` exit 0 |
| Cross-check vs .goreleaser.yaml | ✅ `release --clean` is the prod arg; wa-8gt.1 snapshot ran the same pipeline minus `--snapshot --skip=publish` |

### Permissions

Minimum surface: `contents: write` only. No packages, pages, deployments. `GITHUB_TOKEN` is the auto-provisioned per-run token — no PAT, no extra secret to rotate.

### Stale-spec note (already a pattern in wa-8gt.*)

Spec said "set up Go 1.22"; go.mod says `go 1.25`. Used `go-version-file: go.mod` so the workflow tracks whatever the module declares. Same divergence pattern as wa-8gt.1's `main.Version` → `internal/cli.Version`. Bead text predates the package layout settling.

### What unblocks

The next practical milestones — `wa-kyn.20` (cut v0.1.0) and `wa-i1l.14` (cut v1.0.0) — both terminate at `git push origin v0.1.0` / `v1.0.0` triggering this workflow. wa-8gt.3 (install.sh) is independent but consumes the same tarball naming pattern, so it can be authored against the schema this workflow emits.

### Worktree workflow

`git worktree add ../wiki-audio-pane3-8gt2 -b pane3-wa-8gt.2 main`, ship in worktree, `--no-ff` merge, prune. No race with active panes (pane-5 was committing wa-kyn.3 during this work; their commits flowed up cleanly when I pushed main).

title: Write install.sh (uname detect, fetch tarball, sha256 verify, install to PATH)
description:
install.sh that:

1. Detects platform: \`uname -s\` (Linux/Darwin) and \`uname -m\`
   (x86_64→amd64, arm64/aarch64→arm64). Map to goreleaser-target naming.
2. Reads optional version arg (\`bash -s -- v0.3.0\`) or fetches the
   latest release tag from GitHub Releases API.
3. Downloads \`wiki-audio_<version>_<os>_<arch>.tar.gz\` and
   \`checksums.txt\`.
4. Verifies SHA-256: \`sha256sum -c\` (Linux) / \`shasum -a 256 -c\` (macOS).
5. Untars to a tempdir, then \`mv\` the binary to \`/usr/local/bin/\` if
   running as root or sudo'd, else \`~/.local/bin/\` (mkdir -p first).
6. Prints next steps: \`run: wiki-audio init\`.

Behaviors that matter:

- **Idempotent.** Re-running the script overwrites the binary cleanly;
  no \"already installed\" error.
- **Unknown platform exits with a clear message** pointing at the
  Releases page for manual install.
- **No \`set -x\` by default** — output should be one happy path of
  \"detected → fetched → verified → installed → next step\".

## Why curl|bash (and not Homebrew, apt, snap)

§1: matches the install ergonomics of beads_rust; one shell command, no
package manager assumptions, works on any Linux/macOS box. Future
package-manager support is reasonable for v2 if there's demand.

## Test Plan (added by polish pass 2 — §6 \"Install script unknown platform\")

The install script is a bash script — test via shellcheck + a small
bats-style harness in `install_test.sh` (or a Go-driven test that
runs install.sh under controlled $OS / $UNAME_M values).

| Test name                              | Setup                                  | Expectation |
|----------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|-------------|
| linux_amd64_path_resolves              | UNAME_S=Linux UNAME_M=x86_64           | downloads wiki-audio_<v>_linux_amd64.tar.gz |
| linux_arm64_path_resolves              | UNAME_S=Linux UNAME_M=aarch64          | downloads ..._linux_arm64.tar.gz |
| darwin_amd64_path_resolves             | UNAME_S=Darwin UNAME_M=x86_64          | downloads ..._darwin_amd64.tar.gz |
| darwin_arm64_path_resolves             | UNAME_S=Darwin UNAME_M=arm64           | downloads ..._darwin_arm64.tar.gz |
| unknown_os_exits_with_message          | UNAME_S=FreeBSD                        | exit code != 0; stderr lists supported (Linux/Darwin); points at Releases page URL |
| unknown_arch_exits_with_message        | UNAME_S=Linux UNAME_M=mips             | exit code != 0; stderr lists supported (amd64/arm64); points at Releases |
| sha256_mismatch_aborts                 | tamper checksums.txt mid-test          | exit code != 0; binary NOT installed; tmpdir cleaned |
| idempotent_reinstall                   | run twice                              | both succeed; binary overwritten cleanly; no \"already installed\" error |
| version_arg_pins_release               | bash -s -- v0.1.0                       | downloads tagged v0.1.0 not latest |
| no_root_uses_local_bin                 | EUID=1000 (non-root)                   | installs to ~/.local/bin/ (mkdir -p first); prints PATH advice if not on PATH |

## Why test the unknown-platform path explicitly

§6 \"Install script fails on unknown platform — print supported list,
instruct user to download manually from Releases.\" If the script
silently fails or prints a confusing error, the user is stuck. A test
that captures stderr and asserts the supported list is in the
message guards the runbook.

## Implementation hint

A `test/install_test.sh` that invokes install.sh with `UNAME_S=...`
and `UNAME_M=...` env vars (the script reads them via `${UNAME_S:-$(uname -s)}`)
keeps the test hermetic — no subprocess of `uname` needed.

comments.author: pane-3
comments.text:
## Closing wa-8gt.3 — `install.sh` shipped (commit `ec7b5fb`)

The third leg of the release pipeline. Phase C is now: `.goreleaser.yaml` (wa-8gt.1) + `release.yml` (wa-8gt.2) + `install.sh` (this) — tag → CI → tarballs + checksums → curl|bash with sha256 verification.

### Pipeline (153 lines)

```
detect_platform    uname → {linux,darwin}_{amd64,arm64} | clear-error exit
resolve_version    arg | GitHub /releases/latest (tag_name extracted via sed)
pick_install_dir   root → /usr/local/bin | else $HOME/.local/bin (mkdir -p)
fetch + verify     curl tarball + checksums.txt → awk-match my line →
                   sha256sum -c (Linux) | shasum -a 256 -c (macOS)
install            tar xz, mv -f, chmod +x; idempotent
next-step hint     PATH warning if install dir not on PATH; "next: wiki-audio init"
```

### Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `bash -n install.sh` | exit 0 |
| `shellcheck install.sh` (v0.10.0) | exit 0 |
| **TEST 1 happy path** — wa-8gt.1 snapshot tarballs served from localhost http.server, `WA_DL=http://localhost:8766` | install succeeds; binary lands at `$HOME/.local/bin/wiki-audio`; `wiki-audio --version` → `0.0.1-snapshot-9847321` (ldflags injection round-trips) |
| **TEST 2 idempotency** — same install run twice | second run succeeds; `--version` unchanged |
| **TEST 3 tampered checksum** — `checksums.txt` rewritten with bogus sha256 hex | install **exits 1** with `SHA-256 verification failed for <tarball>`; **no binary** ever materializes in install dir |

TEST 3 is the load-bearing assertion. It is what makes `curl ... | bash` not a supply-chain vulnerability: a man-in-the-middle on the tarball cannot land a poisoned binary on the user's machine without also matching the published sha256 on github.com.

### Override hooks for tests

`WA_API` and `WA_DL` env vars override the GitHub endpoints; the goreleaser-emitted directory layout (`<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/<tag>/{tarball, checksums.txt}`) is reproduced under any local server. This is how all three tests above were run end-to-end against an actual binary.

### Stale-spec note

Spec line "Map to goreleaser-target naming" — confirmed: detect_platform emits `linux_amd64` etc., matching the wa-8gt.1 archive `name_template: 'wiki-audio_{{ .Version }}_{{ .Os }}_{{ .Arch }}'`. No drift between this script and the goreleaser config.

### Worktree workflow

`git worktree add ../wiki-audio-pane3-8gt3 -b pane3-wa-8gt.3 main`, ship in worktree, `--no-ff` merge, prune. Two pane-5 commits (`b15d89d`, `9847321` — wa-kyn.21 config test matrix) were on local main when I pushed; flowed up cleanly with my merge.

### Unblocks

The release trio is now complete. From a clean machine:

```
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jacob2017/wiki-audio/main/install.sh | bash
wiki-audio init
```

Practically blocks `wa-kyn.20` (cut v0.1.0) and `wa-i1l.14` (cut v1.0.0) only on the human running `git tag v0.1.0 && git push origin v0.1.0`.

title: Implement `wiki-audio --version` (ldflags-injected version)
description:
A package-level \`var Version = "dev"\` in main.go that goreleaser
overrides via -ldflags. \`wiki-audio --version\` prints the value.

## Why this matters

§6: \"Tool version mismatch with manifest schema — older tool refuses to
overwrite a newer-schema manifest.\" The version string is the input to
that check. Without ldflags, every binary says \"dev\" and the schema
guard is meaningless.
close_reason: Shipped in 2da3a53. internal/cli/{version,version_test}.go + root.go + root_test.go + .goreleaser.yaml — 222 net lines, 5 new tests. Three ldflags-injected globals (Version/Commit/BuildTime); VersionLine() formats per §3 'wiki-audio <V> (commit <C>, built <T>)'. runtime/debug VCS fallback populates Commit and BuildTime from vcs.{revision,time,modified} for plain go build inside a repo, with +modified suffix on dirty trees. goreleaser injects all three with v-prefix on Version per §3 contract. Manually verified: 'wiki-audio v0.3.1 (commit abc1234, built 2026-05-08T14:00:00Z)' renders correctly under ldflags.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## §3 sample output (polish pass 6) — pin --version format

`wiki-audio --version` should print a single line:

```
$ wiki-audio --version
wiki-audio v0.3.1 (commit abc1234, built 2026-05-08T14:00:00Z)
```

## Format contract

```
wiki-audio v<Version> (commit <ShortCommit>, built <BuildTime>)
```

Three ldflags-injected variables:

```go
var (
    Version    = "dev"          // -X main.Version=v0.3.1
    Commit     = "unknown"      // -X main.Commit=abc1234
    BuildTime  = "unknown"      // -X main.BuildTime=2026-05-08T14:00:00Z
)
```

For dev builds (no goreleaser):

```
$ ./wiki-audio --version
wiki-audio dev (commit unknown, built unknown)
```

…still exits 0; the schema-guard from §6 detects "dev" and refuses to
overwrite a manifest with `tool_version != "dev"`.

## --version vs version subcommand

`wiki-audio --version` is a flag on the root. `wiki-audio version` (no
flag) is NOT defined — Cobra would auto-add it but we suppress that to
keep the surface minimal. If the user runs `wiki-audio version`, Cobra
prints "unknown command" and exits 1. The flag is canonical.

title: Implement `wiki-audio upgrade` (re-run install.sh idempotently)
description:
Subcommand that just shells out to the install.sh URL with curl|bash.
Idempotent. After it runs, the new binary has overwritten the running
one's path; the user re-runs the next command from a fresh process.

## Why a subcommand exists for this (vs. \"just re-run curl\")

Discoverability — \`wiki-audio --help\` lists upgrade, so when a user
wonders how to update, they don't need to find the install URL again.

## Edge case

If the user installed to ~/.local/bin and is now running from
/usr/local/bin, the upgrade should target whichever path the running
binary lives at. Use os.Executable() to figure out the target dir.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## Sample output + path-detection detail (polish pass 6)

§3 only shows the install-script form (`curl ... | bash`); for the
`wiki-audio upgrade` subcommand, this bead's contract is:

```
$ wiki-audio upgrade
detected current binary: /usr/local/bin/wiki-audio
fetching latest release from https://github.com/Jacob2017/wiki-audio/releases/latest
running install.sh with INSTALL_DIR=/usr/local/bin …
detected: linux/amd64
fetching latest release: v0.3.2
downloaded wiki-audio_0.3.2_linux_amd64.tar.gz (12 MB)
verified sha256 ✓
installed: /usr/local/bin/wiki-audio
upgrade complete. (was v0.3.1 → now v0.3.2)
```

## os.Executable() handling

```go
exePath, err := os.Executable()
if err != nil {
    return fmt.Errorf("could not determine current binary path: %w", err)
}
exePath, _ = filepath.EvalSymlinks(exePath)  // resolve any /usr/local/bin → /opt/... symlink
installDir := filepath.Dir(exePath)
```

Pass `INSTALL_DIR=$installDir` as an env var when invoking install.sh
so it overwrites the SAME binary the user is currently running, not a
hardcoded `/usr/local/bin`.

If `installDir` is not writable by the current user, print a clear
message and exit 1 BEFORE downloading anything:

```
$ wiki-audio upgrade
detected current binary: /usr/local/bin/wiki-audio
error: /usr/local/bin is not writable; rerun with sudo or move the binary
```

## Why we use install.sh as a subprocess (not native Go)

install.sh already handles platform detection, sha256 verification, and
extraction; reimplementing that in Go duplicates the logic and creates
a second update path that can drift. The subprocess approach keeps
install.sh as the single source of truth for "how to install".

The cost: `wiki-audio upgrade` requires `bash` and `curl` to be in PATH.
Both are universal on the platforms we target (linux/macos amd64+arm64).

## Self-overwrite caveat

On Linux, you can overwrite a running binary file (the kernel keeps the
already-mapped pages). The next `wiki-audio` invocation runs the new
binary. This works without a stop-restart dance.

On Windows (not a v1 target), you can't overwrite a running .exe; we'd
need a rename-self-then-replace dance. Out of scope until §1 expands
support beyond linux/macos.

comments.author: pane-3
comments.text:
## Closing wa-8gt.5 — `wiki-audio upgrade` shipped (commit `204eb70`)

### What landed

`internal/cli/upgrade.go` (172 lines): replaces the stub. Fetches install.sh from `WIKI_AUDIO_INSTALL_URL` (default: raw.githubusercontent.com `main`), pipes through bash with `INSTALL_DIR=<dir of running exe>`, captures the post-install version. `install.sh` gains a backward-compatible `INSTALL_DIR` env override (15-line additive patch).

Sample run:

```
$ wiki-audio upgrade
detected current binary: /home/u/.local/bin/wiki-audio
current version:        0.3.1
fetching install.sh:    https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jacob2017/wiki-audio/main/install.sh
running install.sh with INSTALL_DIR=/home/u/.local/bin
install: detected: linux_amd64
install: ...
install: installed: /home/u/.local/bin/wiki-audio
upgrade complete. (was 0.3.1 → now 0.3.2)
```

### Design choices worth recording

- **`os.Executable()` + `filepath.EvalSymlinks`**, per the bead's polish-pass-6 comment. Resolves `/usr/local/bin → /opt/homebrew/...` style symlinks so the upgrade lands at the actual binary, not its symlink target. EvalSymlinks failure is non-fatal — keep the original path.
- **Pre-flight writability probe** via `os.CreateTemp` before downloading. Avoids "downloaded 12 MB → mv: permission denied" when the user installed to `/usr/local/bin` without `sudo`.
- **Probe over mode-bits check** because real perms involve uid/gid + ACLs + fs flags — `os.Stat(...).Mode().Perm() & 0o200` lies on NFS / ACL-controlled mounts.
- **install.sh stays the source of truth.** Reimplementing fetch + sha256-verify + extract in Go would create a second update path that drifts. The cost: `wiki-audio upgrade` requires `bash` + `curl` on PATH (universal on linux/macos targets).
- **Self-overwrite is safe.** Linux/macOS keep the running binary's already-mapped pages; the file on disk can be replaced. Spec confirms this; verified by inspection of how install.sh moves the new binary into place (no stop-restart dance).
- **Post-install version probe is best-effort.** A hung or missing `--version` after install doesn't make the upgrade itself look failed — the sha256 has already passed and the new binary is on disk. Three branches: `was X → now Y`, `was X → could not read new version`, `already at X; no version change`.

### `install.sh` change (additive)

`pick_install_dir` now respects `$INSTALL_DIR` first, falling back to the prior root → `/usr/local/bin` / non-root → `$HOME/.local/bin` precedence. Same shellcheck-clean hygiene as the parent script.

### Tests (7, all hermetic — no real network)

| Test | What it pins |
|---|---|
| `TestUpgrade_CheckWritableHappyPath` | t.TempDir is writable |
| `TestUpgrade_CheckWritableRejectsReadOnly` | chmod 0500 dir rejected |
| `TestUpgrade_CurrentBinaryPath` | test binary stat-able |
| `TestUpgrade_PipeInstall_RunsRemoteScript` | httptest-served stub install.sh writes marker file at INSTALL_DIR; env passthrough confirmed |
| `TestUpgrade_PipeInstall_BashNonzeroSurfaces` | stub `exit 7` surfaces as bash error |
| `TestUpgrade_PipeInstall_HTTPErrorSurfaces` | 404 surfaces as curl error (regression guard for the `f` in `-fsSL`) |
| `TestUpgrade_NewUpgradeCmd_HelpMentionsURL` | --url flag wired |

### Manual end-to-end smoke (artifact-level)

Generated goreleaser snapshot tarballs and ran `INSTALL_DIR=/tmp/wa-upgrade-custom-dir WA_DL=http://localhost:8770 bash install.sh v0.0.1-snapshot-...` — binary landed at the custom dir, `--version` matched. Validates the install.sh end of the upgrade pipeline against real artifacts.

### Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `go build ./...` | clean |
| `go vet ./...` | clean |
| `gofmt -d internal/cli/upgrade*.go` | empty |
| `shellcheck install.sh` | exit 0 |
| `go test ./...` | all packages pass |

### Worktree workflow

`git worktree add ../wiki-audio-pane3-8gt5 -b pane3-wa-8gt.5 main`, ship in worktree, `--no-ff` merge, prune. Race-clean. Phase C release surface is now: install (wa-8gt.3), goreleaser config (wa-8gt.1), CI workflow (wa-8gt.2), self-upgrade (this).

title: Cut v0.0.1 stub release (verifies distribution end-to-end)
description:
Tag \`v0.0.1\` and push. CI runs goreleaser, publishes the GitHub Release
with the four tarballs + checksums.

## Why a stub release before any real functionality

Derisks the entire distribution path while the only thing in the repo
is \"hello world\". If goreleaser misconfigures or install.sh has a
uname bug, find out now — not after we've spent days on the extractor.

## Phase C gate (§7)

Install script exits cleanly on a fresh shell:

  \`\`\`
  curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jacob2017/wiki-audio/main/install.sh | bash
  wiki-audio --version
  # → v0.0.1
  \`\`\`

If \`wiki-audio --version\` says anything other than v0.0.1, the ldflags
injection is broken — fix C4 before tagging the release.

## Acceptance criteria — post-tag verification

Done = ALL of the following observable AFTER `git push origin v0.0.1`:

1. `gh release view v0.0.1 --json assets -q '.assets[].name' | sort` lists exactly the four expected goreleaser tarballs (linux/amd64, linux/arm64, darwin/amd64, darwin/arm64) PLUS `checksums.txt`.
2. `gh release view v0.0.1 --json url -q .url` returns a non-404 URL; clicking it shows the release with auto-generated notes.
3. The CI job (`gh run list --workflow=release.yml --limit 1 --json conclusion -q .[0].conclusion`) returned "success".
4. `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jacob2017/wiki-audio/main/install.sh | bash` on a fresh shell:
   - Exits 0.
   - Installs to `/usr/local/bin/wiki-audio` (or `~/.local/bin/wiki-audio` if non-root).
   - `wiki-audio --version` prints exactly `wiki-audio v0.0.1 (commit <sha>, built <ts>)` per wa-8gt.4's format.
5. The downloaded tarball's sha256 matches `checksums.txt`.

If any of (1)-(5) fails: delete the tag (`git push --delete origin v0.0.1` and `git tag -d v0.0.1`), delete the release (`gh release delete v0.0.1 --yes`), fix the underlying bug, re-tag with the SAME version (it's a stub; no semver lossage).

comments.author: pane-3
comments.text:
## v0.0.1 release pipeline status

**Tag pushed:** `v0.0.1` (annotated, sha `dcba098`).
**CI run:** [25581929889](https://github.com/Jacob2017/wiki-audio/actions/runs/25581929889) — `goreleaser release --clean` job, all steps green.
**Release URL:** https://github.com/Jacob2017/wiki-audio/releases/tag/v0.0.1

### Acceptance matrix

| # | Criterion | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5 expected assets present (4 tarballs + checksums.txt) | ✅ |
| 2 | `gh release view v0.0.1 --json url` non-404 | ✅ |
| 3 | `gh run list ... -q .[0].conclusion` returns `success` | ✅ |
| 4a | `wiki-audio --version` prints `wiki-audio v0.0.1 (commit <sha>, built <ts>)` | ✅ — `wiki-audio v0.0.1 (commit 9e7f4a7, built 2026-05-08T22:08:48Z)` (matches the regex `^wiki-audio v0\.0\.1 \(commit [0-9a-f]{7}, built [0-9T:Z+\-\.]+\)$` exactly) |
| 4b | Anonymous `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/.../install.sh \| bash` succeeds | ❌ — **blocked on repo visibility, see below** |
| 5 | Tarball sha256 matches `checksums.txt` | ✅ — `sha256sum -c checksums.txt` reports `OK` for all 4 tarballs |

### Visibility blocker (criterion 4b)

`Jacob2017/wiki-audio` is **private** (per the wa-jlb.1 decision: "publish enclosure URLs that contain the access token … privacy keeps the project boring"). Anonymous reads of `raw.githubusercontent.com/...` and `api.github.com/.../releases/...` return 404 without authentication. So the literal `curl | bash` one-liner from a fresh, unauthenticated shell cannot work today, regardless of how the install.sh is written.

What I verified instead, against the same artifacts:

```
$ gh release download v0.0.1 --repo Jacob2017/wiki-audio
$ sha256sum -c checksums.txt
wiki-audio_0.0.1_darwin_amd64.tar.gz: OK
wiki-audio_0.0.1_darwin_arm64.tar.gz: OK
wiki-audio_0.0.1_linux_amd64.tar.gz: OK
wiki-audio_0.0.1_linux_arm64.tar.gz: OK

$ tar -xzOf wiki-audio_0.0.1_linux_amd64.tar.gz wiki-audio > wa
$ chmod +x wa && ./wa --version
wiki-audio v0.0.1 (commit 9e7f4a7, built 2026-05-08T22:08:48Z)
```

Plus: ran the actual `install.sh` (fetched via `gh api .../contents/install.sh` for auth) against a local mirror of the release artifacts on `localhost:8780` with `WA_DL` override:

```
install: detected: linux_amd64
install: version:  v0.0.1
install: tarball:  wiki-audio_0.0.1_linux_amd64.tar.gz
install: fetching tarball...
install: fetching checksums...
install: verifying SHA-256...
install: extracting...
install: installed: /tmp/wa-001-install-final/.local/bin/wiki-audio

$ /tmp/wa-001-install-final/.local/bin/wiki-audio --version
wiki-audio v0.0.1 (commit 9e7f4a7, built 2026-05-08T22:08:48Z)
```

So **the pipeline itself is correct**. install.sh fetches, sha256-verifies, extracts, installs into the target dir, and the binary runs with the expected version line. The outstanding gap is purely about whether anonymous internet traffic can reach the install.sh source and tarball URLs.

### Decision needed

Three coherent paths, in declining ergonomics-fidelity to §3:

1. **Flip the repo public.** Most aligned with §3 ("`curl ... | bash` ... works on any Linux/macOS box"). Requires re-confirming wa-jlb.1's privacy rationale — the source itself isn't sensitive, but any historical `.env` leak would matter (gitleaks pre-commit hook wa-76r.5 mitigates going forward; would also want a one-time history scan).
2. **Token-aware install.sh.** Add `Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN` headers to the curl calls, with a doc note that users must export `GITHUB_TOKEN` before running. This sacrifices the "one shell command" property — users now need a PAT first.
3. **Keep private; ship `wiki-audio upgrade` and `gh release download` as the install paths.** The curl|bash line in §3 becomes documentation aspirational rather than a tested gate.

I am not closing wa-8gt.6 because criterion 4b is not green. Holding for operator direction.

### Side effect: tag + release stay in place

The v0.0.1 artifacts are correct (5/5 assets, sha256 verified, --version matches). Deleting + re-tagging won't help any of the three paths above; the visibility decision is the actual fix. Leaving the tag in place so wa-8gt.5 (`wiki-audio upgrade`) has a real prior version to compare against in any future test run.

comments.author: pane-3
comments.text:
# Pre-public-flip security audit — Jacob2017/wiki-audio

**Scope:** all 59 commits across all 7 branches + 1 tag (v0.0.1), the live remote, the released binary tarballs, and the CI logs from the v0.0.1 run.

**Method:** direct literal-string scan (`git log -S<value>`) for each of the six known secrets, plus pattern scans for known token shapes, Cloudflare account IDs, the Worker URL host, and any `?t=<token>` URL with embedded value. Released binaries verified via `strings`.

## Verdict

**Zero leakage of any secret value in any commit.** The repo is safe to flip public *after* one operator decision (rotate-or-not the access token) and one optional scrub-or-not pass on a personal handle exposed in 38 hostname references.

## What was scanned (six secrets, by name)

| Secret | Length | Prefix | Found in any commit diff? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` | 51 | `sk_7…` | **No** |
| `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` | 53 | `cfut…` | **No** |
| `R2_TOKEN` | 53 | `cfut…` | **No** |
| `R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID` | 32 | `87d5…` | **No** |
| `R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | 64 | `b796…` | **No** |
| `WIKI_AUDIO_ACCESS_TOKEN` | 43 | `rkOC…` | **No** |

Method: `git log --all -S "$value"` for each, which inspects every diff (added or removed lines) across every reachable commit. Empty output for all six.

## What was also scanned (no hits)

- `.env` files: never appeared as a tracked file in any commit. `.gitignore` correctly excludes `.env`, `.env.*`, and `*.mp3`.
- Cloudflare account ID (32-hex): never appeared in any commit.
- `?t=<43+ char base64url>`: zero occurrences in any historical diff. The only `?t=…` strings are placeholders (`?t=garbage`, `?t=abc123`, `?t=secret`, `?t=$WIKI_AUDIO_ACCESS_TOKEN`) and the `?t=<token>` doc literal.
- Third-party token shapes (AWS AKIA, GitHub PAT `ghp_`/`github_pat_`, Stripe `sk_live_`, OpenAI `sk-`, Slack `xoxb`): zero matches.
- Released binaries (all 4 platforms in v0.0.1): `strings`-grepped for each of the six secret values — zero embeds. The only `workers.dev` string compiled into the binary is `wiki-audio.example.workers.dev` (the placeholder written by `init.go` into a fresh user's `~/.wiki-audio/config.toml`).
- Branch topology: all 7 `pane3-*` branches are ancestors of `main` (merged via `--no-ff`). No orphan ref carries an alternate history.
- CI logs from run [25581929889](https://github.com/Jacob2017/wiki-audio/actions/runs/25581929889): `GITHUB_TOKEN` consistently shown as `***` (GitHub auto-redaction working). No other secret name appears in the log.
- `.goreleaser.yaml` and `.github/workflows/release.yml`: no PAT, no static credentials. Only `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN`, which is auto-provisioned per run and never persisted.

## What IS in the repo (cataloged, not a secret per §9 threat model)

The host `wiki-audio.jabyrne.workers.dev` appears **38 times** across 8 files. The §9 threat model explicitly accepts that someone who already knows the operator and guesses the domain might find the URL — the security guarantee is the constant-time-checked 256-bit token, not URL secrecy. So these references are NOT secrets. But they *do* expose the personal handle `jabyrne` to any public reader, which is worth being deliberate about before flipping the repo public.

| File | Count | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `.beads/issues.jsonl` | 19 | bead descriptions, runbooks, acceptance curls |
| `PLAN_FOR_AUDIO_LIBRARY.md` | 6 | design doc, doctor sample output, RSS enclosure example |
| `internal/cli/root_test.go` | 5 | `RedactURL` test cases |
| `internal/config/loader_test.go` | 2 | TOML loader fixture |
| `internal/config/validation_test.go` | 3 | URL validation tests |
| `internal/model/types.go` | 1 | comment with example BaseURL |
| `test/integration/worker_integration_test.go` | 1 | `defaultWorkerURL` constant (overridable via `WIKI_AUDIO_WORKER_URL`) |
| `worker/wrangler.jsonc` | 1 | comment about the `workers_dev` decision |

Note: `internal/cli/init.go` already uses `wiki-audio.example.workers.dev` as the placeholder when scaffolding a fresh user's config. The real URL only ever sits in the operator's own `~/.wiki-audio/config.toml`, never in committed code — that part is already clean.

## Recommendations

In priority order. None of these are blockers for the visibility flip per se; they are layered defenses.

### 1. Required: confirm or rotate the access token before flipping public

The 43-char `WIKI_AUDIO_ACCESS_TOKEN` has been carried in this session's environment, in `gh run watch` output, in `wrangler` debug logs at `~/.config/.wrangler/logs/`, and the test fixtures referenced it as a `$variable`. The audit confirms it never landed in a commit. But the token has been *handled* in this work session.

If any uncertainty about prior exposure (chat logs, screenshots, paste-into-other-tools), rotate via the wa-76r.4 runbook **before** flipping the repo public:

```
cd worker && wrangler secret put ACCESS_TOKEN  # paste new value
# update ~/.wiki-audio/.env
# update 1Password
# wiki-audio publish --feed-only  # republish feed with new token
# re-paste new feed URL into Pocket Casts
```

After rotation, even if every one of the 38 hostname references stays, an attacker who scrapes the repo cannot construct a valid request.

### 2. Optional, low-effort: scrub the personal handle from runtime code

5 files, 10 LoC of edits, zero functional change:

- `internal/model/types.go` — change comment example to `…example.workers.dev`.
- `internal/cli/root_test.go` (5 refs) — `RedactURL` tests work the same with any host.
- `internal/config/loader_test.go` (2) and `validation_test.go` (3) — same.
- `test/integration/worker_integration_test.go` (1) — change `defaultWorkerURL` to a placeholder; the integration test already requires `WIKI_AUDIO_RUN_INTEGRATION=1` and respects `WIKI_AUDIO_WORKER_URL` override, so a real run still hits the real host via env.

After this pass, the operator's Cloudflare username is not visible from any code that runs in CI or ships in a binary. The hostname only lives in the operator's local config.

### 3. Optional, judgment call: scrub or leave docs

| File | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| `PLAN_FOR_AUDIO_LIBRARY.md` (6 refs) | **Scrub.** Replace with `<your-account>.workers.dev`. Retains design fidelity; no operator handle visible. |
| `worker/wrangler.jsonc` (1 ref, in a comment) | **Scrub.** Same reason. |
| `.beads/issues.jsonl` (19 refs) | **Leave.** This is operational history; references include the actual acceptance-curl invocations against the live host. Scrubbing rewrites archaeology. Either accept the exposure or stop publishing the beads file entirely (it's already pure data; the source-of-truth is in `bv`). |

### 4. Defensive going forward

- **Install gitleaks pre-commit.** Bead **wa-76r.5** is open and unblocked. Catches the next time someone (any pane) tries to commit a credential-shaped string.
- **GitHub secret scanning** flips on automatically when the repo becomes public. Free belt-and-suspenders.
- **Audit the workers.dev account dashboard** for unintended public surfaces (custom domains, dev URL toggle on the bucket) per the wa-3ia.4 yearly verification.

## What I did NOT do (out of audit scope)

- Did not rotate the token unilaterally — operator decision.
- Did not edit any file — this is a read-only audit.
- Did not check operator's local 1Password / chat history / browser history — out of repo scope.
- Did not check whether the operator's GitHub account itself is private (separate question; the org/user `Jacob2017` exists publicly already as the prospective install URL `Jacob2017/wiki-audio`).

## tl;dr

```
secrets in commits: 0
secrets in binaries: 0
secrets in CI logs: 0 (GitHub auto-redacted)
.env in any commit: never (gitignored)

worker URL `wiki-audio.jabyrne.workers.dev` referenced 38× — not a secret
per §9, but exposes the personal handle. Optional scrub: 5 files, 10 LoC.

decision before public flip:
  - rotate WIKI_AUDIO_ACCESS_TOKEN if any uncertainty about prior exposure
  - decide on the handle-scrub
```
