title: [HIGH] tts: output_format goes in query string, not JSON body — wire-level bug
description:
## Defect

`internal/tts/client.go::Synthesize` (lines 101-109) marshals `output_format` into the request JSON body:

```go
reqBody, err := json.Marshal(struct {
    Text         string `json:"text"`
    ModelID      string `json:"model_id"`
    OutputFormat string `json:"output_format"`
}{
    Text:         text,
    ModelID:      c.modelID,
    OutputFormat: c.outputFormat,
})
```

**The ElevenLabs TTS API expects `output_format` as a QUERY STRING parameter**, not as a JSON body field. The endpoint is documented as:

```
POST /v1/text-to-speech/{voice_id}?output_format=mp3_44100_192
```

When `output_format` lands in the body, ElevenLabs silently ignores it and serves the default (128 kbps for flash_v2_5). The body field is silently dropped.

## Empirical confirmation

wa-7t6 re-spike (commit 3314013, run 2026-05-09T07:54:52Z):

- Code default: `mp3_44100_192`
- Config trace shows `output_format=mp3_44100_192` in the marshaled body
- Generated MP3 (`/home/ubuntu/.cache/wiki-audio/out/how-to-do-great-work.mp3`):
  ```
  $ ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=bit_rate ...
  codec_name=mp3
  sample_rate=44100
  channels=1
  bit_rate=128000           <-- WRONG, should be 192000
  format_name=mp3
  duration=3672.502857
  size=58760676
  ```

The 128 kbps result is consistent with ElevenLabs serving the default — it's the same bitrate the original 64-kbps-requested run produced. The user reported "64-kbps-requested served as 128 kbps" pre-wa-7t6, which is exactly what the API does when `output_format` is dropped.

## Fix

In `client.go::Synthesize`:

```go
endpoint := apiBaseURL + "/v1/text-to-speech/" + url.PathEscape(c.voiceID)
q := url.Values{}
q.Set("output_format", c.outputFormat)
endpoint += "?" + q.Encode()

reqBody, err := json.Marshal(struct {
    Text    string `json:"text"`
    ModelID string `json:"model_id"`
}{
    Text:    text,
    ModelID: c.modelID,
})
```

ElevenLabs also accepts `voice_settings` in the body (stability, similarity_boost) — currently unused by us; can stay-out for now.

## Severity rationale: HIGH

- Every real synth call uses the wrong bitrate. The user's voice-quality A/B (which drove wa-7t6) was conducted on a 128 kbps stream they hand-fetched at 192; the production binary cannot produce 192 even with the config bumped.
- Phase G bulk run will produce 53 essays at 128 kbps unless this is fixed first. ~$87 in synth credits + ~600 MB of suboptimal-quality storage that's later thrown away.
- wa-7t6's acceptance criteria #4 (ffprobe bit_rate=192000) fails until this lands.

## Test additions needed

`internal/tts/client_test.go::TestClientSynthesizeHappyPath` already inspects the request — add an assertion that `r.URL.Query().Get("output_format")` equals the configured value, and that the JSON body does NOT contain an `output_format` key.

## Cross-references

- Surfaced by wa-7t6 spike (re-rendering essay how-to-do-great-work post-bitrate-bump).
- Original spike (wa-4cw.8) probably hit this too but the test was a 64-kbps-requested run; the apparent "served 128" was actually the EL default, indistinguishable from a hypothetical "honored 64 served 64".
close_reason: Shipped in fee6807. internal/tts/client.go::Synthesize now emits output_format as a query parameter (?output_format=<value>) instead of a JSON body field. Test pin in TestClientSynthesizeHappyPath: assert query value matches model.DefaultOutputFormat AND body decoded as map[string]any has no 'output_format' key. Loose map decode rather than struct so a regression that re-adds the body field actually fails (struct decode would silently swallow). Tests green. Re-spike at the wire follows under wa-7t6.

title: [HIGH] id3: TestTagIdempotentByteIdentical is flaky — bogem serializes frames in random map order
description:
## Defect

`internal/id3/tagger_test.go::TestTagIdempotentByteIdentical` (added in fb7a123, wa-4cw.4) **fails ~45% of fresh runs** because `bogem/id3v2/v2` serializes frame headers in random map iteration order. The test asserts byte-identical files across two consecutive Tag(meta) calls — an invariant bogem cannot satisfy.

## Reproduction

20-trial loop on this machine produced 11 fails / 9 passes:

```text
trial 0: equal
trial 1: diff at offset 11    [a] TALB→TYER…    [b] TYER→TCON…
trial 2: equal
trial 3: diff at offset 11    [a] TIT2→TPE1…    [b] TYER→TCON…
…
trial 19: diff at offset 11   [a] TALB→TYER…    [b] TIT2→TPE1…
```

The differing bytes always fall at the start of the frame-header region (offset ~11, just past the ID3 header). The body bytes ("Same", "2023", etc.) are deterministic — only the order in which TIT2 / TPE1 / TALB / TYER / TCON appear varies. Sizes match every trial (1164 vs 1164).

## Why this slipped by

Pane-5's commit message claimed "9/9 passing" — likely lucky on the run that was committed. The bead-closure check did not loop the test enough trials to catch the ~45% flake rate. `go test ./...` in this session has been hiding the failure under a stale build cache (the `(cached)` line). `go clean -testcache && for i in 1..5; do go test ./internal/id3/ -count=1; done` reproduces 3-4 fails out of 5.

## Why HIGH

- bead wa-4cw.4 was closed claiming this test passes; reopening / followup is required to keep the audit trail honest.
- CI on a fresh runner will hit the flake within a few PRs.
- The flake will mask real regressions (re-runs become routine).

## Suggested fix

Relax the test from "byte-identical" to "frame round-trip identical + size delta == 0". The actual invariants the bead cares about are:

1. All 5 frame VALUES survive a re-tag (already covered by TestTagWritesAllFrames + TestTagReplacesExistingFrames).
2. Re-tag does not append duplicate frames (already covered by TestTagReplacesExistingFrames's `delta < ±16 bytes` assertion).

`TestTagIdempotentByteIdentical` overlaps with #2 but adds the byte-equality requirement, which bogem can't honor. Replace its body with: read back both tags, assert each Title()/Artist()/Album()/Year()/Genre() round-trips, and assert the file sizes are equal. That keeps the bead's "audio_data_unchanged" semantics without depending on map iteration order.

Alternative if byte-equality is genuinely required (e.g. for content-addressed storage): switch to a deterministic ID3 writer (write frames in a fixed lexical order). bogem doesn't expose this — would require either a fork or a thin wrapper that serializes via Write() with explicit frame ordering.

## References

- Code: `internal/id3/tagger_test.go:158-185` (the failing test)
- Library: `github.com/bogem/id3v2/v2` — `Tag.frames` is a `map[string]frame.Framer`; serialization in `Save()` iterates the map.
- Reviewed at fb7a123 (committed); test currently green only by luck.
- Repro: `go clean -testcache && for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do go test ./internal/id3/ -count=1 -run TestTagIdempotentByteIdentical; done`
close_reason: Shipped in 63a5f69. Renamed TestTagIdempotentByteIdentical → TestTagIdempotentSemantic and rewrote per orchestrator's Option A: parse frames via bogem reader and assert frame-by-frame value equality + audio payload byte-equality + no-new-frame-keys, instead of byte-identical file comparison. Byte-identity was unattainable with bogem (random map iteration order on serialization); semantic identity is what id3 readers actually check. Frame-appending regression still caught by adjacent TestTagReplacesExistingFrames (size delta within ±16 bytes). Verified 20/20 green via go test -count=20.

title: Phase G — Bulk run all 53 essays
description:
# Phase G — Build + publish across the whole PG corpus

Implements: PLAN_FOR_AUDIO_LIBRARY.md §7 Phase G.

## Goal

`wiki-audio build && wiki-audio publish` against every essay under
`raw/processed/paul-graham/` (53 files as of 2026-05-08). Spot-listen
3–5 random essays end-to-end on the phone to catch issues that
wouldn't have shown up in the Phase E single-essay spike.

## Cost expectations

§1, §8.4: ~880,344 characters total, ~440,172 credits at Flash v2.5
rate (0.5 credits/char). Fits within Pro tier monthly quota — no
overage. ~18h47m total audio, ~612 MB on disk.

If the pre-flight cost estimate from `wiki-audio build --dry-run`
exceeds 500k credits, STOP and investigate before calling the API.
A regression in the extractor (e.g. accidentally including the
Metadata block) is the most likely cause.

## What to verify in spot-listening

- No mid-sentence chunk boundaries that produced audible artifacts
- Footnote attribution lines up with the paragraph they belong to
- ID3 metadata renders correctly in Pocket Casts (title, artist, date)
- No essay regenerated unnecessarily (manifest hash logic working)

## Gate

Zero malformed extractions; total cost within estimate; all 53 episodes
appear in the Pocket Casts inbox.

## Operational realism (pass 9)

Concrete numbers for Phase G — verify reality stays within bands or react.

### Bulk run wall-clock estimate

- 880,344 chars / ~3,500 chars per chunk ≈ 252 chunks (essays serial,
  chunks within an essay also serial in v1 — see wa-4cw.5 'Concurrency').
- Flash v2.5 latency: ~150 ms TTFB + stream rate. A 4,000-char chunk
  takes ~30 s wall-clock end-to-end (TTS time-to-final-byte).
- Mean chunk size ~3,500 chars → mean chunk wall time ~26 s.
- Concat (50 ms acrossfade pairwise) adds ~1-2 s per essay.
- ID3 tag pass adds <1 s per essay.

Expected serial wall-clock: 252 × 26 s = 6,552 s ≈ 109 min.
- Low band (best case, no retries):    90 min
- Expected (light retry on 1-2 chunks): 110 min
- High band (rate-limit pressure):     150 min

If wall clock exceeds 150 min, investigate live (see wa-cfn.2's monitoring).
If under 90 min, suspect chunks aren't really hitting the API (cache hit).

### Credit consumption

- 880,344 chars × 0.5 credits/char = 440,172 credits (deterministic).
- Pro tier grants 500,000 credits/month — fits with ~60k credits headroom.
- Headroom covers: Phase E spike (~25k credits for one essay), retry
  burn (each retry on a 4k-char chunk costs 2,000 credits — generous
  10-retry budget = 20k credits), and a few re-runs if extractor
  regression discovered late.

### Disk footprint during the run

- Output MP3s: 612 MB in ~/.cache/wiki-audio/out/ (64 kbps mono, ~30 KB/min × 18h47m).
- Per-chunk tmp MP3s: 252 × ~150 KB ≈ 38 MB total in tmp/, but only
  one essay's worth (~14 chunks, ~2 MB) is alive at any moment because
  the concat step deletes them.
- Peak disk during a single essay: ~600 MB out/ (cumulative) + 12 MB
  tmp/<slug>/ (in-flight) + 50 MB final-essay file → round to **~700 MB peak**.
- The wiki box has tens of GB free; non-issue.

### Network footprint

- TTS download: 880,344 chars × ~30 bytes/char in MP3 = ~26 MB
  (the audio bytes returned from ElevenLabs over the run).
- R2 upload: 612 MB MP3 + ~50 KB manifest snapshots × 53 = ~3 MB
  overhead. Total ~615 MB upload.
- At 50 Mbps residential upload: 615 MB × 8 / 50 Mbps ≈ 100 s.
- At 1 Gbps: ~5-10 s.

### Total Phase G wall-clock from kickoff to feed-live

| Step                           | Est time |
|--------------------------------|----------|
| wa-cfn.1 dry-run preflight     | 30-60 s  |
| wa-cfn.2 bulk synthesis        | 90-150 min |
| wa-cfn.3 publish (R2 + RSS)    | 2-15 min (depends on uplink) |
| wa-cfn.4 spot-listen           | 30-60 min (5 essays × 5-12 min sampled, plus full play of 1) |
| wa-cfn.5 + wa-cfn.6 audits     | 10 min   |
| **Total active time**          | **~2.5-4.5 h** |

### Correction (vs prior text)

Replaced 'hours of wall-clock time' (in wa-cfn.2) and '~600 MB total'
(was approximate) with the explicit numbers above. The 18h47m audio
figure is consistent with ~13,544 s raw speech × ~5 prosody/pause
inflation, but most of that is silence-free; final concatenated
duration matches §1's claim and is preserved as-is.

title: Run `wiki-audio build --dry-run` cost preflight on all 53 essays
description:
Before spending real credits, dry-run estimate against the full corpus:

- Expected total: ~880,344 cleaned chars, ~440,172 credits at flash_v2_5.
- If estimate >500k credits: STOP. Investigate. Most likely cause is an
  extractor regression that re-included Metadata/FullDocument blocks.
- If estimate <300k credits: STOP. Likely the extractor is dropping
  prose unexpectedly.

§7 Phase G gate: pre-flight cost matches expectations within ±15%.

## Acceptance criteria

Done = a single `wiki-audio build --dry-run` invocation in the wiki source dir whose output:
1. Reports total billable credits between 374k and 506k (440k ± 15%).
2. Reports a fits-in-Pro verdict (per wa-kyn.14's plan-fit message taxonomy).
3. Output saved to `~/.cache/wiki-audio/dry-run-bulk-YYYY-MM-DD.txt` for cross-check against wa-cfn.6's actual numbers.

If credit estimate is outside the 374k-506k band, STOP per the existing in-bead instructions (extractor regression suspected). Do NOT proceed to wa-cfn.2.

## Operational realism (pass 9)

Verify the dry-run preflight numbers are computed and reported with the
right granularity. The existing 374k-506k credit band is correct
(440k ± 15%); below is the rest of the realism profile.

### What the preflight should report (concrete)

The output saved to `~/.cache/wiki-audio/dry-run-bulk-YYYY-MM-DD.txt`
should include AT LEAST:

| Field                        | Expected value (53 essays) |
|------------------------------|----------------------------|
| total_essays                 | 53                         |
| total_chars                  | ~880,344 (band 748k-1012k after ±15%) |
| total_credits                | ~440,172 (band 374,146-506,198) |
| total_chunks                 | ~252 (band 220-290 — depends on chunker boundary luck) |
| pro_quota                    | 500,000                    |
| fits_in_pro                  | true                       |
| projected_wall_clock_minutes | 90-150                     |
| projected_audio_minutes      | ~1,127 (≈18h47m)           |
| dollar_cost_pro              | $99.00                    |
| dollar_cost_payg_equivalent  | ~$73.36 (440k credits at $5/30k = $73 — informational) |

### Why Pro is still the right choice despite PAYG looking cheaper

PAYG cost for the bulk run: 440,172 credits × ($5/30,000 credits)
= ~$73.36. Less than $99. BUT PAYG retail rate has rate-limit
constraints + no monthly safety margin for re-runs. Pro buys:

- 60k credits headroom for retries / re-runs without another top-up.
- Higher rate-limit ceiling (faster wall-clock).
- Single $99 invoice instead of multiple top-up receipts.

Net: Pro is +$25 for materially less stress. Worth it for one month.

### Drift watch

- If `total_chars` exceeds 1,012k → STOP, extractor regression suspected
  (Metadata or FullDocument block leaked through).
- If `total_chars` below 748k → STOP, extractor over-stripping.
- If `total_chunks` outside 220-290 → not a stop, but log on wa-cfn.6
  (chunker behavior changed).

title: Run `wiki-audio build` (bulk synthesis, all 53 essays)
description:
Run the full bulk synthesis. Expect ~hours of wall-clock time depending
on ElevenLabs latency + retries.

## What to watch

- Resumability: if it crashes or you Ctrl-C, the next run picks up
  where it left off (manifest is saved per-essay).
- Cost: monitor remaining ElevenLabs credits in the dashboard. If we're
  burning faster than expected, abort and investigate.
- Disk: ~600 MB of MP3 in ~/.cache/wiki-audio/out/. Wiki box has
  plenty of disk; verify before starting.

## When this is done

All 53 essays have ManifestEntry rows with non-empty body_hash and a
file_size_bytes value. \`~/.cache/wiki-audio/out/\` has 53 *.mp3 files.

## Operational realism (pass 9)

### Wall-clock estimate (replaces 'hours' hand-wave)

- 880,344 chars / ~3,500 chars per chunk ≈ 252 chunks.
- Per-chunk wall time at Flash v2.5: ~26 s mean (150 ms TTFB + stream).
- Serial run, no retries: 252 × 26 s ≈ 109 min.
- Bands: low 90 min / expected 110 min / high 150 min (with ~5%
  retry rate). If you hit > 180 min, abort and investigate (see below).
- Concat + ID3 add ~2 min total across the 53 essays — noise vs TTS time.

### Real-time monitoring during the run

In a second tmux pane, tail `~/.cache/wiki-audio/build.log`
(stdout-tee) and watch for:

| Signal                                          | Threshold                  | Action |
|-------------------------------------------------|----------------------------|--------|
| ElevenLabs credit balance (poll dashboard)      | < 50,000 remaining         | Pause; investigate retry storm. |
| Chunk wall time                                 | > 90 s consistently        | Abort; ElevenLabs degraded. |
| 429 retry events                                | > 20 across the run        | Pause 5 min, resume. |
| 5xx events                                      | > 5 across the run         | Same. |
| anomalies.txt entries                           | > 5 (short-chunk warnings) | Tag for spot-listen. |
| Disk free on wiki box (`df ~/.cache`)         | < 2 GB                     | Abort; clean tmp/ first. |

### Disk footprint (concrete)

- Steady-state during run: out/ grows from 0 to ~612 MB linearly.
- tmp/<slug>/ is short-lived: deleted after concat. Typical residency
  10-20 MB at any moment for the in-flight essay.
- Peak: ~700 MB combined (612 MB out + ~50 MB current essay tmp + 50 MB
  partial final essay file).
- The wiki box has tens of GB free. `df -h ~/.cache` should always
  show > 5 GB free during the run; investigate if not.

### Credit consumption rate

- 440,172 credits / ~110 min = ~4,000 credits/min mean rate.
- If the dashboard shows you burning > 6,000 credits/min for >10 min,
  there's likely a retry storm — check build.log for 429/5xx.
- If burning < 2,500 credits/min for >10 min, chunks may be undersized
  (chunker regression) or the API is throttling — investigate.

title: Run `wiki-audio publish` (bulk upload + RSS regen)
description:
Push everything from G2 to R2:

- 53 MP3 uploads (~600 MB total).
- pg.manifest.json with all entries populated.
- pg.xml with 53 <item>s.

Verify: feed loads in browser via the token URL; episode count = 53;
at least one episode is downloadable through the worker.

## Acceptance criteria

Done = `wiki-audio publish` exit 0 on the wiki box AND:
1. `mc ls r2/wiki-audio/pg/ | wc -l` returns 53 (or current essay count).
2. `curl -fsSL 'https://wiki-audio.jabyrne.workers.dev/pg.xml?t=$WIKI_AUDIO_ACCESS_TOKEN' | xmllint --xpath 'count(//item)' -` returns the same 53.
3. Pick any one episode's enclosure URL from the feed; `curl -fsSL -o /tmp/test.mp3 '<url>?t=...'` succeeds and `ffprobe -v error /tmp/test.mp3` is clean (zero output).
4. `pg.manifest.json` in R2 contains 53 ManifestEntry rows with non-empty `body_hash` AND non-empty `r2_etag`.

Verifiable artifact: a single command output summary file saved to `~/.cache/wiki-audio/bulk-publish-YYYY-MM-DD.txt` containing the four numbers above.

## Operational realism (pass 9)

### Upload wall-clock estimate

- Bytes to upload: 612 MB MP3 + 1 manifest snapshot (~50 KB) +
  1 RSS XML (~25 KB at 53 items) ≈ 612 MB total.
- Object count: 53 MP3s + 1 manifest + 1 pg.xml = 55 PutObjects.
- Per-object request overhead at R2: ~100-200 ms TLS handshake + headers.

| Uplink              | Bytes-time | Per-object overhead | Total |
|---------------------|------------|---------------------|-------|
| 50 Mbps residential | 612 MB × 8 / 50 Mbps = 98 s | 55 × 150 ms = 8 s | ~106 s ≈ **2 min** |
| 200 Mbps cable      | 25 s       | 8 s                 | ~33 s   |
| 1 Gbps fiber        | 5 s        | 8 s                 | ~13 s   |
| 100 Mbps office     | 49 s       | 8 s                 | ~57 s   |

Bands: low 13 s (gigabit) / expected 30-60 s (typical home/office) /
high 2-3 min (slow residential). If publish takes > 5 min on a known-
good link, suspect retries — check log for 5xx/429 from R2.

### What 'eventually consistent' means here

R2 is strongly consistent for read-after-write on the same key, so the
manifest+pg.xml upload after the MP3 uploads doesn't need a settle delay.
But Cloudflare's edge cache CAN serve a stale pg.xml for up to the
worker's cache TTL (currently 0 — no edge cache; verify in wa-3ia.2).
The first `curl` of pg.xml after publish should always show 53 items.

### R2 cost on R2 side (free-tier-affordable)

- Storage: 612 MB × $0.015/GB/mo = ~$0.0092/month. Under $0.01.
- Egress: $0 (R2's whole point).
- Class A operations (PutObject): 55 per publish run. Free tier covers
  1M/mo. Negligible.
- Class B operations (GetObject): one per episode listen + one per feed
  poll. At 53 episodes × 1 listen each + 4 polls/day = ~75/day max.
  Free tier covers 10M/mo. Negligible.

title: Spot-listen 3-5 random essays end-to-end on phone
description:
Pick 3-5 essays at random (NOT just the easy ones — include short and
long, technical and discursive). Listen end-to-end on phone.

Acceptance:
- No mid-sentence chunk boundary artifacts.
- Footnote attribution lines up with the right paragraphs.
- ID3 tags display correctly in Pocket Casts (title, artist, date).
- No essay regenerated unnecessarily compared to the spike (i.e., if
  re-running build doesn't change body_hashes, the manifest logic is
  sound).

## Why this gate matters

The Phase E spike validates ONE essay. The bulk run might expose
issues that only appear under variety: an unusual code-block syntax,
an essay with no footnotes at all, a very short essay, etc.

## Failure mode handling

If an essay fails validation, mark it in a follow-up cross-cutting bead
(\"extractor regression in <slug>\") and decide whether to fix-and-rerun
or accept-and-move-on.

## Acceptance criteria

Done = 3-5 essays selected by the procedure below, each listened to end-to-end on the phone (Pocket Casts, real speaker / earbud), and no blocker discovered.

Selection procedure (deterministic — no "I'll listen to my favorites"):
1. From the 53-essay manifest, pick: shortest essay, longest essay, an essay with NO footnotes (rare; if none, pick fewest), an essay with the MOST code-block skipped segments, and one chosen at random via `shuf`. That's 5.
2. If two categories collapse onto one essay (e.g. shortest = no-footnotes), pick a second random one to backfill.

Pass criteria PER ESSAY:
- [ ] No mid-sentence chunk-boundary artifacts (same gate as wa-4cw.9 but applied to bulk variety).
- [ ] Footnote attribution lands on the correct paragraph — listen to one footnote in particular and confirm context.
- [ ] ID3 tags display correctly in Pocket Casts (same four-field check as wa-4cw.10).
- [ ] No mid-essay silence > 5s, no truncation.

PASS overall = all five essays pass all four checks.

Verifiable artifact: a checklist saved to `~/.cache/wiki-audio/spot-listen-YYYY-MM-DD.md` with one row per essay and per-criterion ticks.

## Fail path

- Single-essay regression (e.g. one essay has bad chunk seam) → open follow-up bead "extractor or concat regression in <slug>". Decide:
  - Re-run that ONE essay's build (deletes its body_hash, forces resynth). Cost: <10 credits. Cheap. Default action.
  - Or: accept and skip — only if the regression is cosmetic (not blocker for listening).
- Cross-essay regression (3+ essays have the same issue) → STOP. The bulk run output is suspect. Open a P0 bead. Do not move to Phase H. Investigate at the extractor / concat / id3 layer.
- Manifest re-run check: re-running `wiki-audio build` after spot-listen passes should produce zero new TTS calls (everything cached). If TTS calls happen, body_hash logic is broken — that's a P0 even if audio sounds fine.

title: Verify zero malformed extractions (regression detector)
description:
After G2, sanity-check the manifest:

- For each essay, char_count vs raw markdown size: cleaned should be
  60-95% of raw bytes (Metadata/Full Document headers + footnote moves
  account for some shrink). Anything <40% or >100% is suspicious.
- Total cost (G2 actual) vs G1 dry-run estimate: within ±10%.
- skipped.txt: should be empty or near-empty. Anything in it is a
  regression we missed in Phase D.

## Why a separate verification bead

§6 \"Extractor regression\" detector runs in dry-run mode against the
PREVIOUS manifest. After the first bulk run we have no previous —
this bead is the first chance to detect outliers in absolute terms.

## Source-of-truth for the >50%-drop check (added by polish pass 2)

The §6 "Extractor regression" row says "char_count drops >50% from
previous manifest entry". The previous manifest is the one fetched
from R2 at the start of the build run (wa-4cw.5 step 2). Concrete
contract:

- **First run ever** (no manifest in R2): the comparison is SKIPPED.
  Every essay is a new entry, so by definition no regression. Log
  "first build — extractor regression check skipped" once.
- **Subsequent runs**: for each essay with a body_hash mismatch,
  compare the NEW CharCount to the PREVIOUS manifest entry's
  CharCount. If new < 0.5 * previous, ABORT the build with a
  diagnostic that includes both numbers and the slug.
- **--force-regression**: a CLI flag (separate bead may be needed)
  that downgrades the abort to a warning. For the rare case of a
  legitimate large content removal.
- **New essays (no previous entry)**: no comparison; treated as
  first-time builds.

This bead (wa-cfn.5) is the post-bulk audit checking absolute ratios
of cleaned/raw bytes and skipped.txt content. The dry-run regression
detector (wa-kyn.14) is the *active* defense at build time.

title: Track total cost vs estimate, log surprises
description:
Record actual ElevenLabs credit consumption from G2. Compare to G1
estimate. Note anomalies in a project memory or comment on this bead.

Also: confirm the Pro plan covered the run without overage charges. If
overage hit, it changes Phase H plans (might need Pro for a second
month, or switch tiers).

## Acceptance criteria

Done = ALL:

1. The actual credit count consumed by wa-cfn.2 is captured to `~/.cache/wiki-audio/bulk-run-YYYY-MM-DD.txt` with these lines minimum:
   - `pre_run_credits: <N>` (from `wiki-audio doctor` before bulk).
   - `post_run_credits: <N>` (from `wiki-audio doctor` after bulk).
   - `actual_consumed: <delta>`.
   - `dry_run_estimate: <from wa-cfn.1>`.
   - `delta_pct: <(actual - estimate) / estimate * 100>`.
2. `abs(delta_pct) <= 15` per the §7 Phase G gate. Larger deltas mean the dry-run estimator is mis-calibrated; open a follow-up bead but Phase G still passes if everything else worked.
3. Pro plan covered the run with no overage line item on the next ElevenLabs invoice. If overage hit, note the dollar amount on this bead and decide before Phase H whether to extend Pro for another month.

Verifiable artifacts: the bulk-run log file + the next-billing-cycle invoice PDF (saved or screenshot).

## Operational realism (pass 9)

### What 'in range' means (concrete)

The §7 Phase G gate says "actual cost within ±15% of estimate". Spelled
out:

- Estimate from wa-cfn.1: 440,172 credits (or whatever G1 actually
  reported — not the literal expectation).
- Actual from G2: `actual_consumed` = pre_run_credits - post_run_credits.
- Pass band: `abs((actual - estimate) / estimate) <= 0.15`.
- For the literal expected estimate of 440,172, the pass band is
  **374,146 ≤ actual ≤ 506,198 credits**.
- Within band → Phase G passes; log delta_pct on this bead.
- Outside band BUT < 500,000 (still in Pro) → Phase G passes; open a
  follow-up bead for the dry-run estimator (it's mis-calibrated).
  Don't block Phase H.
- Outside band AND > 500,000 → overage hit; check next invoice for
  the $ amount of overage (Pro overage is ~$0.0002/credit at retail).
  Note on this bead. Decide before Phase H whether to extend Pro
  another month.

### Overage cost math

- Overage: ~25% of monthly quota at retail rate.
- 500,000 base + ~125,000 overage allowance = 625,000 effective ceiling.
- Each overage credit: ~$0.000166 ($5/30,000) at PAYG retail.
- 100,000 credits over (~22% over plan) = ~$16.60. Tolerable surprise.
- > 200k credits over → real money, investigate before next run.

title: build_pipeline: skip TTS for chunks that already exist on disk
description:
Surfaced by wa-4cw.8 spike failure. Currently `internal/cli/build_pipeline.go::synthesizeChunkWithRetry` does NOT check for an existing `<NNN>.mp3` before calling tts.Client.Synthesize. A naive build retry re-synthesizes every chunk, even if byte-stable chunks already exist from a prior partial-failed run. For the 18-chunk how-to-do-great-work essay that's ~33.5k credits (~$5-7) wasted per retry.

## Why this matters

Three real-world failure modes that produce partial chunks:
1. ffmpeg concat timeout (wa-4cw.13's bug) — chunks intact, concat fails.
2. ID3 tagging fails on the final concat — chunks + concat intact.
3. Operator hits Ctrl-C mid-build — chunks intact through last completed.

In all three, the existing chunks on disk are reusable. The build pipeline should treat them as a write-through cache.

## Fix

In `internal/cli/build_pipeline.go::synthesizeChunkWithRetry`, before calling `client.Synthesize`:

```go
chunkPath := cache.TmpDir(slug) + fmt.Sprintf("/%03d.mp3", idx)
if info, err := os.Stat(chunkPath); err == nil && info.Size() > 0 {
    slog.Info("chunk cache hit, skipping synth", "chunk_idx", idx, "path", chunkPath)
    return nil  // chunk is already on disk; no API call needed
}
```

(Adjust to match the actual cache helpers — `cache.TmpDir(slug)` may have different shape after wa-4cw.6's helpers landed.)

## Acceptance criteria

1. Unit test in build_pipeline_test.go that:
   - Creates 5 fake `<NNN>.mp3` files in the tmp dir.
   - Runs the pipeline against an essay that would chunk into 5 chunks.
   - Asserts that tts.Client.Synthesize was NEVER called (use a stub client that fails the test on call).
2. The skip is logged at INFO level so operators can tell from build logs which chunks were cache hits.
3. The skip honors size>0 (zero-byte file is treated as missing — defends against partial writes).

## Coordination

Lives in `internal/cli/build_pipeline.go` — pane-2's wa-4cw.5 territory. Reserve before editing. Coordinate with whoever's currently in flight on adjacent build_pipeline work.

## Why P1

- Without this, every wa-4cw.8 retry burns $5-7.
- Phase G bulk run (wa-cfn.2) is 53 essays. A single mid-bulk failure with naive retry could cost $50+ instead of $0.
- The fix is ~10 LoC + a test.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
[pane-2] Chunk cache-skip landed in `synthesizeChunkWithRetry`.

## Fix

Top of `internal/cli/build_pipeline.go::synthesizeChunkWithRetry`:

```go
if info, err := os.Stat(outPath); err == nil && info.Size() > 0 {
    logger.Info("chunk cache hit, skipping synth",
        "path", outPath, "bytes", info.Size())
    return nil
}
```

Path is the same `filepath.Join(cache.TmpDir(slug), fmt.Sprintf("%03d.mp3", i))` that the producer side already writes to. The size>0 check is the load-bearing guard: a zero-byte file is "crashed mid-write or never wrote anything" and we re-synthesize. `atomic.WriteAtomic` (the producer) only renames a fully-written tmp onto outPath, so any non-empty file at outPath was definitionally fully written by a prior successful Synthesize call.

## Tests (4 new, all passing in 0.016s)

| name | covers |
|------|--------|
| TestSynthesizeChunkWithRetry_CacheHitSkipsAPI | single chunk, pre-populated, fail-on-call httptest server. 0 API calls; cached bytes preserved verbatim. |
| TestSynthesizeChunkWithRetry_CacheHitFiveChunks | the bead's stated acceptance — pre-create 5 `<NNN>.mp3` files matching the build_pipeline naming convention, run synth 5x, assert 0 API calls across all 5. |
| TestSynthesizeChunkWithRetry_ZeroByteFileTreatedAsMissing | pre-create a zero-byte file, assert API IS called and result is written. Defends against partial-write crash leaving a touched-but-empty file. |
| TestSynthesizeChunkWithRetry_MissingFileSynthesizes | negative control — no file at outPath, API IS called, bytes are written. |

The fail-on-call pattern uses `httptest.NewServer` with a handler that calls `t.Errorf` immediately — the test fails with a clear "API was called when chunk cache hit was expected" message naming the chunk index. Adapted from the existing `TestSynthesizeChunkWithRetry_HonorsServerHint` shape for stylistic consistency.

## Acceptance criteria from the bead

- (1) Unit test pre-creates 5 fake MP3s, runs the synth path 5x, asserts NO API calls. ✓ (TestSynthesizeChunkWithRetry_CacheHitFiveChunks)
- (2) Skip is logged at INFO with path + bytes. ✓ (`slog.Info("chunk cache hit, skipping synth", ...)`)
- (3) Size>0 honored — zero-byte file treated as missing. ✓ (TestSynthesizeChunkWithRetry_ZeroByteFileTreatedAsMissing)

## Verification

- `go test ./internal/cli/...` → ok 1.259s (all wa-cfx tests pass; existing pipeline tests including the retry suite still pass)
- `go test ./...` → all 14 packages green
- `go vet ./...` → clean
- `go build ./...` → clean

## Coordination

- Reservations on `internal/cli/build_pipeline.go` and `internal/cli/build_pipeline_test.go` released after commit.
- Did NOT touch `internal/concat/`, `internal/tts/`, `internal/extract/`, `internal/chunk/`, `internal/id3/` per dispatch.
- The fix composes cleanly with pane-3's Path A recovery work — Path A re-runs the build pipeline; this commit makes the re-run no-cost when chunks survive the failure.
- After this lands, **chunks are a write-through cache**: any partial-failure recovery (concat timeout, ID3 fail, Ctrl-C) re-runs build for free.

## Cost ceiling

For wa-4cw.8's 18-chunk how-to-do-great-work essay: pre-fix retry cost was ~$5-7 (33.5k credits). Post-fix retry cost is $0 (the chunks survived). For wa-cfn.2's 53-essay bulk run, a single mid-bulk failure with naive retry could have cost $50+; post-fix it costs $0.

title: concat: replace acrossfade pairwise reduce with stream-copy demuxer (lossless, no generation loss)
description:
## Defect — surfaced by user listening test on wa-4cw.8 spike output

User reported the full concatenated `how-to-do-great-work.mp3` (18 chunks via current concat path) is "very distorted and unclear." A single chunk played in isolation (chunk 000.mp3, no concat) sounded "noticeably better." Same TTS settings (eleven_flash_v2_5, mp3_44100_64), same voice. Therefore the degradation is in the concat path, not the TTS path.

## Root cause — pairwise MP3 generation loss

`internal/concat/concat.go::acrossfadeStep` (line 155) runs ffmpeg's `acrossfade` filter, which is NOT a stream-copy operation. Every pairwise call:

1. Decodes `left` MP3 → PCM
2. Decodes `right` MP3 → PCM
3. Applies acrossfade filter (50ms cross-fade by default)
4. **Re-encodes the combined PCM → MP3** at the default ffmpeg MP3 encoder settings

For an 18-chunk essay, the pairwise reduce performs 17 sequential decode+re-encode cycles on the cumulative left-side. The original chunk 0 is re-encoded **17 times** before reaching the final output. At 64 kbps mono, MP3 generation loss compounds dramatically — high-frequency content degrades, transients smear, sibilants distort.

The 50ms acrossfade is cosmetic (mask chunk-boundary clicks) but its cost is N-fold generation loss across the whole essay.

## Fix — ffmpeg concat demuxer with stream copy

ffmpeg's `concat` demuxer (NOT to be confused with the `concat` filter or `concat:` protocol) joins MP3 chunks losslessly via stream copy. Single-shot, no pairwise reduce, zero re-encoding.

Implementation:

```go
// 1. Write a concat list file:
//    file '/abs/path/000.mp3'
//    file '/abs/path/001.mp3'
//    ...
listPath := filepath.Join(tmpDir, "concat-list.txt")
var lines []string
for _, in := range inputs {
    abs, _ := filepath.Abs(in)
    lines = append(lines, fmt.Sprintf("file '%s'", abs))
}
os.WriteFile(listPath, []byte(strings.Join(lines, "\n")), 0o644)

// 2. Single ffmpeg call: -f concat -safe 0 -i list -c copy out
args := []string{
    "-y",
    "-f", "concat", "-safe", "0",
    "-i", listPath,
    "-c", "copy",
    outPath,
}
runFFmpeg(ctx, opts, args)
```

Properties:
- Wall time: <30s for 18 chunks (vs ~5 min for pairwise reduce).
- Quality: bit-exact frames preserved end-to-end. ZERO generation loss.
- No PerStepTimeout needed (single invocation; existing context timeout suffices).
- intermediate `step_NNN.mp3` files no longer produced (and not needed; concat-list is the only intermediate).

## Acceptance criteria

1. New concat path uses ffmpeg concat demuxer + `-c copy`.
2. The 18-chunk regression test (concat_18chunk_test.go) still passes; ideally add a frame-count assertion: output frame count == sum(input frame counts) within ±1 frame (concat demuxer can occasionally drop a single LAME tag frame).
3. Re-run the wa-4cw.8 spike on the existing chunks at `~/.cache/wiki-audio/tmp/how-to-do-great-work/`. Operator listens to the new MP3 and confirms quality is acceptable. (Use the wa-cfx chunk-cache-skip, so this re-run costs $0 in TTS credits.)
4. The 50ms acrossfade behavior is gone. Document this — if chunk-boundary clicks become audible in some essays, address with a follow-up bead (insert tiny silence files via lavfi anullsrc, still no re-encode).
5. `internal/concat/doc.go` updated to reflect the new approach. The old "pairwise reduce" rationale is now stale.

## Why P1

- Phase E spike (wa-4cw.8) is currently failing the operator voice-quality gate (wa-4cw.9). Without this fix, Phase E never gates green and Phase F (and everything downstream — Phase G bulk run, Phase H operationalize) stays blocked.
- The fix is small (~30 LoC delta) and isolated to internal/concat/.

## Coordination

- Pane-3 owns internal/concat/. They already shipped wa-50g (timeout fix) — natural follow-up.
- Reserve `internal/concat/**` strictly.
- The existing 18 chunks at `~/.cache/wiki-audio/tmp/how-to-do-great-work/` are byte-stable; the wa-cfx chunk-cache-skip means re-running build skips synth. Validate by running `wiki-audio build --slug how-to-do-great-work` after the fix lands and confirming zero TTS calls in logs.

comments.author: pane-3
comments.text:
## wa-fse closed — concat-demuxer + stream copy shipped (commit `5c3fb58`)

Replaces the acrossfade pairwise reduce with a single ffmpeg `concat` demuxer + `-c copy` invocation. ZERO MP3 generation loss across N chunks.

### What landed

`internal/concat/`:
- `concat.go` — single-call demuxer + pre-flight `os.Stat` + `-xerror` defense. `PerStepTimeout` renamed to `Timeout`; `DefaultPerStepTimeout` → `DefaultTimeout` (5m kept as the value).
- `doc.go` — full re-write of the package rationale: pairwise→demuxer, why the 50ms acrossfade is intentionally gone, when to insert silence files instead of bringing acrossfade back.
- `concat_test.go` — 10 tests, several rewritten because the old assertions (acrossfade duration math, step_NNN.mp3 cleanup) no longer apply. New `TestMissingInput_FailsFastBeforeFFmpeg` covers the pre-flight defense.
- `concat_18chunk_test.go` — `TestDefaultTimeout_HasReasonableValue` band lowered to `[1m, 30m]` (stream copy is single-digit seconds for any plausible essay); `TestEighteenChunks_RunsToCompletion` adds an exact-sum duration assertion (±1.0s for LAME info-tag variance).

`cmd/wa-recover-concat/` — deleted (its reason for existing was the now-fixed acrossfade timeout failure).

### Defense-in-depth on missing inputs

Surfaced while writing tests: ffmpeg 7.1.1's concat demuxer silently exits 0 on a missing-input file (logs "Impossible to open" to stderr but produces a partial output). Even `-xerror` does not propagate the demux error to the exit code on this build. Two-layer defense:

1. **Pre-flight `os.Stat`** on every input before invoking ffmpeg. Surfaces the exact missing path with index in actionable wording (`concat: input 1 not readable: ...`).
2. **`-xerror` flag** for any other demux error class ffmpeg DOES escalate (corrupt frames, codec mismatches, future ffmpeg version shifts).

Together: a missing chunk on disk fails fast with a clear error instead of leaking a half-essay MP3 into the publish pipeline.

### Verification matrix

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `go vet ./internal/concat/` | clean |
| `gofmt -d` | empty |
| `go test ./internal/concat/` | 12/12 pass in ~13s |
| `go test -count=20 ./internal/concat/` | **20/20 green** in ~265s |

### End-to-end validation against the wa-4cw.8 spike chunks

`wiki-audio build --slug how-to-do-great-work` re-run with the 18 preserved synth chunks (wa-cfx cache-skip):

```
18/18 chunks: cache hit, NO TTS calls (0 credits)
1 ffmpeg concat call
wall: 3 seconds
out: ~/.cache/wiki-audio/out/how-to-do-great-work.mp3
     58,629,016 bytes (~56 MB)
     duration 3,664.27s (~61.07 min — same audio length as wa-4cw.8 recovery)
     bitrate ~128 kbit/s (vs old 64 kbit/s — source-preserving; the old re-encode flattened the rate)
```

Wall time is ~115× faster than the previous acrossfade pairwise reduce (3s vs 5m45s).

### R2 upload

```
wrangler r2 object put wiki-audio/pg/how-to-do-great-work.mp3 \
  --file=~/.cache/wiki-audio/out/how-to-do-great-work.mp3 \
  --content-type=audio/mpeg --remote
→ Upload complete.
```

Worker HEAD: `200`, `content-type: audio/mpeg`, `cache-control: private`, `etag: "8a1b0a16bee0f17a21abb224ab2cb856"`. Bare URL (no token) still `403`. Local file SHA256 matches the bytes the Worker serves.

**Operator URL for re-listening:** `https://wiki-audio.jabyrne.workers.dev/pg/how-to-do-great-work.mp3?t=$WIKI_AUDIO_ACCESS_TOKEN`

### Side observation worth a follow-up bead

Discovered while verifying the upload byte-match: the Worker source at `worker/src/index.ts` does NOT propagate the incoming `Range` header to `env.BUCKET.get(key)`, so partial-content requests fall through to a full-object fetch. Podcast apps issue Range requests for resume support and large-file efficiency; the current Worker silently returns the whole MP3 every time. Worth a separate bead under wa-3ia or Phase F. Not in scope here; not blocking the listening gate.

### Operator action remaining

Re-listen to the URL above. If the audio quality is acceptable, close **wa-4cw.9** (voice acceptance gate). If still distorted, surface the diagnosis — the structural fix above eliminates the only known generation-loss path, so any remaining distortion would be in the synth chunks themselves (worth a separate investigation; not a concat issue).

title: wiki-audio: PG essays → personal podcast feed
description:
# Master epic — wiki-audio

## What we are building

A standalone Go CLI named `wiki-audio` that turns the 53 Paul Graham essays
already sitting in the wiki (`raw/processed/paul-graham/`) into a personal
podcast feed listenable in Pocket Casts on the phone. Two commands once
installed:

- `wiki-audio build`  — extract markdown → clean text → ElevenLabs TTS → MP3
- `wiki-audio publish` — diff R2, upload new MP3s, regenerate `pg.xml`

## Why this exists

The essays are read at the desk on a different device than the phone. Long
prose is ideal listening material (gym, walks, commutes), but copy/pasting
into a TTS app one essay at a time is friction. Podcast apps already solve
"long-form audio queue with resume across devices" better than any
roll-your-own option. R2 + RSS is the cheapest delivery (no egress fees)
with no server to maintain.

## Architectural pillars (do not relitigate without strong cause)

1. **Separate GitHub repo** `Jacob2017/wiki-audio` — distinct from the wiki
   data repo. Tool's release cadence stays independent of wiki content.
   The wiki repo stays data-only.
2. **Go binary distributed via curl|bash** — single static binary,
   cross-compiled by goreleaser, fetched from GitHub Releases by an
   `install.sh` that does `uname` + sha256 verify. Matches the install
   ergonomics of beads_rust.
3. **R2 bucket is fully private**; access is gated by a Cloudflare Worker
   that validates `?t=<token>` with a constant-time compare. No public dev
   URL, no public bucket, no presigned URLs (they expire and break apps
   that cache feed XML).
4. **Manifest in R2** (`pg.manifest.json`) — wiki box is stateless. The
   body hash includes voice_id + model_id + footnote_policy_version so
   any of those changing automatically invalidates every essay.
5. **ElevenLabs Flash v2.5** for v1, voice "Christopher". Pro tier for one
   month (~$99) covers the bulk run; switch to PAYG afterwards (~$0.50/new
   essay).

## Target outcome

A feed URL `https://wiki-audio.jabyrne.workers.dev/pg.xml?t=<token>` that
Pocket Casts can subscribe to. New episode appears within minutes of
running `wiki-audio build && wiki-audio publish` after dropping a new
essay into the wiki's PG folder.

## Out of scope for v1

- Insight/analysis pages (separate authoring vector)
- Other authors
- The `audio: true` opt-in frontmatter flag (deferred to v2 — see Phase I)

## Plan reference

See PLAN_FOR_AUDIO_LIBRARY.md §1 (executive summary) for the full scoping
document. Every phase epic below cites the section it implements.

## TTS engine alternatives considered (§8.1 — locked-in for v1)

Pillar 5 picks ElevenLabs Flash v2.5. Why not the other options:

- **OpenAI tts-1 / tts-1-hd** (~$13–$26 for the corpus): cheaper but voice
  quality is flatter. Voice quality is the entire reason for paying
  anything at all — saving $80 to listen to 19 hours of less-natural
  speech is a bad trade for the user (chose ElevenLabs deliberately).
- **Google Neural2 / Azure Neural** (~$14): quality comparable to OpenAI,
  no quality win, and adds GCP/Azure billing setup that none of the rest
  of this stack requires. Skip.
- **Kokoro (local, free)**: surprisingly good but has a slight robotic
  edge that compounds over hours of listening. Skip for v1; revisit if
  the 2026 generation closes the gap. Local also forces a GPU on the
  build host or much slower CPU-only inference.
- **Piper (local, free)**: fine for short clips, fatiguing over hours.
  Skip.
- **ElevenLabs Multilingual v2** (~$198–$330 for the corpus): best-in-class
  quality but 2x credits/char. Reserve for a per-page voice override on
  the ~10 most-relistened essays in v2 (Phase I.4); not the v1 default.

Voice model within ElevenLabs (§8.4) — chose `eleven_flash_v2_5` over
`eleven_turbo_v2_5` (slightly less expressive at the same price) and
`eleven_monolingual_v1` (older, costs 2x). See wa-4cw.1.

## Hosting alternatives considered (§8.2 — locked-in for v1)

Pillar 3 picks Cloudflare R2. Why not the other options:

- **AWS S3 + RSS**: same UX as R2 but charges egress per listen. A
  podcast feed's whole point is repeated downloads on different devices;
  egress fees scale with listening. Avoid.
- **Backblaze B2 + RSS** (with Cloudflare in front for free egress):
  technically equivalent cost/UX to R2. Picked R2 because the Cloudflare
  Worker token gate (Phase A) is on the same platform. No layering.
- **Audiobookshelf self-hosted**: dedicated audiobook UI, but needs a
  VPS + reverse proxy + auth. Overkill for a one-author feed; revisit if
  the library grows past ~500 hours.
- **Syncthing folder → phone**: zero infra but loses queueing /
  streaming / resume — the entire reason podcasts apps win. Only use
  if R2 is unavailable.
- **Plex / Jellyfin**: heavy infrastructure for a 50-essay feed.

## Implementation language alternatives (§8.5 — see wa-jlb)

Pillar 2 picks Go. Detailed Python / Rust / Node trade-offs live in
wa-jlb so they're next to the scaffold work. Don't relitigate without
strong cause.

## Privacy threat model (§9 — kept on master so future-me doesn't quietly weaken privacy)

**Acceptable risk.** Someone who already knows me and can guess a domain
might find the feed. The feed and episodes carry personal-use TTS audio
of third-party copyrighted essays.

**Unacceptable risk.** The feed appears in Cloudflare's public dev URL
listings, gets indexed by search engines, or is enumerable from R2
bucket listings. Pillar 3 above (Worker + private R2 + token gate) is
the mitigation. See wa-3ia for the architecture and wa-3ia.5 for the
contract test.

## What the plan does NOT defend against (§9.4 — read this BEFORE proposing OAuth)

Listed here so a future contributor considering "privacy improvements"
sees the threat-model boundaries first:

- **You sharing the feed URL.** Anyone with the token can listen until
  rotation. Mitigation: rotate (wa-76r.4); don't paste it publicly.
- **Cloudflare itself.** Cloudflare can read the bucket. Acceptable for
  personal-use TTS of public essays; NOT acceptable for genuinely
  sensitive material. If the threat model ever changes, this whole
  architecture must be re-examined — don't bolt on encryption.
- **Targeted attacker who has compromised your laptop.** Out of scope.
  If they have the .env they have the token, the ElevenLabs API key,
  and the wiki source. Defended elsewhere (full-disk encryption, etc.),
  not by this tool.
- **Pocket Casts logging.** Pocket Casts servers see enclosure URLs
  (token included) when they download episodes on the user's behalf.
  Acceptable risk; if not acceptable, switch to a strictly-local
  podcast app like Doughnut or AntennaPod that fetches directly from
  the device. Token rotation also invalidates anything PC has cached.

Each of these is an EXPLICIT acceptance, not an oversight. Anyone
proposing an upgrade (OAuth, signed URLs, Cloudflare Access, end-to-end
encryption) should first explain why one of the four bullets above has
moved from "acceptable" to "unacceptable" — otherwise the upgrade trades
real podcast-app compatibility for theater. See §9.3 alternatives table
embedded on wa-3ia and the rotation runbook on wa-76r.4.

## Operational realism (pass 9) — top-line cost & timing summary

This bead's pillar #5 says 'Pro for one month (\~$99) covers the bulk
run; switch to PAYG afterwards (\~$0.50/new essay)'. Concrete back-up:

### One-shot bulk cost

- 880,344 chars × 0.5 credits/char = 440,172 credits.
- Pro plan: $99/mo for 500,000 credits → 60k headroom.
- PAYG-equivalent for the bulk run: 440k × ($5/30k) = ~$73.36 — but
  Pro buys higher rate-limits and re-run safety, see wa-4cw.7.

### Per-new-essay cost (steady state, post-Pro)

- Average PG essay: ~16,610 chars (corpus mean; ranges from ~3k for
  short reflections up to ~52k for 'How to Do Great Work').
- Credits: 16,610 × 0.5 = 8,305 credits per essay.
- PAYG: 8,305 credits × ($5/30,000 credits) = **$1.38 per
  average-length essay**, NOT $0.50.
- Original $0.50 figure was for a SHORT essay (~3,000 chars × 0.5 ÷
  30,000 × $5 = $0.25). Range across the corpus is **$0.25 - $8.66**.
- Annual incremental cost: ~10 new essays/year × $1.38 mean = ~$14/yr.
  Still trivial vs Pro retainer ($1,188/yr).

### Correction

Pillar #5's '\~$0.50/new essay' is an underestimate for typical PG
essays. Updated numbers above. Decision (Pro for bulk, PAYG for steady
state) is unchanged — the corrected $1.38/essay still makes PAYG
clearly the right choice post-bulk. Sub-beads wa-lz9.1 and wa-4cw.7
have the calendar timing.

### Storage & egress (R2)

- Steady state: 612 MB stored × $0.015/GB/mo = **$0.0092/mo** (under 1¢).
- Egress: $0 forever (R2's defining feature; whole reason for choosing
  it over S3 — see §8.2 in PLAN_FOR_AUDIO_LIBRARY.md).
- Worker requests: ~2/day from Pocket Casts polling. Free tier covers
  100k/day. Negligible until forever.

### Total annual TCO post-launch

| Line item                      | Annual cost |
|--------------------------------|-------------|
| ElevenLabs PAYG (~10 new essays/yr) | ~$14    |
| Cloudflare R2 storage          | ~$0.12 ($0.01/mo × 12) |
| Cloudflare Worker              | $0 (free tier) |
| Domain (existing)              | $0 (reused) |
| **Total**                      | **~$14/yr** |

Plus the one-time ~$99 ElevenLabs Pro month for the bulk run.
