title: [REVIEW] Phase F publish path spec analysis
description:
# [REVIEW] Phase F publish path spec analysis

Bounded review by pane-8 (Phase F lead, wait-state) of PLAN_FOR_AUDIO_LIBRARY.md §3 / §5.5 / §6 / §7 Phase F / §9.1 plus all `wa-i1l.*` and `wa-76r.*` beads. Findings only.

## [HIGH] Partial-publish recovery contradicts the write order the publish command is supposed to enforce

**Where**: PLAN §6 row `R2 upload failure`; wa-i1l.4 "Partial-publish recovery"; wa-i1l.7 steps 3-5 + "Atomicity caveat".

wa-i1l.4 says that if 7 of 10 MP3 uploads succeed before a fatal error, those 7 manifest entries end up with `R2Key` set and the next `publish` only retries the remaining 3. wa-i1l.7 says the command order is MP3s first, then manifest, then feed, specifically so the feed never points at missing audio. Those two promises do not fit together unless the manifest is persisted incrementally during the MP3 loop or on failure. As written, the spec simultaneously promises a single manifest write near the end **and** persisted partial-success state on failure.

**Why it matters**: this is the load-bearing recovery contract for retries. Implementers cannot tell whether the next run should rely on persisted `R2Key` state or should simply rediscover already-uploaded objects via HEAD/ETag.

**Fix**: pick one contract explicitly.
- Option A: persist `pg.manifest.json` after each successful upload (feed still last).
- Option B: keep manifest write strictly final and accept that recovery is diff-based, not manifest-state-based.

## [HIGH] Feed generation has no rule for unpublished / degraded manifest entries

**Where**: PLAN §5.5 "Per `ManifestEntry`, emit"; ManifestEntry optional fields in §2; PLAN §6 `R2Key=""` failure row; wa-i1l.4 failure semantics; wa-i1l.8 `publish --feed-only`.

The spec says the feed emits one `<item>` per `ManifestEntry`, but the manifest model explicitly allows entries with empty `R2Key`, empty `R2ETag`, and nil `PublishedAt` while publish is incomplete or has failed. `publish --feed-only` regenerates `pg.xml` from the existing manifest without touching audio. There is no explicit filter rule for which entries are eligible to appear in RSS.

**Why it matters**: a token-rotation or metadata-only republish can produce broken feed items unless the generator is told to skip entries that are not fully published.

**Fix**: define the eligibility gate for RSS items. At minimum: emit only entries with non-empty `R2Key`, non-zero `FileSizeBytes`, non-zero `DurationSeconds`, and non-nil `PublishedAt`.

## [HIGH] Manifest `.bak` fallback is guarded for `--prune`, but not for `publish` / `--feed-only`

**Where**: wa-i1l.2 load-with-bak fallback; wa-i1l.10 explicit `--prune` refusal when the primary manifest is corrupt or `.bak` fallback was used; wa-i1l.7 and wa-i1l.8 lack the same write-path guard.

The spec already recognizes that a degraded manifest source is unsafe for destructive operations: `--prune` must refuse if load failed or if `.bak` was used. But the two write paths that regenerate public artifacts (`publish` and `publish --feed-only`) do not say what happens when `Load()` falls back to `.bak`.

**Why it matters**: a stale-but-valid `.bak` could be used to overwrite the current `pg.xml` or even the current manifest, dropping recently published episodes from the feed during a routine token rotation.

**Fix**: make the degraded-manifest rule uniform across all write paths. If `Load()` used `.bak`, only read-only commands may proceed; `publish`, `--feed-only`, and manifest save must refuse until the manifest is healed.

## [MEDIUM] Token rotation is downtime by construction, but the spec never states whether that downtime is acceptable

**Where**: PLAN §6 access-token-leak row; PLAN §9.1 rotation bullet; wa-76r.4 steps 2-6; wa-3ia "one-touch operation" wording.

The current runbook invalidates the old token at Worker step 2, republishes the feed later, and only then has the user unsubscribe/re-subscribe in Pocket Casts. That means there is no rotate-without-downtime path: old feed URLs 403 immediately, cached enclosure URLs 403 immediately, and any app reading the feed during the cutover has undefined behavior. The spec says this happens, but never says whether it is an accepted outage or a bug to design around.

**Why it matters**: the implementation cannot know whether to support dual-token grace, old-URL grace, or explicit hard cutover.

**Fix**: decide and say it plainly.
- If downtime is acceptable for v1, document the exact blast radius: old feed URL dead immediately, queued downloads may fail, re-subscribe required.
- If downtime is not acceptable, the Worker needs a two-token grace window during rotation.

## [MEDIUM] RSS schema guidance contradicts itself on channel-level `itunes:summary`

**Where**: wa-i1l.11 acceptance criteria; wa-i1l.12 fail path; wa-i1l.5 channel skeleton.

wa-i1l.11 says warnings for missing channel-level `itunes:summary` are acceptable if omitted deliberately. wa-i1l.12 says that a feed validating cleanly but showing zero episodes in Pocket Casts is "likely" caused by missing channel-level `itunes:author` or `itunes:summary`. Those two instructions point in opposite directions: either `itunes:summary` is optional for v1, or it is important enough that its absence is a primary troubleshooting hypothesis.

**Fix**: choose one contract. My recommendation: emit `itunes:summary` in v1, add it to wa-i1l.5's channel skeleton, and pin it in wa-i1l.15 tests so validator success and Pocket Casts success are aligned.

## [MEDIUM] Enclosure and self-link URL composition rules are underspecified

**Where**: PLAN §3 sample URLs; PLAN §5.5 sample enclosure; wa-i1l.5 channel skeleton; wa-i1l.6 token stamping.

The spec shows URLs composed as `{BaseURL}/{FeedPath}?t={token}` and `{BaseURL}/pg/<slug>.mp3?t={token}`, but it never defines:
- whether `FeedConfig.BaseURL` may end with `/`
- whether `FeedPath` may begin with `/`
- whether `BaseURL` may already contain a query string
- whether slugs must be path-escaped before becoming object keys / enclosure paths

**Why it matters**: string-concatenation here can easily yield `//pg.xml`, malformed `?t=`/`&t=` handling, or unescaped enclosure URLs.

**Fix**: require URL construction via `net/url`, normalize slashes, and state that slugs used in RSS paths must already be URL-safe or must be path-escaped at emission time.

## [MEDIUM] Retry safety and change detection are conflated in the ETag story

**Where**: wa-i1l.3 "A new upload of the same MP3 produces the same ETag"; wa-i1l.4 "PutObject is idempotent ... same ETag, no-op effect"; wa-i1l.18 multipart test coverage.

There are two separate claims mixed together:
1. retries are safe because overwriting the same object key is atomic, and
2. same-body re-uploads are a stable identity check because ETag stays the same.

(1) is the important operational property. (2) is much shakier once multipart upload behavior or uploader version changes enter the picture. The current text treats ETag as both a retry-safety guarantee and a stable content fingerprint.

**Fix**: split the contract.
- For retries: say repeated `PutObject` to the same key is safe because the object store exposes whole-object replacement.
- For change detection: either explicitly accept occasional spurious re-uploads from ETag drift, or pin a content hash separate from ETag.

— pane-8

comments.author: pane-3
comments.text:
# pane-3 — additional Phase F findings (complementary to the 7 pane-8 surfaced)

Fresh-eyes review across §2 (model), §3 (CLI surface), §5.4-5.5 (R2 + RSS), §6 (error handling), §7 Phase F, §9.1 (token), and the wa-i1l.* implementer beads. These are the gaps I found that pane-8's 7 didn't cover — pane-8's review remains the source of truth for everything they surfaced; this is purely additive.

## [CRITICAL] No mutual-exclusion model for concurrent `wiki-audio publish` invocations

**Where**: §6 has no row for concurrency; wa-i1l.7 step sequence (load → diff → upload → feed → upload) has no exclusion primitive; wa-i1l.2 manifest save uses naive `.bak` rotation; wa-i1l.8 `--feed-only` reads the same R2 keys.

Two `wiki-audio publish` invocations (or one `publish` + one `publish --feed-only`) racing from different shells, machines, or even cron-on-the-same-box, will both:
1. `Load()` the same manifest version
2. compute their own diff
3. PUT their own manifest back, last writer wins

Possible blast radius:
- **Lost ManifestEntry updates**: shell A uploads MP3 X and updates entry; shell B (started before A's manifest write) overwrites with its older view; X's entry now has empty `R2Key` + ETag despite the object being on R2. Next `publish` re-uploads (wasteful) or, worse with `--prune`, deletes the orphan.
- **Manifest schema-version regression**: pane-2 just shipped `wa-76r.1` (manifest version + forward-compat guard, commit `1509d28`). A racing older binary's `Save()` could downgrade `Version` and tickle the forward-compat refusal on the next run.
- **`pg.xml` torn at the second**: each writer reads its own manifest and emits its own feed; the last `pg.xml` wins. Listeners get whichever feed the racing PutObject finished last.

**Why it matters**: §1 names the wiki box as the only intended writer, but the user's other machines (laptop, future hosts) are all valid `wiki-audio publish` operators per §3. As soon as the user runs two terminals or schedules a cron, this races silently.

**Fix options** (pick one, document):
- Object-lock advisory file at `pg.publish.lock` in R2 with a holder-uuid + timestamp; `publish` must acquire (with TTL-based expiry) before `Load()`. Implementer cost: ~20 LoC.
- Use R2's conditional-PUT (`If-Match: <etag>` on manifest write); fail loudly on ETag mismatch and instruct user to re-run. Implementer cost: smaller; assumes minio-go supports `PutObjectOptions{IfMatch}`.
- Document explicitly that concurrent `publish` is undefined behavior and the user is responsible for serializing.

Either of the first two is preferable for a personal-use tool that will eventually run from cron.

## [HIGH] `WIKI_AUDIO_ACCESS_TOKEN` empty/missing behavior at feed-gen is unspecified

**Where**: wa-i1l.6 ("Read WIKI_AUDIO_ACCESS_TOKEN from env. Append `?t=<token>`"); §9.1 ("Embedded into every URL in the feed at generation time").

Spec doesn't say what happens when the env var is unset, empty string, or set to a value that doesn't match the Worker's `ACCESS_TOKEN`. Three plausible behaviors and each ships a different bug:

| Behavior | Bug |
|---|---|
| Append `?t=` (empty token) silently | Feed publishes; every enclosure URL 403s in Pocket Casts; user thinks the Worker broke. |
| Append `?t=<env_var_value>` regardless of length | Mismatched token: same outcome as above, harder to root-cause because the URL "looks right". |
| Refuse with clear error | Best behavior, but implementers will pick one of the first two by default unless the spec says otherwise. |

**Why it matters**: this is exactly the "silent data loss / wrong-but-passing tests" category the runbook flagged. The unit test at wa-i1l.15 will pass on a 43-char fixture token; the production bug only manifests when the user runs without sourcing `.env`.

**Fix**: state explicitly. My recommendation:
- Refuse with `WIKI_AUDIO_ACCESS_TOKEN: missing or empty (set in ~/.wiki-audio/.env)` if unset or empty.
- Validate length == 43 and charset `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` before stamping; refuse on mismatch with a short explanation pointing at §9.1.

Add a wa-i1l.15 test row pinning each refuse path.

## [HIGH] R2 PutObject `content-type` for `pg.xml` and `pg.manifest.json` unspecified

**Where**: wa-i1l.4 sets `audio/mpeg` for MP3s explicitly; wa-i1l.7 step 5 says "Upload pg.xml AND pg.manifest.json to R2 root" without content-type; wa-i1l.5 doesn't either.

The Worker (§9.2) uses `obj.writeHttpMetadata(headers)` which copies whatever content-type was stored at upload time. If `pg.xml` lands as default `application/octet-stream` (or worse, `text/plain`), Pocket Casts may refuse to parse it as RSS — castfeedvalidator.com (wa-i1l.11) too.

**Why it matters**: wa-i1l.11 acceptance assumes the validator can fetch and parse the feed. A wrong content-type makes wa-i1l.11 fail with an opaque "couldn't fetch" error before it reads the XML.

**Fix**: pin content-type per artifact:
- `pg.xml` → `application/rss+xml; charset=utf-8`
- `pg.manifest.json` → `application/json; charset=utf-8`
- `pg.manifest.json.bak` → same as above (so a manual recovery via `mc cp` pulls a parseable file).

Add to wa-i1l.4 / wa-i1l.7 acceptance criteria. Also worth a wa-i1l.18 integration test row asserting the HEAD response on each artifact has the expected `Content-Type`.

## [MEDIUM] `PublishedAt` mutation policy on CHANGED diff is unspecified

**Where**: §2 `ManifestEntry.PublishedAt *time.Time` (pointer = optional); wa-i1l.4 "On success: update ManifestEntry.R2Key + R2ETag + PublishedAt"; §5.5 "Use `published_at` from the manifest, not the essay's original publish date — controls episode ordering"; wa-i1l.7 step 3 (upload NEW + CHANGED).

wa-i1l.4 says "update PublishedAt" on every successful upload. But CHANGED entries (existing R2 object whose ETag drifted, e.g., from a body-hash regen) are also "uploaded" by wa-i1l.7. So a v1 essay re-synthesized in v2 with the same slug bumps its PublishedAt to the v2 timestamp, jumping it to the top of every listener's inbox as if it were a brand new episode.

§5.5 explicitly says PublishedAt controls inbox ordering — that's the whole point. So the question is: when an essay's body changes, should listeners see it as "new" again? Reasonable arguments both ways:
- **YES**: the content actually changed; listeners should hear the update.
- **NO**: same essay, same listening intent; bumping PublishedAt feels like spam.

**Why it matters**: implementer reading wa-i1l.4 in isolation will pick "update on every successful upload" because that's what's literally written. But that's a semantically loaded choice the user might not agree with.

**Fix**: state the policy explicitly. My recommendation: PublishedAt is set on first upload only; subsequent CHANGED uploads update R2Key + R2ETag but leave PublishedAt unchanged. Add an `UpdatedAt *time.Time` if temporal "last modified" matters for `wiki-audio inspect`.

## [MEDIUM] STALE-in-manifest case missing from wa-i1l.3's diff taxonomy

**Where**: wa-i1l.3 lists NEW / CHANGED / UNCHANGED / STALE-on-r2; missing: STALE-in-manifest (manifest entry exists, source `.md` no longer present, R2 object may or may not exist).

Source-dir state is what `wiki-audio build` walks. If a `.md` is renamed or removed, the next build silently does NOT update its manifest entry — the entry is now orphan-in-manifest. wa-i1l.3 only diffs manifest-vs-R2; it doesn't surface manifest-vs-source.

Possible interactions:
- Pocket Casts continues to show the deleted-from-source episode in its inbox (because RSS still emits it from the manifest).
- `--prune` doesn't fire because the slug IS in the manifest (just not in source).

**Why it matters**: the user's mental model is "if I delete the .md, the episode goes away". The current spec leaves it forever.

**Fix**: extend wa-i1l.3's diff to a fifth category: STALE-in-manifest. Define behavior:
- Default: warn but keep (matches `--prune` default-off conservatism).
- With `--prune`: drop the entry from manifest AND delete R2 object.

Add to `wiki-audio inspect --slug X` output: a "source present? yes/no" line.

## [MEDIUM] Manifest is reachable through the Worker; spec doesn't say if it should be

**Where**: §9.2 worker source serves any non-empty path; wa-i1l.2 manifest path is `pg.manifest.json` (no special-case in Worker); §9 threat model only discusses feed + episodes.

Anyone with the access token who fetches `/pg.manifest.json?t=<token>` gets the full ManifestEntry list — every slug, body_hash, voice_id, model_id, generated_at, published_at, ETag. Not catastrophic (§9.4 already accepts that "anyone with the token can listen"), but the manifest exposes more metadata than necessary for podcast playback.

**Why it matters**: a token leak (§9.4 row 1) currently leaks "what episodes exist + when they were generated + content fingerprints". Compared to the bare minimum (just enclosure URLs that the feed already stamps), this is more attack surface than the threat model committed to.

**Fix options**:
- **A — Worker filtering**: refuse non-allowlisted paths. Allowlist: `pg.xml`, `pg/*.mp3`. Reject `pg.manifest.json*` and any other key.
- **B — Reload-only via S3 API**: `wiki-audio` reads the manifest with R2 access keys (already does — wa-i1l.2 uses minio-go), so the Worker doesn't need to serve it. Document that the manifest is intentionally not Worker-reachable.
- **C — Accept**: explicitly add a §9.4 row "manifest metadata is also leaked on token compromise; rotation per §9.1 mitigates".

A is small (~5 LoC in worker/src/index.ts) and tightens the gate without changing user-visible behavior. Recommendation: A.

## [LOW] wa-i1l.18 integration tests can scribble on production R2 if a test forgets the prefix

**Where**: wa-i1l.18 uses prefix `_integration_test/<random>/` and `t.Cleanup`; same bucket `wiki-audio` as production.

If a test (or a test helper, or a future copy-paste) constructs a key without the prefix — `pg/test.mp3`, `pg.manifest.json` — it will write directly into production. The bucket has no separation between test and prod namespaces; the only barrier is contributor discipline. `t.Cleanup` only fires on tests that registered cleanup; an early `t.Fatal()` outside the prefix scope leaves orphans.

**Fix**: dedicated test bucket. Cloudflare R2 free tier covers it; the cost is one additional row in `~/.wiki-audio/.env` (`R2_TEST_BUCKET`). wa-i1l.18 should refuse to run if `R2_TEST_BUCKET == R2_BUCKET`. Adds ~5 LoC of guard for a much harder-to-foot-gun integration test.

## [LOW] RSS `<item>` ordering in `pg.xml` is unspecified

**Where**: wa-i1l.5 emits "one `<item>` per ManifestEntry"; map iteration order in Go is non-deterministic; spec doesn't mention sort.

Two consecutive `wiki-audio publish` calls with no manifest changes will produce byte-different `pg.xml` outputs because Go's `range over map` doesn't guarantee order. R2 PutObject overwrites the byte-different file; some HTTP caches will see a "changed" feed even though it's semantically identical.

**Why it matters**: not a correctness bug per se (Pocket Casts sorts by pubDate), but it makes `wiki-audio publish --dry-run`'s output noisy and frustrates `castfeedvalidator.com` users who want stable diffs across runs.

**Fix**: sort entries by `PublishedAt desc, Slug asc` before serialization. Add a wa-i1l.15 test row asserting two consecutive marshals produce byte-identical output for the same input.

## Out-of-scope (deliberately not filed as findings)

- **Token rotation race against in-flight Pocket Casts download**: pane-8's MEDIUM finding on rotation downtime already covers this region. My read is the same: accept the brief blast radius for v1.
- **Multipart upload ETag stability**: pane-8's MEDIUM finding on ETag-conflation already names this. No additional angle.
- **Worker request method handling**: §9.2 source only handles GET via the implicit `req` shape; HEAD requests will work via the same path; POST/PUT will be served the same content (which Pocket Casts won't do but a buggy client might). Not worth filing — single-user threat model.

— pane-3 (additive review)

comments.author: pane-3
comments.text:
## Closing wa-hv6 — Phase F spec review complete

Two reviewer passes:
- **pane-8** (the bead's original body): 7 findings. 3 [HIGH] (partial-publish recovery contradiction; feed-emission rule for unpublished entries; `.bak` fallback guard asymmetry); 4 [MEDIUM] (rotation downtime; itunes:summary contradiction; URL composition; ETag retry/identity conflation).
- **pane-3** (just-filed comment, additive): 7 more findings. 1 [CRITICAL] (concurrent-publish mutex), 2 [HIGH] (token-empty behavior; content-type), 3 [MEDIUM] (PublishedAt mutation policy; STALE-in-manifest; manifest reachable through Worker), 2 [LOW] (integration-test bucket-collision risk; RSS `<item>` ordering).

Combined severity totals: **1 CRITICAL · 5 HIGH · 7 MEDIUM · 2 LOW** across 14 findings.

### Cross-reviewer agreement

Both passes independently flag the same load-bearing risk in different framings: the publish flow's recovery / atomicity / concurrency story is under-specified in three orthogonal ways:
- pane-8 [HIGH] **partial-publish recovery contradicts write order** — single-writer recovery semantics
- pane-3 [CRITICAL] **concurrent publish has no mutex model** — multi-writer exclusion semantics
- pane-8 [HIGH] **feed eligibility for unpublished entries** — what listeners see during the partial-fail window

These three should be resolved together as a single Phase F design pass, not addressed in piecemeal. Recommendation: write a short "Phase F atomicity contract" subsection in §6 (or a sub-bead under wa-i1l) that states explicitly:
1. The mutex model (pane-3 CRITICAL)
2. The recovery-state contract (pane-8 HIGH #1)
3. The feed-emission gate (pane-8 HIGH #2)

Plus the `.bak` guard uniformity (pane-8 HIGH #3) as the read-side counterpart.

### Forward-compat angle

pane-2's `wa-76r.1` (manifest version + forward-compat guard, commit `1509d28`) just landed. None of the existing 14 findings reference it directly, but the concurrent-publish CRITICAL has a sharper edge under wa-76r.1: a racing older binary's `Save()` could downgrade `Version` and trip the forward-compat refusal on the very next run. Mention in whichever atomicity sub-bead lands.

### What I deliberately did NOT file

Catalogued at the bottom of pane-3's comment:
- Rotation race vs in-flight Pocket Casts download (covered by pane-8 [MEDIUM] rotation downtime).
- Multipart upload ETag stability (covered by pane-8 [MEDIUM] ETag conflation).
- Worker non-GET method handling (single-user threat model; not worth a bead row).

### Recommended next moves for the implementer (whoever picks up Phase F)

1. **Triage**: read pane-8's 7 + pane-3's 7 findings together. Each finding has a "Fix" stanza with a concrete recommendation; in most cases there's a "pick one" choice for the spec author.
2. **Spec edits before implementation**: at minimum, resolve the CRITICAL (mutex model) and the three [HIGH]s that share the publish-atomicity region. Ship those as PLAN diffs + bead-text edits before claiming wa-i1l.7 (the orchestrator command).
3. **Cheap-and-uncontroversial wins**: the [HIGH] content-type and the [LOW] RSS sort are 5 lines each, no design debate needed. Roll into wa-i1l.4 / wa-i1l.5 acceptance criteria directly.
4. **Test-side guards**: the [LOW] integration-bucket-collision is small and prevents a foot-gun forever; ship alongside wa-i1l.18.

### Bead status

Closing wa-hv6. Two complete reviewer passes are sufficient signal for the implementer to start scoping. Any further pre-implementation review (pane-9 etc.) is welcome but not blocking.

title: Phase F — R2 publish + RSS feed generator
description:
# Phase F — Diff R2, upload, regenerate pg.xml, validate, subscribe

Implements: PLAN_FOR_AUDIO_LIBRARY.md §5.5 (RSS), §7 Phase F, §3
(publish subcommand surface).

## Goal

`wiki-audio publish` does:
1. Fetch the existing manifest + R2 object listing.
2. Diff: which slugs are new vs. changed vs. unchanged vs. stale-on-R2.
3. Upload new/changed MP3s with minio-go.
4. Regenerate `pg.xml` (iTunes-namespaced RSS) from manifest entries.
5. Upload `pg.xml` and `pg.manifest.json` to R2 root (with `.bak`
   rotation on the manifest — never silently overwrite a good one).

Also: `--feed-only` (regenerate XML without re-uploading audio),
`--dry-run` (show diff + feed XML without uploading), `--prune` (remove
R2 objects whose slug is no longer in the manifest — default OFF, silent
prune is dangerous).

## RSS specifics — pubDate and guid policies

- **pubDate** uses `published_at` from the manifest, NOT the essay's
  original publish date. This controls episode ordering: newest publish
  appears at the top of the inbox = \"just generated\" pops up first,
  matching listening flow.
- **guid** is `pg-<slug>`, stable across regenerations. Changing it
  causes podcast apps to re-download every episode.

## iTunes namespace — own the small bit, don't pull a library

§8.6: `encoding/xml` + custom struct tags handle the iTunes namespace in
about 60 lines. External podcast libraries are over-engineered for one
feed and add a dependency we don't otherwise need.

## Gate

`wiki-audio publish` after the spike yields a feed validating cleanly in
castfeedvalidator.com; Pocket Casts subscribes successfully on first try
with the token-bearing URL.

title: Implement internal/r2/ minio-go client
description:
Wraps minio-go/v7 with our config:

- Endpoint: \`https://<R2.AccountID>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com\` (derived,
  not configured)
- Region: \`auto\` (R2 quirk)
- Credentials: R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID + R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY from .env
- BucketLookup: BucketLookupPath (R2 doesn't support virtual-hosted style)

Methods needed:
- \`PutObject(key, reader, size, contentType)\` for MP3 + manifest + feed
- \`GetObject(key) (io.ReadCloser, error)\` for manifest fetch
- \`HeadObject(key) (etag, size, error)\` for diff
- \`ListObjects(prefix)\` for diff and prune

## Why minio-go (not aws-sdk-go-v2)

§8.6: ~3 MB compiled vs ~30 MB. Full S3 compatibility, works with R2,
maintained, well-tested.

## Region quirk

R2 reports \`auto\` as the region in S3 API calls. The SDK doesn't
require it but minio-go validates input; pass \`auto\` literally.

## Why we don't use Cloudflare's R2 API directly

R2 has a non-S3 API too (R2_TOKEN-based). It would let us avoid the
S3 sigv4 dance, but minio-go is mature, our token is already provisioned
with S3-style access keys, and using S3 keeps us drop-in compatible
with Backblaze B2 / AWS S3 if we ever migrate. R2_TOKEN in our .env is
unused for now (kept in case a future feature needs it).
close_reason: Shipped in 1d57d25. internal/r2/{client,errors,client_test}.go — 391 net lines (replaces wa-i1l.17 stub). Real minio-go-backed Client satisfies pane-9's Storage interface (PutObject/GetObject/HeadObject/DeleteObject/ListObjects). R2 quirks pinned: Region='auto', Secure:true. Endpoint normalization accepts hostname or full URL. GetObject Stats up-front to surface NoSuchKey before stream open. ETag quotes stripped to match Fake. ListObjects sorted for stable diff. Typed error sentinels: ErrNoSuchKey/ErrAccessDenied/ErrThrottled/ErrNetwork classified via minio.ToErrorResponse.Code. 12 new tests (constructor validation + endpoint forms + 5 mapError code classes). Pane-9's fake.go + r2_test.go untouched per coordination. Live-R2 integration deferred to wa-i1l.18.

title: Implement `wiki-audio publish --prune` (off by default)
description:
Remove R2 objects whose slug is not in the manifest. Default OFF —
silent prune is dangerous (a misconfigured config.toml could empty R2).

Behavior:
- Lists pg/*.mp3 in R2.
- For any object whose slug is not a manifest key, log a deletion line.
- Without --prune: just lists \"would delete\". With --prune: actually
  deletes.

Always print the slug being deleted so the user has audit trail.

## Why this exists at all

§6: \"Stale R2 objects (essay deleted from raw/) — wiki-audio publish
--prune removes them. Default off — silent prune is dangerous.\"

If we ever rename or delete an essay, the old MP3 hangs around in R2
forever without --prune. That's fine for storage cost (~$0.01/mo) but
the orphan does appear in the bucket listing forever.

## Manifest-corruption interaction (added by polish pass 2)

§6 \"Stale R2 objects\" + \"Manifest JSON corruption\" interact: --prune
deletes objects NOT in the manifest. If the manifest itself is corrupt,
the manifest-load path (wa-i1l.2) refuses to overwrite and returns an
error. Concretely:

- `wiki-audio publish --prune` first calls manifest.Load.
- If Load fails OR returns a manifest that fell back to .bak (i.e., the
  primary was corrupt), --prune is REFUSED with a clear error:
    \"refusing to --prune: manifest source is degraded; resolve the
     manifest first (see wa-i1l.2 recovery instructions)\"
- The user must heal the manifest before running --prune. This avoids
  the catastrophic case: corrupt manifest + --prune == empty bucket.

## Test rows

| Test name                              | Setup                                  | Expectation |
|----------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|-------------|
| prune_refuses_on_corrupt_manifest      | main + .bak corrupt                    | exits non-zero; bucket unchanged |
| prune_refuses_on_bak_fallback          | main corrupt; .bak valid               | exits non-zero with degradation note |
| prune_dry_run_lists_orphans            | manifest with 2 slugs; bucket has 3    | prints would-delete line for orphan; nothing deleted |
| prune_with_flag_deletes_orphans        | as above + --prune                     | orphan deleted; manifest's 2 retained |
| prune_logs_each_deletion               | bucket has 5 orphans                   | 5 separate log lines, slug-by-slug |
| prune_never_deletes_manifest_keys      | manifest's slug present in bucket      | NOT deleted (sanity guard) |

title: Validate generated pg.xml at castfeedvalidator.com
description:
After F7's first end-to-end publish, paste the feed URL into
castfeedvalidator.com (or equivalent). Address every error/warning.

Expect: zero errors, possibly some warnings about optional fields
(itunes:image is optional in v1; cover art is deferred per §10).

## Why a third-party validator

Pocket Casts is a single client and may tolerate malformed XML that
other apps reject. If we ever switch apps (Overcast, Apple Podcasts),
we want the feed to be portable. castfeedvalidator hits all the major
apps' compliance lists.

## Acceptance criteria

Done =
1. https://castfeedvalidator.com (or equivalent) report against `https://wiki-audio.jabyrne.workers.dev/pg.xml?t=$WIKI_AUDIO_ACCESS_TOKEN` shows ZERO errors. Warnings allowed only for: missing `itunes:image`, missing `itunes:summary` channel-level (if we omit it deliberately), or other optional-field warnings.
2. Screenshot or copy-paste of the validator output saved to `~/.cache/wiki-audio/castfeedvalidator-YYYY-MM-DD.txt` for posterity.
3. Cross-check with one other validator (https://podba.se/validate or https://www.feedvalidator.org) showing zero errors. Two independent validators agreeing is the bar.

## Fail path

For each error reported:
- Identify the offending element (validator points at line + element).
- Locate the corresponding XML emitter in `internal/feed/` (wa-i1l.5).
- Fix the marshalling. Re-run `wiki-audio publish --feed-only`.
- Re-validate.

Loop until zero errors. Don't ship a feed with errors — even if Pocket Casts tolerates it, future-app-switch breaks.

title: Subscribe Pocket Casts on phone to https://...wiki-audio.jabyrne.workers.dev/pg.xml?t=<token>
description:
On the phone, in Pocket Casts: Discover → Add URL → paste the feed URL
including the \`?t=<token>\` query string.

Verify:
- All 53 episodes (or however many at this point) populate.
- Title, artist, date display correctly.
- Tap an episode → downloads → plays.

This is the moment the project exists. After this works, the rest is
operationalizing.

## Token note

Once Pocket Casts has the feed URL, it stores it. Token rotation
(future-me): regen, update Worker secret + .env, run
\`wiki-audio publish --feed-only\`, then in Pocket Casts unsubscribe
and re-subscribe to the new URL. Old token 403s immediately.

## Acceptance criteria

Done = on the actual production phone (Pocket Casts app, NOT a different podcast app):

1. The full feed URL (with token) was pasted into Add URL.
2. The feed parsed without an error message.
3. Episode count in the app matches the count in pg.xml's `<item>` elements (cross-check via `xmllint --xpath 'count(//item)' <(curl ...pg.xml)`).
4. For at least 3 episodes (first, last, one random middle one):
   - Title displays correctly (matches the essay title, not the slug).
   - Artist / Album display correctly.
   - Tap → download progresses to 100% → plays.
5. The token-bearing URL is the ONLY input the user provided — no Pocket Casts auth setup, no extra credentials.

Verifiable artifact: a screenshot showing the subscribed feed listing in Pocket Casts → save to `~/.cache/wiki-audio/pocket-casts-subscribed-YYYY-MM-DD.png`.

## Fail path

- Feed URL rejected by Pocket Casts → run `curl ...pg.xml` against the URL on a separate device; if curl returns 200 + valid XML, the issue is Pocket Casts cache; try in a private session or wait 5 min and retry. If curl fails, the publish path is broken — investigate before re-trying.
- Episodes appear but won't play → token mismatch between pg.xml and Worker secret. Re-run `wiki-audio publish --feed-only` after confirming $WIKI_AUDIO_ACCESS_TOKEN matches what's in the worker secret.
- Feed validates at castfeedvalidator (wa-i1l.11) but Pocket Casts shows zero episodes → likely missing `<itunes:author>` or `<itunes:summary>` at channel level; some apps swallow malformed channel-level metadata silently. Inspect feed XML; fix in internal/feed/ (wa-i1l.5).

title: Implement `wiki-audio inspect --slug X` (read-only diagnostics)
description:
Read-only diagnostics command (§3 sample):

\`\`\`
\$ wiki-audio inspect --slug beating-the-averages
title:        Beating the Averages
chars:        8,210 (cleaned) / 11,402 (raw)
dropped:      4 code blocks (Lisp), 0 footnotes
chunks:       3 × ~2,700 chars
last build:   2026-05-08T14:21:03Z
last publish: 2026-05-08T14:24:11Z
r2 url:       https://wiki-audio.jabyrne.workers.dev/pg/beating-the-averages.mp3?t=<token>
duration:     12m04s
\`\`\`

Combines: live extractor run + manifest entry + token from .env.

## Why this is its own bead

Useful for debugging individual essays without re-running build. \"Why
isn't this essay regenerating?\" → check inspect → see the body_hash
hasn't changed → realize the source markdown didn't actually change.

## Where it lives in Phase F (not D)

inspect needs the manifest + R2 URL formation, which is Phase F
plumbing. Could live in D as extraction-only, but the value is in
combining build state with publish state, so it sits here.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## Format contract for the 8-row table (polish pass 6)

The §3 sample output (already in this bead) is the contract. Concretely:

| Row label    | Source                                | Format |
|--------------|---------------------------------------|--------|
| title        | manifest.Title (or essay frontmatter) | string, no truncation |
| chars        | extractor (live) + manifest.RawChars  | `<cleaned> (cleaned) / <raw> (raw)`, comma-grouped |
| dropped      | extractor (live)                      | `<K> <kind>[, …]` joined by commas; `none` if all zero |
| chunks       | chunker (live)                        | `<N> × ~<avg-chars> chars` |
| last build   | manifest.LastBuild                    | RFC3339 UTC |
| last publish | manifest.LastPublish                  | RFC3339 UTC; `<never>` if absent |
| r2 url       | feed-URL builder (with token)         | full URL with `?t=<token>` |
| duration     | manifest.DurationSeconds              | `<H>h<M>m<S>s` (omit unit if 0) |

Eight rows, fixed order, left-padded to 13-char column for the label.

## Missing slug behavior

`wiki-audio inspect --slug nonexistent`:

```
no manifest entry for slug "nonexistent"
hint: was the essay built? run `wiki-audio build --slug nonexistent` first
```

…exits with code 2 (distinguishes from infrastructure errors at exit 1).

## Live extraction even if manifest exists

The chars/dropped/chunks rows ALWAYS run extractor live so a manifest
that pre-dates an extractor change still surfaces correct numbers. The
"last build" timestamp is purely informational — it does NOT mean the
chars displayed reflect that build.

If the live extraction yields different chars than manifest.CharCount,
append a notice line at the bottom:

```
note: live extraction differs from last build (was 8,210 → now 8,214);
      run `wiki-audio build --force --slug X` to reconcile
```

## --json output mode

When `--json` global flag is set, emit a single JSON object instead of
the table:

```json
{"slug":"…","title":"…","chars":{"cleaned":8210,"raw":11402},"dropped":[…],
 "chunks":{"count":3,"avg_chars":2700},"last_build":"…","last_publish":"…",
 "r2_url":"…","duration_sec":724,"live_diff":null}
```

…parseable for scripted diagnostics.

title: Cut v1.0.0 release (Phase F gate)
description:
Tag v1.0.0. Pre-flight:

- All Phase F leaves complete.
- pg.xml validates clean at castfeedvalidator.com (F11).
- Pocket Casts successfully subscribes (F12).
- One full \`wiki-audio publish\` round-trip works on a single new
  essay end-to-end (synthesize → upload → feed regen → episode
  appears in app).

After release: re-install on wiki box. Move on to Phase G.

## Acceptance criteria — post-tag verification

Done = ALL of the following observable AFTER `git push origin v1.0.0`:

1. `gh release view v1.0.0` shows 4 tarballs + checksums.txt; CI job for release.yml returned "success".
2. On the wiki box, re-run install.sh; `wiki-audio --version` prints `v1.0.0 (commit ...)`.
3. Full round-trip on a single new essay (different from any synthesized during development):
   - `wiki-audio build --slug <new-slug>` → exits 0; .mp3 produced.
   - `wiki-audio publish` → exits 0; uploads chunk + regen feed.
   - Pocket Casts pull-to-refresh → new episode appears.
   - Tap → downloads → first 30s plays clean.
4. `castfeedvalidator.com` against `https://wiki-audio.jabyrne.workers.dev/pg.xml?t=$WIKI_AUDIO_ACCESS_TOKEN` returns zero errors (warnings about optional fields acceptable).
5. `wiki-audio inspect --slug <new-slug>` shows the manifest entry exists with non-empty body_hash and matching r2_etag.
6. `go test ./...` from a clean checkout of v1.0.0 tag passes (unit tests only — integration tests gated by env, not required for tag).

Fail path: delete tag + release; fix; re-tag. v1.0.0 is the v1 milestone — only re-cut as v1.0.1+ if any third-party install of v1.0.0 happened. We're solo, so re-cut is fine pre-distribution.

title: Unit tests for internal/feed/ RSS XML marshalling (iTunes namespace)
description:
Table-driven tests in `internal/feed/feed_test.go` for the
encoding/xml-based RSS generator built in wa-i1l.5 + wa-i1l.6.

## Test Plan

| Test name                          | Setup                                   | Expectation |
|------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|-------------|
| empty_manifest                     | 0 entries                               | Valid RSS, empty <channel>, no <item> |
| single_entry                       | 1 ManifestEntry                         | Exactly one <item>; required fields present |
| multiple_entries_pubdate_order     | 3 entries with different PublishedAt    | <item>s ordered newest-first by pubDate |
| itunes_namespace_declaration       | any                                     | xmlns:itunes attribute on <rss> root |
| atom_self_link_present             | any                                     | <atom:link rel="self"> with token-stamped URL |
| enclosure_url_token_stamped        | WIKI_AUDIO_ACCESS_TOKEN=foo             | <enclosure url="...?t=foo"> |
| enclosure_url_token_missing        | env unset                               | Returns error; refuses to marshal |
| enclosure_length_matches_filesize  | FileSizeBytes=1234567                   | length="1234567" attr |
| guid_is_pg_slug_prefix             | slug=how-to-do-great-work               | <guid>pg-how-to-do-great-work</guid>, isPermaLink=false |
| stable_guid_across_regen           | regen twice with same slug              | guid byte-identical |
| itunes_duration_seconds            | DurationSeconds=4924                    | <itunes:duration>4924</itunes:duration> |
| itunes_explicit_false              | default                                 | <itunes:explicit>false</itunes:explicit> |
| itunes_author_per_entry            | EssayMeta.Author="Paul Graham"          | <itunes:author>Paul Graham</itunes:author> |
| description_uses_publish_date_text | "July 2023"                             | <description> contains "July 2023" |
| xml_special_chars_escaped          | title="Foo & Bar <baz>"                 | Escaped properly in <title> |
| xml_validates                      | any                                     | xmllint --noout passes (skip if xmllint missing) |
| feed_self_url_uses_FeedConfig      | FeedConfig.BaseURL + FeedPath           | self link composes correctly |

## Golden file test

Generate pg.xml from a fixture manifest with 3 entries (mirrors the
3 example essays). Compare byte-for-byte to a checked-in
`testdata/feed/golden_3essays.xml`. Regenerate with `-update` flag:

  go test ./internal/feed -run TestGoldenRSS -update

Use the same flag convention across all golden-file tests in this
project (see e2e bead).

## Castfeedvalidator parity check (informational)

A separate, non-blocking subtest reads the golden file and checks
that key elements (atom self link, every <enclosure>, <guid>) match
what castfeedvalidator.com requires. Pure structural — doesn't make
network calls.

## Structured logging during tests

slog.With("test", t.Name(), "n_items", len(entries)). On failure,
log the full marshalled XML so diffs are visible in CI output.

## Why xml diffs matter

A single missing namespace attribute would cause Pocket Casts to skip
every episode silently. Byte-exact golden tests + namespace assertions
catch that class of regression at PR review.

## Namespace-URL exact-match test rows (added pass 3, cross-ref wa-i1l.5)

These tests verify the load-bearing namespace constants documented in
wa-i1l.5 (§5.5 specifics). A typo silently breaks Pocket Casts.

| Test name                            | Expectation |
|--------------------------------------|-------------|
| itunes_ns_uri_exact                  | xmlns:itunes attr value == "http://www.itunes.com/dtds/podcast-1.0.dtd" (HTTP not HTTPS) |
| atom_ns_uri_exact                    | xmlns:atom attr value == "http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" |
| rss_version_attr                     | <rss version="2.0"> attribute present |
| guid_ispermalink_false_explicit      | isPermaLink="false" attribute literally present (not omitted) |
| channel_has_itunes_owner_email       | <itunes:owner><itunes:email> contains FeedConfig.OwnerEmail |
| channel_has_itunes_category          | <itunes:category text="Technology" /> emitted |

title: Unit tests for internal/manifest/ load-with-bak fallback
description:
Tests in `internal/manifest/manifest_test.go` covering the load + save
behaviors of wa-i1l.2 — specifically the .bak rotation that prevents
losing the source-of-truth on JSON corruption.

## Test Plan

The R2 client is mocked via an interface. Use a fake `R2Storage` that
backs onto an in-memory map[string][]byte so tests run in microseconds.

| Test name                              | Setup                                | Expectation |
|----------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|-------------|
| load_missing_returns_empty             | No pg.manifest.json in fake R2       | Returns Manifest{Version:1, Entries:{}} (no error) |
| load_valid_returns_parsed              | pg.manifest.json valid               | Returns parsed manifest |
| load_corrupt_falls_back_to_bak         | main corrupt; .bak valid             | Returns .bak's contents; logs warning |
| load_both_corrupt_aborts               | main + .bak both corrupt             | Returns error mentioning both keys + manual recovery instruction |
| load_main_valid_bak_corrupt            | main valid; .bak corrupt             | Returns main; doesn't touch .bak |
| save_rotates_existing_to_bak           | pre-existing main                    | After save: .bak == old main bytes; main == new bytes |
| save_when_no_existing_main             | empty bucket                         | After save: main == new bytes; .bak absent (skipped) |
| save_overwrites_old_bak                | pre-existing .bak                    | New .bak overwrites old; new main is current |
| version_guard_refuses_overwrite        | Loaded Version=99 (>known)           | Save returns error; doesn't write |
| version_guard_allows_older_read        | Loaded Version=0 (<known)            | Load succeeds; save bumps Version to current |
| save_writes_atomic_per_object          | concurrent reader during save        | Reader sees either old or new, never partial |
| roundtrip_preserves_unknown_fields     | manifest with extra JSON keys        | Save preserves unknowns (forward-compat) |

## Why an R2Storage interface

Mocking at the storage interface (not http.Client) means we test the
manifest module's logic without coupling to minio-go internals. The
interface lives in internal/r2/ and satisfies real minio + the fake.
This is also the foundation for wa-i1l.16 (R2 client unit tests).

## Manual-recovery message assertion

When both files are corrupt, the error must literally say something
like:

    both pg.manifest.json and pg.manifest.json.bak are corrupt;
    refusing to overwrite. Inspect via:
      mc cat r2/wiki-audio/pg.manifest.json
      mc cat r2/wiki-audio/pg.manifest.json.bak

The exact text is part of §6's recovery story — a test pinning the
message guards the runbook.

## Structured logging during tests

slog.With("test", t.Name(), "scenario", scenarioName). When fallback
to .bak triggers, the manifest module emits a warning log. Test that
the warning is emitted with the right level (WARN, not ERROR) and
includes both keys in attrs.

## Why this is its own bead

Manifest corruption recovery is a "you only need it once but absolutely
need it then" story. The whole point of .bak rotation is to be there
when JSON parsing fails. Untested = unverified = false confidence.

title: Unit tests for internal/r2/ client (mockable interface, in-memory fake)
description:
Tests in `internal/r2/r2_test.go` plus an exported `Fake` storage
implementation in `internal/r2/fake.go` that other packages
(manifest, feed, publish) can use as a drop-in for unit testing.

## Public interface (defined in this bead)

```go
type Storage interface {
    PutObject(ctx context.Context, key string, r io.Reader, size int64, contentType string) (etag string, err error)
    GetObject(ctx context.Context, key string) (io.ReadCloser, error)
    HeadObject(ctx context.Context, key string) (etag string, size int64, err error)
    ListObjects(ctx context.Context, prefix string) ([]ObjectInfo, error)
}
```

The minio-go-backed implementation in wa-i1l.1 satisfies this.
`internal/r2.Fake` (new) backs onto map[string][]byte for tests.

## Test Plan — Fake correctness

| Test name                         | Behavior verified                          |
|-----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
| put_then_get_roundtrip            | PutObject + GetObject returns same bytes   |
| put_returns_etag                  | etag is sha256 (or md5) of body, hex       |
| head_after_put                    | HeadObject returns correct size + etag     |
| head_missing_returns_NoSuchKey    | error matches an exported sentinel         |
| get_missing_returns_NoSuchKey     | same sentinel                              |
| list_with_prefix                  | only keys under prefix                     |
| list_empty                        | returns []ObjectInfo{}, nil (not nil slice)|
| put_overwrites_existing           | new etag, new size                         |
| concurrent_put_get                | -race clean; mutex guards map              |

## Test Plan — Real client (skippable)

A separate file `r2_integration_test.go` with build tag
`//go:build integration` exercises the minio-go client against a
real R2 bucket. Skipped unless `WIKI_AUDIO_RUN_INTEGRATION=1` is set
AND R2 credentials are present in env. Confirms:

- Endpoint URL composition (https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com)
- BucketLookupPath setting works
- Path-style URLs not virtual-host
- Region "auto" accepted
- ETag format matches what we compare in F3 diff

## NoSuchKey sentinel

Export a sentinel error so callers can `errors.Is(err, r2.ErrNoSuchKey)`.
Without this the fallback-to-.bak logic in manifest tests has to do
fragile string matching.

## Structured logging during tests

slog.With("test", t.Name(), "fake", true). The Fake records every
operation so tests can assert "was List called?" without exposing
internals.

## Why a Fake (not gomock / testify mocks)

A hand-rolled in-memory Fake is ~80 lines and behaves exactly like
real R2 for the operations we care about. Generated mocks force you
to script every call, which is brittle when the production code
refactors. Fake = behavioral parity = real test coverage.

title: Integration test: real R2 PutObject/GetObject/Head/List (opt-in)
description:
A `//go:build integration` test in `internal/r2/r2_integration_test.go`
that exercises the minio-go-backed R2 client (wa-i1l.1) against a
real Cloudflare R2 bucket. Gated by build tag + `WIKI_AUDIO_RUN_INTEGRATION=1`
(see wa-76r.10).

## Test Plan

All tests use a unique key prefix `_integration_test/<random>/` so they
don't collide with real episodes. Cleanup runs in `t.Cleanup`.

| Test name                            | Expectation |
|--------------------------------------|-------------|
| put_then_head                        | etag returned, size matches body |
| put_then_get                         | bytes round-trip identical |
| put_overwrite                        | second put returns new etag, size |
| head_missing                         | errors.Is(err, r2.ErrNoSuchKey) |
| get_missing                          | errors.Is(err, r2.ErrNoSuchKey) |
| list_with_prefix                     | only our integration keys |
| list_returns_etags                   | matches HEAD-derived etags |
| put_large_multipart                  | 10 MB body uses multipart; works |
| put_small_single_part                | 100 KB body uses single PUT |
| content_type_audio_mpeg              | HEAD reflects content-type set on PUT |
| concurrent_put                       | 5 goroutines × 5 keys; no errors; race-clean |
| region_auto_accepted                 | client uses Region="auto" successfully |

## Cleanup contract

`t.Cleanup` deletes every key created. Failure to delete is logged but
not failed (don't mask the underlying test failure). The unique prefix
means orphans are easy to find: `mc rm --recursive r2/wiki-audio/_integration_test/`.

## Cost guard

The full suite uploads <50 MB and downloads same. R2 is free egress;
storage is ~$0.015/GB/mo. Total cost: a fraction of a cent if cleanup
runs; ~free even if it doesn't.

## Structured logging

slog.With("test", t.Name(), "service", "r2", "bucket", cfg.Bucket,
"prefix", testPrefix). On any failure, the prefix is in the log
so manual cleanup is straightforward.

## What this catches that unit tests don't

- R2's quirks (BucketLookupPath, region "auto", path-style URLs)
- Multipart threshold behavior on real network
- ETag format differences between minio S3 and CF R2
- Auth signature compatibility (sigv4 against R2's sigv4 acceptance)

title: Implement internal/manifest/ load + save with .bak rotation
description:
Manifest lives at R2 key \`pg.manifest.json\`. Operations:

- **Load**: GET pg.manifest.json. If missing, return empty Manifest{Version:1, Entries:{}}.
  If present but unmarshal fails, look at pg.manifest.json.bak; if THAT
  also fails, abort with a clear message instructing manual inspection.
- **Save**: before writing, rename current pg.manifest.json to
  pg.manifest.json.bak (overwriting any old .bak). Then write new
  manifest. Atomic enough — R2's PutObject is atomic per object, so a
  partial upload doesn't replace a good object.

## Why .bak rotation matters

§6: \"Manifest JSON corruption — R2 keeps the previous manifest at
pg.manifest.json.bak (rotated before each save). If both corrupt,
abort with instruction to manually inspect. Never silently overwrite.\"

The manifest is the source of truth for what's been built. Losing it =
re-running the whole bulk run = wasted credits. The .bak is cheap
insurance.

## Schema version guard

If loaded Manifest.Version > our binary's known version, refuse to
overwrite (§6). Tells the user to upgrade. Forward-compat-friendly:
older manifests with smaller Version are fine to read.

title: Implement R2 list + ETag diff against manifest
description:
Compute the publish set:

- For each manifest entry: HEAD R2 object at \`pg/<slug>.mp3\`.
  - 404 → NEW (upload required)
  - ETag mismatch with ManifestEntry.R2ETag → CHANGED (upload required)
  - ETag match → UNCHANGED (skip upload)
- ListObjects(\"pg/\"): any *.mp3 not in manifest → STALE (eligible for
  --prune; default leaves it alone)

Print the diff: \`diff: 4 new, 1 changed, 0 stale-on-r2\` (matches §3
sample output).

## Why ETag (not body_hash)

ETag is what R2 reports; it's MD5 of the upload (or multipart hash for
large objects). It's the only thing we can compare against without
re-fetching the object. body_hash already lives in the manifest entry
locally — we use it to decide whether to re-RUN, not whether to re-UPLOAD.

A new upload of the same MP3 produces the same ETag, so unchanged
content stays unchanged on R2.

## Why HEAD per object (not just ListObjects)

HEAD gives us ETag without fetching the body. ListObjects also returns
ETags but the response can be paginated — for ~50 objects it's cheap
either way. HEAD per known slug is simpler code.

## Recovery test rows (added by polish pass 2 — §6 \"R2 listing failure\")

§6 says: \"R2 listing failure during diff — abort publish; nothing
uploaded; safe to retry.\" Concretely: ListObjects errors are NOT
retried inline (that's the R2 client's job, see wa-i1l.1 / wa-i1l.4
shared retry policy). After exhausting client-level retries, surface
the error and exit. The publish run is safe to re-invoke because no
mutating operation has been issued yet (HEAD + ListObjects are
read-only).

| Test name                              | Setup                                  | Expectation |
|----------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|-------------|
| listobjects_persistent_5xx_aborts      | fake R2 returns 503 always for List    | publish exits non-zero with clear error; no PutObject calls issued |
| listobjects_transient_5xx_recovers     | fake R2 returns 503 twice then 200     | publish completes; uses retry policy |
| head_persistent_5xx_aborts             | HEAD returns 503 always                | publish exits non-zero |
| listobjects_auth_failure_aborts        | fake R2 returns 403                    | exits non-zero; no PutObject calls |
| safe_to_retry_after_listing_failure    | run #1 fails listing; run #2 lists OK  | run #2 completes normally |

title: Uploader with retries (PutObject, atomic semantics)
description:
Upload MP3s identified by F3's diff:

- Read MP3 from \`~/.cache/wiki-audio/out/<slug>.mp3\`.
- PutObject to \`pg/<slug>.mp3\` with content-type \`audio/mpeg\`.
- Retry on transient errors (5xx, network) up to 3 times with exp
  backoff.
- On success: update ManifestEntry.R2Key + R2ETag + PublishedAt.
- On final failure: leave ManifestEntry.R2Key empty; surfaces in next
  publish run. Local cache MP3 retained — no rebuild.

## Why we update PublishedAt only on successful upload

§5.5 \"pubDate policy\" — the RSS feed uses PublishedAt as <pubDate>,
which controls episode order in podcast apps. Setting it before
upload would risk an unpublished essay appearing at the top of the
feed. Set after, never optimistically.

## Don't set Content-Disposition

Pocket Casts and friends use the URL path's last segment as the file
name when downloading. Adding a Content-Disposition header is
unnecessary and can confuse some apps.

## Concrete retry policy (added by polish pass 2 — addresses §6 hand-waviness)

| Knob                          | Value          | Notes |
|-------------------------------|----------------|-------|
| Max retry attempts            | 3              | Same shape as TTS retry (wa-4cw.2) for consistency. |
| Backoff base                  | 2s             | attempt N waits 2^N seconds. |
| Backoff jitter                | uniform [0,1)s | Avoid thundering herd if many uploads fail simultaneously. |
| Backoff cap                   | 30s            | Lower than TTS cap (60s) — R2 uploads are fast, long sleeps mean give-up. |
| Per-request timeout           | 120s           | Larger than TTS because MP3 bodies are 5-10 MB. |
| Total per-upload budget       | ~370s          | 3 × 120s + 2s + 4s + jitter. |

## Errors that ARE retried

- net.Error with Temporary() == true
- minio-go ErrorResponse with Code in {InternalError, RequestTimeout,
  ServiceUnavailable, SlowDown}
- HTTP 5xx generally
- HTTP 429 (Cloudflare R2 does not commonly emit this, but if it does,
  honor Retry-After with the same cap rules as wa-4cw.2: ≤300s)

## Errors that ARE NOT retried (FATAL for this upload)

- HTTP 401, 403 (auth) — surface to user, abort publish run.
- HTTP 400 (bad request) — programmer error; abort.
- 5xx that persists across all 3 attempts — leave R2Key="" on the
  manifest entry per §6, surface in next publish.

## Idempotency

PutObject is idempotent on R2 (same key + same body == same ETag,
no-op effect). So retries are safe even if a previous attempt
partially succeeded — we never end up with a half-uploaded MP3
visible to readers (R2 PutObject is atomic per object).

## Partial-publish recovery

If 7 of 10 essays uploaded before a fatal error, the 7 manifest
entries have R2Key set; the 3 don't. The next publish re-runs the
diff (wa-i1l.3) and only attempts the 3 that lack R2Key. No work
duplicated; the user just re-runs . wiki-audio publish.

## Operational realism (pass 9) — publish wall-clock

### Per-object timing

- Mean MP3 size: 612 MB / 53 = ~11.5 MB per object.
- TLS handshake + headers per request: ~150 ms (R2 typical from US/EU).

| Uplink              | Mean per-object | All 53 sequential |
|---------------------|-----------------|-------------------|
| 50 Mbps residential | 11.5 MB × 8 / 50 = 1.84 s + 0.15 s = ~2 s | 53 × 2 s = ~106 s |
| 200 Mbps cable      | 0.46 s + 0.15 s = ~0.6 s | 32 s |
| 1 Gbps fiber        | 0.09 s + 0.15 s = 0.24 s | 13 s |

The minio-go default is to use HTTP/2 multiplexing where supported,
so connection reuse keeps TLS overhead amortized. In practice:

- Fresh publish (53 new MP3s): 60-180 s wall clock depending on uplink.
- Incremental publish (1 new MP3): 2-5 s wall clock (mostly the
  manifest+pg.xml round-trip).

### Concurrency note

v1 uploads sequentially. minio-go supports parallel PutObject and a
4-way concurrent uploader would cut bulk publish time by ~3×, but the
complexity isn't worth it for an operation that already takes < 3 min.
If publish wall-clock ever exceeds 10 min, revisit (likely uplink is
the cause, not concurrency).

### Retry budget vs total wall-clock

The retry policy (3 attempts, 2s/4s/8s backoff, 30s cap, 120s timeout)
gives ~370 s worst-case per object. If 1 of 53 hits worst case:
- Best case publish: 13 s.
- Expected (no retries): 30-60 s.
- Expected with one slow object: +6 min.
- All 53 at worst case (catastrophic): 53 × 370 s ≈ 5.5 h. NEVER seen
  in practice; would imply R2 being completely down, in which case
  abort manually before retry storm.

title: Implement internal/feed/ RSS XML generator (iTunes namespace, encoding/xml)
description:
Generate \`pg.xml\` — iTunes-namespaced RSS 2.0. Use stdlib
\`encoding/xml\` with custom struct tags. The iTunes namespace requires
hand-crafted \`xml:\"itunes:author\"\` etc.

Per ManifestEntry, emit one <item>:

\`\`\`xml
<item>
  <title>How to Do Great Work</title>
  <enclosure url=\"https://wiki-audio.jabyrne.workers.dev/pg/how-to-do-great-work.mp3?t=<token>\"
             length=\"65437184\" type=\"audio/mpeg\" />
  <guid isPermaLink=\"false\">pg-how-to-do-great-work</guid>
  <pubDate>Thu, 08 May 2026 14:21:03 GMT</pubDate>
  <itunes:author>Paul Graham</itunes:author>
  <itunes:duration>4924</itunes:duration>
  <itunes:explicit>false</itunes:explicit>
  <description>Originally published July 2023.</description>
</item>
\`\`\`

Channel-level fields come from FeedConfig (Title, Description, Author,
OwnerEmail, BaseURL, FeedPath, Language, optional CoverImageURL).

## guid policy (§5.5)

\`pg-<slug>\`. STABLE across regenerations. Changing the guid causes
podcast apps to re-download every episode, which is rude.

## pubDate policy (§5.5)

Use ManifestEntry.PublishedAt, NOT the essay's original publish date.
This controls episode ordering: newest publish appears at top of
inbox = \"just generated\" pops up first.

## Why no external podcast library

§8.6: encoding/xml + struct tags handles iTunes namespace cleanly in
about 60 lines. External libraries are over-engineered for one feed
and add a dependency we don't otherwise need.

## Pre-flight: validate the XML

Run \`xmllint --noout\` (if available) on the generated XML before
upload, OR check that encoding/xml's marshal succeeded with no
unbalanced namespaces. Dropping a malformed feed into R2 would brick
Pocket Casts subscriptions until republish.

## Algorithm specifics — RSS root + namespaces (added pass 3)

The §5.5 sample only shows one <item>; here is the full channel
skeleton the marshaller must emit. Critical: the iTunes namespace URL
is **load-bearing** — Pocket Casts, Apple Podcasts, and Overcast all
look it up by exact URI. A typo here silently breaks subscribers.

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rss version="2.0"
     xmlns:itunes="http://www.itunes.com/dtds/podcast-1.0.dtd"
     xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom">
  <channel>
    <title>{FeedConfig.Title}</title>
    <link>{FeedConfig.BaseURL}</link>
    <atom:link rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"
               href="{FeedConfig.BaseURL}/{FeedConfig.FeedPath}?t={token}" />
    <description>{FeedConfig.Description}</description>
    <language>{FeedConfig.Language}</language>
    <itunes:author>{FeedConfig.Author}</itunes:author>
    <itunes:owner>
      <itunes:name>{FeedConfig.Author}</itunes:name>
      <itunes:email>{FeedConfig.OwnerEmail}</itunes:email>
    </itunes:owner>
    <itunes:explicit>false</itunes:explicit>
    <itunes:category text="Technology" />
    <!-- optional: <itunes:image href="{FeedConfig.CoverImageURL}" /> -->
    <!-- one <item> per ManifestEntry, ordered newest pubDate first -->
  </channel>
</rss>
```

### Load-bearing constants

- `xmlns:itunes` MUST be exactly `http://www.itunes.com/dtds/podcast-1.0.dtd`
  (note: HTTP, not HTTPS; Apple has not migrated this namespace URI and
  changing it would break clients).
- `xmlns:atom` MUST be exactly `http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom`.
- `<rss version="2.0">` — RSS 2.0, not Atom-as-primary.

### encoding/xml struct-tag pattern

Because Go's encoding/xml treats `xmlns:itunes` as just an attribute,
the cleanest way is one struct per element with explicit XMLName:

```go
type rssRoot struct {
    XMLName       xml.Name `xml:"rss"`
    Version       string   `xml:"version,attr"`
    XMLNSItunes   string   `xml:"xmlns:itunes,attr"`
    XMLNSAtom     string   `xml:"xmlns:atom,attr"`
    Channel       channel  `xml:"channel"`
}
type itunesAuthor struct {
    XMLName xml.Name `xml:"itunes:author"`
    Value   string   `xml:",chardata"`
}
// ...etc for itunes:owner, itunes:explicit, itunes:category, itunes:duration
```

Set the namespace attrs once when constructing rssRoot (don't try to
let encoding/xml figure them out — it can't, because Go's xml package
doesn't model RSS-style colon-prefixed namespaces natively).

### Item-level guid contract

`<guid isPermaLink="false">pg-<slug></guid>` — the `isPermaLink="false"`
attribute is required. Without it, RSS 2.0 spec defaults isPermaLink to
"true", and podcast clients then attempt to GET the guid value as a
URL, causing 404 noise.

### Test rows that wa-i1l.15 must add (already present, restated for clarity)

- `xmlns:itunes` attr value MUST equal the exact URI above.
- `xmlns:atom` attr value MUST equal the exact URI above.
- `<guid>` MUST have `isPermaLink="false"`.
- Marshal-then-unmarshal round-trips namespace attrs verbatim.

title: Stamp ?t=<token> on every enclosure URL at feed-gen time
description:
Read \`WIKI_AUDIO_ACCESS_TOKEN\` from env. Append \`?t=<token>\` to:

- The feed self-link (\`<atom:link rel=\"self\">\`).
- Every \`<enclosure url=\"...\">\` in the channel.

## Why not put the token in the URL path

§9.3: Token in query string survives object renames; if we ever rotate
the token, only the Worker secret + feed regen are needed — no R2 key
rewrites. Path-based tokens force re-keying every object.

## Why the SAME token everywhere (not per-episode)

One token = one rotation. Per-episode tokens would multiply rotation
work without buying additional security (the threat model in §9 is
\"someone gets the URL\", not \"someone enumerates all URLs given one\").

## Refuse to publish without token

If WIKI_AUDIO_ACCESS_TOKEN is empty, abort the publish run with a clear
error. Better than silently publishing a feed with bare URLs.

title: Implement `wiki-audio publish` (full path: diff → upload → feed → upload)
description:
The default-path publish command:

1. Load manifest from R2 (F2).
2. Diff against R2 (F3): identify NEW + CHANGED.
3. Upload NEW + CHANGED MP3s (F4) — update manifest entries.
4. Regenerate pg.xml (F5 + F6).
5. Upload pg.xml AND pg.manifest.json to R2 root.
6. Print the live feed URL: `https://<base>/pg.xml?t=<token>`.

Sample output target (§3):

```
diff: 4 new, 1 changed, 0 stale-on-r2
uploading how-to-do-great-work.mp3 (62.4 MB) → r2://wiki-audio/pg/how-to-do-great-work.mp3 ✓
...
regenerating pg.xml (53 items) → r2://wiki-audio/pg.xml ✓
feed live at https://wiki-audio.jabyrne.workers.dev/pg.xml?t=<token>
```

## Atomicity caveat

There's no R2-level transaction across multiple objects. Order matters:
upload MP3s FIRST, then manifest, then feed. So if a partial run
succeeds, the feed never points at a missing MP3. Write the feed last
so a partial run leaves an old (but consistent) feed in place.

## Test Plan

End-to-end orchestration tests in `internal/publish/publish_test.go`
using the in-memory R2 Fake from wa-i1l.17. NO real R2; NO real
ElevenLabs (publish doesn't talk to it directly).

| Test name                              | Setup                                   | Expectation |
|----------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|-------------|
| empty_bucket_uploads_all               | manifest with 3 entries, R2 empty       | 3 PutObject calls; final manifest reflects all |
| existing_etag_match_skips_upload       | R2 has matching etag                    | 0 mp3 uploads; manifest still rewritten |
| changed_etag_uploads                   | R2 etag differs                         | upload + manifest update |
| upload_order_mp3s_then_manifest_then_feed | 3 new + feed regen                   | call order asserted via Fake's recording |
| partial_failure_leaves_consistent_state | first upload OK; second fails          | feed NOT regenerated; first MP3 still there |
| feed_regenerated_after_uploads         | after successful uploads                | pg.xml in R2 mentions all uploaded slugs |
| token_required_to_publish              | WIKI_AUDIO_ACCESS_TOKEN unset           | refuses; clear error before any upload |
| dry_run_no_writes                      | --dry-run flag (covered by wa-i1l.9)    | 0 PutObject; 0 manifest changes; only logs |
| diff_count_logged                      | mixed new + changed + unchanged         | log line "diff: N new, M changed, K unchanged" |
| manifest_save_uses_bak_rotation        | existing manifest                       | wa-i1l.16's .bak rotation triggered |

## Structured logging during tests

Use a captured slog handler with `slog.With("test", t.Name(),
"phase", "publish")`. Every operation in the publish pipeline logs:

  slog.Info("uploading", "slug", slug, "size_bytes", size, "key", key)
  slog.Info("uploaded",  "slug", slug, "etag", etag, "duration_ms", elapsed)
  slog.Info("regen_feed", "items", n)
  slog.Info("feed_uploaded", "url", url)

Tests assert these log lines exist with the right attrs. The polish
prompt explicitly calls for "great, detailed logging so we can be
sure that everything is working perfectly after implementation".

## Why orchestration tests live here (not in unit tests of F1-F6)

F1-F6 each have their own focused unit tests (wa-i1l.15, .16, .17).
This bead's tests verify the *sequence* — the upload-order invariant,
the dry-run no-writes invariant, the token-required-to-publish
invariant. Those can only be tested at the orchestration level.

comments.author: jacob
comments.text:
## Upload order is an invariant, not a preference

Within a `wiki-audio publish` run:

1. MP3s upload first (one or more).
2. pg.manifest.json upload (so it reflects what's now in R2).
3. pg.xml upload LAST.

If we upload pg.xml BEFORE all the MP3s, a podcast app that fetches
the feed mid-run sees a feed pointing at MP3s that don't exist yet,
producing "episode unavailable" errors.

If a partial run dies (Ctrl-C, network error) after step 1 but before
step 3, the OLD pg.xml in R2 still points at OLD MP3s — the only
"loss" is that the new MP3s aren't yet announced via feed. Re-running
publish picks up where it left off.

The corollary: never upload pg.xml in --feed-only mode without first
re-fetching the manifest from R2. A stale local manifest could cause
the regenerated feed to drop episodes that were uploaded by a parallel
run or a previous run.

title: Implement `wiki-audio publish --feed-only`
description:
Skip the diff + upload steps. Just regenerate pg.xml from the existing
manifest (which we still load from R2 to be sure we have the latest)
and upload the new feed.

Use cases:
- Edited feed.toml metadata (title, description, cover image URL).
- Rotated the access token; need to republish enclosure URLs.
- Fixed a bug in the RSS generator (F5 / F6).

## Why this exists as a separate flag

A regular publish always does diff + maybe-upload. After token rotation
or feed-config edits, all 53 MP3s are unchanged on R2 — we don't want
to HEAD-check 53 objects unnecessarily. --feed-only is the fast path.

title: Implement `wiki-audio publish --dry-run`
description:
Show diff + emit feed XML to stdout. Do NOT upload anything. Used
before bulk publishes to sanity check.

Output format: the diff lines + the full pg.xml on stdout. Bytes
expected to upload printed as a summary at the end.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## §3 sample output (polish pass 6) — pin dry-run preview format

Verbatim target from §3 for `wiki-audio publish --dry-run`:

```
$ wiki-audio publish --dry-run
```

§3 doesn't expand the body, but the contract is: the output is the same
diff line + per-essay would-upload lines + would-regenerate-feed line
that `publish` emits, with each "uploading"/"uploaded" line replaced by
"would upload" and the feed-XML emitted to stdout (not uploaded).

## Sample dry-run output (synthesized from §3 publish format)

```
$ wiki-audio publish --dry-run
diff: 4 new, 1 changed, 0 stale-on-r2
would upload how-to-do-great-work.mp3 (62.4 MB) → r2://wiki-audio/pg/how-to-do-great-work.mp3
would upload beating-the-averages.mp3 (9.1 MB) → r2://wiki-audio/pg/beating-the-averages.mp3
would upload …
would regenerate pg.xml (53 items) → r2://wiki-audio/pg.xml
--- pg.xml preview ---
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rss version="2.0" xmlns:itunes="http://www.itunes.com/dtds/podcast-1.0.dtd">
…
</rss>
--- end pg.xml ---
total: 5 mp3s (74.3 MB), 1 feed (47 KB) — would have been written
```

## Contract

- "would upload" / "would regenerate" instead of "uploading" / "regenerating".
- ✓/✗ glyphs SUPPRESSED (no actual upload happened).
- Feed XML emitted between sentinel lines `--- pg.xml preview ---` and
  `--- end pg.xml ---` so it's machine-extractable.
- Final summary: byte totals that *would have been* written.
- Exit code 0 even if the diff is huge (dry-run doesn't gate on size).

## Why feed XML on stdout

Lets the user pipe `wiki-audio publish --dry-run | grep -A 9999 "preview" | head -n -1`
into `xmllint --noout -` for a quick sanity check before the real
publish. The sentinel lines are the agreed contract for that pipe.

title: Phase B — Scaffold the wiki-audio Go repo
description:
# Phase B — New repo + Go module + skeleton

Implements: PLAN_FOR_AUDIO_LIBRARY.md §3 (CLI surface), §7 Phase B.

## Goal

Stand up `github.com/Jacob2017/wiki-audio` as a private GitHub repo with:

- `go mod init github.com/Jacob2017/wiki-audio`
- Cobra-based command tree wired in `cmd/wiki-audio/main.go`
- Empty `internal/` packages (extract, chunk, tts, concat, id3, manifest,
  r2, feed, config, model, cli) with package docs but no logic yet
- Worker code migrated from old wiki location to `worker/` here
- `go build ./...` succeeds; `wiki-audio --help` prints all subcommands

## Why a separate repo (not a wiki subdir)

Three reasons (§1):
1. Tool's release cadence is independent of wiki content cadence.
2. Same CLI installs on multiple machines (work box, future machines)
   without dragging the wiki along.
3. Matches the install ergonomics of tools like beads_rust: one shell
   command, no clones, no source tree on the consuming machine.

## Why Go (not Python or Rust)

§8.5: Python ships via pipx/uv tool, which requires a Python toolchain
on the target. Go binary has zero runtime deps, cross-compiles cleanly,
ships at ~12 MB. Rust is even leaner but doubles project effort with no
quality win for this pipeline.

Trade-off accepted: Go has no `pysbd`-grade sentence segmenter. Mitigated
by paragraph-bounded chunking (§5.2) which is sufficient for PG-length
prose and avoids the need for sentence boundaries.

## Dependency choices (§8.6 — frozen until proven otherwise)

- cobra (CLI), BurntSushi/toml (config), godotenv (.env), minio-go/v7
  (R2 — ~3MB vs ~30MB for aws-sdk-go-v2), bogem/id3v2/v2 (ID3 tags),
  net/http + encoding/xml + crypto/sha256 + log/slog (stdlib).

## Gate

`go build ./...` succeeds; `wiki-audio --help` prints all subcommands;
`cd worker && wrangler deploy` still deploys the Worker.

## Full §8.5 alternative table (kept here so future-me doesn't re-debate)

| Option | Why we said no |
|--------|----------------|
| **Go** (chosen) | Single ~12 MB static binary, no runtime deps, cross-compile via `goreleaser`, matches beads_rust install ergonomics. |
| Python (pipx / uv tool) | Lowest cost to ship (richest libs: pysbd, pydantic, feedgen) BUT requires Python 3.11+ + a bootstrapper (`uv` or `pipx`) on the target. Fights the "single curl line" install goal. |
| Python (PyInstaller) | "Single binary" is really a bundled interpreter (~30–50 MB), slow startup, fragile with C extensions. Worst of both worlds: heavy AND brittle. |
| Rust | Even leaner than Go (~5–8 MB), but async ecosystem + audio/markdown libs less mature, doubling project effort with no quality win for this pipeline. Reconsider only if Go runs into limits we can't engineer around. |
| Node.js + pkg/SEA | Bundled binary ~40–50 MB, slow startup, distribution worse than Go for similar effort. |

Trade-off accepted with Go: no `pysbd`-grade sentence segmenter. Mitigated
by paragraph-bounded chunking (§5.2), which is sufficient for PG-length
prose and avoids needing sentence boundaries at all.

title: Create Jacob2017/wiki-audio private GitHub repo
description:
\`gh repo create Jacob2017/wiki-audio --private --clone\` on the dev
machine. Push an initial commit with just .gitignore (mirroring the one
at /data/projects/wiki-audio/.gitignore — exclude .env, example essays,
build artifacts, .cache/, *.mp3) and an empty README placeholder.

## Why private

Even though the code is mundane and the source is not the secret, we
publish enclosure URLs that contain the access token (it's stripped
before commit but referenced in scripts during development). Privacy
keeps the project boring and reduces scrutiny.

## Why the org/user "Jacob2017"

That's the user's GitHub handle. Hard-coded into the install URL
(\`raw.githubusercontent.com/Jacob2017/wiki-audio/main/install.sh\`).

2. `gh repo view Jacob2017/wiki-audio --json url -q .url` returns "https://github.com/Jacob2017/wiki-audio".
3. The local clone has at least one commit on `main` with non-empty author / committer.
4. Local clone has `.gitignore` listing AT MINIMUM: `.env`, `.env.*`, `*.mp3`, `.cache/`, `/wiki-audio` (the binary).

title: Initialize Go module: go mod init github.com/Jacob2017/wiki-audio
description:
\`go mod init github.com/Jacob2017/wiki-audio\` in the repo root.
Require Go 1.22+ in go.mod.

## Why Go 1.22+

- log/slog (1.21+) is the structured logging story we picked (§8.6).
- Improved range-over-func / iter behavior in 1.22 simplifies extractor
  loops if we want it later.
- 1.22 is well past the cutting edge — broad availability on Ubuntu LTS
  and Homebrew. No reason to constrain below.

Don't pin a higher version unless we adopt a stdlib feature only
available there.

## Acceptance criteria

Done = a `go.mod` exists at the repo root with these EXACT first two lines (modulo whitespace):

```
module github.com/Jacob2017/wiki-audio

go 1.22
```

Verifiable:
- `head -1 go.mod` matches `module github.com/Jacob2017/wiki-audio`.
- `grep -E '^go [0-9]+\.[0-9]+' go.mod` returns a line where the version is `1.22` or higher.
- `go build ./...` from the repo root succeeds (zero output, exit 0). Will trivially succeed since there's no Go code yet — that's fine; the toolchain is installed and the module path is parseable.

## Frozen choices — do not swap without a reason

§8.6 spells out the rationale for each. The trade we explicitly DECLINED:

- aws-sdk-go-v2 over minio-go: ~30 MB vs ~3 MB compiled. minio-go is

- resty/req over net/http: not needed for one external API.

## Verification

\`go mod tidy && go build ./...\` after this completes. Don't add any
other deps without explicit reason — keeping the surface small is the
whole point of the language choice.

2. Registers stub subcommands: \`init\`, \`doctor\`, \`build\`, \`publish\`,
   \`inspect\`, \`cost\`, \`upgrade\`.

disappear across versions, --help loses signal. Easier to stub all then
fill in.

subcommands. \`./wiki-audio doctor\` exits non-zero with \"not yet
