title: Write AGENTS.md (contributor onboarding surface)
description:
Write `AGENTS.md` at the repo root of `Jacob2017/wiki-audio` so a fresh
contributor (human or coding agent) can onboard from a single file and
pick up the conventions established across the polish loop. The README
(wa-lz9.2) is the user-facing manual; AGENTS.md is the contributor manual.

## Why this exists

The bead graph at `.beads/` is the implementation plan and is fully
self-contained per pass-10 verdict. AGENTS.md is the entry point that
tells a contributor where to find what — the index above the index.
Without it, a contributor must read 108 beads to discover the
conventions that the polish loop established.

## Required sections (8)

1. **Project orientation** (1 paragraph): what wiki-audio is, link to
   master bead `wa-hqn` for the "why", point at `PLAN_FOR_AUDIO_LIBRARY.md`
   in the wiki repo as the design doc.

2. **Workflow with `br`**: how to use `br ready` to find unblocked
   work, `br dep tree wa-hqn` to see the full graph, `br show <id>` to
   read a bead, and the canonical `BR_ACTOR=jacob` env var. Include the
   "modify beads only via `br` CLI; never edit `issues.jsonl` directly"
   rule from the polish-loop constraint.

3. **Coding conventions** — the patterns the polish loop pinned:
   - **Structured logging**: `log/slog` everywhere, secrets never logged
     (cross-link wa-76r.3). Tests use `slog.With("test", t.Name(), ...)`
     so failure logs are reproducible.
   - **Atomic local writes**: `os.CreateTemp` + `os.Rename` (cross-link
     wa-76r.2). All manifest / .env / config writes go through this
     helper. Never do a non-atomic `os.WriteFile` for state.
   - **Body-hash invariants** (cross-link wa-kyn.1, wa-kyn.9):
     `body_hash = sha256(body || voice_id || model_id ||
     footnote_policy_version)`. Concatenation is byte-level. Changing
     any input invalidates every essay. Bitrate is NOT in the hash —
     a format change requires `--force` rebuild.
   - **Manifest schema**: `schema_version` field (wa-76r.1 forward-compat
     guard). Refuse to load newer schemas; refuse to write degraded
     manifests.
   - **Cobra subcommand structure**: stub-and-fill pattern (wa-jlb.5).
     Every flag listed in §3 has an owning bead — see wa-hqn comment
     "CLI surface map".

4. **Test conventions** — the conventions pinned by passes 1, 2, 8:
   - **Three test tiers**: unit (always run, hermetic) → orchestration
     (R2 Fake + httptest ElevenLabs) → integration (opt-in via
     `WIKI_AUDIO_RUN_INTEGRATION=1` env var, see wa-76r.10).
   - **Integration-test gating**: `t.Helper()` `RequireIntegration(t)`
     skips when env unset; CI never burns credits by accident.
   - **Golden-file convention**: every golden regenerates via `go test
     ./... -update` (a SINGLE flag, not per-package — see wa-kyn.22).
   - **Structured-logging assertion**: tests assert log lines contain
     `test=<TestName>` so a CI failure log is greppable to the test
     that produced it.
   - **No `t.Skip()` without a reason string**: every skip names the
     missing precondition.

5. **Security posture** — the §9 threat model boundaries (cross-link
   wa-hqn's §9 section + wa-3ia + wa-76r.4):
   - Token rotation runbook: wa-76r.4. Token format: 32 bytes from
     `crypto/rand`, base64-url-NoPadding, exactly 43 chars.
   - constant-time compare (Worker timingSafeEqual): see embedded TS
     source on wa-3ia.1. Replacing with `===` is a regression.
   - The four §9.4 explicit acceptances (URL sharing, Cloudflare itself,
     compromised laptop, Pocket Casts logging). Anyone proposing OAuth /
     signed URLs / Cloudflare Access must explain which of the four
     moved from acceptable to unacceptable. See wa-hqn §9 section.
   - `.env` gets chmod 600; failing-closed check `mode & 0077 != 0`
     (wa-kyn.3).
   - Never log the access token, ElevenLabs API key, or any value from
     `.env`.

6. **Release & distribution** — cross-links to Phase C beads:
   - goreleaser matrix: linux/amd64+arm64, darwin/amd64+arm64 (wa-8gt.1).
   - install.sh: `uname` detect, sha256 verify, install to PATH (wa-8gt.3).
   - Three release tags: v0.0.1 (wa-8gt.6 — distribution smoke),
     v0.1.0 (wa-kyn.20 — Phase D milestone), v1.0.0 (wa-i1l.14 — Phase F
     gate). Post-tag verification checklist on each.

7. **What this project will NOT do** (cross-link wa-hqn "Out of scope"
   and wa-o2f deferred):
   - Insight/analysis pages (separate authoring vector).
   - Other authors (per-author voice/branding is post-v2).
   - The `audio: true` opt-in frontmatter (Phase I deferred).
   - Multi-feed (insights.xml — Phase I deferred).
   - Per-page voice override (Phase I deferred).

8. **Quick-start for a new contributor**:
   - Clone `Jacob2017/wiki-audio`.
   - Read `wa-hqn` (the master bead) — the canonical reference index is
     the single comment listing where every fact lives.
   - Run `br ready` — work the unblocked leaves.
   - When in doubt about a number/format/contract: `br show <id>` the
     owning bead BEFORE re-reading `PLAN_FOR_AUDIO_LIBRARY.md`. The
     bead graph is the source of truth; the plan is the provenance.

## Length and grep-verifiable content

- Length 200-400 lines (Reasonable upper bound; longer = bloating).
- Each of the 8 sections has a level-2 heading.
- Cross-link table: at least 12 distinct `wa-XXX` IDs cited (verify
  via `grep -oE 'wa-[a-z0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?' AGENTS.md | sort -u | wc -l`,
  must >= 12).
- `BR_ACTOR=jacob` appears verbatim.
- The 8-section ordering is stable: contributors who read it once and
  return for a refresh expect section 5 to be Security every time.

## What it should NOT be

- A duplicate of the master bead's content. AGENTS.md cites bead IDs;
  it does not embed their bodies. If a fact lives in a bead, link to
  the bead.
- A re-write of `PLAN_FOR_AUDIO_LIBRARY.md`. The plan is provenance;
  AGENTS.md is operating instructions.
- Marketing copy. This is the contributor manual.
- A tutorial. The README (wa-lz9.2) is the install + quickstart.

## Acceptance criteria

Done = `AGENTS.md` exists at repo root, committed to main, with:
- All 8 sections present with level-2 headings (verifiable via
  `grep -c '^## ' AGENTS.md` >= 8).
- Length 200-400 lines.
- At least 12 distinct `wa-XXX` IDs cited.
- The phrase `BR_ACTOR=jacob` appears verbatim at least once.
- The phrase `crypto/rand` appears in the security section.
- The phrase `WIKI_AUDIO_RUN_INTEGRATION` appears in the test section.
- No PLAN_FOR_AUDIO_LIBRARY.md content duplicated; only cited.
- A pull request reviewed by the human (one-author project; this is
  a self-review checkpoint).

## Why this is a Phase B (scaffold) bead

AGENTS.md must exist BEFORE Phase D extractor work can be picked up by
a fresh contributor. Phase B's gate (wa-jlb.6) currently is "go build
./... succeeds + wrangler deploy still works". Adding AGENTS.md to the
gate ensures the scaffold is genuinely usable as an onboarding surface,
not just a directory layout. Without this bead, a contributor can land
on the repo and have to read 108 beads to discover the conventions.

## Test plan

- `grep -c '^## ' AGENTS.md` returns >= 8.
- `wc -l AGENTS.md` returns 200-400.
- `grep -oE 'wa-[a-z0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?' AGENTS.md | sort -u | wc -l`
  returns >= 12.
- Manual: read AGENTS.md cold, then ask "where do I find the body_hash
  formula?" — answer must be in section 3 with a `wa-kyn.1` cross-link.
- Manual: read AGENTS.md cold, then ask "how do I run integration
  tests?" — answer must be in section 4 with the env var and wa-76r.10
  cross-link.

## Plan reference

PLAN_FOR_AUDIO_LIBRARY.md is the design doc; README.md (wa-lz9.2) is
the user manual; AGENTS.md is the contributor manual. Three documents,
three audiences, no overlap.

title: Phase D — Markdown extractor + chunker + dry-run
description:
# Phase D — Markdown → CleanedDocument → AudioChunks

Implements: PLAN_FOR_AUDIO_LIBRARY.md §5.1 (extraction), §5.2 (chunking),
§3 (init/doctor/build --dry-run subcommands).

## Goal

Given a raw Readwise-style markdown essay file, produce:
- `CleanedDocument{Body, BodyHash, CharCount, ...}` ready for TTS
- `[]AudioChunk` with paragraph-bounded segmentation, ≤4000 chars each
- A body hash that includes voice_id + model_id + footnote_policy_version
  so changing any of those auto-invalidates every essay (no manual cache
  busting).

Plus the supporting CLI surface that exercises this without calling any
external API:

- `wiki-audio init`           — scaffold ~/.wiki-audio/
- `wiki-audio doctor`         — verify config + reachability
- `wiki-audio build --dry-run` — extract + chunk + cost estimate, no API
- `wiki-audio build --extract-only` — print cleaned text to stdout

## Footnote handling — the central design choice

PG essays put `[N]` markers in the prose and definitions in a `**Notes**`
section at the end. Three options were considered:

1. **Skip footnotes entirely** — fastest to ship, but loses content.
2. **Read all footnotes at end of essay** — preserves content but the
   listener has forgotten what `[3]` referred to by then.
3. **Read footnotes at end of containing paragraph** — preserves context
   AND content. Listener has just finished the thought; the footnote
   elaborates; next paragraph begins.

**Chose (3).** §5.1 step 8 spells out the algorithm. Footnote markers are
stripped from prose; `Footnote N: <body>` lines are appended after the
paragraph that referenced them.

The extractor's invariants for edge cases (no Notes section, orphan
markers, doubly-referenced markers, link debris) are tabulated in §5.1
and must be implemented as unit tests.

## Why drop code blocks (rather than describe them)

§5.1: PG's code is often the *point* of a paragraph (Beating the
Averages, Revenge of the Nerds) but reads atrociously aloud. Better to
skip cleanly than mangle. Those essays can be read at desk.

## Gate

`wiki-audio build --extract-only --slug beating-the-averages` prints
clean text with code blocks dropped, footnotes appended at paragraph
ends, no formatting debris (no markdown links, no wikilink syntax, no

title: Implement internal/model/ data structs (§2)
description:
Translate §2 into Go structs in internal/model/:

- EssayMeta (slug, title, author, source_path, source_url, publish_date_text)
- CleanedDocument (Meta, Body, BodyHash, CharCount, WordCount, SkippedSegments)
- AudioChunk (Index, Text, CharCount)
- ManifestEntry (slug, title, body_hash, voice_id, model_id, char_count,
  chunk_count, duration_seconds, file_size_bytes, r2_key, r2_etag,
  generated_at, published_at)
- Manifest (Version, Entries map[string]ManifestEntry, LastBuildAt,
  LastPublishAt)
- Config (Wiki, TTS, R2, Feed) and the four sub-configs

JSON tags drive the on-the-wire manifest format; TOML tags drive the
config file format. Both encoders ship in stdlib + BurntSushi/toml.

## Schema versioning

Manifest.Version starts at 1. Older binaries that read a Manifest with
Version > known refuse to overwrite (§6 "Tool version mismatch"). This
is a one-line guard but a load-bearing one.

## Why JSON tags and TOML tags coexist on Config

We don't actually need Config to round-trip through JSON, but having
both tags adds zero runtime cost and lets us debug a loaded Config by
`json.Marshal`-ing it to stderr. Pure ergonomics.

## Body hash composition

`sha256(body || voice_id || model_id || footnote_policy_version)`.
The latter three are constants for v1 (Christopher voice, flash_v2_5,
"v1" footnote policy). The point is that ANY of them changing
auto-invalidates every essay — we never hand-bust caches.

## Body-hash byte-level definition (pass 10 — pin the formula form)

The exact byte sequence that goes into sha256 is:

    body_bytes ++ voice_id_bytes ++ model_id_bytes ++ footnote_policy_version_bytes

i.e. plain concatenation of the UTF-8 encoded strings, no separator,
no length-prefixing. Different bead descriptions have written this as
`body || voice_id || model_id || footnote_policy_version` (math-style
||) and `body + voice_id + model_id + footnote_policy_version`
(plus-style); both refer to the SAME operation: byte concatenation.

For v1 the trailing three are constants (the chosen voice_id, the model
id "eleven_flash_v2_5", and the policy version "v1"); changing any of
them changes the hash and auto-invalidates the cached MP3 (per pillar
#4 on wa-hqn). The exact Go implementation is:

    h := sha256.New()
    h.Write([]byte(body))
    h.Write([]byte(voiceID))
    h.Write([]byte(modelID))
    h.Write([]byte(footnotePolicyVersion))
    bodyHash := hex.EncodeToString(h.Sum(nil))

Tested by wa-kyn.9's test plan rows `body_hash_includes_voice_id`,
`body_hash_includes_model_id`, `body_hash_includes_policy_version`,
`body_hash_format_is_hex`.

title: Implement internal/chunk/ paragraph-bounded chunking (§5.2)
description:
Greedy paragraph-bounded chunker, max 4000 chars per chunk:

\`\`\`go
paragraphs := strings.Split(body, \"\\n\\n\")
var chunks []string
var cur strings.Builder
for _, p := range paragraphs {
    if cur.Len() + len(p) + 2 > maxChars && cur.Len() > 0 {
        chunks = append(chunks, strings.TrimSpace(cur.String()))
        cur.Reset()
    }
    cur.WriteString(p)
    cur.WriteString(\"\\n\\n\")
}
if cur.Len() > 0 { chunks = append(chunks, strings.TrimSpace(cur.String())) }
\`\`\`

## Why paragraph-bounded (NOT sentence-bounded)

§5.2: Mid-sentence breaks would produce audible glitches in concatenated
audio. Paragraph boundaries are natural pause points the listener
already expects. Avoids needing a Go equivalent of pysbd (no library at
that quality exists in Go).

## Why 4000 chars

ElevenLabs documents 5000 as the per-request limit for flash_v2_5; 4000
gives us comfortable headroom for prosody markers and avoids errors on
edge cases like \"4998 chars + a paragraph break\".

## Edge case: paragraph itself > maxChars (D11 covers fallback)

If any single paragraph is longer than 4000 chars, this chunker would
produce a chunk longer than the limit. D11 implements the sentence-style
fallback. For now, this task can ignore — D11 is its own bead.
close_reason: Shipped in d9a3a35. internal/chunk/{chunk,chunk_test}.go — 243 lines, 10 unit tests passing. Greedy paragraph-bounded chunker per §5.2; AudioChunk.CharCount uses runes (matches model.CleanedDocument.CharCount, keeps wa-kyn.22 sum-equality valid on em-dash essays); single-paragraph-too-long fallback deferred to wa-kyn.11 as documented.

title: Chunker fallback for overlong paragraphs (sentence-style split)
description:
If any paragraph exceeds 4000 chars, fall back to sentence-style split
on \`[.!?]\\s+(?=[A-Z])\`. Log a warning so we know it tripped. PG essays
rarely produce paragraphs that long, but a few do (long footnotes, dense
arguments).

## Why sentence-style only as fallback

We don't want sentence-mid splits in the common case (audible glitches).
But for an overlong paragraph, sentence boundaries are still better than
arbitrary character cuts, and the listener's experience already has a
mid-paragraph break either way.

## The regex isn't perfect

\`[.!?]\\s+(?=[A-Z])\` doesn't handle \"Mr. Smith\", abbreviations,
quotes, etc. We accept the imperfection because (a) this code path is
hit rarely, and (b) building a real sentence segmenter for one edge
case is wildly disproportionate. If we ever hit a tricky overlong
paragraph in PG's corpus, the fix is to manually break the paragraph
in the markdown source.
close_reason: Shipped in 2a5d34c. internal/chunk/{chunk,fallback,fallback_test}.go — 404 lines net, 23 tests passing (10 from wa-kyn.10 + 13 new). Sentence-split fallback per §5.2 step 5; uppercase-lookahead constraint enforced post-regex (Go RE2 has no lookahead). Single oversized sentence emitted as an overlong chunk per bead acceptance. WARN logged once per overlong paragraph with prefix snippet for corpus auditing.

title: Implement `wiki-audio init` (scaffold config dir, generate tokens)
description:
\`wiki-audio init\` creates:

1. \`~/.wiki-audio/\` directory (mkdir -p).
2. \`config.toml\` with placeholders + comments (commented examples for
   wiki source dir, voice ID, R2 bucket name, etc.).
3. \`.env\` with \`chmod 600\` and empty values for the four required
   env vars.

If files already exist, prompt before overwriting. \`--force\` bypasses
the prompt for non-interactive use.

## Token generation

If \`WIKI_AUDIO_ACCESS_TOKEN\` is empty in the existing .env (or the
file is being created fresh), generate a token via crypto/rand:

\`\`\`go
b := make([]byte, 32)
rand.Read(b)
token := base64.URLEncoding.WithPadding(base64.NoPadding).EncodeToString(b)
\`\`\`

Yields a 43-char URL-safe string matching the format from §9.1. Print
it once, instruct the user to also store the token in 1Password and as
the Cloudflare Worker secret \`ACCESS_TOKEN\`.

## Output

Final message: \"next: edit config.toml and populate .env, then run
\`wiki-audio doctor\`\".

## --env-local flag

\`--env-local\` is a new boolean flag (mutually exclusive with
\`--env <path>\`) that overrides the env-file path to
\`<cwd>/.env\` — i.e. loads \`.env\` from the current working
directory instead of \`~/.wiki-audio/.env\`. Useful for development
runs where the project-local \`.env\` should win over the user's
global config.
close_reason: Shipped in fcb5c09. internal/cli/{init,init_test}.go — 682 lines, 14 tests. mkdir -p ~/.wiki-audio/ → write config.toml from template → generate 32-byte/43-char crypto/rand token → write .env chmod 0o600 with token + empty placeholder vars → print 3-line §3 summary + token mirror instructions. Idempotent: refuse-without-force on populated files, surgical top-up when only token line is empty (preserves operator-entered API keys), --force regenerates everything. envHasFilledToken treats whitespace-only as empty for typo recovery.

title: Implement `wiki-audio doctor` (full health check)
description:
Diagnostics before any real work. Runs all 7 checks; exits non-zero at the end if any check failed (full diagnostic in one shot — see the pass-6 comment for fail-aggregation rationale).

Checks:
1. config.toml present + valid TOML + required keys present.
2. .env present + chmod 600 + 4 required env vars populated.
3. ffmpeg in PATH (\`exec.LookPath\`).
4. Wiki source dir exists, contains *.md files, count is reasonable
   (>0 — preferably print the count).
5. ElevenLabs API: GET /v1/user authenticates; voice configured by
   voice_id is reachable; report remaining credits on the plan.
6. R2: HEAD on bucket succeeds (auth + bucket exists).
7. Worker access contract: bare URL → 403, wrong token → 403, correct
   token + missing key path → 404. (Three curl-equivalent http calls.)

Output format: each check on a line, ✓ or ✗, with a short status. The
example in §3 (\"all checks passed.\") is the target shape.

## Why doctor is its own command (not a flag on every command)

Discoverability. New install → \`init\` → \`doctor\` → \`build\`. Three
commands map to three setup steps and the user can think about them
separately.
close_reason: Shipped in 3445824. internal/cli/{doctor,doctor_test}.go — 1050 net lines, 17 tests. Implements §3 seven-check matrix with fail-aggregation (no short-circuit), skip-not-fail for prereq failures, U+2713/U+2717 glyphs at 20-char label pad, humanCommas + UTF-8-safe shorten helpers. doctorOpts injects URLs for httptest stubs on ElevenLabs/Worker; minio-go path covered only at construction (full S3 mock out of scope, lives in wa-3ia.5). Worker probe path is timestamped to avoid collision with real R2 keys.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## §3 sample output (polish pass 6) — pin the full check list

Verbatim target from §3 — this is the contract for what `doctor` checks AND the line format:

```
$ wiki-audio doctor
config.toml         ✓ /home/jacobuntu/.config/wiki-audio/config.toml
.env                ✓ all 4 required env vars present
ffmpeg              ✓ ffmpeg version 6.1.1
wiki source dir     ✓ 53 .md files at /home/jacobuntu/dev/wiki/Wiki/raw/processed/paul-graham
ElevenLabs API      ✓ authenticated, voice "Christopher" reachable, 487,222 credits remaining on plan
R2 bucket           ✓ wiki-audio (private, 0 objects)
worker access       ✓ https://wiki-audio.jabyrne.workers.dev returns 403 without token, 404 with token
all checks passed.
```

## Format contract

- One line per check.
- Left column: check label (~20-char left-pad).
- Glyph: `✓` (U+2713) on pass, `✗` (U+2717) on fail.
- Right column: short status (path / count / version / etc).
- Final line on full success: `all checks passed.`
- On any failure: print failing line(s); final line: `N of 7 checks failed.`; exit code 1.

## Exit codes

- 0 — all 7 checks passed
- 1 — any check failed (still print every check; no fail-fast — the user wants the full diagnostic in one shot)

## Failure output sample (synthesized — pin in implementation)

```
$ wiki-audio doctor
config.toml         ✓ /home/jacobuntu/.config/wiki-audio/config.toml
.env                ✗ missing ELEVENLABS_API_KEY
ffmpeg              ✓ ffmpeg version 6.1.1
wiki source dir     ✗ 0 .md files at /home/jacobuntu/dev/wiki/Wiki/raw/processed/paul-graham
ElevenLabs API      - skipped (no API key)
R2 bucket           ✗ s3.SigV4 unauthorized: invalid key id
worker access       ✓ https://wiki-audio.jabyrne.workers.dev returns 403 without token
3 of 7 checks failed.
```

`-` (U+2010) marker for skipped checks (dependency missing).

## Why no fail-fast

The user invoked `doctor` to learn what's broken. Bailing on the first
failure means a second-issue check (e.g. ffmpeg missing AND .env empty)
takes two runs to surface. Always run all 7; fail at the end.

title: Implement `wiki-audio build --dry-run`
description:
Walks the source dir, runs extractor + chunker on every essay, prints:

- Per-essay: char count after cleaning, chunk count, dropped segments.
- Total: chars across all essays, estimated credits (Flash v2.5: 0.5
  credits/char), estimated $ cost on Pro tier.

NO API calls. NO MP3 generation. Used for cost preflight before bulk
runs and for verifying extractor output without spending credits.

## Why the cost estimate matters

§7 Phase G: if the pre-flight cost exceeds 500k credits (vs. expected
~440k), STOP and investigate. A regression in the extractor (e.g.
accidentally including the Metadata block) inflates char count and is
the most likely cause.

## Test Plan

Tests in `internal/cmd/build_test.go` (or wherever the cobra
subcommand lives) using a small fixture dir with the 3 example essays
already on hand:

| Test name                              | Expectation |
|----------------------------------------|-------------|
| dry_run_makes_no_network_calls         | RoundTripper that fails any HTTP request; test passes |
| dry_run_creates_no_files               | tmp-watching helper; assert no files written |
| dry_run_uses_no_credits                | output reports >0 estimated credits; integration tests confirm 0 actual |
| dry_run_per_essay_lines                | each of 3 essays shown with char + chunk counts |
| dry_run_total_estimate                 | sum-of-chars × 0.5 == estimated credits |
| dry_run_handles_extractor_skip         | malformed essay reports skip; counted separately |
| dry_run_with_slug_filter               | --slug X narrows to one essay |
| dry_run_exit_zero_always               | exit code 0 even with extractor warnings |
| stable_across_runs                     | same essays → same output bytes (golden) |

## Golden file for dry-run output

`testdata/build/golden_dry_run_3essays.txt` captures the expected
stdout. Regenerate via `-update`. Catches accidental output format
changes that would break the (eventual) `wiki-audio cost`-vs-dry-run
parity check.

## Structured logging during tests

slog.With("test", t.Name(), "phase", "dry-run", "n_essays", n).
Test asserts that no log line contains "uploading" or
"calling elevenlabs" or other live-action verbs.

## Extractor-regression check during dry-run (added by polish pass 2)

Per §6 "Extractor regression": dry-run is the active defense site.
After fetching the previous manifest from R2 (read-only — dry-run
never writes), for every essay where new body_hash != previous
body_hash:

    if previous != nil and new.CharCount < 0.5 * previous.CharCount:
        diagnostic: "slug=X cleaned chars dropped from N to M (>50%);
                     review extraction with --extract-only --slug X"
        exit code 2 (regression detected; not a hard error)

If --force-regression is passed, downgrade to a warning and exit 0.

If there is NO previous manifest (first run), skip the regression
check and log "first build — regression check skipped".

## Test rows for the regression check

| Test name                              | Setup                                  | Expectation |
|----------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|-------------|
| regression_detected_aborts             | prev CharCount=10000, new=4000         | exit code 2; slug + numbers in stderr |
| regression_within_threshold_passes     | prev CharCount=10000, new=6000 (40% drop) | exit code 0 |
| regression_force_overrides             | --force-regression flag set            | exit code 0; warning logged |
| no_previous_manifest_skips_check       | empty R2                               | exit code 0; "first build" logged |
| new_essay_no_comparison                | slug not in prev manifest              | exit code 0; treated as new |

comments.text:
## §3 sample output (polish pass 6) — pin dry-run cost estimate format

Verbatim target from §3 for `wiki-audio build --dry-run`:

```
$ wiki-audio build --dry-run
estimate: 880,344 chars × 0.5 credits/char (flash_v2_5) = 440,172 credits
estimate: ~$87 on Pro tier overage; fits within Pro monthly quota
```

Two summary lines plus the per-essay extraction details (chars + chunks +
dropped segments, identical to the build-pipeline format from wa-4cw.5
but WITHOUT the "generated …mp3" line).

## Format contract

Line 1 — credits:
```
estimate: <total-chars> chars × <credits-per-char> credits/char (<model>) = <total-credits> credits
```

Line 2 — dollars + tier guidance:
```
estimate: ~$<dollars> on <tier> tier overage; <plan-fit-message>
```

Where `<plan-fit-message>` is one of:
- `fits within Pro monthly quota` (≤500k credits)
- `exceeds Pro; Scale tier required for one-shot run` (>500k, ≤2M)
- `requires multi-month split or Enterprise quote` (>2M)

## Interaction with --slug

`wiki-audio build --dry-run --slug X` narrows to one essay; the estimate
lines reflect just that essay's chars. Useful for sanity-checking a single
essay's cost in isolation.

## Why two lines (credits + dollars) instead of one

Credits are the unit ElevenLabs bills in. Dollars are the unit the user
budgets in. Showing both forces the user to internalize the conversion
(0.5 credits/char × $99/500k credits ≈ $0.0001/char) so that future
tier-shopping feels concrete.

title: Implement `wiki-audio cost` subcommand
description:
A standalone cost calculator, separate from build --dry-run. Reports:

- Char count across all essays.
- Cost on flash_v2_5 (0.5 credits/char) → fits Pro \$99/mo.
- Cost on multilingual_v2 (1 credit/char) → Scale \$330/mo OR Pro × 2 months.

Sample output in §3:

  cleaned chars across 53 essays: 880,344
  flash_v2_5  (0.5 credits/char): 440,172 credits → fits Pro \$99/mo
  multilingual_v2 (1 credit/char): 880,344 credits → Scale \$330/mo

## Why a separate command (vs. just --dry-run)

cost is an answer to \"should I subscribe?\" — a tier-level question.
build --dry-run answers \"will THIS run blow my budget?\" — a per-run
question. Different audiences, different framings; same underlying
calculation, but the surface is worth keeping distinct.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## §3 sample output + flag clarification (polish pass 6)

§3 shows ONLY `wiki-audio cost --all`:

```
$ wiki-audio cost --all
cleaned chars across 53 essays: 880,344
flash_v2_5  (0.5 credits/char): 440,172 credits → fits Pro $99/mo
multilingual_v2 (1 credit/char): 880,344 credits → Scale $330/mo (1 month) or Pro $99 × 2
```

## What `cost` (no flag) does, vs `cost --all`

- `wiki-audio cost`: report on the manifest entries currently in scope —
  i.e., what's already been built and tracked. Useful when iterating
  ("how much have I spent so far?").
- `wiki-audio cost --all`: walk the source dir AND extract everything
  fresh, then report. This is what §3 shows; this is the "should I
  subscribe to Pro?" answer because it covers essays not yet built.

If the manifest is empty (fresh install, never built), `cost` (no flag)
prints:

```
manifest empty — run `wiki-audio cost --all` to estimate from source
```

…and exits 0.

## Format contract — three lines for --all

Line 1: `cleaned chars across N essays: <total-chars>`
Line 2: `flash_v2_5  (0.5 credits/char): <credits> credits → <plan-message>`
Line 3: `multilingual_v2 (1 credit/char): <credits> credits → <plan-message>`

Plan messages mirror wa-kyn.14's plan-fit-message but framed at the tier
level (which subscription tier covers this run on a monthly basis).

## Why both flags exist (vs. just one of them)

`cost` (no flag) is fast — no extraction needed; just reads manifest.
`cost --all` requires walking + extracting all source files (~seconds).
The latency difference matters for a tier-decision question that the
user might run repeatedly.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
# wa-kyn.19 validation report — Phase D extractor against 3 example essays

Validated by pane-5 against examples/ on 2026-05-08. Methodology: a
small in-tree Go harness (now removed) imported `internal/extract`,
`internal/chunk`, `internal/model` directly and ran the full §5.1
pipeline (Parse → SplitNotes → ParseFootnotes → StripMarkdown →
WeaveFootnotes → Finalize → Chunk) on each .md under
`/data/projects/wiki-audio/examples/`. The CLI flag
`build --extract-only` (wa-kyn.15) is not yet wired, so direct
package use was the practical path.

## Per-essay results

### 1. `How to Do Great Work.md` (PG, large, 29 footnotes)

- Title parsed: `"How to Do Great Work"` ✓
- Metadata block + Full Document marker stripped cleanly ✓
- 29 footnote definitions parsed; 29 `Footnote N:` lines emitted in
  body ✓
- Footnote weaving sample (Footnote 1): body shows
  `…aptitude for and great interest in.` (blank line)
  `Footnote 1: I don't think you could give a precise definition…`
  — paragraph-attributed per §5.1 step 8 ✓
- No `## Metadata`, `## Full Document`, `](http`, `![`, `[[`, or
  ``` ``` `` ``` ` ` debris ✓
- 67141 chars, 11829 words, 18 chunks
- Sum of chunk char counts = 67106; expected delta = 2×(N−1) = 34;
  actual delta = 35. Off-by-one — see Finding F4.

### 2. `High Agency — In 30 Minutes.md` (non-PG, no footnotes, many images)

- Title parsed: `"High Agency"` (the `# High Agency` line; subtitle
  `In 30 Minutes` follows — see Finding F2)
- 0 footnotes parsed ✓
- 0 fenced code blocks; 0 `SkippedSegments`
- Body starts with `# High Agency\nIn 30 Minutes\n\n.png)\n\n…` —
  the `.png)` is leftover image-strip debris. See Finding F3.
- 45156 chars, 7856 words, 13 chunks
- Sum = 45132; delta 24 = 2×12 ✓ (consistent)

### 3. `How to Get Startup Ideas.md` (non-Readwise, frontmatter)

- **PARSE ERROR**: `extract: missing '## Metadata' header (file is
  not a Readwise canonical export)`
- File uses YAML frontmatter (`---\ntitle:…\n---`), not Readwise
  `## Metadata` / `## Full Document` headers
- Has a `**Notes**` section with `\[N\]` (escaped brackets) markers
- Bead description claimed this essay had code blocks; visual
  inspection found none
- **Phase D gate cannot validate this essay end-to-end as shipped.**
  See Finding F1.

## Findings

### [HIGH] F1 — Extractor refuses YAML-frontmatter essays

`extract.ParseFile` requires Readwise's `## Metadata` and
`## Full Document` headers (`extract.go:86-91`). The
`How to Get Startup Ideas.md` example uses YAML frontmatter and is
rejected outright. One in three Phase D fixtures cannot pass the
gate.

Options:
1. Teach the extractor to recognize YAML frontmatter as an
   alternative metadata format (parse + drop, then strip the
   `---` fences).
2. Normalize the example fixture to Readwise format (rewrite the
   file).
3. Tighten the corpus contract to "Readwise-only" and flag the
   non-conforming example as out-of-scope.

Recommendation: option 1. The PLAN says "uniform corpus" but the
corpus the user actually has is mixed. A tolerant frontmatter parser
is ~30 lines and unblocks any future PG essay imported via a
non-Readwise path.

### [HIGH] F2 — `# Title` heading line survives into Body

`extract.Parse` captures the title from the `# Title` line but does
NOT remove that line from the body. Both shipped essays render the
title twice when read aloud:

- `How to Do Great Work` body: `# How to Do Great Work\n\nJuly 2023…`
- `High Agency` body: `# High Agency\nIn 30 Minutes\n\n.png)…`

The TTS will speak "Hash How to Do Great Work" or pause and re-read
the heading. On a 1-hour essay, the dual-render is unmistakable.

`stripReadwiseHeaders` in `extract.go:72-96` drops only the metadata
block; it leaves headings (including the `# Title`) in place. Fix:
when `firstHeading` succeeds, drop the matched line from the body
before returning.

Cross-reference: PLAN §5.1 step 2 says
`title = first line matching ^# (.+)$` — that's a capture
instruction; the spec doesn't say to KEEP the line. Implementer
chose conservative; should be removed.

### [HIGH] F3 — Image regex breaks on `(...)` in URLs (Substack/CDN paths)

`strip.go:12` defines `imageRe = !\[[^\]]*\]\([^)]*\)`. The `[^)]*`
stops at the first `)`. `High Agency` has image URLs like
`...High%20Agency%20(2).png`, where `(2)` produces an embedded `)`.
The regex matches up through that early `)` and the trailing
`.png)` is left as text.

Result in body:
```
# High Agency
In 30 Minutes

.png)

**Warning: This is not doom scrolling.** ...
```

Two of the eleven image refs in the file have parens-in-URL; both
leave debris. The other nine images strip cleanly because their
URLs use only `%XX`-encoded specials.

Fix: tolerate one level of nested parens, e.g.
`!\[[^\]]*\]\(([^()]*\([^)]*\))*[^)]*\)`, or scan to the line-end
`)` (`!\[[^\]]*\][^\n]*\)$`) — context-aware.

### [MEDIUM] F4 — Sum-of-chunks vs body delta is off-by-one on
`How to Do Great Work`

Body chars: 67141. Sum of chunk `CharCount`: 67106. Delta: 35.
With 18 chunks, expected delta = 2×17 = 34 (one `\n\n` trimmed at
each chunk boundary). Off-by-one.

`High Agency`: delta = 24 = 2×12 across 13 chunks ✓.

Likely cause: a chunk has trailing whitespace inside it (not at the
boundary) that survives the chunker's `TrimSpace`. Or one paragraph
ends with extra spaces that the rune-count differs from. Minor —
won't break TTS — but worth a closer look before wa-kyn.22's
`total_chunk_chars_match_body` golden assertion is locked in.

### [LOW] F5 — wa-kyn.19 bead text is wrong about `How to Get Startup Ideas`

The bead says this essay exercises code-block stripping (D7d). The
file has zero fenced code blocks. Either the bead text is stale
(was written before the file was selected) or the file shown is not
the one the bead author had in mind. Update the bead description
when fixing F1.

### [INFO] F6 — Footnote weaving on `How to Do Great Work` is correct

29 of 29 footnote definitions land as `Footnote N:` lines after
their referencing paragraph, in order. Spot-checked Footnote 1 — it
lands after "…aptitude for and great interest in." separated by a
blank line. §5.1 step 8 contract honored.

## Phase D gate verdict

**Not ready to cut v0.1.0** as defined by wa-kyn.20 unless F1, F2,
F3 are addressed. F1 alone disqualifies one of the three required
example essays. F2 ships an audibly-bad title dual-render. F3 leaks
visible debris into the most easily inspected essay.

F4 is non-blocking but should be diagnosed before wa-kyn.22 locks a
golden.

## Recommended next beads

- **F1, F2, F3 → fix in `internal/extract/`** before wa-kyn.20.
  Each is a small surgical change. F2 and F3 are 1-2 lines each;
  F1 is ~30 lines for tolerant frontmatter parsing.
- After fixes land, re-run this validation harness. The harness is
  worth keeping — propose folding it into wa-kyn.22's e2e test
  bead so Phase D regressions surface in CI rather than via manual
  spot-check.

— pane-5

title: Implement internal/config/ TOML loader
description:
Load \`~/.wiki-audio/config.toml\` (override with --config) into
the Config struct from D1. Apply defaults from §2:

- TTSConfig.ModelID         = \"eleven_flash_v2_5\"
- TTSConfig.ChunkMaxChars   = 4000
- TTSConfig.RequestTimeoutS = 60
- TTSConfig.RetryAttempts   = 3
- TTSConfig.RetryBackoffBase= 2
- TTSConfig.OutputFormat    = \"mp3_44100_64\"
- FeedConfig.FeedPath       = \"pg.xml\"
- FeedConfig.Language       = \"en-us\"

Validation:
- WikiConfig.SourceDir must exist and be a directory (refuse otherwise).
- TTSConfig.VoiceID must be non-empty.
- R2Config.AccountID + Bucket must be non-empty.
- FeedConfig.BaseURL must be a valid URL.

If any required field is missing, return an error pointing at the
offending TOML key. \`wiki-audio doctor\` surfaces these errors.

## Why TOML and not YAML

§2: \"TOML is checked-in-friendly... we'd want to track voice ID changes
if config were git-tracked.\" YAML's whitespace fragility burns us
eventually; TOML doesn't. Also: BurntSushi/toml is the most mature TOML
lib in Go, struct-tag-driven, no surprises.

LoadConfig(path) returns *model.Config with §2 defaults applied via model.Default* constants (single source of truth) and required-field validation pointing at TOML keys. Unknown keys WARN instead of fail (forward-compat).

title: Cut v0.1.0 release (Phase D milestone)
description:
Tag v0.1.0 and let goreleaser publish. Re-install on the wiki box.

Now \`wiki-audio init\`, \`doctor\`, \`build --dry-run\`,
\`build --extract-only\`, and \`cost\` all work. No TTS yet — Phase E.

## Why a release here (not just on main)

Phase D ends with a meaningful user-facing capability — extraction is
done, dry-run cost estimates are real. Tagging v0.1.0 lets us pin to
this version on the wiki box if Phase E breaks something during
development. Cheap insurance.

## Acceptance criteria — post-tag verification

Done = ALL of the following observable AFTER `git push origin v0.1.0`:

1. `gh release view v0.1.0` shows 4 tarballs + checksums.txt; `gh run list --workflow=release.yml --limit 1` returned "success".
2. On the wiki box, re-run install.sh; `wiki-audio --version` prints `v0.1.0 (commit ...)`.
3. Each of the five Phase D commands runs successfully on the wiki box:
   - `wiki-audio init --force` (in a scratch $XDG_CONFIG_HOME) → exits 0; populates 3 files.
   - `wiki-audio doctor` → exits 0; all checks pass (or only the TTS / R2 ones reference Phase E/F surfaces — those should still pass since the live tokens are configured).
   - `wiki-audio build --dry-run` → exits 0; prints the 2-line cost estimate.
   - `wiki-audio build --extract-only --slug how-to-do-great-work` → exits 0; produces a clean extract.
   - `wiki-audio cost` → exits 0; prints summary (likely empty manifest pre-Phase F, that's fine).
4. No subcommand from later phases (`build` without flags, `publish`) succeeds — they should still print "not yet implemented" or skip TTS. Confirms the version is a Phase D milestone, not a Phase E preview.

Fail path: same as wa-8gt.6 — delete tag + release, fix, re-tag. v0.1.0 can be re-cut without semver consequence as long as no third party has pinned to it (we have none).

title: End-to-end test harness for extract → chunk pipeline using 3 real essays + golden files
description:
A test suite in `internal/e2e/extract_chunk_test.go` (or a similar
location) that runs the real extractor and chunker against the three
example essays already on disk at `/data/projects/wiki-audio/`:

- `How to Do Great Work.md`         (large; many footnotes; exercises wa-kyn.8)
- `How to Get Startup Ideas.md`     (medium; code blocks; exercises wa-kyn.7)
- `High Agency — In 30 Minutes.md`  (non-PG author; exercises author-agnostic logic)

These are real PG-style markdown files with footnotes. They are
deliberately NOT mocked or stubbed. The test calls extract.Extract +
chunk.Chunk in-process and asserts on the output.

## Critical: NO external API calls

This e2e harness exercises only the offline pipeline (extract, chunk,
hash, cost-estimate). It does NOT call ElevenLabs, R2, or the Worker.
Those live in dedicated integration beads (see wa-4cw.12, wa-i1l.18).
This test is fast, hermetic, and runs in normal CI.

## Test Plan

For each of the three essays:

| Assertion                              | Expectation |
|----------------------------------------|-------------|
| extraction_succeeds                    | no error, CleanedDocument non-empty |
| body_hash_stable_across_runs           | same input → same hash |
| body_hash_changes_with_voice_id        | different voice → different hash (key invariant from wa-kyn.1) |
| char_count_within_expected_band        | per-essay expected range (encoded as constants) |
| word_count_within_expected_band        | per-essay expected range |
| no_markdown_link_syntax_in_body        | regex `\]\(http` not present |
| no_image_ref_in_body                   | regex `!\[` not present |
| no_wikilink_braces                     | `[[` and `]]` not present |
| no_metadata_block                      | "## Metadata" string not present |
| no_full_document_block                 | "## Full Document" string not present |
| footnote_lines_appear                  | at least one "Footnote " line for essays with notes |
| no_orphan_footnote_markers             | `[1]` `[2]` ... not present in standalone form |
| chunks_each_under_max_chars            | every AudioChunk.CharCount ≤ 4000 |
| chunks_paragraph_bounded               | no chunk starts mid-sentence (heuristic: starts with capital or quote) |
| total_chunk_chars_match_body           | sum(chunks) == CharCount (modulo trim whitespace) |
| skipped_segments_match_expected        | per-essay expected count |

## Golden files

For each essay, check in:

- `testdata/extract/golden/<slug>.cleaned.txt`     — the cleaned body
- `testdata/extract/golden/<slug>.meta.json`       — the EssayMeta
- `testdata/extract/golden/<slug>.skipped.txt`     — list of skipped segments
- `testdata/extract/golden/<slug>.chunks.json`     — the chunk array

Tests assert byte-for-byte equality with the goldens. Regenerate via:

  go test ./internal/e2e -run TestExtractChunkGolden -update

The `-update` flag is the project-wide convention; same flag in feed
tests (wa-i1l.15) and any future golden suite.

## Source-of-truth fixtures

The three essays live at the repo root today, but the harness needs
them in a stable location for CI. Plan: at the start of the test suite,
SETUP copies them from a `testdata/essays/` directory checked into the
repo. The SOURCE files are the canonical fixtures going forward —
the live ones in /data/projects/wiki-audio/ are the user's working
copies.

Step 1 of this bead: copy the three essays into `testdata/essays/` and
git-add them. Step 2: build the harness. Step 3: regenerate goldens
once and lock them in.

## Structured logging during tests

```go
slog.With(
  "test", t.Name(),
  "essay_slug", slug,
  "char_count", doc.CharCount,
  "chunk_count", len(chunks),
)
```

On any failure, dump the offending essay's CleanedDocument body to
the test log so the failure is reproducible from the artifact.

## Why three essays minimum

The plan §7 (Phase D gate) calls out exactly these three because they
collectively exercise: heavy footnotes, code-blocks, and
non-PG-author edge cases. A subset would leave gaps. More would be
diminishing returns until we have ALL 53 essays in Phase G.

## Why golden files instead of property assertions only

Property assertions catch obvious regressions (empty body, missing
fields). Goldens catch subtle ones (a regex change that silently
swallows an extra space, a footnote weave reorder). Both, not either.

## Diff-friendly goldens

Cleaned text is plain UTF-8 with consistent line endings. JSON goldens
use indent=2 + sorted keys (json.MarshalIndent + manual key sort) so
diffs in PR review are line-by-line readable.

title: Implement internal/config/ .env loader (godotenv) + chmod 600 enforcement
description:
Load \`~/.wiki-audio/.env\` (override with --env) via godotenv.

Required env vars:
- ELEVENLABS_API_KEY
- R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID
- R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
- WIKI_AUDIO_ACCESS_TOKEN (embedded into feed enclosure URLs at gen time)

Plus optional:
- R2_TOKEN (the .env we received also has this — used by some Cloudflare
  client paths but not by minio-go; treat as informational unless
  needed)

## chmod 600 enforcement (§6)

Stat the .env file before loading. If the mode bits indicate it is
group- or world-readable (mode & 0077 != 0), refuse to start with a
loud error: \"refusing to load .env: file is readable by other users.
Run: chmod 600 ~/.wiki-audio/.env\".

## Why this guard exists

Plenty of projects ship .env files with chmod 644 because the user
forgot. Failing closed prevents the API key from being readable by
another user on a shared machine. Cheap defense.

## Never log the secrets

slog redaction: when logging Config, redact .env values. Trivial today
because Config doesn't embed secrets — they live in os.Getenv. Just be
careful never to add Secret fields to Config and log them.

title: Extractor — read file, parse title, drop Metadata + Full Document headers (§5.1 steps 1-4)
description:
First-pass extraction following §5.1 steps 1-4:

1. Read the file as UTF-8.
2. \`title = first line matching \`^# (.+)$\`\`. If absent, fall back to
   the filename's title-cased stem.
3. Drop everything from \`## Metadata\` to the line before \`## Full Document\`.
4. Drop the \`## Full Document\` header line itself.

Result: the rest of the buffer is \`raw_body\`, ready for steps 5-9.

## Why \"## Metadata\" and \"## Full Document\" specifically

These are Readwise's canonical Markdown export headers. Every essay in
\`raw/processed/paul-graham/\` follows the pattern. Verify by inspecting
3 example essays at planning/.

If a future essay doesn't follow the pattern, the extractor should fail
loudly (raw_body is empty) so we notice. Better that than silently
including the metadata in the audio.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
[pane-2] Implementation complete in internal/extract/extract.go + 11 hermetic unit tests in extract_test.go.

## Public API

```go
type Parsed struct {
    Title   string
    RawBody string
}

func ParseFile(path string) (Parsed, error)
func Parse(content, name string) (Parsed, error)
```

`Parse` is the testable core; `ParseFile` is the os.ReadFile wrapper. Downstream beads (wa-kyn.5+) consume `Parsed.RawBody`.

## Behaviour against §5.1 steps 1-4

1. Read UTF-8 (BOM stripped if present, CRLF tolerated).
2. Title: `(?m)^# (.+)$` regex against the buffer; first match wins. Falls back to a title-cased filename stem (replaces - and _ with space, capitalises each word). The fallback is naive about function words ('to', 'the', etc.) — flagged in the doc comment, fires only for malformed input where the result is replaceable.
3. Drop `## Metadata` line through line BEFORE `## Full Document` (header line included; metadata bullets included; trailing blank before Full Document included).
4. Drop the `## Full Document` header line itself.

Header matching trims trailing whitespace so `## Metadata   ` still matches the canonical form.

If either header is missing the function returns an error mentioning the missing header — extractor fails loudly, raw_body never silently includes metadata.

The `# Title` line itself is preserved in RawBody. Downstream markdown stripping (wa-kyn.7) handles heading markers in the body.

title: Extractor — split prose vs Notes section (§5.1 step 5)
description:
Split raw_body at the FIRST occurrence of either \`**Notes**\` or
\`## Notes\` (case-insensitive, near end of essay):

- prose_part = everything BEFORE that heading
- notes_part = everything AFTER (may be empty if essay has no footnotes)

## Why two heading forms

Readwise's exports have varied between bold-text \"**Notes**\" and
proper heading \"## Notes\" depending on era / source format. Both
appear in the corpus.

## Edge case

If neither heading exists, prose_part = raw_body, notes_part = \"\".
Step 6 will produce an empty footnote_map; step 8 becomes a no-op.
Mark as \"normal\" — many essays have no footnotes.

[pane-2] SplitNotes shipped on top of wa-kyn.4's Parse contract.

## Public API

```go
func SplitNotes(rawBody string) (prose, notes string)
```

Lives in internal/extract/extract.go alongside Parse/ParseFile. Consumers (wa-kyn.6 onwards) call `SplitNotes(parsed.RawBody)` to get the two halves.

## Algorithm

Walk RawBody line-by-line. For each line, take `strings.TrimSpace(line)` and case-insensitively compare against the two canonical markers:
- `**Notes**`  (older Readwise bold-text export)
- `## Notes`   (modern h2 heading)

First match splits: prose = everything before, notes = everything after, marker line itself is dropped (appears in neither).

If neither marker is found: prose = rawBody, notes = "".

Variants like `## Notes:`, `### Notes`, `** Notes **`, mid-line occurrences, etc. are deliberately NOT matched — exact form (after trim + casefold) is the only signal.

## Smoke against real essays (now-removed test)

Updated wa-kyn.4's Parsed.RawBody comment to point at SplitNotes for the next step.

## To wa-kyn.6 (next step in chain)

The notes_part is `notes` from `prose, notes := SplitNotes(parsed.RawBody)`. Note that `notes` may have a leading newline (the line right after the marker) and a trailing newline (file's final \\n). Trim before parsing footnote bodies if needed.

title: Extractor — parse footnote_map from notes_part (§5.1 step 6)
description:
Parse notes_part into \`map[int]string\` of footnote definitions.

Each note starts with \`[N] \` on its own line; body continues until the
next \`[M] \` line or the end of notes_part. Strip leading/trailing
whitespace from each body. Drop malformed entries silently.

## Implementation hints

A line-by-line scan with a small state machine works well. Regex
\`^\\[(\\d+)\\]\\s+(.*)\` against each line; on match, flush the previous
note, start a new one. On no match, append to the current note's body.

## Why drop malformed entries silently

PG's notes are hand-typed and occasionally have OCR-style typos. We do
not want a single typo to abort the whole essay. Log at debug level so
we can audit if needed.

## Edge case

A note may itself contain bracketed numbers like \"see [1] above\". The
regex must match ONLY at line start, not arbitrary positions.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
[pane-2] ParseFootnotes shipped on top of wa-kyn.5's SplitNotes.

## Public API

```go
func ParseFootnotes(notesPart string) map[int]string
```

In internal/extract/footnote.go. Consumers (wa-kyn.8 onwards) call `ParseFootnotes(notes)` after `prose, notes := SplitNotes(parsed.RawBody)`.

## Algorithm

One-pass state machine over notesPart's lines.
- Header regex `^\\[(\\d+)\\]\\s+(.*)$` — anchored at line start so 'see [1] above' inside a note body is NOT a new header.
- Match → flush previous entry, start new entry with N as key and trailing capture as first body line.
- Non-match → append verbatim to current entry's body. Lines arriving before any header line are dropped (orphan continuation).
- TrimSpace on the joined body at flush; empty-after-trim entries dropped (malformed).
- Duplicate keys: last write wins.
- Returned map is always non-nil; empty map for empty/headerless input.

## Tests (14, all passing)

| name | covers |
|------|--------|
| TestParseFootnotes_EmptyInput | non-nil empty map |
| TestParseFootnotes_SingleNote | happy path |
| TestParseFootnotes_MultipleNotes | three notes parsed |
| TestParseFootnotes_MultiLineBody | continuation lines join with \\n |

title: Extractor — strip image refs, links, wikilinks, code blocks (§5.1 step 7)
description:
On prose_part, in this exact order (order matters):

a. Remove \`![alt](url)\` image refs entirely (regex: \`!\\[[^\\]]*\\]\\([^)]*\\)\`).
b. Replace \`[text](url)\` → \`text\` (regex: \`\\[([^\\]]+)\\]\\([^)]+\\)\`).
c. Replace \`[[slug|display]]\` → \`display\`; \`[[slug]]\` → \`slug.replace('-', ' ')\`.
d. Strip fenced code blocks \`\`\`...\`\`\`. Record count in skipped_segments.

## Why this order

Image refs (a) MUST go first — they look like links \`!\\[\\]()\\` and
the link rule (b) would otherwise accidentally extract the alt text as
content. Fenced code blocks last so links inside code don't get mangled
before we drop the whole block.

## Why drop code blocks rather than describe them

§5.1: PG's code is often the *point* of the paragraph (Beating the
Averages, Revenge of the Nerds) but reads atrociously aloud. Better to
skip cleanly than mangle. Listener can read those at desk.

## What about inline code (\`like this\`)?

Read aloud as plain text. \`fmt.Println\` voiced as \"fmt dot println\"
is a cost we accept; the alternative (stripping inline code) loses
content. Inline code is rare in PG's prose anyway.

## Wikilink display rule rationale

\`[[startup-ideas]]\` becomes \"startup ideas\" rather than a noun-phrase
fragment. \`[[startup-ideas|finding ideas]]\` uses the explicit display
text. Matches Obsidian's rendering.

## Public API

```go
func StripMarkdown(prose string) (cleaned string, skipped []string)
```

In internal/extract/strip.go. Consumers call it on the prose half of `SplitNotes`. `skipped` is appended to wa-kyn.9's CleanedDocument.SkippedSegments.

## Algorithm — four steps in declared order

| step | regex | replacement | notes |
|------|-------|-------------|-------|
| a. images | `!\\[[^\\]]*\\]\\([^)]*\\)` | "" | drop entire ref |
| b. links | `\\[([^\\]]*)\\]\\(([^)]*)\\)` | `$1` | keep text drop URL |
| c. wikilinks | `\\[\\[([^\\]]+)\\]\\]` | display half OR slug-with-hyphens-as-spaces | via ReplaceAllStringFunc |
| d. fenced code | `(?ms)^\`\`\`([^\\n]*)\\n(.*?)\\n\`\`\`[^\\n]*$` | "" + record "code_block" or "code_block:lang" in skipped | (?ms) for line-anchored multi-line |

title: Extractor — paragraph-attributed footnote weaving (§5.1 step 8) [load-bearing]
description:
THE CENTRAL DESIGN CHOICE OF THE EXTRACTOR. Read §5.1 step 8 carefully.

Algorithm:

a. Split prose_part into paragraphs by \`\\n\\s*\\n\`.
b. For each paragraph:
   i.   Find all \`[N]\` markers (where N matches a key in footnote_map).
        Use a regex that does NOT match markdown link openers — those
        were replaced in D7 step b, so any remaining [N] is a footnote
        marker. But add a defensive guard: skip if preceded by \`]\` or
        followed by \`(\` (link debris).
   ii.  Strip the markers from the paragraph prose.
   iii. If markers were found, append after the paragraph (separated by
        a blank line):
          \"Footnote {N}: {footnote_map[N]}\"
        — one line per marker, in order of appearance. Markers
        referenced multiple times in the same paragraph emit ONCE.

## Why paragraph-end (not essay-end, not inline)

§5.1: Hearing the footnote within the same listening \"beat\" as the
text it annotates preserves context, but interrupting mid-sentence
breaks flow. Paragraph boundaries are the natural seam. Listener has
just finished a thought; the footnote elaborates; next paragraph begins.

## Why bake \"footnote_policy_version\" into the body hash

D1: if we ever change this algorithm (e.g. switch to inline asides),
every essay should regenerate automatically rather than serve stale
audio mixed with the new style. Bumping the version constant is a
one-line cache invalidation for the entire corpus.

## Edge case matrix (must have unit tests for each)

- No Notes section → footnote_map empty; step 8 no-op.
- Marker in prose with no matching note → strip silently. Log debug.
- Note defined but never referenced → dropped. Log info.
- Same [N] in one paragraph twice → emit footnote ONCE.
- Link debris that looks like [N] → skip (preceded by ]/followed by ().
- **Notes** absent but markers exist → strip silently.

comments.author: jacob
comments.text:
## Worked example for the paragraph-end footnote weave

Input prose paragraph (after D7 link/wikilink/image scrubbing):

> Working hard isn't enough[1]. You have to work on the right things[2].

footnote_map (parsed from notes_part by D6):
- 1 → "By 'hard' I mean ... long hours."
- 2 → "Choosing the topic matters more than effort."

After D8 weaving:

> Working hard isn't enough. You have to work on the right things.
>
> Footnote 1: By 'hard' I mean ... long hours.
> Footnote 2: Choosing the topic matters more than effort.

The `[1]` and `[2]` are stripped from prose; one Footnote line per
unique marker, in marker-order-of-appearance, blank line separating
prose from footnote block.

## Why one paragraph at a time (not whole-essay end)

Listening test: with whole-essay-end footnotes, by the time the reader
hits "Footnote 14", they've forgotten what context [14] was anchored
to. With paragraph-end, the relevant context is still in working
memory.

## Why not inline ("Aside: ...")

Interrupts the prose mid-sentence in TTS, breaks rhythm. Paragraph
boundaries are natural pause points the listener already expects.

[pane-2] WeaveFootnotes shipped — the load-bearing extractor step closes.

## Public API

```go
type WeaveStats struct {
    Unknown      []int  // marker N referenced in prose with no map key (caller logs debug)
    Unreferenced []int  // map key never matched in prose (caller logs info)
}

func WeaveFootnotes(prose string, footnotes map[int]string) (string, WeaveStats)
```

In internal/extract/weave.go. Consumers call after StripMarkdown on the prose half.

## Algorithm

1. Split prose by /\\n\\s*\\n/ — exactly the bead's spec.
2. For each paragraph: `FindAllStringSubmatchIndex` over `\\[(\\d+)\\]`. Apply the **defensive guard** at index level: skip a match if `para[start-1] == ']'` or `para[end] == '('`. (Real PG corpus has no link debris; the guard is for spec compliance.)
3. Strip surviving markers via byte-slice splice (preserves all non-marker characters verbatim, including spacing).
4. Collect unique Ns in **first-appearance order** — duplicates within the same paragraph emit ONCE per the bead.
5. For each N: if in map → emit `Footnote N: <body>` and mark referenced; else add to Unknown.
6. After all paragraphs: collect `footnotes` keys not referenced into Unreferenced (sorted ascending for stable test/log output).
7. Join paragraphs with `\\n\\n` — exactly one blank line between (step 9 collapses any later runs).

Worked example from the bead's comment is a verbatim test case.

title: Extractor — finalize: collapse blanks, compute hash, return CleanedDocument (§5.1 steps 9-12)
description:
Steps 9-12 of §5.1:

9.  Reassemble paragraphs with blank-line separators. Collapse runs of
    blank lines to a single blank line.
10. Leave paragraph boundaries intact — chunker reflows on \n\n, not
    sentences. Go has no pysbd-grade sentence segmenter; paragraph-
    bounded chunking avoids the need and is sufficient for PG-length
    prose.
11. `body_hash = sha256(body + voice_id + model_id + footnote_policy_version)`.
12. Return CleanedDocument with all populated fields (Meta, Body,
    BodyHash, CharCount, WordCount, SkippedSegments).

## Length sanity check

If `len(body) < 200` after extraction, mark the document as malformed
and skip during build (§6). Most likely cause: the Metadata/FullDocument
heading detection went wrong. Log a warning to ~/.cache/wiki-audio/skipped.txt.

## Test Plan

Specific test cases for this step land in wa-kyn.17 (extractor unit
tests). Add these rows to that suite:

| Test name                          | Input                                | Expectation |
|------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|-------------|
| collapse_double_blank_lines        | "para1\n\n\n\npara2"                 | "para1\n\npara2" |
| collapse_triple_blank_lines        | "p1\n\n\n\n\np2"                     | "p1\n\np2" |
| body_hash_stable                   | same input twice                     | identical hex hash |
| body_hash_includes_voice_id        | same body, different voice_id        | different hash |
| body_hash_includes_model_id        | same body, different model_id        | different hash |
| body_hash_includes_policy_version  | same body, different policy ver      | different hash |
| body_hash_format_is_hex            | any input                            | matches `^[a-f0-9]{64}$` |
| body_under_200_marks_malformed     | body=150 chars                       | document marked Malformed=true |
| body_over_200_passes               | body=201 chars                       | not malformed |
| char_count_matches_utf8_bytes      | body with em dash "—"                | CharCount == utf8.RuneCount, not byte len |
| word_count_simple_split            | "hello world foo"                    | WordCount == 3 |
| skipped_segments_aggregated        | code block + image                   | SkippedSegments == 2 |

## Why CharCount uses runes not bytes

ElevenLabs bills per character; their definition is rune (Unicode code
point), not byte. PG essays have em-dashes, smart quotes, and the
occasional Unicode punctuation. Using utf8.RuneCount matches billing
and avoids over-estimating cost.

title: Phase H — Operationalize for ongoing use
description:
# Phase H — Steady-state ergonomics

Implements: PLAN_FOR_AUDIO_LIBRARY.md §7 Phase H.

## Goal

Daily ergonomics: drop a new essay markdown into the wiki's PG folder,
run `wiki-audio build && wiki-audio publish`, and a new podcast episode
appears within minutes — no manual steps, no surprises.

## Tasks

- Cancel the ElevenLabs Pro subscription after the bulk run (§7 Phase H).
- Switch billing to PAYG top-ups for incremental essays (~$0.50 each).
- Write README.md install/usage docs (the README the curl|bash users
  read; should answer: install, init, doctor, daily flow).
- Annual reminder via /schedule to re-verify the bucket has no public
  access and the dev URL is still off (§6 — defends against dashboard
  drift).

## Why a yearly reminder for bucket privacy

§6 \"Bucket accidentally made public\" — Cloudflare's dashboard UX has
historically made it easy to flip dev URLs on by accident. A defensive
yearly check ensures we catch drift even if no one touched the bucket
deliberately.

## Operational realism (pass 9) — corrected per-essay PAYG cost

The 'Switch billing to PAYG top-ups for incremental essays (\~$0.50
each)' line above is an underestimate. Corrected from wa-hqn realism:

- Average PG essay length: ~16,610 chars across the corpus.
- Credits: 16,610 × 0.5 = 8,305 credits per average essay.
- PAYG rate: $5 / 30,000 credits = $0.000167 per credit.
- Per-average-essay: 8,305 × $0.000167 = **\~$1.38**.

Range across the corpus: $0.25 (shortest, ~3k chars) to $8.66
(longest, ~52k chars).

Decision (cancel Pro, go PAYG) is unchanged: ~10 new essays/year ×
$1.38 mean = ~$14/year. Vastly cheaper than Pro retainer ($1,188/yr).

The original $0.50 was based on shorter essays; updated here so the
runbook future-self has the right number when topping up.

### PAYG top-up cadence (concrete)

- One $5 top-up = 30,000 credits.
- 30,000 credits / 8,305 credits-per-essay = ~3.6 average-length essays.
- Empirical pattern: top up $10 (60k credits) on day 30 (when Pro
  expires) = ~7 essays of buffer = ~8-10 months of incremental writing.
- Top up another $5-10 when balance drops below ~10k credits.

title: Cancel ElevenLabs Pro after bulk run, switch to PAYG
description:
After Phase G is verified successful (and Phase H demo H4 confirms
incremental flow works), cancel the Pro subscription. Switch to
pay-as-you-go top-ups for incremental new essays.

## Cost math

PAYG: ~\$0.50 per new PG-length essay added. Adding ~10 essays/year
~= \$5/year. Pro retainer would be \$1188/year for capacity we don't
need.

## Gate before canceling

- All 53 episodes accessible in Pocket Casts.
- Demo flow (H4) succeeds: drop new essay → build → publish → episode
  appears.
- A few weeks of lived-in use (the user wants to be sure the corpus
  doesn't need re-runs before commiting to PAYG).

If any extraction issues surface in spot-listening (G4) and require
re-running essays, do that BEFORE canceling — re-run is much cheaper
on the existing Pro plan.

## Acceptance criteria

Done = ALL:
1. Pre-cancellation gate (the bullets in the "Gate before canceling" section above) all checked off; record on this bead via comment.
2. ElevenLabs dashboard shows subscription status "will not renew" or "cancelled" (depending on the current term). Screenshot saved to `~/.cache/wiki-audio/elevenlabs-cancel-YYYY-MM-DD.png`.
3. Confirmation email from ElevenLabs received (PDF or screenshot saved alongside).
4. After the current Pro term expires, run `wiki-audio doctor` and confirm the credits check shows the PAYG balance (or zero) and synthesis still works for a one-essay test on PAYG dollars.
5. README / runbook updated if any user-visible behavior changed (e.g. new top-up flow). If nothing changed, no doc edit needed.

Verifiable artifacts: the two saved files (cancel screenshot + confirmation email) plus a successful `doctor` run on the post-expiry day.

## Operational realism (pass 9) — calendar timing

### When to cancel (target day)

Cancel **Day 25-26** of the Pro term (i.e. ~5 days before the auto-renew
date noted in wa-4cw.7). Reasoning:

- Day 25 leaves 5 days of paid coverage in case Phase H demo (wa-lz9.4)
  exposes an extractor bug requiring a re-run.
- Cancelling Day-of-renewal is too late: Pro typically requires
  cancellation 24-48 h before renewal to take effect for the upcoming
  cycle (verify on dashboard at cancel time).
- Cancelling earlier than Day 20 throws away cheap re-run capacity.

### Pre-cancel checklist (concrete day-by-day)

| Day | Action |
|-----|--------|
| 20  | Confirm wa-cfn.2 (bulk synthesis) passed. |
| 21  | Confirm wa-cfn.3 (publish) passed: feed loads, 53 episodes in Pocket Casts. |
| 22  | Spot-listen verification (wa-cfn.4) complete. |
| 23  | Phase H demo (wa-lz9.4) succeeds: drop a new essay → build → publish → episode appears. |
| 24  | Re-run `wiki-audio build` with no flags; confirm zero TTS calls (manifest cache valid). |
| 25  | Click 'Cancel subscription' on ElevenLabs dashboard. Save screenshot. |
| 26  | Confirmation email arrives; save PDF. |
| 27-29 | Watchful waiting (any fire-drill re-runs still on Pro $$, free). |
| 30  | Pro term ends. `wiki-audio doctor` should now report PAYG/zero balance. |
| 30+ | Top up $5 PAYG (\~30k credits) to seed incremental new-essay budget. |

### Why a 5-day buffer specifically

Empirically, edge cases discovered in Phase G/H surface within the
first week of normal use. Cancelling Day 25 gives 5 days of free
re-run capacity for those late-arriving issues. Cancelling Day 20
risks paying $73 PAYG for a re-run that would have been free.

### Cost of getting timing wrong

- Cancel too early (Day 15): If a bug surfaces Day 18 requiring a
  full re-run, you'd pay ~$73 PAYG. Total: $99 + $73 = $172.
- Cancel too late (forgot, Day 31): Pro auto-renews. Total: $198 for
  a second month of capacity you don't need.
- Cancel on time (Day 25): Total: $99. The target.

title: Write README.md (install line, init/doctor, daily ergonomics)
description:
The README curl|bash users land on. Sections:

- What is wiki-audio (1 paragraph)
- Install (the curl line)
- Quickstart: \`init\` → edit config + .env → \`doctor\` → \`build\` → \`publish\`
- Daily flow: drop new essay into source dir → \`build && publish\` → done
- Configuration reference: every TOML key explained
- Required env vars
- Token rotation runbook (cross-link to cross-cutting epic)

## What it should NOT be

- A theory document about why podcasts are good
- A long aside on Cloudflare Worker internals
- Marketing copy

Length goal: ~300 lines max. Future-me's actual reference card.

## Plan reference

PLAN_FOR_AUDIO_LIBRARY.md is the design doc; README is the user manual.
Keep them separate. The plan stays in the wiki, the README lives in the
wiki-audio repo.

## Acceptance criteria

Done = top-level `README.md` exists in the `Jacob2017/wiki-audio` repo, committed to main, with:

- All 7 sections from the bullet list above present, each with a level-2 heading.
- Install section contains the EXACT curl|bash one-liner from wa-8gt.3 / wa-8gt.6 (`curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jacob2017/wiki-audio/main/install.sh | bash`).
- Quickstart section walks through 5 commands in this order: `init`, edit `config.toml`, edit `.env`, `doctor`, `build && publish`. No skipped steps, no ordering shuffle.
- Daily flow section is < 10 lines (it's a paragraph, not a sub-tutorial).
- Configuration reference: every TOML key appearing in `config.example.toml` (wa-76r.9) has a row in the README's reference table, OR a sentence in a per-key paragraph. Verifiable via `grep ^[a-z_]*\ = config.example.toml | cut -d= -f1` and confirming each key appears in README.md.
- Token rotation section cross-links to wa-76r.4 (or its successor doc location).
- Length 200-400 lines. > 400 = bloating; cut.

Verifiable artifact: git commit, plus `grep -c '^## ' README.md` >= 7.

## Fail path

If the README on first read makes a future contributor (or future-me at 6 months out) ask "how do I install this" or "what does `build` do", the section is missing or buried. Add or restructure. Don't add a FAQ — fold the answer into the relevant section.
close_reason: Shipped in 1660a33. README extended (+205/-13) with user-facing onboarding sections — Install, Quickstart, Daily flow, Configuration reference, Required env vars table, Token rotation (cross-link to worker/README canonical runbook). Existing wa-76r.8 cache-layout content preserved verbatim. 317 lines total; force-closing past dependency wa-cfn.3 which is unrelated infra.

title: Add LICENSE file
description:
Pick a permissive license — MIT or Apache 2.0. Repo is private but a
LICENSE file is good hygiene if it ever opens up.

## Recommendation: MIT

Simplest, broadly understood. No patent grant strings (we have none).

## Acceptance criteria

Done = a `LICENSE` file at the repo root containing the standard MIT license text (https://opensource.org/license/mit), with:

- Copyright year filled (current year, set when committed).
- Copyright holder filled: "Jacob Byrne".
- No modifications to the standard MIT body — keep it identical to the canonical text. Modified MIT licenses confuse downstream tools (gh / OSI scanners).
- File ends with a single trailing newline (POSIX-compliant text file).

Verifiable: `head -1 LICENSE` returns "MIT License"; `grep -c 'Copyright (c)' LICENSE` returns 1; `shasum -a 256 LICENSE` produces a hash that matches a freshly-pulled MIT template with only the year + holder substituted (compare manually first time).

comments.author: pane-3
comments.text:
## wa-lz9.3 closed — MIT LICENSE shipped (commit `4b28588`)

### Acceptance matrix (all criteria from this bead)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `head -1 LICENSE` returns `"MIT License"` | ✅ |
| `grep -c 'Copyright (c)' LICENSE` returns `1` | ✅ |
| POSIX trailing newline (last byte 0x0a; previous byte not 0x0a) | ✅ — last 5 bytes `4152 452e 0a` (`ARE.\n`) |
| Standard MIT body, byte-identical to canonical | ✅ — see below |

### Byte-identical to canonical attestation

```
$ curl -sS https://api.github.com/licenses/mit -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github+json' \
  | python3 -c "import sys,json; sys.stdout.write(
      json.load(sys.stdin)['body']
        .replace('[year]', '2026')
        .replace('[fullname]', 'Jacob Byrne'))" \
  | sha256sum
e7cee9030f1be1d9735392e532c17457166323cf7c70faa575c0034900cbe451  -

$ sha256sum LICENSE
e7cee9030f1be1d9735392e532c17457166323cf7c70faa575c0034900cbe451  LICENSE

$ diff <(curl ... | substitute) LICENSE
(empty — byte-identical)
```

The hash matches the GitHub License API's canonical MIT template with only the year and fullname placeholders substituted. This is the strongest attestation I could find: any future tool (OSI scanner, gh license detection, SPDX parser) sees the unmodified standard text.

### Year + holder

- Copyright year: `2026` (current year, set at commit time per the bead).
- Copyright holder: `Jacob Byrne` (the runbook's specified name; matches the operator handle used in the rotation runbook + token mirror).

### What did NOT change

- No README.md exists at repo root yet — `wa-lz9.2` is the deliverable for that. When the README lands, the "License: MIT" badge + one-liner can be added there. The wa-lz9.3 spec's step-5 ("Add a one-line license note + badge to README.md if there's a top-of-file matter section") is a no-op until then.
- No Go `doc.go` advertises licensing today (`grep -rn -iE 'licens|copyright' --include='*.go'` is empty), so step-5's "mention in any package-doc.go" is also a no-op.
- `worker/README.md` is the Worker operational runbook, not a project README. Adding a top-of-file license stanza there would be misplaced. Skipped.

GitHub will now auto-detect the license and show "MIT License" on the repo page sidebar within a few minutes of the next push. Anyone landing on https://github.com/Jacob2017/wiki-audio sees the standard signal.

title: End-to-end demo: new essay → build → publish → episode in Pocket Casts
description:
The Phase H gate (§7):

1. Drop a new (real or test) PG-style markdown into the wiki source dir.
2. SSH to the wiki box.
3. \`wiki-audio build && wiki-audio publish\`.
4. Within minutes, the episode appears in Pocket Casts.

Time-from-drop-to-listen should be a few minutes total (extraction is
instant; TTS for one essay is ~1 min; publish is seconds).

If anything in the daily flow has rough edges (\"oh, you need to run X
first\"), fix the rough edge — do not document it.

## What this gate proves

That v1 is operationally complete. Anything beyond this is v2 (Phase I)
or polish.

## Acceptance criteria

Done = a single observed sequence on the wiki box, timed end-to-end:

1. Drop a NEW (not previously synthesized) PG-style markdown into the wiki source dir. Note the wall-clock time T0.
2. SSH to wiki box.
3. Run `wiki-audio build && wiki-audio publish` (no flags).
4. After publish completes, pull-to-refresh in Pocket Casts on phone. Note wall-clock time T1 when the new episode appears.
5. Tap the episode → it downloads → plays the first 30 seconds without error.

Pass criteria:
- T1 - T0 < 5 minutes for a typical PG-length essay.
- No commands required between step 1 and step 3 (no `init`, `doctor`, manual upload, or env-var fixup). If you find yourself running ANY other command, that's a fail — the rough edge gets fixed in code, not documented.
- No errors logged during build or publish (warnings about extant skipped segments are OK).
- The episode shows in Pocket Casts within one pull-to-refresh.

Verifiable artifact: a single git-committed entry in CHANGELOG (or a comment on this bead) with T0, T1, slug, and the build/publish log file path.

## Fail path

The bead is the gate. It cannot be "deferred" — it's the v1 definition of done.

- T1 - T0 > 5 min → profile what's slow. Likely culprits in order: (a) ElevenLabs latency on a long essay (acceptable up to ~2 min), (b) R2 multipart upload retries (investigate), (c) Pocket Casts feed cache (try Pocket Casts force-refresh from settings).
- Any extra command needed → file the rough edge as a follow-up bead and FIX IT in code before claiming v1 done. The README must not gain a "if it doesn't work, run X first" section.
- Build error → blocker; debug.
- Episode plays but with audio defect → this is wa-cfn.4 / wa-4cw.9 territory, not wa-lz9.4 — the demo is about the FLOW, not the audio quality. Audio quality should already be locked by Phase G.

## Operational realism (pass 9) — concrete demo timing

The existing 'few minutes total' is right in spirit but vague. Concrete
breakdown for a typical incremental essay (e.g. 16,610 chars, 5 chunks):

| Step                                | Wall clock |
|-------------------------------------|------------|
| Drop file in wiki source dir        | 1-5 s (cp) |
| Extract + chunk (zero-API)          | <1 s |
| Manifest fetch from R2              | 0.3-1 s |
| TTS for ~5 chunks (5 × 26 s)        | ~2 min |
| Concat 5 chunks via ffmpeg          | ~1 s |
| ID3 tag                             | <1 s |
| Upload MP3 (~12 MB) to R2           | 0.5-3 s (uplink dependent) |
| Manifest + pg.xml upload            | ~1 s |
| Pocket Casts pull-to-refresh round-trip | 1-2 s |
| **T1 - T0 expected**                | **~2-3 min** |

The 5 min pass criteria has ~2 min of slack for: a slightly longer
essay, retry on one chunk, slow uplink, or initial Pocket Casts
caching. If T1 - T0 > 5 min consistently, the per-chunk ~26 s TTS
assumption may be off — re-measure on a known essay.

For a SHORT essay (e.g. ~3,000 chars, 1 chunk):
T1 - T0 ≈ 35-45 s end-to-end.

For a LONG essay (e.g. how-to-do-great-work, ~52,000 chars, 14 chunks):
T1 - T0 ≈ 6-8 min — exceeds the 5 min gate. Use a typical-length
essay (~10-25k chars) for the demo. Note this in the artifact.
