title: Phase I — Deferred v2 expansion (audio: true, multi-author)
description:
# Phase I — Deferred for v2 (do not start until v1 is shipped + lived-in)

Implements: PLAN_FOR_AUDIO_LIBRARY.md §7 Phase I, §8.3.

## Why deferred

v1 is intentionally narrow: one author, one folder, one feed. The opt-in
mechanism (§8.3) and per-page voice override are real features, but they
add real complexity (frontmatter parsing, conflict rules, second feed
plumbing). Better to ship v1 and live with it for a few weeks before
deciding which of these are actually wanted vs. speculatively useful.

## Candidate v2 work (priority unknown until lived-in)

- `audio: true` opt-in flag in YAML frontmatter on summary/insight pages.
  Chosen mechanism (§8.3) — grep-able, survives renames, per-file
  granularity. Folder-based and registry-file alternatives rejected.
- Source→raw resolution: when an `audio: true` page is a summary, find
  the underlying raw original to read instead.
- Optional second feed `insights.xml` for non-PG content.
- Per-page voice override (`audio_voice: hq` → use eleven_multilingual_v2
  for that one page). Useful for ~10 most-relistened essays.

## Decision rule

Don't start any of this without a concrete listening-fatigue signal or
a desire to add specific non-PG content. Speculative implementation is
the enemy.

## §8.3 opt-in mechanism alternatives (full table)

When v2 design starts, choose `audio: true` in YAML frontmatter for these
reasons. The table is here so the choice doesn't get re-debated:

| Mechanism                          | Discoverable | Survives renames | Per-file | Verdict |
|------------------------------------|-------------|------------------|----------|---------|
| **`audio: true` in YAML frontmatter** | grep-able | Yes | Yes | **Chosen** |
| Tag-based (`#audio` or `tags: [audio]`) | grep-able | Yes | Yes | Equivalent on the technical merits, BUT user already uses `tags:` for retrieval-style indexing. Co-opting it for processing flags muddies the namespace. A dedicated `audio:` key is more idiomatic. |
| Folder-based (`audio/` subfolder)  | Visual only | No (Obsidian links rot on move) | Coarse | Worse — moving a file to opt-in breaks links. Rejected. |
| Central registry file              | Single source of truth | Manual | Yes | Drifts from reality whenever someone adds/renames a page without updating it. Rejected. |
| Path glob in config                | Easy bulk include | No | Coarse | This is what v1 uses implicitly (whole PG folder). Not "opt-in" — it's "everything in path X". Useful for bulk inclusion of a new author's folder, NOT for per-page selection. |

title: Spec the audio: true frontmatter mechanism (deferred)
description:
DEFERRED. Do not start until v1 has shipped and been lived-in for a few
weeks.

When picked up: design how \`audio: true\` in YAML frontmatter on
summary/insight pages flags them for inclusion in a feed.

## Open design questions (don't decide until needed)

- Which feed? (Same pg.xml as PG, or a new insights.xml?)
- Voice override per page? (Phase I.4 covers this.)
- What happens when the source page changes — same body_hash logic?
- Do we resolve summary → raw original when present (Phase I.2)?

## Why deferred

§7 Phase I: v1 is intentionally narrow. Adding frontmatter parsing,
multi-feed routing, voice resolution, etc. before validating the v1
feed is real listening fodder is speculative.

title: Source→raw resolution (when summary page → raw original) (deferred)
description:
DEFERRED. When implementing I1, decide what an \`audio: true\` summary
page should read aloud — the summary itself, or the raw original it
links to.

For PG essays: summary pages live alongside the raw originals; the raw
is what the user actually wants to listen to.

title: Optional second feed (insights.xml) (deferred)
description:
DEFERRED. Possibly: a second podcast feed for non-PG content. Subscribe
to whichever feed(s) you want listening fodder from.

## Why a separate feed (not one mixed feed)

Listening contexts differ: PG essays are walks/gym; insight notes are
dense and might be desk-only. Different feeds = different listening
queues without manual filtering.

title: Per-page voice override (`audio_voice: hq`) (deferred)
description:
DEFERRED. Allow a frontmatter key like \`audio_voice: hq\` to override
the default voice/model for individual pages. Useful for ~10 most-
relistened essays where the multilingual_v2 quality bump might be
worth the 2× credit cost.

## Implementation note for future-self

The body_hash already includes voice_id + model_id (D1). Per-page
override means resolving the effective voice_id at extraction time
based on frontmatter, then computing the hash from THAT voice_id. The
manifest entry stores the resolved voice_id; changing the override
auto-invalidates the body_hash for that one page.

title: [REVIEW] Phase E build pipeline spec analysis
description:
# [REVIEW] Phase E build pipeline spec analysis

Bounded review by pane-6 (Phase E lead, wait-state) of PLAN_FOR_AUDIO_LIBRARY.md
§3 / §4 / §5.3 / §5.4 / §7 Phase E and all wa-4cw.* beads. Findings are
severity-tagged. Each cites the specific spec/bead location so the fix can
be applied without re-reading everything.

---

## P0 — must resolve before Phase E spike fires

### P0-1. Spike duration acceptance band contradicts §3 example

**Where**: wa-4cw.8 acceptance bound `Duration is between 50 and 75 minutes`
vs. §3 sample output line `generated how-to-do-great-work.mp3 (62.4 MB, 1h22m)`.

`1h22m` = 82 minutes, which falls **outside** the 50–75 acceptance band. One
of the two is wrong: either the §3 example was a finger-in-the-air estimate
and the spike pass band should be widened (e.g. 50–95 min), or the band is
correct and §3's example needs a corrected duration. As-written, the spike's
duration check would FAIL on the example value.

**Fix**: pick a number from a real measurement (run `wiki-audio cost --slug
how-to-do-great-work` for the char count; estimate at 145 wpm narration pace)
or widen the band to [50, 100] min. Don't ship two contradictory numbers.

### P0-2. wa-4cw.12 integration test depends on wa-4cw.7 (Pro subscription)

**Where**: wa-4cw.12 `Dependencies → wa-4cw.7 (blocks)`.

The integration test smokes the API contract (single 25-char request, ~13
credits, ~$0.0001) — exactly the kind of thing you want to run BEFORE
spending $99 on a Pro subscription, to prove the API key works, the voice ID
resolves, and net/http handshake/JSON shape are correct. Blocking the
integration test on Pro subscription means the user pays $99 with no
prior live API verification.

**Fix**: drop wa-4cw.7 from wa-4cw.12's blockers. The test needs only
a valid API key on a free / trial / PAYG account (any tier with even 100
credits will run the smoke). Move wa-4cw.12 to before wa-4cw.7 in the
critical path.

---

## P1 — under-specified gates / edge cases

### P1-3. Voice quality gate has no "give-up after N voice swaps" exit

**Where**: wa-4cw.9 fail path: "Voice issue → swap voice_id, regen all chunks."

Spec says "decide before Phase F: ship vs. adjust" but doesn't bound the
adjust loop. If voice swap #1 also fails the human gate, do we swap again?
Indefinitely? Or is there a "TTS unviable; defer Phase F until ElevenLabs
ships a better model" exit? Without a limit, this gate can spin forever on
a subjective call.

**Fix**: cap at 2 voice swaps. After that, declare the gate failed, open a
P0 follow-up bead, and pause Phase F.

### P1-4. Voice quality gate is location/hardware-relative but spec doesn't pin

**Where**: wa-4cw.9 acceptance: "Pocket Casts on phone, NOT desktop."

Phone listening conditions vary wildly: quiet room with earbuds vs. gym
treadmill vs. street walk. PG essays will be listened to in all three. The
gate as-written passes if it sounds OK in the environment the user happens
to test in. A passing gate may still fail in the gym.

**Fix**: explicit listening-condition checklist: (a) quiet room, earbuds,
volume 50%; (b) walking outdoors, earbuds, volume 75%; (c) treadmill or
similar background-noise environment, earbuds, volume 90%. All three must
pass. Cheap to test (one hour, three devices/contexts).

### P1-5. Overlong-paragraph fallback split regex is brittle

**Where**: §5.2 step 5: `[.!?]\s+(?=[A-Z])` for the rare paragraph >maxChars.

Cases the regex mishandles:
- `"...he said." Next sentence` → splits AFTER the period BEFORE the close
  quote (lookahead requires capital, but `"` precedes the capital). Result:
  chunk ends `"...he said."` cleanly — actually OK. But:
- `Dr. Smith said...` → splits at `Dr. ` because `S` is capital. Mid-name
  split → audible glitch in TTS chunk.
- `A.D. 1492` / `e.g. consider` / `etc. The next` → false splits.
- `It costs $5.50. Then` → splits at `5.50.`? No, no capital after the
  decimal. Then splits at `50. T` — depends on regex anchoring.

Net: PG essays do contain abbreviations (Dr., e.g., i.e., etc.) and dollar
amounts. False splits cause mid-sentence chunk boundaries, which
acrossfade can't fully hide and sound jarring on listen.

**Fix**: either (a) negative-lookbehind to skip common abbreviations
`(?<!\b(?:Dr|Mr|Mrs|Ms|e\.g|i\.e|etc|vs|St|Mt|Inc|Ltd))[.!?]\s+(?=[A-Z])` —
note Go's RE2 doesn't support lookbehind, so this needs a manual scan; or
(b) abandon sentence-split entirely and fall back to char-count hard-cut at
the nearest whitespace, accepting the glitch as rare. wa-kyn.10 should
own this fix — flag it now so the chunker test plan includes adversarial
abbreviation cases.

### P1-6. Mid-essay timbre drift is gated by humans only

**Where**: wa-4cw.9 box "Voice consistent across the hour (no mid-essay
timbre shift)" + wa-cfn.4 "Spot-listen 3-5 random essays."

ElevenLabs Flash v2.5 has a known characteristic: each TTS call samples
slightly different prosody/timbre. Across 14 chunks of HTGW, subtle drift
may register as "the narrator sounds tired in chunk 9 vs. chunk 1." Spot-
listening 3-5 of 53 essays at Phase G means ~48 essays ship without anyone
listening to them end-to-end. Drift in those 48 surfaces only when the
user encounters them in the wild.

**Fix**: either accept the risk explicitly (document "drift is below
detectability threshold based on spike validation; not separately gated"),
or add an automated check — measure RMS amplitude per chunk and flag
chunks whose RMS deviates >2σ from the essay mean. Cheap (ffprobe one-pass).
Open as a P2 follow-up bead either way.

### P1-7. Hash invariant excludes output_format and chunker version

**Where**: §2 ManifestEntry hash: `body_hash = sha256(body + voice_id +
model_id + footnote_policy_version)`. wa-4cw.1 explicitly notes "body_hash
includes voice_id + model_id but NOT bitrate explicitly."

Documented but not enforced. Two silent-staleness paths:
- (a) Operator changes `output_format` from `mp3_44100_64` to e.g.
  `mp3_44100_128` in config.toml. Manifest hashes still match. New essays
  generate at 128k; old ones stay at 64k on R2. Mixed-bitrate feed.
- (b) Chunker (wa-kyn.10) algorithm change (e.g. fix to P1-5 above) changes
  ChunkCount but not body_hash. Manifest's ChunkCount field becomes stale;
  no rebuild triggered.

**Fix**: extend hash to `sha256(body + voice_id + model_id +
footnote_policy_version + output_format + chunker_version)`. One-time
invalidation cost is acceptable. Or document an explicit `--force` discipline
for these two knobs and add a doctor check that warns when manifest
output_format != current config output_format.

### P1-8. No chunk-level cache; mid-essay TTS failures waste prior chunks

**Where**: wa-4cw.5 step (i) uploads manifest snapshot AFTER each ESSAY
completes. Per §6 retry policy, abort-that-essay leaves "partial chunks
discarded."

For HTGW (~14 chunks, ~26s/chunk = ~6 min serial): a chunk-13 failure
discards 12 successful TTS calls (~24k credits, ~$2.40 wasted). For the
bulk run (~252 chunks across 53 essays, ~2h wall-clock), one fatal-after-N
abort can waste tens of dollars. Resumability is per-essay, not per-chunk.

**Fix** (cheap): persist per-chunk MP3s under
`~/.cache/wiki-audio/tmp/<slug>/<index>.mp3` (already done in wa-4cw.5 step
d). On retry of a failed essay, check for existing chunk files and skip
TTS for chunks already on disk. Refresh the chunk text→hash cache so
mid-flight extraction changes don't reuse stale audio. Add to wa-4cw.5 test
plan: `essay_resume_skips_completed_chunks`.

### P1-9. Retry classifier doesn't cover TLS/DNS/connect-refused

**Where**: wa-4cw.11 test table covers `connection_reset`,
`net.Error{Temporary=true}`, `context.DeadlineExceeded`. No coverage for:
- TLS handshake failure (e.g. certificate transient)
- DNS NXDOMAIN to api.elevenlabs.io (CDN flap)
- `connection refused` (e.g. their proxy reboots)
- HTTP/2 stream errors (`stream closed`, `RST_STREAM`)

§5.3 says "timeout / 5xx / 429 → retry with backoff." Doesn't classify
the above. Default behavior of the implementation as-described will likely
NOT retry TLS/DNS/connect-refused — they'll surface as
`url.Error{Err: ...}` and bypass the http.Response branch.

**Fix**: classifier branch on `errors.Is(err, syscall.ECONNREFUSED)`,
`x509.UnknownAuthorityError`-class, `*net.DNSError`. All retryable. Add
test rows to wa-4cw.11 — fast (httptest with `Listener.Close()` mid-flight).

### P1-10. TTS retries may double-bill on partial-response failures

**Where**: §5.3 retry path. No mention of idempotency.

If ElevenLabs serves the first ~50% of MP3 bytes then connection drops,
client retries. ElevenLabs may have already metered the call (credits
deducted) AND the retry burns more credits. Across 252 chunks and a 5%
retry rate, this could add ~$5-10 of phantom billing.

**Fix**: investigate whether ElevenLabs supports an `Idempotency-Key`
header (some TTS APIs do). If yes, send a stable per-chunk key (e.g.
`sha256(chunk.Text + voice_id + model_id)[:32]`) so retries don't
double-bill. If no, accept the cost and document. Either way, log
`credits_before` and `credits_after` per essay (wa-4cw.12 already plans
this for the integration test) and surface unexpected delta in build
output.

### P1-11. 402-out-of-credits has no auto-recovery hook for bulk run

**Where**: §6 row "Out of credits / auth failure (HTTP 402, 403) → FATAL
aborts the whole run." wa-4cw.7 sizing: "Pro headroom (500k base + 25%
overage) covers up to ~625k. Total expected within the month: ~525k-535k."

Bulk run is sized at 440k credits within 500k Pro quota. If extraction
yields more chars than estimated (a regression in extractor that doesn't
strip code blocks correctly, e.g.), bulk run could hit 500k mid-essay 35
of 53. Spec: abort. Operator pays for top-up, restarts, manifest skips
done essays. OK for a one-shot run, but no warning before crossing
quota.

**Fix**: pre-flight check in `wiki-audio build` (not just `--dry-run`)
that compares sum-of-cleaned-chars × 0.5 against current credit balance
fetched from `xi-api-key` user-info endpoint. If estimated > balance × 0.95,
abort BEFORE first TTS call with a clear message. wa-cfn.1 (`build
--dry-run` cost preflight) already does this for dry-run; replicate the
check in wet-run path.

---

## P2 — clarifications / housekeeping

### P2-12. Spike credit-consumption measurement source unspecified

**Where**: wa-4cw.8 acceptance "ElevenLabs credit consumption logged:
between 22k and 30k credits used."

How is this measured? Options:
- (a) Dashboard delta — manual, screenshot-based.
- (b) ElevenLabs `/v1/user` endpoint, called pre/post — automated.
- (c) Sum of `chunk.CharCount × 0.5` from the build itself — predictive,
  not actual.

(c) doesn't catch double-billing from retries. (b) is best. Spec doesn't
say which. wa-4cw.12 integration test logs `credits_before/credits_after`
— same logging should apply to the wet-run wa-4cw.5 build path.

**Fix**: standardize on (b), implemented as a build-pipeline step in
wa-4cw.5 (post-essay manifest snapshot includes `credits_used` field).

### P2-13. wa-4cw.6 "out/<slug>.mp3 retention after publish" still TODO

**Where**: wa-4cw.6 explicit "Or keep ... for fast republish — pick one
and document."

Unresolved. P2 because the answer doesn't block Phase E, but it does
block Phase F (publish needs to know whether to read from out/ or
re-trigger build).

**Fix**: keep them. ~600 MB on a wiki box is nothing; Phase F republish
without re-TTS is the common case (RSS regen, token rotation). Document
in wa-4cw.6 description and wa-76r.8 README.

### P2-14. Footnote-policy-version bump cost wording is misleading

**Where**: wa-4cw.9 fail path: "Footnote cadence intrusive → revisit
footnote_policy_version. This is the heaviest fix because changing the
policy invalidates every essay's body_hash."

Context: wa-4cw.9 fires AFTER spike (1 essay), BEFORE bulk run. At that
point invalidating "every essay's body_hash" invalidates ONE essay
(HTGW). The fix is cheap, not heavy. The wording is correct for a
post-bulk-run cadence change, but misleading for the gate it lives in.

**Fix**: clarify in wa-4cw.9 that fix-at-spike-gate is cheap; the heavy
cost only applies if the policy is revisited post-Phase-G.

### P2-15. Chunk audio length anomaly threshold (1s) lacks justification

**Where**: §6 "duration < 1s for non-empty chunk" + wa-4cw.5 "duration
< 1s AND chunk's text was non-empty (>=20 chars)."

Why 1s? A 4000-char chunk at 145 wpm produces ~4 minutes of audio. A
"non-empty" 20-char chunk could legitimately produce ~5s. The 1s
threshold catches truncation but not 50%-truncation (a 4000-char chunk
returning 30s instead of 240s). Better threshold: `expected_seconds =
chars × 0.06` (rough words-per-minute conversion); flag if
`actual < expected × 0.5`.

**Fix**: replace fixed-1s rule with proportional-to-chars rule. Adds
an `anomalies.txt` row for each off-by-half chunk; user reviews
post-run.

### P2-16. ID3 TYER fallback to "year-of(GeneratedAt)" loses signal

**Where**: wa-4cw.4 "TYER falls back to year-of(GeneratedAt) when
publish_date_text absent."

If we generate audio in 2026 for a PG essay published in 2003, podcast
app shows "2026" as the date. Operator can't distinguish "essay from
this year" vs. "essay generated this year." Minor for personal use.

**Fix**: prefer a heuristic regex over the essay body for `^\s*##?
(?:Metadata|Original Date)?:?\s*(\w+ \d{4})$` — most PG essays carry
"July 2023" or similar in the metadata block. If both fail, fall back
to GeneratedAt year as today, but log a warning per essay so operator
knows when the heuristic missed.

---

## Cross-reference: credit budget consistency check

Re-read §1 cost block ("~$99 one-shot ... ~$0.50 per new PG-length essay")
against wa-4cw.7 timeline ("525k-535k credits expected within the month;
Pro headroom up to 625k"):

- Bulk corpus: 880k chars × 0.5 cred/char = 440k credits (spec consistent).
- Spike + iteration buffer: ~25k + ~50k = ~75k.
- Late-run buffer: ~10-60k.
- Total max planned: ~575k. Pro covers ~625k. Margin: ~50k credits (~9%).

**Concern**: margin is thin. P1-7 (output_format silent change forcing
re-render of N essays) or P1-8 (chunk-level retry waste at 5% rate) could
each consume ~20-50k credits unexpectedly. Combined: bulk run risks
spilling into PAYG mid-run.

**Fix**: pre-bulk-run, doctor reports both `credits_remaining` AND
`estimated_bulk_run_credits`. If the latter exceeds 90% of the former,
abort with instruction to top up first. Minor change to wa-kyn.13
(`doctor`) — add the projection check.

---

## Summary — what to fix before Phase E spike

Must (P0): #1 (duration band), #2 (move integration test before Pro sub).
Should (P1): #3 (gate fail-cap), #4 (listening conditions), #5 (chunker
abbreviation handling), #6 (drift detection optional), #7 (hash
invariants), #8 (chunk-level resume), #9 (TLS/DNS classifier rows),
#10 (idempotency check), #11 (pre-flight credit check).
Nice (P2): #12-16, plus the credit-budget margin concern.

The P0/P1 set is ~3-5 hours of bead/spec edits; nothing requires code.
Phase E unblocks once Phase D ships (wa-kyn.20). After that, claim order
recommendation: wa-4cw.1 → wa-4cw.2 → wa-4cw.11 (ahead of wa-4cw.5 to lock
classifier behavior) → wa-4cw.4 → wa-4cw.3 → wa-4cw.6 → wa-4cw.5
(orchestrator) → wa-4cw.12 (smoke before $99) → wa-4cw.7 → wa-4cw.8
(spike) → wa-4cw.9 + wa-4cw.10 (gates).

— pane-6 (Phase E lead, wait-state)

comments.text:
# pane-5 addendum findings — implementation-side spec drift

Filed by pane-5 (wrote wa-4cw.5 build pipeline + wa-4cw.6 cache). Pane-6's
existing P0/P1/P2 sweep (16 findings above) is comprehensive on the
spec/gate side. Adding three findings the implementation side surfaces:
spec gaps that are silently load-bearing in the code today and would
break Phase G if a future refactor undoes the workaround.

Bar applied per orchestrator's note: "would actually break Phase G bulk
run or cost money." Skipped 4–5 candidate findings (chunker concurrency,
Retry-After cap formalization, skipped.txt format, manifest "last
attempted" timestamp) because they're either covered by pane-6 (P1-8 ↔
wa-cfx) or operability-only.

---

## [HIGH] PANE5-1. ID3 encoding contract is implicit, not in PLAN — silent regression risk

**Where**: §5.5 + §8.6 + wa-4cw.4 acceptance ("ID3 v2.3 frames").

§5.5 mentions ID3 v2.3 frames (TIT2/TPE1/TALB/TYER/TCON). §8.6 lists
bogem/id3v2/v2 as the library. **Neither pins the text encoding.**

ID3 v2.3 only allows two encodings: ISO-8859-1 (encoding byte 0) and
UTF-16 with BOM (encoding byte 1). UTF-8 was added in v2.4 and is
*invalid* at v2.3.

bogem's default for `SetTitle` etc. is **ISO-8859-1**. ISO-8859-1
**cannot encode em-dashes (U+2014), smart quotes (U+201C/D), ellipses
(U+2026)**, or anything else outside the Latin-1 block. PG essays
contain em-dashes routinely — `"How to Do Great Work — A Guide"` would
fail with `"rune not supported by encoding"` at `tag.Save()`.

The wa-4cw.4 implementation works around this with `tag.SetDefaultEncoding(id3v2.EncodingUTF16)` between `SetVersion(3)` and the `SetTitle/etc.` calls (commit fb7a123). The workaround is the **only** thing keeping em-dash titles from breaking. **PLAN doesn't enforce this.**

### Why this breaks Phase G if undone

- A future refactor that "tidies" the tagger and removes the explicit `SetDefaultEncoding` call → all em-dash essays fail to tag → essay aborts mid-pipeline → manifest doesn't update → next bulk run re-attempts → fails again. Silent until somebody reads the build output.
- Approximately 40% of the 53-essay PG corpus contains em-dashes per a quick `grep` of the examples directory (HTGW alone has 27).
- `internal/cli/build_pipeline.go::buildOneEssayFull` aborts on `id3.Tag` error; the chunks + concat output are preserved but the operator has to manually clear the partial out file to retry.

### Fix

Add to PLAN §5.5 (RSS section is wrong place; better in §8.6 row "ID3
tagging"):

> **Encoding contract**: ID3 v2.3 frames are written as UTF-16 with
> BOM (encoding byte 1). UTF-8 is invalid at v2.3 and ISO-8859-1
> cannot encode em-dashes / smart quotes that PG essays contain.
> The tagger MUST call `tag.SetDefaultEncoding(id3v2.EncodingUTF16)`
> after `SetVersion(3)` and before any `Set*` call.

Plus a regression test that pins this — `internal/id3/tagger_test.go`'s
`TestTagUTF8RoundTrip` (em-dash in title) already does this, but the
test doesn't carry a comment explaining the load-bearing nature. Add
the comment.

---

## [MEDIUM] PANE5-2. Manifest schema-mismatch refusal has no downgrade-path doc

**Where**: §6 row "Tool version mismatch with manifest schema" + my
`internal/cli/build_pipeline.go::readLocalManifest` enforcement (commit
45df37d).

§6 says: *"Older tool refuses to overwrite a newer-schema manifest.
User instructed to upgrade via the install script."*

`readLocalManifest` enforces this:
```go
if m.Version > model.ManifestSchemaVersion {
    return nil, fmt.Errorf("manifest version %d > known %d — upgrade wiki-audio (§6 schema-mismatch guard)", ...)
}
```

The contract assumes a forward-only path: schema bumps from 1→2→3, and
a v1 binary refuses a v2 manifest with "upgrade your binary."

**The unspecified case**: an operator on a wiki box deliberately pinned
to v0.3.0 (because v0.4.0 broke something for them) sees a v0.4-schema
manifest in R2 because they ALSO ran v0.4 from a different machine. The
v0.3.0 binary refuses with "upgrade wiki-audio" — but the operator
doesn't *want* to upgrade. There's no `wiki-audio --downgrade-manifest`
or `wiki-audio publish --manifest-version=1` escape hatch. The only
recovery is to:

1. Manually edit the R2 manifest down to v1 schema (lossy if v2 added
   fields)
2. OR delete the R2 manifest and rebuild every essay from scratch
   (~$50 in EL credits)

### Why this matters

Bulk run (~440k credits, ~$87) is the most expensive single action in
this project. A schema-mismatch lockout that costs $50 to recover from
is a real money risk, not a hypothetical one.

### Fix (cheap)

Document the recovery path in §6 row text. Two options:

**Option A** (preferred): require schema bumps to be **strictly
backward-compatible** (only add optional fields, never remove or
rename). v1 binaries reading a v2 manifest succeed if all v1 required
fields are still present; just ignore the v2 additions. The
`Version > known → refuse` check still fires for `Version > known + 1`
(major bumps), but minor additions don't lock out.

**Option B**: ship a `wiki-audio manifest migrate --to-version N` CLI
that does a deliberate, lossy downgrade with an `--accept-data-loss`
flag. Higher engineering cost.

---

## [LOW] PANE5-3. §5.3 retry pseudocode doesn't cap server's Retry-After

**Where**: §5.3 retry pseudocode (line 532-533): `time.Sleep(parseRetryAfter(resp) | backoff(attempt))`.

The pseudocode reads as "honor server hint or fall back to backoff,"
which is what wa-3gf shipped. But the spec doesn't pin a **cap** on
the server hint. If ElevenLabs returns `Retry-After: 600` (10 min),
the spec implies we sleep 10 min.

`internal/cli/build_pipeline.go::computeRetryDelay` (commit 8a89527)
caps the hint at `retryAfterCap = 60s` based on orchestrator guidance
in the wa-3gf brief, not spec text. `internal/tts/retry.go::parseRetryAfter`
also has a `maxRetryAfter = 300s` cap that filters values out of the
APIError entirely.

So: spec → "honor hint." Implementation → "honor hint up to 60s" (with
an additional 300s upstream filter). The implementation is more
conservative than the spec. That's a forward-compatible drift — but if
a future maintainer reads the spec literally and removes the cap,
bulk runs can wedge for 5+ minutes per chunk on quota-exceeded
responses, blowing wall-clock budget.

### Why this is LOW (not blocking)

- The bulk run cost-of-spinning is bounded: at most `cfg.RetryAttempts`
  × cap × 252 chunks. Worst case at 60s cap: 252 × 3 × 60 = ~12.6h
  added to bulk run wall-clock. Annoying but not fatal.
- ElevenLabs Pro is unlikely to issue a 600s Retry-After on a
  paying account — that's the kind of value seen on free-tier hard
  blocks.

### Fix

Inline the cap into §5.3 pseudocode:
```
sleep := parseRetryAfter(resp)
if sleep == 0 { sleep = backoff(attempt) }
if sleep > 60*time.Second { sleep = 60*time.Second }  // cap, see wa-3gf
time.Sleep(sleep)
```

One-line spec fix; no implementation change needed.

---

## Cross-references

- PANE5-1 overlaps with no existing finding. Pane-6's P1-7 covers
  output_format + chunker_version in body_hash but not ID3 encoding.
- PANE5-2 overlaps with no existing finding. Pane-6's P1-7 mentions
  the hash-invalidation cost but not the schema-version refusal
  recovery path.
- PANE5-3 is implementation-down-stream of wa-3gf (which I shipped).
  Pane-6's P1-9, P1-10, P1-11 cover other classifier gaps but not the
  Retry-After cap.

— pane-5

title: [REVIEW] Phase G/H operational + cost analysis
description:
## [HIGH] The Pro-tier budget story is not "comfortable" even on the spec's own numbers, and the live ElevenLabs billing model has moved underneath it
- wa-cfn.1 sizes the bulk corpus at `880,344` chars / `440,172` Flash credits.
- wa-4cw.7 then adds the spike + iteration + rerun buffer on top of that. Its own timeline budgets roughly `25k` (spike) + `up to 50k` (Phase E iteration) + `up to 10k` (post-bulk reruns) + `up to 60k` (late buffer) + `<5k` (H demo). The buffered month therefore lands around `525k-580k` credits, which is already above the old `500k` Pro-base story.
- Current ElevenLabs docs checked on `2026-05-08` make the assumption weaker, not stronger: Flash/Turbo still costs `1 credit / 2 chars`, API list price is `$0.05 / 1K chars`, PAYG is `$3 / 30k credits`, and PAYG is the replacement for usage-based billing on new self-serve subscriptions.
- Consequence: the plan's `$87 on Pro overage` and `$73.36 PAYG` math is stale. `880,344 × $0.05 / 1,000 = ~$44.02` at current API/PAYG pricing. Also, a new self-serve Pro subscription should not be modeled as "500k plus automatic postpaid overage" unless the account is explicitly grandfathered.
- Fix: rewrite wa-cfn.1 / wa-cfn.6 / wa-4cw.7 / wa-lz9.1 around live account state (`current quota`, `PAYG balance`, `top-up enabled`) instead of hard-coded `fits Pro` language.

## [HIGH] Phase H cancel timing is aimed at the wrong failure mode; the real risk is ending Pro without funded PAYG continuation
- wa-lz9.1 treats the critical timing question as "cancel before auto-renew" and asserts a likely `24-48 h` cutoff.
- Current ElevenLabs cancel docs say cancellation can be scheduled at any time and takes effect at the end of the current billing cycle; the official risk is not a vendor cutoff window, it is forgetting to cancel at all.
- Current PAYG docs say subscription credits are consumed first, then PAYG balance; if PAYG balance hits `$0` and Auto Top Up is off, service pauses immediately.
- Consequence: the spec can satisfy the Day-25 cancellation ritual and still fail the first post-expiry essay if Top Up / Auto Top Up was never enabled before the Pro term ended. That directly conflicts with the Phase H promise that adding a new essay stays a zero-manual-step flow.
- Fix: add a pre-expiry step before wa-lz9.1 closes: enable Top Up, fund a balance, configure Auto Top Up (or explicitly accept manual top-ups), then run the post-expiry one-essay smoke test before calling the cancellation workflow done.

## [HIGH] Build resumability is not end-to-end idempotent until cache retention and rebuild conditions are nailed down
- wa-4cw.5 marks an essay as built by updating the manifest snapshot in R2 after local MP3 generation.
- wa-i1l.4 / wa-i1l.7 later publish from `~/.cache/wiki-audio/out/<slug>.mp3` only.
- wa-4cw.6 still leaves the critical invariant undecided: `delete out/<slug>.mp3 after publish` vs `keep it`.
- Failure case: manifest snapshot says essay `X` is built, local `out/X.mp3` disappears, rerun sees `body_hash` hit and skips synthesis, publish sees no local MP3, and the system is stuck in a "built but not uploadable" state.
- Fix: make `out/<slug>.mp3` retention until successful upload an explicit invariant, and make `wiki-audio build` treat `manifest hit + R2Key empty + local out file missing` as stale/rebuild-needed instead of cache-hit/skippable.

## [MEDIUM] `wiki-audio doctor` does not check the two run-blockers that matter in Phase G/H: credit sufficiency and post-build publishability
- wa-kyn.13 verifies auth, voice reachability, a live credit number, R2 bucket HEAD, and the Worker `403/403/404` contract.
- It does NOT tell the operator whether the currently available subscription/PAYG balance can cover the queued run, and it does NOT tell the operator whether every manifest entry that still needs publish has a corresponding local `out/<slug>.mp3` artifact.
- Consequence: `doctor` can be green immediately before a bulk run that will die mid-flight on exhausted credits, or immediately before a publish rerun that has nothing local left to upload.
- Fix: extend wa-kyn.13 with two explicit checks: `(estimated required credits <= available subscription+PAYG spendable balance)` and `(for every manifest entry with empty R2Key, local out/<slug>.mp3 exists)`.

## [MEDIUM] The demo gate depends on release/install state, but Phase H never re-verifies the wiki box is on the intended binary
- Phase F says `Cut v1.0.0. Re-install on wiki box.`
- wa-8gt.7 proves the install path on the stub release track, not that the wiki box used for wa-lz9.4 is actually running the Phase-F binary when the timed demo starts.
- A stale binary on the wiki box will look exactly like a Phase-H flow failure.
- Fix: add a pre-demo prerequisite outside the timed `T0 -> T1` window: `wiki-audio --version` on the wiki box must match the intended release tag, and `wiki-audio doctor` must pass immediately before the no-extra-commands demo begins.

## [MEDIUM] ElevenLabs' own current plan/quota docs are internally inconsistent, so the spec should stop baking exact plan numbers into gates
- The live API pricing page presents plan value in included Flash/Turbo characters and current list pricing.
- Help Center quota / rollover / limit articles still speak in the older credit-quota vocabulary and do not line up cleanly with the pricing-page story.
- Consequence: hard-coded gates like `374k-506k credits`, `fits Pro`, `500k base + 25% overage`, and day-30 quota assumptions are brittle by definition.
- Fix: treat plan constants as runtime inputs gathered from the live account at subscription time or from `doctor`, not as stable facts frozen into wa-cfn.* / wa-lz9.*.

title: [REVIEW] PLAN §1/§2/§6 ambiguities
description:
Audit of PLAN_FOR_AUDIO_LIBRARY.md §1 (intro), §2 (data model), §6 (errors). Severity-tagged findings only.

## [HIGH] Manifest persistence cadence is contradictory across sections
§4 architecture diagrams describe an in-memory Manifest that is "built during build phase" and only persisted in the publish pipeline ("upload pg.xml + pg.manifest.json to R2 root"). §6 "Network outage mid-bulk-run" states "Manifest is uploaded after each essay completion. Ctrl-C → re-run resumes from where it left off." These are mutually exclusive. Implementer needs a decision: per-essay R2 PUT (resumable, more requests) vs end-of-build PUT (atomic, lossy on crash). This affects wa-i1l.2 (manifest save) and wa-4cw.5 (build pipeline wiring) directly. Pick one and update the diagram or §6.

## [HIGH] §5.1 strips the metadata block before §2 fields can be read from it
§2 EssayMeta has SourceURL and PublishDateText (e.g. "July 2023") that must come from the Readwise-style header in each .md. §5.1 step 3 says "Drop everything from '## Metadata' to the line before '## Full Document'" — but never specifies a parse-before-drop step. As written, the extractor cannot populate SourceURL/PublishDateText. wa-kyn.4 ("read file, parse title, drop Metadata + Full Document headers") inherits this gap — the title is parsed but the URL/date are not. Spec needs an explicit "parse metadata key/values into EssayMeta, then drop the block" step.

## [HIGH] `footnote_policy_version` is referenced in the hash formula but never defined
§2: "BodyHash = sha256(body + voice_id + model_id + footnote_policy_version)". §5.1 step 11 repeats this. But footnote_policy_version is not a TOML key, not a struct field, not a named constant, and not enumerated anywhere. Implementer of wa-kyn.9 has no source of truth for the value. Needs to be a const in internal/extract/ (e.g. `const FootnotePolicyVersion = "v1"`) with a versioning policy ("bump when step 8 algorithm changes").

## [HIGH] Manifest map keyed by slug AND ManifestEntry has its own Slug field — source-of-truth ambiguity
`Manifest.Entries map[string]ManifestEntry` keyed by slug, but `ManifestEntry.Slug` is also a field. If they ever disagree (manifest mutation bug, hand-edit), which is authoritative? Manifest load code in wa-i1l.2 needs an explicit invariant — either drop the field, or validate `entry.Slug == key` on load.

## [HIGH] Worker timing oracle: §9.2 sketch early-returns on length mismatch
The provided `timingSafeEqual` returns false immediately if `a.length !== b.length`. That leaks token length via timing. The token length is fixed (43 chars per §9.1), so the oracle reveals little — but the spec markets this as a "constant-time string compare to defeat timing oracles" (§9.1) and the implementation does not deliver that property. Cloudflare Workers exposes `crypto.subtle.timingSafeEqual` natively; use it, or compare both strings to a fixed-length canonical form. Affects wa-3ia.5 acceptance test (it should also test that wrong-length tokens take the same code path as wrong-content tokens).

## [MEDIUM] R2 ETag-based diff is unreliable across multipart vs single-part uploads
§4 publish pipeline: "HEAD each pg/<slug>.mp3, compare etag". minio-go switches to multipart at a size threshold; multipart ETags are not the MD5 of the object (they're "<md5-of-md5s>-<part-count>"). If a future re-upload uses a different chunk size or threshold, the ETag changes despite identical bytes — causing spurious re-uploads. Conversely, a re-upload with the same multipart layout but different bytes might collide structure. The spec should either (a) pin a single-part PUT path under a size threshold and use ETag = content MD5, or (b) compare local sha256 vs a custom metadata header (`x-amz-meta-sha256`) instead of the S3 ETag. wa-i1l.3 needs this clarified.

## [MEDIUM] Atomic local write via os.Rename can fail with EXDEV on cross-FS temp
§6: "Atomic local writes via os.CreateTemp + os.Rename ensure partial files don't replace good ones." If `os.CreateTemp("", ...)` is used (TMPDIR), and TMPDIR is on a different mount than `~/.cache/wiki-audio/`, `os.Rename` returns EXDEV. Spec needs to specify "create the temp file inside the destination directory" (`os.CreateTemp(filepath.Dir(target), ...)`), otherwise the atomicity guarantee is broken on common Linux setups (e.g. tmpfs /tmp).

## [MEDIUM] TOML-default values are stated inline but no application locus is specified
§2 has many "default X" comments (ModelID="eleven_flash_v2_5", ChunkMaxChars=4000, RequestTimeoutS=60, etc.). BurntSushi/toml does not apply defaults — it leaves missing fields zero-valued. Spec needs to designate where defaults are applied (a `Validate()` method on Config? defaults baked in `internal/config/loader.go`?). wa-kyn.2 will otherwise produce zero-valued surprises (e.g. ChunkMaxChars=0 → infinite-loop chunker; RequestTimeoutS=0 → no timeout).

## [MEDIUM] OutputFormat "mp3_44100_64" doesn't specify channels — risk of stereo doubling file size
§8.7 chooses "MP3 64 kbps mono" deliberately for ~520 MB total. But the format string `mp3_44100_64` (per ElevenLabs' API) does not embed a channel count; ElevenLabs may default to mono or stereo depending on the voice/model. If stereo, total size doubles to ~1 GB. Spec should either confirm the format-string-to-channels mapping (cite ElevenLabs docs) or add an explicit channels assertion in wa-4cw.1's acceptance test (probe one chunk with ffprobe and assert `channels=1`).

## [MEDIUM] Partial chunk failure burns credits with no resume path
§6: "After final failure, abort that essay only; partial chunks discarded; R2 manifest unchanged so next run retries cleanly." The chunks that DID succeed used credits — those credits are lost on retry. For an essay with 14 chunks where chunk 12 fails, ~85% of cost is wasted. Spec should either (a) explicitly accept this as a cost trade-off in §6 (so reviewers stop flagging it) or (b) cache per-chunk MP3s under `~/.cache/wiki-audio/tmp/<slug>/chunk-NNN.mp3` and resume from the failed chunk. Interacts with wa-4cw.2 (retry classifier).

## [MEDIUM] Bucket-public regression: yearly /schedule check is too infrequent
§6: "Add yearly reminder via /schedule to re-verify." A misclick in the Cloudflare dashboard could expose the bucket for a year before detection. The Worker itself could include a self-check on a CRON trigger that fetches the bare bucket URL (no Worker) and asserts 403. Or `wiki-audio doctor` could be wired into a daily systemd timer. Yearly is "policy theater" for a security-relevant regression.

## [MEDIUM] R2Config has no Endpoint field but the comment says one is derived
§2 R2Config: `// Endpoint derived: https://<AccountID>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`. The struct has no Endpoint field. Where is this assembled? In wa-i1l.1's minio client constructor? If yes, the comment belongs there, not on R2Config. If it's expected to be settable for testing (e.g. against a local minio mock — see wa-i1l.17), an optional `Endpoint string` field would be useful for the in-memory fake.

## [LOW] §4 architecture diagram says `audio.<domain>/pg.xml` but every other section uses `wiki-audio.jabyrne.workers.dev`
The custom-domain promise is not reflected in §1, §3 doctor output, §5.5 RSS sample, §6, §9, or §10 (all say `wiki-audio.jabyrne.workers.dev`). Either drop the `audio.<domain>` aspirational form from §4 or add a Phase to wire a custom domain.

## [LOW] §1 says "cancel ElevenLabs Pro" after one-shot; §7 Phase H says "switch to pay-as-you-go top-ups"
ElevenLabs subscription cancellation and a "pay-as-you-go" tier are not the same thing. Plan should pick one (cancel & re-subscribe per refresh, vs downgrade to a metered tier).

## [LOW] BodyHash includes voice_id+model_id, but ManifestEntry stores VoiceID and ModelID as separate fields
Redundant. If the hash and the explicit fields disagree (e.g. manifest mutation), which wins for cache lookup? Spec should specify: hash is authoritative; explicit fields are diagnostic only.

## [LOW] world-readable .env check is too lax for chmod 600
§6: "Tool refuses to start if .env is world-readable." chmod 600 also forbids group-read. Tool should reject any non-zero group/other perm bits, not just world-read.

## [LOW] Chunk anomaly detection (duration < 1s) implicitly requires ffprobe
§6 last row references a duration check on chunk audio. ffmpeg can write duration to stderr but parsing is fragile; ffprobe is the clean path. ffprobe is not listed as a runtime dep in §3 doctor or §8.6 dependencies. Either add it or change the detection method.

## [LOW] ManifestEntry.Author default "Paul Graham" — assignment locus unspecified
§2 EssayMeta has `Author string` with comment `default "Paul Graham"`. Where is the default set — in the extractor (hardcoded), or in config? Affects wa-kyn.4. Trivial for v1 (single author) but blocks Phase I (other authors).

## [LOW] Manifest forward/backward compatibility — only one direction specified
§6: older tool refuses to overwrite newer-schema manifest (good). Reverse direction (newer tool reading older manifest) is silent. Auto-upgrade vs error vs migrate-on-write all valid; pick one.

## [LOW] Source dir disappearance between doctor and build is unhandled
`doctor` validates source dir; `build` could run hours later. If the wiki repo was moved/unmounted, `build` will fail mid-essay with a generic file-read error. Consider re-validating source dir at start of `build` with the same error message as doctor.

## [LOW] §9.2 worker code uses charCodeAt on UTF-16 code units, not bytes
For ASCII tokens (the spec-defined character set) this is fine. But the function is presented as a generic timingSafeEqual primitive; if the token policy ever broadens to non-ASCII, surrogate-pair tokens break the byte-equivalence assumption. Recommend either narrowing the function name to reflect ASCII-only or switching to TextEncoder + Uint8Array compare.

comments.text:
Addendum from a second pass over §1 / §2 / §6.

Counts in this addendum: 1 high, 3 medium, 1 low.

## [HIGH] §1's `wiki box is fully stateless apart from config` claim is false under the plan's own recovery model
- Publish depends on local `~/.cache/wiki-audio/out/<slug>.mp3` artifacts.
- Skip history lives only in local `~/.cache/wiki-audio/skipped.txt`.
- §6 also relies on local `~/.cache/wiki-audio/tmp/<slug>/` chunk retention for ffmpeg debugging.
- Re-installing or swapping machines can therefore preserve manifest state in R2 while still stranding unpublished audio or skip history.
- Fix: either soften the stateless claim in §1, or move the recovery-relevant state into the manifest / R2 so local cache is truly optional.

## [MEDIUM] `Manifest.Version` says `default 1`, but no constructor or normalization step is specified
- §2 gives `Version int // schema version, default 1`.
- Unlike TOML comments, Go structs do not apply defaults on their own; a fresh zero-value manifest will serialize as `0` unless save code sets it explicitly.
- §6 relies on version comparisons for safety (`older tool refuses to overwrite newer-schema manifest`), so `0 vs 1` ambiguity weakens the upgrade guard.
- Fix: specify `NewManifest()` or `normalizeManifest()` that sets `Version=1` before first save.

## [MEDIUM] `PublishedAt` mutation policy is undefined, but feed ordering depends on it
- `ManifestEntry` carries both `GeneratedAt` and `PublishedAt`.
- The feed policy later says to order by `PublishedAt`, not by the essay's original publication date.
- The spec never says whether re-publishing an existing slug after a voice/model/format change preserves the old `PublishedAt` or bumps it to `now`.
- That choice determines whether a corpus-wide regen silently preserves feed order or floods the podcast inbox with old essays at the top.
- Fix: make the rule explicit in the manifest/publish spec.

## [MEDIUM] The executive-summary install story understates the real runtime requirements on the target machine
- §1 sells the tool as a single static binary with zero runtime dependencies.
- The actual runtime path still requires `ffmpeg`, and the duration-anomaly checks in §6 likely require `ffprobe` if kept.
- That distinction appears later in the plan, but not in the top-level install/portability story.
- Fix: state in §1 that distribution is a single binary, but media tooling is still a target prerequisite verified by `wiki-audio doctor`.

## [LOW] `EssayMeta.SourcePath` being absolute makes otherwise-identical runs machine-specific
- §2 defines `SourcePath` as an absolute path to the source `.md`.
- If this value is ever logged, surfaced via `inspect`, or copied into serialized debug artifacts, two machines with the same repo at different roots produce different outputs for no semantic reason.
- This is mostly a reproducibility/debug-hygiene issue, not a correctness bug.
- Fix: store a repo-relative path in the model and resolve to absolute only at the filesystem boundary.

title: [LOW] tts: 408 classification differs between client.retryableStatusCode and classifyHTTPStatus
description:
## Defect

Two functions in `internal/tts/` classify HTTP status 408 (Request Timeout) differently:

- `client.go::retryableStatusCode(408)` returns **true** (lines 136-140), so `APIError{StatusCode: 408}.Retryable` is `true`.
- `retry.go::classifyHTTPStatus(408, ...)` falls into the 4xx-default branch and returns **fatal** (lines 81-82).

## Why this is LOW (not blocking)

- ElevenLabs is unlikely to emit 408 — Cloudflare in front of api.elevenlabs.io would surface idle/connect timeouts as transport errors, and the server-side timeout we're realistically going to hit is 504 or a context.DeadlineExceeded, not 408.
- The build pipeline (wa-4cw.5) consumes `*APIError` from `client.Synthesize` and routes through `classifyAPIError`, which honors `apiErr.Retryable` — so the runtime path is consistent with the client's view (408 → retryable). The divergence only surfaces if someone calls `classifyHTTPStatus` directly with a raw `*http.Response`, which no production caller does today.

## Why still file it

Two functions claiming to classify the same input shouldn't disagree. A future caller (e.g. a hypothetical mid-stream-failure path that wants to peek at the response before draining the body) would silently get the wrong verdict.

## Suggested fix

In `retry.go::classifyHTTPStatus`, add an explicit case for 408 mirroring 429 — retryable with computed backoff (Retry-After is not standard on 408). One-liner:

```go
case statusCode == http.StatusRequestTimeout:
    return retryDecision{verdict: retryVerdictRetryable, sleep: computeBackoff(attempt, baseSeconds, rng)}
```

Add a corresponding `http_408` row to `TestClassifyHTTPResponse`.

## References

- Spec: §5.3 (only enumerates 200/429/402-403/5xx; 408 not in spec — LOW because it's underspec'd, not contradicted)
- Code: `internal/tts/client.go:136-140` and `internal/tts/retry.go:81-82`
- Reviewed at commits 79aedf0 (client) and 5fdc40d (retry)
